discovery.summary: Analyze an Animation Sequence's motion from its own frames: how far and fast the root travels and turns, when each foot is planted and how fast a planted foot still moves, how closely the last frame meets the first, and the bones with the sharpest rotation spikes.
whenToUse: Footstep notifies must go where the feet land (feet[].contacts are the planted intervals in seconds).
A walk or run must match the character's movement speed: an in-place clip's plantedSpeed is the ground speed it implies; a root-motion clip's should be near 0.
A clip must be checked for a clean loop or for pops before it is used.
whenNotToUse: Only the length, notifies or curves are needed (use get_animation_info).
A character playing in a running game must be measured (use control_actor get_transform motion).

assetPath.description: Animation Sequence asset path, e.g. /Game/Anims/A_Run (a montage or blend space is refused: analyze the sequences it plays).

feet.description: Foot bones to check (default every bone whose name holds foot but not ik, e.g. foot_l and foot_r).

contactHeight.description: cm above a foot's lowest point that still counts as planted (default 5).

maxSamples.description: Frames sampled, spread evenly with the first and last always in (default 300, at most 2000; a shorter clip samples every frame).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

rootMotion.description: The root bone's path in component space (in-place clips stay at 0).

enabled.description: Whether the sequence has root motion enabled.

displacement.description: From the first to the last frame, [x, y, z] in cm.

loop.description: Last frame against the first, every bone but the root in its parent's space: near 0 is a clean loop.

worstBone.description: The bone with the largest rotation.

contacts.description: Planted intervals as [start, end] in seconds (at most 32).

plantedRatio.description: Share of sampled frames the foot is planted (0-1).

plantedSpeed.description: Average horizontal speed of the planted foot in cm/s: the ground speed an in-place clip implies, or foot slide on a root-motion clip.

pops.description: The three bones whose rotation spikes fastest: a pop shows as one far above the rest.

examples.title: Analyze an Animation Sequence's motion from its own frames: how far and fast the root travels and turns, when each foot is planted and how fast a planted foot still moves, how closely the last frame meets the first, and the bones with the sharpest rotation spikes.

output.message: A_Run: 0.70 s, 22 frames; the root travels 0.0 cm (0.0 cm/s); 2 foot bone(s); loop seam 0.05 cm, 0.4 deg.

discovery.summary: Lay out a locomotion blend space from its clips' own motion: each Animation Sequence in animationPaths is read from its frames (a root that travels is the clip's motion; a root that stays is an in-place clip, read from its planted feet, which slide backward at the ground speed) and placed by its speed and direction in the character's frame. forwardAxis is the way the character faces in its clips (+Y for the UE mannequin). axes picks what each axis holds: speed (cm/s), direction (degrees: 0 forward, +90 right, 180 back), forwardSpeed or rightSpeed (signed cm/s); default speed for a Blend Space 1D, direction and speed for a Blend Space. The axes are set to hold every sample: speed from 0 to the top speed rounded up to 50, signed speeds symmetric, direction -180 to 180 with wrapping input. A clip within 10 degrees of backward takes both direction edges, an idle (under 10 cm/s) takes every direction used, at speed 0, and a position another clip or a kept sample already holds is refused (refused in that clip's row). The listed clips replace the samples, or with keepSamples join them, in one undo step, saved unless save is false; dryRun answers the same and changes nothing. Refused, changing nothing: BLENDSPACE_NOT_FOUND, ANIMATION_NOT_FOUND, ANIMATION_INCOMPATIBLE (another skeleton, or an additive type the blend space or the other clips do not share), EMPTY_ANIMATION, BONE_NOT_FOUND (a bone named in feet), INVALID_ARGUMENT (an Aim Offset, an unknown axis, axes that do not fit the blend space).
whenToUse: A walk/run (1D) or a directional locomotion (2D) blend space must place its clips where their motion puts them, instead of guessing speeds.
Checking how fast and which way each clip moves before building a blend space (dryRun).
whenNotToUse: One sample must go at a chosen value (use edit_blend_space with add_blend_sample).
An Aim Offset (use add_aim_offset_sample).
Only one clip's motion must be read (use analyze_animation).

assetPath.description: Blend Space or Blend Space 1D asset path, e.g. /Game/Anims/BS_Locomotion.

animationPaths.description: The Animation Sequences to place (1-32), each of the blend space's skeleton.

axes.description: What each axis holds, horizontal first: one for a Blend Space 1D (default speed), two different ones for a Blend Space (default direction, speed).

forwardAxis.description: The way the character faces in its clips' component space (default +Y, as the UE mannequin; a mesh made facing +X takes +X). Right is forward turned +90 degrees in yaw.

feet.description: Foot bones read for an in-place clip (default every bone whose name holds foot but not ik, e.g. foot_l and foot_r).

contactHeight.description: cm above a foot's lowest point that still counts as planted (default 5).

keepSamples.description: Keep the samples the blend space holds and add the clips beside them (default false: the clips replace them). The axes then also hold the kept samples.

dryRun.description: Measure and lay out, changing nothing.

save.description: Save the blend space afterwards (default true).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

axes.description: Each axis as set (or as it would be under dryRun).

axisName.description: Speed, Direction, Forward Speed or Right Speed.

wrapInput.description: Input past an edge wraps around (direction).

clips.description: One row per clip, in the order given.

direction.description: Degrees: 0 forward, +90 right, 180 back (0 for an idle).

source.description: root: its root travels; feet: in place, read from its planted feet.

positions.description: Where its samples went, as [x, y] (y 0 in a Blend Space 1D).

refused.description: Positions dropped because another clip or a kept sample holds them.

samples.description: Samples the blend space holds now (under dryRun: the samples the layout would add).

saved.description: Whether the blend space was saved.

undo.description: What editor undo takes back: {undoable, transactionScope}; the whole layout is one step.

discovery.summary: Delete animation assets by path (artifacts), each closed in any editor and garbage collected first. Paths that do not exist are listed under missing; when none of them existed the call still succeeds, saying nothing needed removing. No undo and no reference check: an asset others still use leaves them pointing at nothing.

whenNotToUse: The work should be kept.
Other assets may still use them: check their referencers first (asset.inspect_asset with lookup=dependencies and referencers=true).

discovery.summary: Change an Animation Blueprint's AnimGraph, chosen by edit. add_layered_blend_per_bone adds a Layered Blend Per Bone node that layers each blend pose over the bones its branch filters name (a bone not on the skeleton is BONE_NOT_FOUND) and names the node for wiring. set_value sets a node setting (Alpha, PlayRate, bLoopAnimation, NodeComment) or the animation an asset player plays, by node name or nodeId, and reads it back; NODE_NOT_FOUND lists the nodes and AMBIGUOUS_NODE the matches. Both save unless save is false.
whenToUse: edit=add_layered_blend_per_bone: Part of the body must play another animation than the rest, such as attacking or aiming while walking.
edit=set_value: A graph node property must change.
edit=set_value: A Sequence Player or Blend Space Player must play a different animation.
whenNotToUse: edit=add_layered_blend_per_bone: A whole-body blend between poses (add_blend_node).
edit=set_value: Use add_blend_node.

blueprintPath.description: Animation Blueprint whose AnimGraph is edited.

layerSetup.description: One entry per blend pose, in pin order: [{ branchFilters: [{ boneName, blendDepth }] }]. A filter takes boneName and every bone under it from that blend pose over the base pose: blendDepth 0 (default) at full weight at once, N ramps the weight up over N bones down the chain (the named bone gets 1/N), and a negative depth on a bone under an earlier filter takes that branch back out (-1 removes it). Every bone must be on the Animation Blueprint's skeleton (BONE_NOT_FOUND).

boneName.description: Shorthand for one layer filtering this bone and its children; ignored when layerSetup is sent.

positionX.description: Graph X position of the new node (default 0).

positionY.description: Graph Y position of the new node (default 0).

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

nodeName.description: The node: its object name (AnimGraphNode_SequencePlayer_0), its GUID (the nodeId create_node, add_state and inspect_graph report), or a custom name set in its NodeComment or its title when one node has it. Looks in the AnimGraph and in the state machines and states under it; a name that matches nothing answers NODE_NOT_FOUND listing every node (nodes), and one that matches several AMBIGUOUS_NODE listing them (candidates).

nodeId.description: The node GUID; an alternative to nodeName.

propertyName.description: The property: a member of the node's settings struct (Alpha, PlayRate, bLoopAnimation, Sequence) or of the graph node (NodeComment), with dots for a nested one (Node.PlayRate). On an asset player the asset property (Sequence, BlendSpace) is written through the node's own setter and read back, and fails when the node did not take it; any other property is written by reflection and its stored value read back.

value.description: The value: a number, boolean or string, an {x,y,z} or {r,g,b,a} object for a struct, or for an asset property the asset path (/Game/Anims/A_Idle).

edit.description:
Which configure anim graph node variant to run.
add_layered_blend_per_bone: Add a Layered Blend Per Bone node to an Animation Blueprint's AnimGraph: its base pose everywhere, with each blend pose layered over the bones its branch filters name (layerSetup, or boneName for one layer from that bone down). The classic use is an attack on the upper body, from spine_01 through the arms and head, while the legs keep the walk of the base pose. One Blend Poses pin is made per layer: the node takes BasePose, BlendPoses_N and BlendWeights_N (weight 1 by default) and outputs Pose. A bone not on the skeleton is BONE_NOT_FOUND and a malformed entry INVALID_LAYER_SETUP; with neither layerSetup nor boneName the node blends nothing, and the message says so. The node is placed unwired at positionX, positionY; the reply names it (nodeName, nodeId) for manage_blueprint edit_graph connect_pins. Saved unless save is false (saved).
set_value: Set a value on an AnimGraph node: a setting of the node (Alpha, PlayRate, bLoopAnimation, NodeComment), or the animation an asset player plays (Sequence on a Sequence Player, BlendSpace on a Blend Space Player) by its asset path; the reply reads the stored value back.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

nodeName.description: Object name of the node made.

nodeId.description: GUID of the node made: the nodeId graph edits take.

layerCount.description: Blend poses with branch filters set.

saved.description: Boolean parameter.

propertyName.description: Echoes propertyName.

value.description: The value now stored, read back from the node: the asset path for an asset property.

examples.title: Change an Animation Blueprint's AnimGraph, chosen by edit. add_layered_blend_per_bone adds a Layered Blend Per Bone node that layers each blend pose over the bones its branch filters name (a bone not on the skeleton is BONE_NOT_FOUND) and names the node for wiring. set_value sets a node setting (Alpha, PlayRate, bLoopAnimation, NodeComment) or the animation an asset player plays, by node name or nodeId, and reads it back; NODE_NOT_FOUND lists the nodes and AMBIGUOUS_NODE the matches. Both save unless save is false.

output.message: Layered blend per bone node created with 1 layer(s)

discovery.summary: Sockets on a skeleton (skeletonPath; a skeletal mesh path uses its skeleton), chosen by socketOp; each change is saved unless save is false (saved). create (add) puts socketName on attachBoneName, which both require, at relativeLocation, relativeRotation and relativeScale (default zero, zero and one); a bone the skeleton lacks is BONE_NOT_FOUND and a taken name SOCKET_EXISTS. configure (modify) changes an existing socket: attachBoneName moves it, and relativeLocation, relativeRotation and relativeScale replace only the parts given; a missing socket is SOCKET_NOT_FOUND and a call naming nothing to change is refused.
whenToUse: socketOp=configure|modify: Socket offset must change.
socketOp=add|create: An attach point is needed.
whenNotToUse: socketOp=add|create: Use an existing socket.

relativeLocation.description: Socket location relative to its attach bone as [x, y, z].

relativeRotation.description: Socket rotation relative to its attach bone as [pitch, yaw, roll].

relativeScale.description: Socket scale relative to its attach bone as [x, y, z].

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

socketOp.description:
Which configure socket variant to run; omit for 'configure'.
configure: Change an existing socket of a skeleton (skeletonPath; a skeletal mesh path uses its skeleton): attachBoneName moves it to another bone, and relativeLocation, relativeRotation and relativeScale replace only the parts given. A missing socket is SOCKET_NOT_FOUND, an unknown bone BONE_NOT_FOUND, and a call naming nothing to change is refused. The skeleton is saved unless save is false (saved).
add: Put a socket named socketName on attachBoneName of a skeleton (skeletonPath; a skeletal mesh path uses its skeleton), at relativeLocation, relativeRotation and relativeScale (default zero, zero and one). A bone the skeleton lacks is BONE_NOT_FOUND and a name already taken SOCKET_EXISTS. The skeleton is saved unless save is false (saved).
create: Put a socket named socketName on attachBoneName of a skeleton (skeletonPath; a skeletal mesh path uses its skeleton), at relativeLocation, relativeRotation and relativeScale (default zero, zero and one). A bone the skeleton lacks is BONE_NOT_FOUND and a name already taken SOCKET_EXISTS. The skeleton is saved unless save is false (saved).
modify: Change an existing socket of a skeleton (skeletonPath; a skeletal mesh path uses its skeleton): attachBoneName moves it to another bone, and relativeLocation, relativeRotation and relativeScale replace only the parts given. A missing socket is SOCKET_NOT_FOUND, an unknown bone BONE_NOT_FOUND, and a call naming nothing to change is refused. The skeleton is saved unless save is false (saved).

discovery.summary: Create an animation asset: a sequence, montage, blend space (1D/2D), aim offset, pose asset from a sequence, or procedural animation.
whenToUse: kind=asset|blend_space: An animation asset or graph must be authored.
kind=sequence: A keyframed clip is needed.
kind=montage: A playable montage is needed.
kind=blend_space_1d: A single-axis blend is needed.
kind=blend_space_2d: A two-axis blend is needed.
kind=aim_offset: Aim blending by look direction is needed.
kind=pose_library: Named poses (facial shapes, hand poses, correctives) must be blended by name in an Animation Blueprint.
kind=procedural: A runtime-authored animation is needed.
whenNotToUse: kind=aim_offset: Use a blend space.
kind=pose_library: A playable clip is needed; use kind sequence or montage.
kind=procedural: Use a static sequence.

name.description: Name for the created asset or actor.

path.description: Canonical /Game output path for the created asset.

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

animationPath.description: Sequence the montage plays; its skeleton is used when skeletonPath is omitted.

slotName.description: Name of the montage slot (default DefaultSlot).

sourceAnimationPath.description: AnimSequence whose key frames become the poses; its skeleton is used.

poseNames.description: Distinct names for the poses in frame order; frames without a name keep the engine default name.

additive.description: Make the poses additive against pose 0, as facial and corrective poses are (default false).

boneTracks.description: Bone tracks to key: [{ boneName, frames: [{ frame, rotationDelta?: {pitch,yaw,roll}, rotation?: {pitch,yaw,roll}|{x,y,z,w}, location?: {x,y,z}, scale?: {x,y,z} }] }]. frame runs 0 to numFrames inclusive. Only the poses that matter need keys: frames between two keys of a channel are blended (rotation slerped), frames before its first key or after its last hold that key. Channels left out keep the reference pose of that bone, so a rotation-only track poses without collapsing the skeleton. Prefer rotationDelta, which bends the bone relative to its rest orientation; plain rotation replaces the local rotation outright and needs the rest orientation to already be known. Calling it again with the name of an existing clip re-keys that clip from empty (its additive settings are kept).

kind.description:
Which create animation asset variant to run; omit for 'asset'.
asset: Create an empty Animation Sequence (assetType sequence, the default) or Montage on skeletonPath, named name in path (default /Game/Animations, made if missing), and save it. A montage starts with the DefaultSlot track and no animation. An asset of that class already at the path is reused (existingAsset); another class there is ASSET_TYPE_MISMATCH. For a sequence with a length and frame rate use kind sequence; for a montage from an animation, kind montage.
sequence: Create an Animation Sequence asset.
montage: Create a montage asset, optionally from a sequence.
blend_space: Create a 2D Blend Space for skeletonPath (required) as name in path (default /Game/Animations) and save it: horizontal axis horizontalAxisName (Direction, -180 to 180 by default), vertical verticalAxisName (Speed, 0 to 600), 4 grid divisions each; add_blend_sample places animations on it. A blend space already there is kept as it is and answered with existingAsset and the axes it has (set_axis_settings changes them); another asset there is ASSET_TYPE_MISMATCH. The reply gives assetPath and saved.
blend_space_1d: Create a 1D Blend Space for skeletonPath (required) as name in path (default /Game/Animations) and save it: one axis, axisName (Speed by default) from axisMin to axisMax (0 to 600), 4 grid divisions. A blend space already there is kept as it is and answered with existingAsset and the axis it has (set_axis_settings changes it); another asset there is ASSET_TYPE_MISMATCH. The reply gives assetPath and saved.
blend_space_2d: Create a 2D Blend Space, as kind=blend_space does: skeletonPath required, horizontal axis Direction -180 to 180 and vertical Speed 0 to 600 unless given, saved; one already there is kept and answered with existingAsset and its axes.
aim_offset: Create an Aim Offset for skeletonPath (required) as name in path (default /Game/Animations) and save it, with the axes aim offsets use: Yaw -180 to 180 and Pitch -90 to 90, 4 grid divisions each (set_axis_settings changes them). Its samples are additive rotation-offset (mesh space) poses, added with add_aim_offset_sample. A taken name is refused. The reply gives assetPath and saved.
pose_library: Create a Pose Asset from an animation sequence, one pose per key frame, on the sequence's skeleton; PoseByName and PoseBlender nodes play its poses.
procedural: Create a procedural anim asset.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

poseNames.description: Pose names read back from the asset.

saved.description: Whether the pose asset was saved.

skeletonSaved.description: UE 5.0 to 5.2: whether the skeleton, which holds the pose curve names there, was saved.

discovery.summary: Create or tune a physical material: friction (an icy or slippery floor, a grippy one), bounce (restitution), density and how two touching surfaces combine them. A mesh takes it through control_actor edit_component property PhysMaterialOverride (edit_scs set_property on a class template).
whenToUse: An object must bounce, slide or grip differently: a bouncy ball (restitution 0.9, restitutionCombineMode Max), an ice floor (friction 0.05, frictionCombineMode Min).
A physical material must be adjusted: the same name and path tune it in place.
whenNotToUse: A character slides or grips the ground: use manage_character set_movement_property (ground friction, braking).

name.description: Asset name, e.g. PM_Bouncy.

path.description: Folder for the asset (default /Game/Physics).

friction.description: Kinetic friction, 0 (ice) to 1 and above (rubber); the engine default is 0.7.

staticFriction.description: Friction at rest, before a body starts to slide.

density.description: Density in g/cm3, which sets mass from volume (water is 1).

frictionCombineMode.description: How this surface and the one it touches combine their friction: Min lets the slipperier (or deader) one win, Max the grippier (or bouncier) one; Average when not set.

restitutionCombineMode.description: How this surface and the one it touches combine their bounce: Min lets the slipperier (or deader) one win, Max the grippier (or bouncier) one; Average when not set.

physicalMaterialPath.description: Object path of the physical material.

created.description: True when this call made it; false when it tuned one already there.

discovery.summary: Edit an Animation Blueprint graph: blend, cached-pose and slot nodes, state machines, states, transitions and transition rules, blend trees. Any other AnimGraph node (Two Bone IK, Modify Bone, Blend Space Player) is created by class with manage_blueprint edit_graph create_node.
whenToUse: edit=add_blend_node: Graph needs a blend node.
edit=add_cached_pose: One pose (a locomotion state machine) must feed several places of the AnimGraph without being evaluated twice.
edit=add_slot_node: Montages (attacks, reloads, emotes) must play on a character whose Animation Blueprint has no Slot node for their slot.
edit=create_state_machine: State-driven animation is needed.
edit=add_state_machine: A state machine must be embedded.
edit=add_state: A new animation state is needed.
edit=add_transition: States must connect.
edit=set_transition_rules: Transition condition must change.
edit=set_transition_rules: A state machine must actually be able to leave a state: author the condition here after add_transition.
edit=delete_transition: A transition was authored between the wrong two states.
edit=delete_transition: A transition is dead weight and its rule graph should go with it.
edit=create_blend_tree: Several animations must be switchable through one blend node in an AnimBlueprint.
whenNotToUse: edit=add_cached_pose: Inline pose suffices.
edit=add_slot_node: The montage asset itself is made (create_montage).
edit=create_state_machine: A single graph suffices.
edit=delete_transition: The state itself must go, not just the transition.

blueprintPath.description: Animation Blueprint whose AnimGraph is edited.

positionX.description: Graph X position of the new node (default 0).

positionY.description: Graph Y position of the new node (default 0).

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

slotName.description: Slot name.

groupName.description: Slot group a new slot joins on the skeleton (default DefaultGroup). Montages in one group interrupt each other; a slot already on the skeleton keeps its group.

transitions.description: Transitions to create between the listed states, as [{ sourceState, targetState }].

stateMachineName.description: Target state machine name inside the Animation Blueprint.

animations.description: Animation asset paths to play in this state; one Sequence Player is created per entry and the first drives the state Result pose. Without it the state is created empty and the character holds its reference pose.

crossfadeDuration.description: Transition blend duration in seconds. blendTime is accepted as an alias.

priorityOrder.description: Evaluation order when several transitions out of one state can fire on the same frame; the lowest wins.

automaticRule.description: Fire the transition when the source state's sequence player reaches the end of its animation instead of testing a condition. Left alone when omitted.

bidirectional.description: Whether the transition also applies from toState back to fromState. Left alone when omitted.

conditionVariable.description: Animation Blueprint variable the transition rule tests, e.g. Speed or bFalling. Without it the rule graph is left unconnected, which reads as false forever and the state machine never leaves its entry state.

conditionComparison.description: How conditionVariable is tested: greater (default), less, greater_equal, less_equal for a numeric variable; true or false for a bool.

conditionValue.description: Right-hand value for a numeric conditionComparison (default 0). Ignored for true/false.

name.description: Name for the created asset or actor.

treeName.description: Comment/name for the blend node (alias of name).

connectToOutput.description: Wire the blend node into the AnimGraph output pose (default true).

edit.description:
Which edit anim graph variant to run.
add_blend_node: Add a blend node to an AnimGraph.
add_cached_pose: Add a Save Cached Pose node named cacheName to the AnimGraph of an Animation Blueprint, at positionX, positionY (default 0, 0); a Use Cached Pose node of that name then reads the pose anywhere in the graph. A name another cached pose in the Blueprint has is CACHE_NAME_TAKEN. The Blueprint is compiled and saved unless save is false; the reply gives cacheName as the node holds it, nodeId and saved.
add_slot_node: Add a Slot node to an Animation Blueprint's AnimGraph: a montage plays only through a Slot node whose slotName matches its slot track, so put one between the locomotion pose and the output. slotName is the bare name montages use (DefaultSlot, UpperBody). A new slot goes in groupName on the skeleton (default DefaultGroup; another group is added and the skeleton saved, skeletonSaved); a slot the skeleton already has keeps its group, and a different groupName is refused (SLOT_IN_OTHER_GROUP). The node is placed unwired at positionX, positionY (its Source input takes the pose to play over, its Pose output goes on toward the Output Pose node's Result); the reply names it (nodeName, nodeId) for manage_blueprint edit_graph connect_pins. Saved unless save is false (saved).
create_state_machine: Create a State Machine graph asset.
add_state_machine: Add a State Machine node to an AnimGraph.
add_state: Add a state to a State Machine.
add_transition: Add a transition between two states.
set_transition_rules: Set transition rule logic: the condition a transition tests, plus its blend timing.
delete_transition: Delete a transition from a State Machine.
create_blend_tree: Author a blend tree in an AnimBlueprint AnimGraph: a Blend List (by int) node fed by one Sequence Player per animation, optionally wired to the output pose.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

slotName.description: The slot name the node plays.

groupName.description: The slot group the slot is in on the skeleton.

nodeName.description: Object name of the node made.

nodeId.description: GUID of the node made: the nodeId graph edits take.

saved.description: Whether the Animation Blueprint reached disk.

skeletonSaved.description: Whether the skeleton, given a new slot group, reached disk.

animationsApplied.description: One entry per created Sequence Player. Only the first can be connected to the state Result pose.

animationsFailed.description: Requested animation paths that could not be loaded.

condition.description: The rule that was written into the transition graph. Absent means no conditionVariable was given, so the transition stays false and the state is never left.

deleted.description: True when the transition and its rule graph were removed.

discovery.summary: Edit an animation sequence: bone tracks and keys, curve keys, notifies, sync markers, additive and root-motion settings, length, aim-offset samples.
whenToUse: edit=add_bone_track: A bone must be animated.
edit=set_bone_key: Keyframe a bone pose.
edit=set_curve_key: Animate a curve.
edit=add_notify: Frame event in a sequence.
edit=add_notify_state: A ranged notify is needed.
edit=add_sync_marker: Sync groups needed.
edit=set_additive_settings: Additive layering needed.

edit=set_additive_settings: A hand-keyed move (an arm raise, a head turn) must play on top of a mocap clip: key it as a procedural clip relative to the reference pose, then make it LocalSpaceAdditive with basePoseType RefPose.
edit=set_root_motion_settings: Root motion locomotion needed.
edit=set_sequence_length: Clip duration must change.
edit=add_aim_offset_sample: Aim sample must be added.
whenNotToUse: edit=add_bone_track: Track exists.
edit=add_notify: Use add_montage_notify.
edit=add_sync_marker: No sync required.
edit=set_additive_settings: Absolute pose.
edit=set_root_motion_settings: In-place animation.
edit=set_sequence_length: Use create_animation_sequence.
edit=add_aim_offset_sample: Use create_aim_offset.

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

location.description: Bone location relative to its parent; left out, the bone keeps its own at this frame.

rotation.description: Bone rotation relative to its parent as [pitch, yaw, roll]; left out, the bone keeps its own at this frame.

scale.description: Bone scale as [x, y, z]; left out, the bone keeps its own at this frame.

value.description: Property value (any type).

createIfMissing.description: Create the curve when the sequence does not have it (default true).

notifyClass.description: AnimNotify (or AnimNotifyState) class name; prefixed with AnimNotify_/AnimNotifyState_ automatically when missing.

time.description: Trigger time in seconds, used when frame is omitted.

trackIndex.description: Notify track index within the animation sequence.

startFrame.description: First frame of the notify state range.

endFrame.description: Last frame of the notify state range.

additiveAnimType.description: NoAdditive (default) plays the clip as a full pose. LocalSpaceAdditive keeps only its difference from the base pose and adds that on top of whatever plays under it (a Sequencer section on another row, Apply Additive in an Animation Blueprint). MeshSpaceAdditive adds rotations in mesh space, for aim offsets; Sequencer cannot play it.

basePoseType.description: What the additive difference is taken from (default RefPose): RefPose = the skeleton reference pose, AnimScaled = basePoseAnimation frame by frame, AnimFrame = one frame (basePoseFrame) of basePoseAnimation.

basePoseFrame.description: Frame used as the additive base pose.

basePoseAnimation.description: Animation sequence to take the additive base pose from.

enableRootMotion.description: Move the character by the motion of the root bone instead of playing in place (default true).

rootMotionRootLock.description: The pose the root is locked to: RefPose (default), AnimFirstFrame or Zero, in any case; another value reads as RefPose.

forceRootLock.description: Whether root motion is force-locked to the reference pose.

length.description: New length in seconds, used when numFrames is omitted.

frameRate.description: Frames per second; the sequence keeps its current rate when omitted.

edit.description:
Which edit animation variant to run.
add_bone_track: Add an empty transform track for boneName to an animation sequence (assetPath, or animationPath), to key with edit=set_bone_key. A bone its skeleton lacks is BONE_NOT_FOUND_IN_SKELETON, listing bones. A track the sequence already has is left as it is and answered with alreadyExists true and nothing saved; otherwise the sequence is saved unless save is false (saved).
set_bone_key: Set a bone transform key at a frame; a location, rotation or scale left out keeps the value the bone has there (the key of its track, or the reference pose for a bone with no track yet). Frame 0 is the first key and the sequence's frame count its last (a 1 s clip at 30 fps keys frames 0 to 30); past either end is FRAME_OUT_OF_RANGE.
set_curve_key: Set a key of the float curve curveName in an animation sequence at frame (default 0) to value: a curve the sequence lacks is added (curveCreated) unless createIfMissing is false, which refuses it (CURVE_NOT_FOUND), and a key the engine does not take is CURVE_KEY_FAILED. The reply reads the curve back at that frame (value) and says whether it saved (saved, unless save is false). Curves drive morph targets and material parameters, and AnimBlueprints read them by name.
add_notify: Add a frame notify to a sequence (authoring).
add_notify_state: Add a notify state spanning a frame range.
add_sync_marker: Add a sync marker to a sequence.
set_additive_settings: Configure additive animation settings.
set_root_motion_settings: Configure root motion on an animation sequence: whether the motion of the root bone moves the character (enableRootMotion), which pose the root is locked to while that motion is taken out (rootMotionRootLock), and whether the root is locked even without root motion (forceRootLock). Saved unless save is false; SEQUENCE_NOT_FOUND when no sequence loads.
set_sequence_length: Set the length of an Animation Sequence.
add_aim_offset_sample: Add a sample pose to an Aim Offset.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Edit an animation sequence: bone tracks and keys, curve keys, notifies, sync markers, additive and root-motion settings, length, aim-offset samples.

discovery.summary: Edit a Blend Space or Aim Offset (assetPath), chosen by edit. add_sample places animationPath at sampleValue (a number on a 1D blend space, {x, y} on a 2D one; the axis range grows to fit) and returns sampleIndex; a position another sample holds, or an animation of another skeleton or additive type, is refused (SAMPLE_REJECTED). set_axis_settings changes one axis (Horizontal, the default, or Vertical; a 1D blend space has Horizontal only): only the axisName, minValue, maxValue and gridDivisions sent change, minValue stays below maxValue, and the reply gives the axis as it now is. set_interpolation_settings sets input smoothing on every axis and the sample weight speed, only the fields sent. rebuild drops invalid samples, rebuilds the grid and recompiles the Animation Blueprints that use it (compileReferencers, default true), listing any that fail. Saved unless save is false (saved).
whenToUse: edit=add_sample: Blend sample needed.
edit=set_axis_settings: Axis labels/ranges must change.
edit=set_interpolation_settings: Interpolation must change.
edit=rebuild: Axis bounds changed and dependents must recompile.
whenNotToUse: edit=add_sample: Use create_blend_space.
edit=rebuild: Normal save suffices.

sampleValue.description: Sample position: a number on a 1D blend space, or {x, y} (or [x, y]) on a 2D one.

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

axis.description: Axis to change: X or Horizontal (default), Y or Vertical.

gridDivisions.description: Number of grid divisions on the axis.

interpolationType.description: Input smoothing type for every axis; it only acts while interpolationTime is above 0.

interpolationTime.description: Input smoothing time in seconds for every axis (0 turns smoothing off).

targetWeightInterpolationSpeed.description: Sample weight speed per second (0 turns weight smoothing off).

edit.description:
Which edit blend space variant to run.
add_sample: Add a blend sample to a Blend Space.
set_axis_settings: Change one axis of a blend space (axis: X or Horizontal, the default, or Y or Vertical, which a 1D blend space lacks): axisName, minValue, maxValue and gridDivisions, each kept when not sent. minValue must stay below maxValue and gridDivisions at least 1. Samples are checked against the new range and the runtime data rebuilt, as the blend space editor does. The reply reads the axis back and gives saved (unless save is false).
set_interpolation_settings: Set Blend Space input smoothing and sample weight speed; only the fields sent change.
rebuild: Force a Blend Space rebuild and recompile referencers.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Edit a Blend Space or Aim Offset (assetPath), chosen by edit. add_sample places animationPath at sampleValue (a number on a 1D blend space, {x, y} on a 2D one; the axis range grows to fit) and returns sampleIndex; a position another sample holds, or an animation of another skeleton or additive type, is refused (SAMPLE_REJECTED). set_axis_settings changes one axis (Horizontal, the default, or Vertical; a 1D blend space has Horizontal only): only the axisName, minValue, maxValue and gridDivisions sent change, minValue stays below maxValue, and the reply gives the axis as it now is. set_interpolation_settings sets input smoothing on every axis and the sample weight speed, only the fields sent. rebuild drops invalid samples, rebuilds the grid and recompiles the Animation Blueprints that use it (compileReferencers, default true), listing any that fail. Saved unless save is false (saved).

discovery.summary: Edit a Control Rig: add a unit node (list_rig_units finds them), connect or disconnect pins, set a pin value, remove a node, import the skeleton's bones, add a bone, null or control, or remove an element; one edit or many steps, then one compile and save. The reply lists what each edit made (a new node with its pins).
whenToUse: A Control Rig needs its logic built: units such as Get Transform, Two Bone IK or Set Transform wired from the Forwards Solve event (a new rig may have none: add_unit BeginExecution adds it).
A rig needs bones from its skeleton, or controls and nulls to drive them.
whenNotToUse: The rig asset does not exist yet (use create_control_rig).
Only reading the rig (use get_control_rig).
An IK Rig or retargeter (use create_ik_rig, setup_ik).

edit.description: The edit to make (each step of steps names its own).

unit.description: add_unit: the unit, as an object path (/Script/ControlRig.RigUnit_SetTransform), its struct name with or without RigUnit_ (SetTransform), or its display name.

name.description: add_unit: the new node's name (default the unit's, made unique); add_bone, add_null, add_control, remove_element: the element's name.

position.description: add_unit: graph position [x, y] (default right of the last node).

from.description: connect, disconnect: the output pin, Node.Pin as get_control_rig lists it; execution runs from the event's execute pin to each unit's (ExecutePin in UE 5.8).

to.description: connect, disconnect: the input pin, Node.Pin.

pin.description: set_pin: the pin, Node.Pin; a struct member has its own pin (SetTransform.Item.Name, SetTransform.Transform.Translation.X).

value.description: set_pin: the value as text (Bone, foot_l), a number, or true/false.

skeletonPath.description: import_bones: the skeleton whose bones are imported (default the skeleton of the rig's preview mesh).

parent.description: add_bone, add_null, add_control: the parent element's name (a bone, null or control); omitted, the top of the hierarchy.

location.description: add_bone, add_null, add_control: location [x, y, z] in cm (a control's offset), relative to the parent unless global.

rotation.description: add_bone, add_null, add_control: rotation [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees.

scale.description: add_bone, add_null, add_control: scale [x, y, z] (default 1).

global.description: add_bone, add_null: location, rotation and scale are in rig space, not relative to the parent.

controlType.description: add_control: the value the control drives (default transform).

steps.description: Several edits in order, each an object with edit and its own fields as above; the first that fails stops the rest, and those before it stay (failedStep names it).

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

made.description: What the edits made: {node, unit, pins} for an added unit, {pin, value} for a set pin (the value as stored), {element} for an added element, {importedFrom, bones} for a skeleton's bones imported (bones the rig already had are matched in place).

compiled.description: Whether the rig compiled after the edits.

compileErrors.description: The compile errors, when there were any.

saved.description: Whether the rig was saved.

failedStep.description: steps: the step that failed (0-based); the ones before it were applied, compiled and saved.

examples.title: Edit a Control Rig: add a unit node (list_rig_units finds them), connect or disconnect pins, set a pin value, remove a node, import the skeleton's bones, add a bone, null or control, or remove an element; one edit or many steps, then one compile and save. The reply lists what each edit made (a new node with its pins).

discovery.summary: Edit an animation montage, chosen by edit; each change is saved unless save is false (saved). add_montage_section adds a section at startTime (a name already there is SECTION_EXISTS) and set_section_timing moves one; link_sections makes fromSection play into toSection (SECTION_NOT_FOUND lists the sections); add_montage_slot adds an animation of a skeleton the montage takes as a segment of a slot, refused where it would overlap one already there, and grows the montage to fit; add_montage_notify adds a notify of notifyClass, or a named notify event, at a time within the montage; set_blend_in and set_blend_out set blendTime and blendOption, refusing a call with neither.
whenToUse: edit=add_montage_notify: Timed event needed in montage.
edit=add_montage_section: Montage needs a section.
edit=add_montage_slot: Montage must expose a slot.
edit=link_sections: Sections must chain.
edit=set_blend_in: Smooth entry needed.
edit=set_blend_out: Smooth exit needed.
edit=set_section_timing: Section timing must change.
whenNotToUse: edit=add_montage_notify: Use add_notify_state.
edit=add_montage_section: Use create_montage.
edit=add_montage_slot: Default slot.

notifyClass.description: AnimNotify (or AnimNotifyState) class name; prefixed with AnimNotify_/AnimNotifyState_ automatically when missing.

trackIndex.description: Notify track index within the animation sequence.

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

animationPath.description: Sequence to add as a segment of the slot.

slotName.description: Slot name.

blendOption.description: Blend curve; left as it is when omitted.

edit.description:
Which edit montage variant to run.
add_montage_notify: Add a notify to a montage at time (seconds, default 0, within the montage's length) on notify track trackIndex (default 0; tracks are added up to it): notifyClass makes an AnimNotify of that class (the AnimNotify_ prefix may be left off; an abstract or unknown class is refused), notifyName alone a named notify event the anim graph answers in its AnimNotify_<name> event. A time outside the montage or a negative track is refused. Saved unless save is false (saved).
add_montage_section: Add a section named sectionName to a montage at startTime (default 0; within the montage's length); the section added before it, when it had no next section, now plays into it. A name already there is SECTION_EXISTS, listing the sections. Saved unless save is false (saved).
add_montage_slot: Add animationPath to a montage as a segment of slot slotName (default DefaultSlot; a new slot track is made) from startTime (default 0). Refused when its skeleton is one the montage does not take (SKELETON_MISMATCH) or it would overlap a segment already on that slot (SEGMENT_OVERLAP, naming where the slot ends); the montage grows to fit (montageLength). Saved unless save is false (saved).
link_sections: Make section fromSection of a montage play into toSection when it ends (a section may link to itself to loop). A section the montage lacks is SECTION_NOT_FOUND, listing the sections. Saved unless save is false (saved).
set_blend_in: Set how a montage blends in when it starts: blendTime (seconds, 0 or more) and blendOption (Linear, Cubic or Sinusoidal); each is set only when given, and a call with neither is refused. Saved unless save is false (saved).
set_blend_out: Set how a montage blends out when it stops or ends: blendTime (seconds, 0 or more) and blendOption (Linear, Cubic or Sinusoidal); each is set only when given, and a call with neither is refused. Saved unless save is false (saved).
set_section_timing: Move section sectionName of a montage to startTime, within the montage's length; a section runs until the next one starts. SECTION_NOT_FOUND lists the sections. Saved unless save is false (saved).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Edit an animation montage, chosen by edit; each change is saved unless save is false (saved). add_montage_section adds a section at startTime (a name already there is SECTION_EXISTS) and set_section_timing moves one; link_sections makes fromSection play into toSection (SECTION_NOT_FOUND lists the sections); add_montage_slot adds an animation of a skeleton the montage takes as a segment of a slot, refused where it would overlap one already there, and grows the montage to fit; add_montage_notify adds a notify of notifyClass, or a named notify event, at a time within the montage; set_blend_in and set_blend_out set blendTime and blendOption, refusing a call with neither.

discovery.summary: Create a morph target, set its deltas, import morph targets from another mesh, or set a morph target value on an actor.
whenToUse: edit=create: Facial/shape blending needed.
edit=set_deltas: Morph shape must be authored.
edit=import: A mesh must get the blend shapes of a sculpted or imported variant.
edit=set_value: A morph target weight must be previewed on a placed actor.
whenNotToUse: edit=create: No morph targets.
edit=import: The morph is authored by hand on this mesh (edit create or set_deltas).

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

sourceMeshPath.description: Skeletal mesh that owns the morph targets (its LOD 0 source data).

morphTargets.description: Names to import (default all the source mesh has in its source data).

dropRenderOnlyMorphs.description: The edit rebuilds the mesh from its source data, which deletes morph targets that exist only in render data (made by create_morph_target or set_morph_target_deltas). Without true, a mesh that has any is refused with RENDER_ONLY_MORPHS naming them and nothing changes (default false).

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

value.description: Property value (any type).

edit.description:
Which edit morph target variant to run.
create: Create a morph target on a skeletal mesh.
set_deltas: Set vertex deltas for a morph target.
import: Copy morph targets (blend shapes) from another skeletal mesh into this mesh's source data, each vertex taking the delta of the nearest source vertex, so they survive every rebuild.
set_value: Set a morph target weight (value 0 to 1, clamped) on the skeletal mesh component of a placed actor for this editor session (not saved with the level); a weight of 0 clears it. The morph must exist on the mesh (MORPH_TARGET_NOT_FOUND otherwise); the reply gives the weight the component holds and every active morph.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

name.description: Morph target.

verticesAffected.description: Vertices it moves on this mesh.

replaced.description: Morph targets the mesh already had and were replaced.

builtMorphTargets.description: Imported names that exist as morph targets after the rebuild.

unmatchedVertices.description: Vertices farther than 2% of the source size from any source vertex.

morphTargetsDropped.description: Render-only morph targets the rebuild removed, only with dropRenderOnlyMorphs true.

saved.description: Whether the mesh was saved.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

value.description: Weight applied to the morph target.

activeMorphTargets.description: Morph targets currently driven on the actor.

examples.title: Create a morph target, set its deltas, import morph targets from another mesh, or set a morph target value on an actor.

discovery.summary: Create a physics asset or edit it, chosen by edit; each change is saved unless save is false (saved). create builds bodies and joints from skeletalMeshPath as the editor's Create Physics Asset does, at outputPath (or name in path; default <mesh>_PhysicsAsset beside the mesh): geomType Capsule (default), Box, Sphere, TaperedCapsule (cloth only), SingleConvexHull or MultiConvexHull, any other name refused; bones shorter than minBoneSize get no body unless bodyForAll; createConstraints joins the bodies; assignToMesh (default false) makes the mesh use it; a build that makes no body is refused (BODY_GENERATION_FAILED). add_body gives boneName a Capsule (default), Sphere or Box shape sized by radius and length or width, depth and height, placed by center and rotation; a bone that already has a body gets the shape added to it (created false), and a bone the skeleton lacks is BONE_NOT_FOUND. configure_body (modify_body) sets mass (kg, above 0, as the body's mass override), linearDamping, angularDamping, collisionEnabled and simulatePhysics (true simulates with the ragdoll, false is Kinematic and follows the animation), and refuses a call that sets none of them. add_constraint joins bodyA and bodyB with a joint Limited to 45 degrees on every axis (both bodies must exist, BODY_NOT_FOUND; a second joint on the pair is CONSTRAINT_EXISTS); set_constraint changes the pair's joint or makes one; configure_constraint_limits sets swing1, swing2 and twist angles and motions from limits. assign makes skeletalMeshPath (or meshPath) use physicsAssetPath and saves the mesh.
whenToUse: edit=create: Ragdoll/physics needed.
edit=add_body: A bone needs a collision body.

outputPath.description: Canonical /Game path for the generated Physics Asset.

name.description: Asset name (alternative to outputPath).

path.description: Destination folder (with name).

geomType.description: Body shape for every bone: Capsule (default; Sphyl too), Box, Sphere, TaperedCapsule (cloth only), SingleConvexHull or MultiConvexHull; any other name is refused and nothing is created.

minBoneSize.description: Bones shorter than this (cm, editor default 20) get no body unless bodyForAll.

bodyForAll.description: Create a body for every bone regardless of size.

assignToMesh.description: Make the skeletal mesh use the new asset and save the mesh too (default false).

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

bodyType.description: Shape added to the bone's body: Capsule (default), Sphere or Box; any other name is refused.

length.description: Capsule length between the end caps (default 20).

center.description: Physics body centre offset relative to its bone as [x, y, z].

rotation.description: Box or capsule rotation relative to the bone as [pitch, yaw, roll].

mass.description: Body mass in kg, above 0: sets the body's mass override (without one its mass comes from density and volume).

simulatePhysics.description: true: the body simulates whenever the mesh simulates physics (PhysicsType Default, as in a ragdoll); false: it follows the animation (Kinematic).

constraintName.description: Name of the created physics constraint.

limits.description: Angular limits. Only the axes named change; an angle without a motion makes that axis Limited.

edit.description:
Which edit physics asset variant to run.
create: Create a PhysicsAsset for a skeletal mesh.
add_body: Add a physics body to a PhysicsAsset.
configure_body: Configure the physics body of boneName in a Physics Asset, each field only when sent: mass in kg (the mass override), linearDamping, angularDamping, collisionEnabled (query and physics, or none), simulatePhysics (simulate with the ragdoll, or follow the animation as Kinematic). A call sending none is refused; the reply gives mass, damping and physicsType after the change, and saved.
modify_body: The edit=modify_body spelling of edit=configure_body: set a body's mass (kg), damping, collision or whether it simulates, each only when sent; a call sending none is refused and the reply gives the values after the change.
add_constraint: Add a physics constraint between two bodies; refuses a pair that already has one.
set_constraint: Create or update the constraint between two physics bodies: an existing pair is edited in place, not duplicated.
configure_constraint_limits: Configure constraint angular/linear limits.
assign: Assign a Physics Asset to a Skeletal Mesh.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

physicsAssetName.description: Name of the generated Physics Asset.

examples.title: Create a physics asset or edit it, chosen by edit; each change is saved unless save is false (saved). create builds bodies and joints from skeletalMeshPath as the editor's Create Physics Asset does, at outputPath (or name in path; default <mesh>_PhysicsAsset beside the mesh): geomType Capsule (default), Box, Sphere, TaperedCapsule (cloth only), SingleConvexHull or MultiConvexHull, any other name refused; bones shorter than minBoneSize get no body unless bodyForAll; createConstraints joins the bodies; assignToMesh (default false) makes the mesh use it; a build that makes no body is refused (BODY_GENERATION_FAILED). add_body gives boneName a Capsule (default), Sphere or Box shape sized by radius and length or width, depth and height, placed by center and rotation; a bone that already has a body gets the shape added to it (created false), and a bone the skeleton lacks is BONE_NOT_FOUND. configure_body (modify_body) sets mass (kg, above 0, as the body's mass override), linearDamping, angularDamping, collisionEnabled and simulatePhysics (true simulates with the ragdoll, false is Kinematic and follows the animation), and refuses a call that sets none of them. add_constraint joins bodyA and bodyB with a joint Limited to 45 degrees on every axis (both bodies must exist, BODY_NOT_FOUND; a second joint on the pair is CONSTRAINT_EXISTS); set_constraint changes the pair's joint or makes one; configure_constraint_limits sets swing1, swing2 and twist angles and motions from limits. assign makes skeletalMeshPath (or meshPath) use physicsAssetPath and saves the mesh.

discovery.summary: Edit a skeleton (skeletonPath), chosen by edit. add_bone adds boneName under parentBoneName (needed once the skeleton has bones; a taken name is BONE_EXISTS) at location, rotation and scale relative to the parent. set_bone_parent moves boneName, with its children, under parentBoneName, where it keeps its place in the reference pose: its own descendants are refused, and the parent it already has changes nothing (changed false). Both change the skeleton asset only; the skeletal meshes on it keep their own bones. set_bone_transform rewrites boneName in the reference pose of the skeletal mesh (skeletalMeshPath, or the skeleton's preview mesh), only the location, rotation or scale sent. create_virtual_bone adds a virtual bone from sourceBoneName to targetBoneName named boneName, or VB <source>_<target>; the engine's VB prefix is added when missing. rename_bone renames virtual bones only; a real bone takes a reimport of the mesh (OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED). Saved unless save is false (saved).
whenToUse: edit=add_bone: A skeleton, bone, socket, physics body or morph target must be authored.
edit=rename_bone: A virtual bone needs renaming.
edit=set_bone_parent: Bone hierarchy must change.
edit=set_bone_transform: A bone rest pose must change.
edit=create_virtual_bone: A virtual bone is needed for IK.
whenNotToUse: edit=add_bone: Bone already exists.
edit=rename_bone: Name is correct.
edit=rename_bone: The bone is a real skeleton bone.
edit=set_bone_parent: Hierarchy is correct.
edit=set_bone_transform: Use runtime animation.
edit=create_virtual_bone: Use a real bone.

location.description: World or relative location as [x, y, z].

rotation.description: Rotation as [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees.

scale.description: Uniform scale factor, or non-uniform scale as [x, y, z].

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

edit.description:
Which edit skeleton variant to run.
add_bone: Add boneName to a skeleton under parentBoneName at location, rotation and scale relative to its parent (scale a number for uniform, or {x, y, z}); a skeleton with bones refuses a new root (PARENT_REQUIRED), and a taken name is BONE_EXISTS. One undo step (the reply's undo block says so), saved unless save is false; the reply gives boneCount.
rename_bone: Rename a virtual bone on a skeleton (real skeleton bones cannot be renamed and answer OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED).
set_bone_parent: Move boneName, with its children, under the existing bone parentBoneName, where it keeps its place in the reference pose; the reply gives newBoneIndex (bones can be reordered) and changed. The parent it already has answers changed false and writes nothing; the bone itself or one of its descendants as parent is INVALID_ARGUMENT, a bone not in the skeleton BONE_NOT_FOUND or PARENT_NOT_FOUND. One undo step (the reply's undo block says so), saved unless save is false.
set_bone_transform: Set the rest transform of a bone.
create_virtual_bone: Create a virtual bone between two bones.

discovery.summary: Edit skeletal-mesh skin weights: auto-skin, set vertex weights, copy them from another skinned mesh, mirror one side onto the other, or prune tiny influences. Weights are always normalized on write.
whenToUse: edit=auto: A mesh needs skinning.
edit=set: Manual weight painting is required.
edit=copy: A new or re-modelled mesh must deform like an already skinned one.
edit=mirror: One side of a symmetric character is weighted and the other must match.
edit=prune: Auto-skinning or a transfer left tiny noisy influences.
whenNotToUse: edit=auto: Weights already exist.
edit=auto: The weights should be copied from a dressed body mesh (use skin_mesh_to_skeleton).
edit=set: Auto-skin suffices.
edit=copy: The mesh has no weights and no skinned mesh to copy from (edit auto).
edit=mirror: The mesh is not symmetric or has no left and right bones.
edit=prune: Joints should stay soft; a high threshold stiffens them.

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

weights.description: Per-vertex skin weight descriptors with bone influences.

sourceMeshPath.description: Skinned mesh to copy the weights FROM (its LOD 0).

targetMeshPath.description: Skeletal mesh whose weights are replaced in place.

dropRenderOnlyMorphs.description: The edit rebuilds the mesh from its source data, which deletes morph targets that exist only in render data (made by create_morph_target or set_morph_target_deltas). Without true, a mesh that has any is refused with RENDER_ONLY_MORPHS naming them and nothing changes (default false).

axis.description: Symmetry axis in mesh space: X (default), Y or Z.

direction.description: positive_to_negative (default: the positive side is copied onto the negative side) or negative_to_positive.

threshold.description: Influences below this weight are removed, above 0 and below 0.5 (default 0.01).

edit.description:
Which edit skin weights variant to run.
auto: Recompute LOD 0 skin weights of a skeletal mesh by smooth binding to its own skeleton (UE 5.5+ with GeometryScripting).
set: Set explicit vertex skin weights.
copy: Replace the skin weights of an existing skeletal mesh with those of another skinned mesh (for example the body under a garment), vertex by nearest vertex, mapping bones by name; the mesh keeps its geometry, physics asset, sockets and LODs.
mirror: Mirror the skin weights of one side of a skeletal mesh onto the other, swapping left and right bones by name (_l and _r, Left and Right, .L and .R); vertices on the symmetry plane keep their weights.
prune: Remove skin influences below a weight threshold (each vertex keeps its strongest bone) and renormalize; a mesh with nothing below it is left untouched.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

boneVertexCounts.description: before and after: bone name to the number of vertices it influences, read back from the source data.

morphTargetsDropped.description: Render-only morph targets (made by create_morph_target or set_morph_target_deltas) the rebuild removed, only with dropRenderOnlyMorphs true; import_morph_targets writes morphs that survive.

saved.description: Whether the mesh was saved.

verticesWritten.description: Target vertices that took new weights.

verticesFarFromSource.description: Target vertices farther than 2% of the source size from any source vertex; check those areas.

unmappedBones.description: Source bones the target lacks; their weight went to the nearest parent bone it has.

verticesMirrored.description: Vertices that took the mirrored weights.

unmatchedVertices.description: Destination-side vertices with no mirror partner; they kept their weights.

bonePairs.description: Left and right bone pairs that were swapped.

maxInfluencesBefore.description: Most influences on one vertex before.

maxInfluencesAfter.description: Most influences on one vertex after.

examples.title: Edit skeletal-mesh skin weights: auto-skin, set vertex weights, copy them from another skinned mesh, mirror one side onto the other, or prune tiny influences. Weights are always normalized on write.

A montage's sections and slots, or a blend space's axes, must be checked before editing.

boneTracks.description: A sequence: the bones it has tracks for (set_bone_key keys them).

numBoneTracks.description: How many bone tracks the sequence has.

whenToUse: Before editing a rig: the exact pin paths connect and set_pin take, and what is already wired.
To check a rig after edits: links, hierarchy, compile state.
whenNotToUse: Finding a unit to add (use list_rig_units).

node.description: One node's name: only that node, with every struct member pin by its full path.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

links.description: Each link: from (output pin) and to (input pin).

elements.description: Hierarchy elements in order (up to 500): type (Bone, Null, Control, Curve ...), name and parent.

compiled.description: Whether the rig is compiled and up to date.

nodeNames.description: With a node that is not there: the nodes there are.

discovery.summary: Read a skeleton, skeletal mesh or Physics Asset, chosen by info (a skeletal mesh path reads its skeleton, or its assigned Physics Asset). skeleton gives counts of bones, virtual bones and sockets; bones lists every bone in hierarchy order with index, parent and reference-pose location, the names other calls take (layer filters, sockets, IK, physics bodies); sockets lists each socket with its bone and offset; virtual_bones lists virtual bones with source and target; bone_transform reads one bone's reference-pose transform and parent; morph_targets lists a mesh's morph targets and their delta counts; physics_asset reads a Physics Asset's bodies (the shapes in each) and constraints; physics_bodies lists only the body names. A path that does not load is SKELETON_NOT_FOUND or MESH_NOT_FOUND, a bone the skeleton lacks BONE_NOT_FOUND.
whenToUse: info=skeleton: A skeleton's size must be checked, such as before retargeting or adding bones.
info=bones: Bone names must be known before naming one in another call.
info=sockets: Enumerate sockets.
info=virtual_bones: Existing virtual bones must be discovered before adding another.
info=bone_transform: A bone position must be read before placing a socket or constraint.
info=morph_targets: The available morph targets must be discovered before driving one.
info=physics_asset: The contents of a Physics Asset must be inspected before editing it.
info=physics_bodies: Enumerate physics bodies.
whenNotToUse: info=sockets: Mutate sockets.
info=virtual_bones: A virtual bone must be created (use create_virtual_bone).
info=morph_targets: A morph target must be created (use create_morph_target).
info=physics_bodies: Mutate bodies.

skeletalMeshPath.description: A skeletal mesh whose skeleton to read, instead of skeletonPath.

info.description:
Which get skeleton info variant to run; omit for 'skeleton'.
skeleton: Count what a skeleton holds (skeletonPath, or a skeletal mesh's skeleton): boneCount, virtualBoneCount and socketCount. The names come from info=bones, info=sockets and info=virtual_bones.
bones: List every bone of a skeleton (skeletonPath, or a skeletal mesh's skeleton) in hierarchy order, parents before children: name, index, parentIndex (-1 for the root), parentName and reference-pose location relative to the parent. These are the exact names layer filters, sockets, IK chains and physics bodies take.
sockets: List sockets of a skeleton.
virtual_bones: List the virtual bones declared on a skeleton.
bone_transform: Read the reference-pose transform and parent of a bone.
morph_targets: List the morph targets declared on a Skeletal Mesh.
physics_asset: Read the bodies and constraints declared by a Physics Asset.
physics_bodies: List physics bodies of a PhysicsAsset.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

bones.description: One entry per bone in reference-skeleton order.

boneIndex.description: Index of the bone in the reference skeleton.

parentBone.description: Name of the parent bone, empty for the root.

parentIndex.description: Index of the parent bone, -1 for the root.

location.description: Reference-pose location.

rotation.description: Reference-pose rotation.

numBodies.description: Number of physics bodies in the asset.

numConstraints.description: Number of constraints in the asset.

whenToUse: A unit is needed for add_unit and its name is not known.
whenNotToUse: Reading what a rig already holds (use get_control_rig).

units.description: Matching units sorted by struct name: unit (the object path add_unit takes), name and category.

discovery.summary: Play an animation montage on a placed skeletal actor (the playing one while Play In Editor runs): Montage_Play through its Anim Instance at playRate, or the montage as a single-node animation when the mesh has none, which switches that component's animation mode. The reply gives playMode and montageLength; outside play the actor does not tick, so nothing moves, playing is false and a warning says so.
whenToUse: A montage (an attack, an emote, a hit reaction) must play on a character while the game runs, to see it or to test it.
whenNotToUse: The game should play it: call Play Montage in the character's Blueprint (manage_blueprint edit_graph).
The montage asset itself must be made or edited.

actorName.description: The actor's label, object name or path, matched whole (no partial match); its first skeletal mesh plays the montage.

montagePath.description: Montage asset path, e.g. /Game/Anims/AM_Slash. It must use the skeleton of the actor's mesh, or Montage_Play refuses it (MONTAGE_PLAY_FAILED).

playRate.description: Speed (default 1; 2 plays it twice as fast).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Play an animation montage on a placed skeletal actor (the playing one while Play In Editor runs): Montage_Play through its Anim Instance at playRate, or the montage as a single-node animation when the mesh has none, which switches that component's animation mode. The reply gives playMode and montageLength; outside play the actor does not tick, so nothing moves, playing is false and a warning says so.

discovery.summary: Remove part of a skeleton or physics asset, chosen by element. bone removes boneName from the skeleton: with removeChildren its whole branch goes, otherwise its children move up to its parent and keep their place in the reference pose; the only root a skeleton has is refused. socket removes socketName from the skeleton (a socket defined on a mesh is not found here). physics_body removes the body of boneName from physicsAssetPath together with every constraint that uses it. A missing bone, socket or body is refused. Saved unless save is false (saved).
whenToUse: element=bone: A bone must be removed.
element=socket: An attach point must be taken off a skeleton.
element=physics_body: A bone should no longer simulate.
whenNotToUse: element=bone: Keep the bone.
element=socket: The socket transform should change; use configure_socket.
element=physics_body: The body only needs different parameters (use configure_physics_body).

removeChildren.description: Whether child bones are removed with the target bone.

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

element.description:
Which remove skeleton element variant to run.
bone: Remove boneName from a skeleton, with its children when removeChildren is true; otherwise its children move up to its parent and keep their place in the reference pose. A virtual bone is BONE_NOT_FOUND (delete_virtual_bone removes it). The only root a skeleton has is refused (CANNOT_REMOVE_ROOT); a second root is removed like any bone. One undo step (the reply's undo block says so), saved unless save is false; the reply gives boneCount.
socket: Remove a socket from a skeleton or skeletal mesh.
physics_body: Remove a physics body from a Physics Asset.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

remainingSockets.description: Number of sockets left on the asset after the call.

remainingBodies.description: Number of physics bodies left on the asset after the call.

discovery.summary: Set up IK: create an IK rig or IK retargeter, a Control Rig for IK solvers, or set which source chain drives each target chain of a retargeter.
whenToUse: kind=setup: IK chains must be authored in a Control Rig.
kind=rig: IK retargeting source needed.
kind=retargeter: Animation must be retargeted between two skeletons.
kind=chain_mapping: A limb retargets from the wrong source chain after setup_retargeting or create_ik_retargeter.
whenNotToUse: kind=setup: An IK Rig asset is needed (kind rig).
kind=rig: Use create_control_rig.
kind=rig: A whole retarget from one character to another is wanted: setup_retargeting builds both rigs and the retargeter.
kind=retargeter: Both characters share one skeleton.
kind=chain_mapping: The retargeter does not exist yet (kind retargeter).

name.description: Name for the created asset or actor.

path.description: Folder for the Control Rig (default /Game/Animations).

skeletalMeshPath.description: Skeletal mesh the IK Rig is built on; its skeleton is used.

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

targetChain.description: Target IK Rig chain to map; required unless autoMap.

sourceChain.description: Source IK Rig chain that drives it; empty or None clears the mapping.

autoMap.description: Map every unmapped chain: exact name matches first, then the closest names (default false).

kind.description:
Which setup ik variant to run; omit for 'setup'.
setup: Create a Control Rig Blueprint named name in path (default /Game/Animations) to host IK solvers, previewing the preview mesh of skeletonPath; its rig hierarchy starts empty (import the bones in the Control Rig editor). An existing Control Rig at the path is reused, another asset there is refused. Saved.
rig: Create an IK Rig named name in path (default /Game/Retargeting). On UE 5.6 and later, given skeletalMeshPath (or skeletonPath, whose preview mesh is used) it is characterized from the mesh as setup_retargeting does: retarget chains and the pelvis filled in, ready for a retargeter, and an IK Rig already under that name is rebuilt in place. It is saved unless save is false; the reply gives assetPath and saved.
retargeter: Create an IK Retargeter asset named name in path (default /Game/Retargeting) between sourceIKRigPath and targetIKRigPath, each optional (kind=chain_mapping needs both); a rig path that does not load is IK_RIG_NOT_FOUND before anything is made, and a taken path ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS. On UE 5.6 and later the default retarget ops are added. Saved unless save is false.
chain_mapping: Set which source IK Rig chain drives a target chain in an IK Retargeter (None clears it), or auto-map every unmapped chain by name; replies with the whole mapping.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

sourceChain.description: Source chain driving it, or None.

mapping.description: Every target chain with the source chain now driving it (None when unmapped).

saved.description: Whether the retargeter was saved.

examples.title: Set up IK: create an IK rig or IK retargeter, a Control Rig for IK solvers, or set which source chain drives each target chain of a retargeter.

discovery.summary: Make a skeletal actor go limp in the running game (Play or Simulate), chosen by ragdoll. setup switches every physics body of its skeletal mesh to simulate, assigning physicsAssetPath first when given; activate turns that on or off (activate, default true). A mesh with no physics asset is refused (NO_PHYSICS_ASSET), and ragdollActive reads back whether it now simulates. A Character keeps its capsule and movement running, so stop those as well for a body that falls.

Which setup ragdoll variant to run; omit for 'setup'.

activate: Switch ragdoll simulation on/off at runtime on a skeletal actor via the distinct native ragdoll=activate action (editor build).

whenToUse: Clothing, armour or a prop must move with the body instead of holding its shape.
A garment downloaded as a static mesh needs to be worn.
whenNotToUse: The mesh is already a SkeletalMesh on the right skeleton.

staticMeshPath.description: StaticMesh to skin, e.g. a coat downloaded as a rigid mesh.

skeletalMeshPath.description: SkeletalMesh whose geometry to re-skin, for a dressed character whose own rig will not retarget. Its materials carry over. Use instead of staticMeshPath.

outputPath.description: Canonical /Game path for the SkeletalMesh this writes.

sourceSkeletalMesh.description: An already-skinned mesh on the same skeleton to copy weights from, such as the body the garment is worn over. Beats computing weights fresh wherever the garment hugs the body. Falls back to smooth binding when omitted.

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

weights.description: Which binding ran: 'transferred' from sourceSkeletalMesh, or 'smooth'.
