discovery.summary: Inspect an asset: metadata, what it uses or what uses it (referencers), its dependency graph, an exists-and-loads check, a directory report, or a diff: its unsaved changes against the saved file, or a compare with another asset.
whenToUse: lookup=metadata: What was recorded on an asset must be read back: its registry tags and the package metadata that asset.set_metadata writes, tags included (a tag set with kind=tags shows under metadata as "true").
lookup=dependencies: Before deleting or replacing an asset, the packages, Blueprints and levels that use it must be listed.
lookup=dependencies: The packages an asset itself uses must be listed (direct ones only).
lookup=graph: The reference graph of an asset must be walked several levels deep in one call (depth is capped at 8).
lookup=validate: An asset must be confirmed to exist and load before other calls rely on it (no content, reference or data checks are run).
lookup=report: Every asset under a directory, with name, path and class, must be listed in one reply, optionally saved as a JSON file in the project.
lookup=diff: What changed in an asset since it was last saved must be known before saving or discarding it.
lookup=diff: Two versions of an asset must be compared, such as a backup copy and the current one.
whenNotToUse: lookup=metadata: The asset's own values are wanted, such as a texture size or material parameters (use texture.get_texture_info or material.get_material_info).
lookup=dependencies: The node graph inside a material or Blueprint is wanted, not package links (use asset.query_asset with lookup=graph).
lookup=graph: Only the direct packages an asset uses, or the packages that use it, are needed (use lookup=dependencies, which is cheaper).
lookup=graph: A material's package references are wanted; a plain material answers here with its expression nodes (use lookup=dependencies).
lookup=validate: Every asset in a folder must be checked for load errors (use system_control.validate_assets).
lookup=report: A paged view of one folder is enough (use asset.list); the report returns the whole tree unpaged.
lookup=diff: The asset's current values are wanted (use blueprint.get_blueprint or inspect.get_property).
lookup=diff: A level or another kind of asset must be compared; only Blueprints, DataTables and data assets are.

referencers.description: List the packages that USE this asset (Blueprints that spawn it, levels that place it) instead of the ones it uses; check this before deleting or replacing an asset.

againstPath.description: Another asset of the same kind to compare with, such as a duplicate kept as a backup. Omitted, the asset is compared with its own saved file, so the reply lists its unsaved edits.

lookup.description:
Which inspect asset variant to run.
metadata: Retrieve metadata and tags for an asset.
dependencies: List the packages an asset uses, or with referencers the packages that use it. Direct packages only; lookup "graph" walks dependencies recursively.
graph: Retrieve the asset reference graph directly via the lookup=graph bridge action.
validate: Confirm an asset exists and loads. It runs no content, reference or data checks.
report: Generate an asset report for a directory.
diff: Compare a Blueprint, DataTable or data asset with its saved file (its unsaved edits) or with another asset: changed, added and removed properties and class defaults, Blueprint components and graph changes, DataTable rows. Read-only.

tags.description: Asset Registry tags (key-value). A tag written by set_tags appears here only when its name is listed under Project Settings > Asset Manager > Metadata Tags For Asset Registry.

metadata.description: Package metadata (key-value): what set_metadata wrote, and each set_tags tag as its name with the value "true".

details.description: Operation details.

graph.description: Adjacency map of asset path -> array of dependency paths.

maxDepth.description: Traversal depth actually used after clamping.

truncated.description: True when the walk hit the depth or node ceiling and the graph is partial.

against.description: What the asset was compared with: "saved file", or the againstPath asset.

propertyChanges.description: Saved properties that differ, at most 50: object (asset, defaults for a Blueprint's class defaults, component <name>, or row <name>), property, change (changed, added or removed) and now and saved (the other side) as text, each cut at 200 characters.

componentChanges.description: Blueprint components added, removed, or moved to another class or parent, at most 50: component, change, now and saved; a component's changed values are under propertyChanges.

graphChanges.description: Blueprint graph changes, at most 50, node moves left out: graph, change (graph added, graph removed, node added, node removed, or changed), node and nodeId when a node is named (nodeId is the live graph's node where it has one), and detail, the engine's own description.

rowChanges.description: DataTable rows added or removed, at most 50: row and change; a changed row's values are under propertyChanges.

examples.title: Inspect an asset: metadata, what it uses or what uses it (referencers), its dependency graph, an exists-and-loads check, a directory report, or a diff: its unsaved changes against the saved file, or a compare with another asset.

discovery.summary: List the assets and subfolders in a folder (path), the registered content sources, or the instances of a material.
whenToUse: kind=assets: what a folder holds must be seen (subfolders included unless recursive is false).
kind=content_sources: which template, feature pack, plugin or Fab folders exist to copy content from.
kind=material_instances: which material instances use a parent material.
whenNotToUse: An asset must be found by name, class or tag anywhere in the project (use query_asset).

path.description: Canonical /Game path to list.

limit.description: Page size (1-500, default 50).

offset.description: Zero-based offset into the full result set.

limit.description: Page size (1-500, default 50).

offset.description: Zero-based offset into the full result set.

pagination.description: Nested pagination envelope. Top-level limit/offset take precedence when both are supplied.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned by a previous list response. Forward verbatim to resume.

recursive.description: Include the assets of every subfolder (default true); false lists only this folder's own assets, its subfolders still named under folders.

includeTags.description: When true, include asset tags in the listing response.

includeMetadata.description: When true, include the file size and modification date of each asset.

filter.description: Substring filter. Listing assets: a case-insensitive match on the asset name, and on the own name of each folder listed. Listing content sources: a case-sensitive match on the source id and, for plugins, the category.

sourceRoot.description: Restrict the listing to one root. One of: engineTemplates | engineFeaturePacks | engineContent | enginePlugins | megascansLibrary | fabLibrary | projectContent | projectPlugins. Omit to list every root.

includePackageCounts.description: Include packageCount per source. Costs a recursive file scan per returned entry, so leave off for a broad sweep and turn on once the candidate list is short.

kind.description:
Which list variant to run; omit for 'assets'.
assets: List assets under a /Game path with bounded pagination and opaque cursor continuation.
content_sources: Enumerate reusable content already installed on this machine: engine templates (vehicle, first person, ...), engine and plugin content, and Quixel Bridge / Fab packs already downloaded by those plugins. Call this before authoring assets from scratch — a production-grade vehicle, track kit or Megascans surface is usually already on disk. Feed a returned sourceRoot + sourceId straight into asset.migrate_assets. Results are paginated (default 50): an unfiltered sweep finds several hundred sources because every engine plugin that ships content counts, so narrow with sourceRoot or filter rather than paging through all of them.
material_instances: List material instances using a parent material.

limit.description: Applied page size.

offset.description: Applied zero-based offset.

hasMore.description: True when more results exist beyond the current page.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the current page, or null when the page was requested without one.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null on the last page.

sources.description: Discovered sources. Each entry carries sourceRoot, sourceId, kind (template | featurePack | megascansPack | plugin | contentFolder), hasContentFolder, migratable, and packageCount when requested.

rootDirectories.description: Absolute directory each root token resolved to, so an operator can confirm where the Bridge library was found.

missingRoots.description: Root tokens whose directory does not exist on this machine.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: List the assets and subfolders in a folder (path), the registered content sources, or the instances of a material.

discovery.summary: Content maintenance: bulk-rename assets, fix up redirectors, refresh the nodes of every Blueprint in a folder, or migrate packages from another content source.
whenToUse: maintenance=bulk_rename: A naming convention must be enforced across a folder or a list, such as swapping a prefix or adding a suffix to every asset.
maintenance=bulk_rename: Several unrelated assets must each get a specific new name in one call (the renames list).
maintenance=fixup_redirectors: Redirectors left in a folder by earlier moves or renames must be resolved: referencers are repointed and the redirectors deleted.
maintenance=refresh_blueprints: Blueprints in a folder or a list need every node refreshed, then compiled and saved, for example after a class was renamed.
maintenance=migrate: Loose .uasset content from an engine template, plugin or downloaded Fab or Megascans pack must be copied into the project.
maintenance=migrate: A migration must be previewed with a dry run before any file is copied.
whenNotToUse: maintenance=bulk_rename: One asset or one folder gets a new name (use asset.rename).
maintenance=fixup_redirectors: Redirectors should only be listed before anything changes (use asset.query_asset with lookup=search and classNames ObjectRedirector).
maintenance=refresh_blueprints: One Blueprint only needs compiling (use blueprint.compile).
maintenance=migrate: A source file (FBX, PNG, WAV) must become an asset (use asset.import).
maintenance=migrate: The available sources are still unknown (use asset.list with kind=content_sources).

pattern.description: Search pattern (used when searchText is absent).

replacement.description: Replacement text (used when replaceText is absent).

checkoutFiles.description: Check out files in source control.

renames.description: Explicit renames, each asset to its own new name in its own folder, all in this one call: [{sourcePath, newName}]. An entry whose asset is missing, or whose newName is taken, is skipped and named under skipped. Replaces the pattern fields.

path.description: Alternative directory path.

sourceRoot.description: Content source root token. One of: engineTemplates | engineFeaturePacks | engineContent | enginePlugins | megascansLibrary | fabLibrary | projectContent | projectPlugins. A filesystem path is never accepted here — the token is resolved plugin-side, so no directory outside these roots is reachable. megascansLibrary probes both the shell Documents folder and the profile Documents folder (OneDrive redirects the first) and honours MCP_MEGASCANS_LIBRARY_DIR; fabLibrary reads the Fab plugin's own UFabSettings.CacheDirectoryPath and honours MCP_FAB_LIBRARY_DIR. The Fab plugin owns its own sign-in and downloading — these roots only read what it already placed on disk.

sourceId.description: Relative id under sourceRoot, exactly as returned by list_content_sources (for example "TP_VehicleAdvBP"). Must be relative: no "..", no leading "/", no drive prefix. Omit to migrate the root itself.

subPath.description: Optional folder under the source content directory, to migrate one subtree instead of the whole pack.

destinationPath.description: Root the copied tree lands under. Leave at "/Game" to preserve the source layout and keep internal references valid; any deeper path relocates the tree and flags referenceIntegrity as "at-risk".

overwrite.description: Overwrite packages that already exist at the destination. Default false, which skips them and reports skippedCount.

dryRun.description: Report what would be copied without writing anything. Returns the same counts and packagePaths sample.

maxPackages.description: Refuse the migration when the source holds more files than this, so a mistyped source cannot copy tens of gigabytes. Narrow with subPath or raise deliberately.

maintenance.description:
Which maintain content variant to run.
bulk_rename: Rename multiple assets in one call: by a pattern (search/replace, prefix, suffix) over a folder or a list, or to explicit new names with renames.
fixup_redirectors: Fix up redirector assets in a directory.
refresh_blueprints: Refresh every node of the Blueprints under a folder (or listed), then compile and save each; run it after renaming or moving classes so casts and node titles follow.
migrate: Copy a content tree from an allowlisted source root into this project and scan it into the asset registry. This is how a Quixel Bridge / Fab pack or an engine template (its Blueprints, meshes, materials and maps) becomes usable content in the current project. IMPORTANT: package files store their references as absolute /Game/... paths and a copy cannot rewrite them, so the default destinationPath of "/Game" — which reproduces the source layout exactly — is the only setting that guarantees the migrated assets still resolve each other. Any other destinationPath relocates the tree and comes back with referenceIntegrity "at-risk". Run with dryRun first to see the file count and the package paths that will appear.

details.description: Operation details.

sourceDirectory.description: Absolute directory the packages were read from.

copiedCount.description: Files copied (or that would be copied under dryRun).

skippedCount.description: Files already present at the destination and left alone because overwrite was false.

failedCount.description: Files that could not be copied.

totalFiles.description: Package files discovered in the source.

dryRun.description: True when nothing was written.

referenceIntegrity.description: "preserved" when the source layout was reproduced under /Game, "at-risk" when destinationPath relocated it.

packagePaths.description: Up to 40 destination package paths, for verifying the migration landed where expected.

failedFiles.description: Up to 20 source-relative paths that failed to copy.

warnings.description: Advisory messages, including the reference-integrity warning for a relocated destination.

examples.title: Content maintenance: bulk-rename assets, fix up redirectors, refresh the nodes of every Blueprint in a folder, or migrate packages from another content source.

discovery.summary: Move an asset to a new path, or a whole folder: every asset under it moves (sub-folders kept) and references, redirectors and project settings follow.
whenToUse: An asset must go to another folder; references and project settings (default map, game mode) that point at it follow.
A whole content folder must relocate with its sub-folders; its redirectors are resolved and the emptied source folder is removed.
whenNotToUse: Only the name changes and the asset stays in its folder (use asset.rename).
The asset must be copied and the original left in place (use asset.duplicate).

sourcePath.description: Source /Game asset path, or a folder: everything under it moves into destinationPath, keeping sub-folders, and the emptied folder is removed.

newName.description: Rename in place instead: the asset keeps its folder and takes this name (used when destinationPath is omitted).

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Move an asset to a new path, or a whole folder: every asset under it moves (sub-folders kept) and references, redirectors and project settings follow.

discovery.summary: Turn Nanite on for a static mesh asset, or several in one call (assetPaths), and set the share of its triangles Nanite keeps; each mesh is rebuilt and saved, and the reply reads naniteEnabled and trianglePercent back from it.
whenToUse: A static mesh needs Nanite enabled, or the percentage of triangles Nanite keeps changed.
Several meshes need Nanite: assetPaths does them all under one consent.
whenNotToUse: A dynamic mesh must be baked into a new Nanite static mesh asset (use manage_geometry.convert_to_nanite).
Plain LOD levels are wanted for a mesh that will not use Nanite (use asset.process_asset with process=lods).
The mesh has a translucent material slot (glass): Nanite draws only opaque and masked materials, so the call leaves such a mesh as it is (NANITE_UNSUPPORTED_MATERIAL).

assetPaths.description: Several static meshes, each turned on, rebuilt and saved in this one call (a whole imported pack, or every heavy mesh get_stats statsKind=frame lists); one mesh that fails does not stop the others.

trianglePercent.description: Percent of the source triangles Nanite keeps, 0-100 (default 100).

naniteEnabled.description: Nanite is on, read back from the mesh.

trianglePercent.description: Percent of its triangles Nanite keeps, read back from the mesh.

saved.description: It was saved.

materialsFlagged.description: Materials of the mesh, and those its placed copies in the open level override its slots with (from UE 5.8, material instances too), that lacked the Nanite usage flag: it is set and they are saved, since the editor sets a missing one only when it next draws the mesh, never saves it, and a packaged game draws that surface without it. Absent when none lacked it.

meshes.description: With assetPaths: one row per mesh, {assetPath, naniteEnabled, trianglePercent, materialsFlagged} for one rebuilt and saved, or {assetPath, error} for one that is not a static mesh, holds a translucent material, is outside the allowed paths or could not be saved; any error fails the call (NANITE_PARTIAL) with the other meshes done.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Rebuild Nanite data after a mesh edit

topics: assign materials to a static mesh
discovery.summary: Process an asset, chosen by process. thumbnail renders its preview at width by height (default 512, 1 to 4096) and stores it in the asset, which is left unsaved (thumbnailCached; engine content keeps its own), writing it as a PNG as well when outputPath names a project-relative file. lods gives static meshes lodCount LODs in all (default 4, LOD 0 included, each half the triangles of the one before), replacing LODs past the count and hand-tuned settings, then rebuilds and saves each. mesh_materials sets the materials in the slots of a static or skeletal mesh asset, by slot index or name, so every placement shows them; an engine mesh changes for this session only and is never saved (saveSkippedReason). mesh_collision sets the collision of a static mesh asset (a fitted box, sphere or capsule, its render triangles, or none), rebuilds every placed copy and saves it. lods and mesh_collision refuse engine meshes (ENGINE_CONTENT): duplicate one into /Game first.
whenToUse: process=thumbnail: An asset needs a preview image, optionally written as a PNG file inside the project.
process=lods: One or several static meshes need LOD levels generated so distant copies render cheaper.
process=mesh_materials: An imported mesh came in with every slot on the default grid material and each slot needs its own material, once for every placement of the mesh.
process=mesh_materials: Several slots of a static or skeletal mesh asset get their materials in one call, by index or by slot name.
process=mesh_materials: Every mesh of an imported pack needs the same slot-name to material map (base, Material_0 ...): assetPaths with the slot names.
process=mesh_collision: An imported or Fab mesh has no simple collision, so pawns fall through it or walk through it.
process=mesh_collision: A decorative mesh (grass, flowers, small debris) must stop blocking the player.
process=mesh_collision: A terrain-like or concave mesh must collide exactly with its own triangles (complex).
whenNotToUse: process=thumbnail: The image should show the editor viewport or a level camera view (use control_editor.screenshot).
process=lods: LOD reduction settings or screen sizes must be tuned by hand (use manage_geometry.configure_mesh_lods).
process=lods: The mesh should use Nanite instead of discrete LODs (use asset.nanite_rebuild_mesh).
process=mesh_materials: Only one placed actor must look different from its mesh (use control_actor.set_material, which overrides a component and leaves the asset alone).
process=mesh_materials: It is not known yet which slot holds which part of the mesh (inspect.inspect_object with objectKind=mesh lists every slot with the triangle count and bounds of its geometry).
process=mesh_collision: A dynamic mesh actor needs collision generated (use manage_geometry.configure_mesh_collision).
process=mesh_collision: Only one placed copy should stop colliding (use control_actor.set_actor_collision).
process=mesh_collision: It must be checked whether a placed mesh blocks at all (use inspect.raycast_world).

outputPath.description: Project-relative PNG file to write, e.g. Saved/Thumbnails/SM_Crate.png.

assetPaths.description: Several asset paths to process in one call: lods generates LODs for each; mesh_materials sets the same materials entries on each mesh by slot name, passing over a slot a mesh lacks (an entry no mesh has fails the call), as a whole imported pack needs.

lodCount.description: Number of LOD levels to generate (1-50, default 4).

slot.description: The slot to set: its 0-based index (9) or its slot name ("hull"), as inspect_object objectKind=mesh lists them under materialSlots.

materialPath.description: Material or material instance asset path, e.g. /Game/Materials/M_Hull. It must load: a path that does not is refused, never swapped for a default material.

materials.description: The slots to set, one entry per slot: [{slot, materialPath}]. slot is a 0-based index or a slot name (inspect_object objectKind=mesh lists both under materialSlots). Every entry is checked first. One that is refused (index out of range, unknown slot name, a material that does not load) is named under refused and fails the call, while the valid entries are applied together in a single rebuild of the mesh.

save.description: Save the mesh after the change. Defaults to true.

collisionType.description: box, sphere or capsule: one shape fitted to the mesh bounds (a capsule stands upright along Z) replaces its simple collision. complex: the render triangles are the collision, exact for terrain-like or concave meshes but costlier. none: no collision, so pawns and traces pass through.

process.description:
Which process asset variant to run.
thumbnail: Render the preview of an asset and store it as its thumbnail (the asset is left unsaved; engine content keeps its own), and write it as a PNG when outputPath is given.
lods: Give one or several static mesh assets lodCount LODs in all (default 4, 1 to 50, LOD 0 included): each LOD keeps half the triangles of the one before (50%, 25%, ...), LODs past the count and the hand-tuned settings of the others are replaced, and each mesh is rebuilt and saved. Engine meshes are not changed: they are listed under engineContentPaths (ENGINE_CONTENT when nothing else was given), so duplicate one into /Game first. The reply counts processed out of requested and lists notFoundPaths and notMeshPaths; in a headless editor the build is skipped and each mesh is only checked.
mesh_materials: Set the materials in the slots of a static or skeletal mesh asset, by slot index or slot name, so every placement of the mesh shows them.
mesh_collision: Set the collision of a static mesh asset: one box, sphere or capsule fitted to its bounds, its own render triangles (complex), or none; every placed copy is rebuilt to match and the mesh is saved.

details.description: Operation details.

meshes.description: With assetPaths: one row per mesh, {assetPath, changed (slots this call changed on it), error (it is not a mesh, or does not load), saved (false only when it could not be saved)}.

materialSlots.description: Every slot of the mesh after the call, each {slotIndex, slotName, material (the asset path the slot holds, empty for none), changed (true when this call changed it)}.

applied.description: Entries that were valid and applied.

changed.description: Slots whose material this call changed; an entry that names the material a slot already holds changes nothing.

refused.description: Entries that were refused, each {index (its position in materials), slot (as given), materialPath, code, reason}: a slot index out of range, an unknown slot name, a material that does not load. A refused entry changes nothing, the call fails (MATERIAL_SLOTS_PARTIAL, or MATERIAL_SLOTS_REFUSED when no entry was valid) and the valid entries stay applied.

saved.description: Whether the mesh was saved.

saveSkippedReason.description: Why nothing was saved: save was false, or the mesh is engine content, which is never written.

collisionType.description: The collision the mesh has now.

shapeCount.description: Simple collision shapes the mesh holds after the call (0 for complex and none).

componentsRefreshed.description: Placed copies of the mesh in open worlds whose collision was rebuilt to match.

examples.title: Process an asset, chosen by process. thumbnail renders its preview at width by height (default 512, 1 to 4096) and stores it in the asset, which is left unsaved (thumbnailCached; engine content keeps its own), writing it as a PNG as well when outputPath names a project-relative file. lods gives static meshes lodCount LODs in all (default 4, LOD 0 included, each half the triangles of the one before), replacing LODs past the count and hand-tuned settings, then rebuilds and saves each. mesh_materials sets the materials in the slots of a static or skeletal mesh asset, by slot index or name, so every placement shows them; an engine mesh changes for this session only and is never saved (saveSkippedReason). mesh_collision sets the collision of a static mesh asset (a fitted box, sphere or capsule, its render triangles, or none), rebuilds every placed copy and saves it. lods and mesh_collision refuse engine meshes (ENGINE_CONTENT): duplicate one into /Game first.

discovery.summary: Query assets: existence, search by name/class, find by tag, find where a text appears inside assets (graph nodes by title too, so every call of a function), the node graph inside a material or Blueprint, material stats, source-control state.
whenToUse: lookup=exists: A path must be tested for an asset, or several paths at once, before creating, importing or referencing one.
lookup=search: Assets must be found across the project by name, class, folder or asset-registry tag.

lookup=by_tag: Assets under /Game must be found by an asset-registry tag, optionally with one value, such as the ParentClass tag every Blueprint carries. A tag written by asset.set_metadata with kind=tags is in the registry only when its name is listed under Project Settings > Asset Manager > Metadata Tags For Asset Registry and the asset has been saved; otherwise nothing matches (asset.inspect_asset lookup=metadata reads one asset).
lookup=text: A piece of text, such as a UI label or dialogue line, must be traced to the Blueprint, widget, table row or level actor holding it.
lookup=graph: A material or Blueprint must be summarised: node counts, parameters, blend mode or graph count.
lookup=material_stats: A material's shading model, blend mode, domain, node and parameter counts, or the input pins its Main result node accepts, must be read.
lookup=source_control_state: Before editing, it must be known whether assets are checked out, modified or held by someone else.
whenNotToUse: lookup=exists: A folder's contents must be browsed rather than one path tested (use asset.list).
lookup=search|by_tag: Actors placed in the open level must be found (use control_actor.find).
lookup=text: One known Blueprint graph must be read node by node (use blueprint.inspect_graph).
lookup=graph: One Blueprint's variables, functions or components are wanted (use blueprint.get_blueprint).
lookup=material_stats: The individual nodes of a material and their connections are needed (use material.get_material_info).
lookup=source_control_state: Assets must be checked out or submitted (use asset.source_control).

assetPaths.description: Several asset paths checked in one call; the reply maps each to true or false under existsByPath.

classNames.description: Asset classes to filter: a short class name (StaticMesh, Blueprint, ObjectRedirector, InputMappingContext) or a full class path (/Script/Engine.StaticMesh).

limit.description: Page size (1-500, default 50).

offset.description: Zero-based offset into the full result set.

tag.description: Asset-registry tag name, for example ParentClass, which every Blueprint carries.

value.description: Optional tag value to match, ignoring case.

includeLevel.description: Also search the actors and components of the open level: true or false outright; omitted, only when that level lies under packagePaths (always with the default /Game).

recursive.description: Also report every /Game package the assets depend on, transitively (up to 512).

lookup.description:
Which query asset variant to run.
exists: Check whether an asset exists at a given path, or which of several do.
search: Find or search assets by text, class, or package path with bounded pagination.
by_tag: Find /Game assets that carry an asset-registry tag, optionally with a given value (compared ignoring case).
text: Find where a piece of text appears: Blueprint graph nodes by title (every call of a function, by its name as the graph shows it), literals, assets picked on pins and comments, variable and component defaults (a reference to another asset matches by its path, so a sound name finds the node or component that plays it), widget texts, DataTable rows, String Table entries, and the actors of the open level.
graph: Analyze the node graph inside a material or Blueprint asset; a MetaSound, Niagara or Behavior Tree asset answers with the nextCall that reads its graph.
material_stats: Retrieve rendering statistics for a material.
source_control_state: Retrieve source-control state for an asset.

details.description: Operation details.

limit.description: Applied page size.

offset.description: Applied zero-based offset.

hasMore.description: True when more results exist beyond the current page.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the current page, or null when the page was requested without one.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null on the last page.

matches.description: Each match: asset, where (graph and node title, widget, row, string key or actor label), field, the full text, and nodeId for a graph literal.

matchCount.description: Every match found; more than the matches returned when truncated.

scannedAssets.description: Blueprints, DataTables and String Tables searched.

truncated.description: True when limit cut the list; raise limit to see the rest.

assetClass.description: Concrete UClass name of the analyzed asset.

graphType.description: Graph kind analyzed: Material, Blueprint, None, or the class of an asset whose graph another action reads (see nextCall).

nodeCount.description: Material expression nodes in the graph.

parameterCount.description: Material parameter expressions in the graph.

textureSampleCount.description: Texture sample expressions in the graph.

isMaterialInstance.description: True when the asset is a material instance.

isTwoSided.description: True when the material renders two-sided.

isMasked.description: True when the material uses masked blending.

blueprintType.description: Blueprint kind: Class, Interface, MacroLibrary, or FunctionLibrary.

totalNodes.description: Total nodes across every Blueprint graph.

graphCount.description: Number of graphs in the Blueprint.

message.description: Explanation when the asset type carries no graph, or which action reads it.

nextCall.description: A MetaSound, Niagara or Behavior Tree asset: the execute call of the action that reads its graph.

examples.title: Query assets: existence, search by name/class, find by tag, find where a text appears inside assets (graph nodes by title too, so every call of a function), the node graph inside a material or Blueprint, material stats, source-control state.

discovery.summary: Query marketplace libraries: Fab listing details, Fab downloads, Fab library, Fab search, Megascans library, and the status of a Fab import that is running.
whenToUse: lookup=fab_listing_details: A Fab search hit must be judged before adding it: description, seller, rating, price, file formats, sizes, and whether the project can import it.
lookup=fab_downloads: It must be known which Fab packs are already downloaded to this machine and where they are cached.
lookup=fab_library: The Fab listings the signed-in account owns must be listed, each with an id for adding to the project (an empty table is synced by the call itself).
lookup=fab_search: Content must be found on Fab by keyword, optionally from one publisher or of one kind, or free listings only, to get listing ids and to tell a Megascans hit from a random upload.
lookup=megascans_library: The Megascans packs downloaded by Bridge on this machine must be listed before one is imported.
lookup=fab_import_status: A Fab add has returned an operationId and it must be known whether the import is downloading, importing, done or failed, and where the content landed.
whenNotToUse: lookup=fab_listing_details: The listing is chosen and must be added to the project (use asset.import_marketplace_asset with marketplace=fab_listing).
lookup=fab_downloads: A downloaded pack must be copied into the project (use asset.maintain_content with maintenance=migrate).
lookup=fab_library: A listing from the library is ready to add to the project (use asset.import_marketplace_asset with marketplace=fab_listing).
lookup=fab_search: Content already installed in an engine template, plugin or Bridge folder is wanted (use asset.list with kind=content_sources).
lookup=megascans_library: A listed pack should be imported into the project (use asset.import_marketplace_asset with marketplace=megascans).
lookup=fab_import_status: The listing has not been added yet (use asset.import_marketplace_asset with marketplace=fab_listing).

listingId.description: Fab listing uid. Restricted to [A-Za-z0-9_-], 64 characters max. fab_import_status also takes it, in place of operationId, to report the newest import of that listing.

columnTypes.description: Column struct paths to read, for example "/Script/Fab.FabObjectNameColumn". Defaults to the name column plus "/Script/Fab.FabObjectColumn", which carries AssetId, ListingType, Seller and Source. Selecting a column is also the row filter, so naming one Fab does not write for every row will hide rows. Override this when a Fab update renames or adds columns; unresolved paths are reported rather than failing the call.

filter.description: Case-sensitive substring matched against each serialized row. Use "fab" to drop the legacy "uem" engine and plugin entries that otherwise fill the row limit.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return, clamped plugin-side.

query.description: Free-text search. At most 128 characters, and no quotes, backslashes or control characters.

seller.description: Only listings published by this seller, by name, for example Quixel Megascans. At most 128 characters, and no quotes, backslashes or control characters. Omit for every publisher.

listingType.description: Only this content kind, as a row's listingType names it, for example 3d-model or material. One token of [A-Za-z0-9_-], at most 40 characters. Omit for every kind.

operationId.description: Operation id from the add reply. Restricted to [A-Za-z0-9_-], 64 characters max. Give this or listingId, or neither to list the queue.

lookup.description:
Which query marketplace variant to run.
fab_listing_details: Describe one Fab listing: what it is (description, tags, publisher, category, rating, licenses, price, publication date and a preview image) and what adding it would do (the format it imports, the build or file it fetches, its size, whether a build exists for the running engine, and why it would refuse), so a caller can choose between search hits and know before adding. Opens the Fab tab when it is closed and waits up to 15 seconds for its page to load (PAGE_NOT_READY after that) instead of failing on the first call; the account must be signed in there. It reads the listing and its asset-formats resources and claims nothing. canAddToProject says whether add_fab_asset_to_project can import the listing, and when it cannot, addBlockedCode and addBlockedReason say why: COMPLETE_PROJECT (a whole project cannot be added to an existing one: create it as a new project from Fab, then migrate its content), METAHUMAN_FORMAT (Fab hands a MetaHuman listing to a workflow the add does not drive) or NO_IMPORTABLE_FORMAT (it ships none of unreal-engine, gltf, glb, fbx, obj or usdz). Megascans listings are importable like any other, because the add claims the listing itself. addFormat is the format the add would import (unreal-engine first, else gltf, glb, fbx, obj, usdz). For a unreal-engine pack, versionName, pickedEngineVersion and engineMatch name the build it would take (the highest at or below the running engine, else the lowest above it), engineVersions lists every engine the pack declares and supportsRunningEngine says whether the running engine is one of them. For a source format, downloadFile, quality and qualities (Megascans offers raw, high, mid and low) name the file. downloadBytes is the size of exactly the file or build the add would fetch and is left out, with downloadSizeKnown false, when Fab publishes none, which is every pack: unknown is never reported as zero. formats lists every format with its files and their sizes. isFree is derived from price, because the listing's own isFree flag disagrees with it and is not reported. addWarnings lists what would surprise the caller: a pack with no build for the running engine, and a mesh file so large that the add refuses it until combineMeshes is chosen. The preview comes back as imageBase64, promoted into a real MCP image block rather than a URL, and is omitted rather than truncated past the reply cap. When a field cannot be read the response names the keys it did see, so a Fab schema change reports itself.
fab_downloads: Report what the Fab plugin has already downloaded to this machine, with the cache directory it used. Pair with list_content_sources(sourceRoot="fabLibrary") and asset.migrate_assets to bring a downloaded pack into the project. This reads local state only: the archives Fab has finished fetching into its cache. Finding a listing is lookup=fab_search and adding one is asset.import_marketplace_asset; a download that is still running is not listed until it ends (the add's import status shows its progress), and a unreal-engine pack is installed by Fab straight into the project, so it never appears here.
fab_library: List your Fab "My Library" entries that the Fab plugin has synced into the editor's data storage (TEDS). This is the searchable inventory of what your Fab account owns — distinct from lookup=fab_downloads, which only reports packs already downloaded to disk. Each row carries the listing AssetId, so a row can be handed straight to add_fab_asset_to_project instead of being a name you have to search for again. A table with no rows has never been synced, so this runs Fab's own sync itself (the Fab.TEDS.MyFolderIntegration console command, a thousand rows a page) and waits for rows, up to about 12 seconds and until their count has held still for a moment: syncTriggered and syncWaitedSeconds say that it happened. The remaining pages keep loading in the background, so a very large library may need a second call. A table that already holds rows is read as it is, because the sync first removes every row; to refresh one, run Fab.TEDS.MyFolderIntegration through control_editor.console_command. When no rows arrive the account's library is empty or the Fab tab is signed out: Fab.Login opens Epic's account portal, and no credential ever passes through this tool. A synced library is mostly engine versions and plugins carrying Source "uem", so filter for "fab" to see actual content. Columns are resolved by path, and the data storage is reached through the modular-features registry, so this never links the Fab module and keeps working when Fab changes its schema.
fab_search: Search the whole public Fab catalog through the signed-in Fab tab and get listing ids you can pass straight to add_fab_asset_to_project. Opens the Fab tab when it is closed and waits up to 15 seconds for its page to load (PAGE_NOT_READY after that) instead of failing on the first call; the account must be signed in there. seller narrows the search to one publisher by name (Quixel Megascans for the Megascans library) and listingType to one content kind (3d-model, material), so a Megascans surface is one call rather than a page of unrelated uploads. Every hit says who published it, which category it is in, how it is rated, what it costs and which formats it ships, as far as the search itself returned them; a fact the row did not carry is left out, never filled in, and nothing more is fetched per row. isFree is derived from price, because the listing's own isFree flag disagrees with it and is not reported. A hit is a candidate, not a promise: no channel filter is applied, because pinning one hid the Quixel/Megascans library entirely. Whether a listing can be imported is resolved at add time, which reports NO_IMPORTABLE_FORMAT only when the listing ships none of unreal-engine, gltf, glb, fbx, obj or usdz; call lookup=fab_listing_details first for canAddToProject, the engine build and the download size up front. Results carry ids and labels only; no thumbnail, download URL or account field leaves the page.
megascans_library: List the Quixel Bridge / Megascans library index on this machine. This reads the packs a Quixel Bridge install has already downloaded: Bridge writes a plain uassetsData.json next to them, so the inventory is an ordinary local read. Megascans listings that are not downloaded yet are found with lookup=fab_search (seller Quixel Megascans) and imported straight from Fab with import_marketplace_asset (marketplace=fab_listing). Pair this with import_megascans_asset to bring a downloaded entry into the project.
fab_import_status: Report a Fab import that asset.import_marketplace_asset (marketplace=fab_listing) started, by operationId (from the add reply) or by listingId (its newest import), together with the queue it is in; give neither to list just the queue. It reads the adapter's own record, never Fab's page, so it needs no sign-in and answers at once — except while Fab is importing: the import holds the editor for minutes and every call, this one included, then answers EDITOR_BLOCKED. That is the import working, not a failure: retry every 20 to 30 seconds. phase is queued (another import runs first; queuePosition and the queue say how many are ahead, and it starts by itself), resolving (asking Fab for the download), downloading (downloadPercent is the figure on Fab's own download notification, for a unreal-engine pack and a source format alike; downloadedBytes of downloadBytes too when Fab's download folder shows them, which a pack's does not), importing (Fab's importer is running; assetsSoFar counts what the asset registry has gained), cancelling (a cancel was accepted; the import ends within a second), done (importedRoot, assetCount and sampleAssetPaths, meshes first) or failed (failureCode, failure, and fabErrors quoting what Fab logged). cancellable says whether a cancel would stop the import right now. Stop polling when finished is true. The editor keeps the last 16 imports of the session and forgets them on restart. Do not call add again to look at progress.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

categoryPath.description: Category path, slash-joined, when Fab publishes one.

averageRating.description: Average rating as Fab reports it. Absent when the listing has none.

ratingCount.description: How many ratings the average rests on. Absent when Fab publishes no count.

licenseNames.description: Names of the licenses the listing is offered under.

isCc0.description: True when a license of the listing is CC0 (public domain, no credit needed), read from the license names: Fab's own flag is also set on CC-BY licenses. Absent when the listing publishes no licenses.

attributionRequired.description: True when a license of the listing is Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY, CC BY-SA ...): an asset used under it needs a credit line in the project naming its title, author, source and license, and saying what was changed. Absent when the listing publishes no licenses.

price.description: Starting price in Fab's own units; 0 is free. Absent when the price field has a shape this does not know (see priceShape).

currency.description: Currency code of price, when Fab publishes one.

isFree.description: True when price is 0. Derived from price: the listing's own isFree flag disagrees with it and is never reported. When the price cannot be read this falls back to that flag and priceShape says so.

priceShape.description: Key names of a price field this does not recognise, so a Fab change reports itself. Present only then.

publishedAt.description: When the listing was published, as Fab states it.

imageBase64.description: Preview image bytes, base64. Promoted to an MCP image content block.

hasImage.description: False when no preview could be inlined.

imageOmitted.description: Present when the preview was skipped for exceeding the reply cap.

descriptionKeys.description: Listing keys observed when no description field matched.

thumbnailShape.description: Thumbnail keys observed when no image URL matched.

assetFormats.description: Asset format codes this listing ships, e.g. unreal-engine, fbx, gltf.

hasUnrealBuild.description: True when the listing ships a packaged unreal-engine build, which Fab imports through its pack workflow.

formats.description: Every format the listing ships: code, and files each with name, bytes (left out when Fab publishes no size) and quality when the name carries a tier.

addFormat.description: The format add_fab_asset_to_project would import: unreal-engine, else gltf, glb, fbx, obj or usdz. Absent when none is importable.

distributionMethod.description: How Fab distributes a unreal-engine listing: asset_pack (content for a project) or complete_project (a whole project). Present only for a listing that ships unreal-engine.

runningEngine.description: The editor's engine version, major.minor, that supportsRunningEngine and engineMatch are judged against.

engineVersions.description: Every engine version a unreal-engine pack declares, lowest first, as Fab spells them (UE_5.4).

supportsRunningEngine.description: True when a build of the pack declares exactly the running engine. Present only for a unreal-engine listing that publishes versions.

engineMatch.description: exact, older or newer: the build the add would take against the running engine. older is the newest build for an earlier engine, newer the oldest build for a later one. Absent when no version declares an engine.

versionName.description: Name of the pack build the add would take.

pickedEngineVersion.description: The engine version that build declares, for example UE_5.4.

downloadFile.description: The file of a source format the add would download.

quality.description: Quality tier of that file (raw, high, mid or low), when the listing publishes tiers.

qualities.description: The quality tiers the source format offers, best first. add_fab_asset_to_project takes the highest of high, mid, low, raw that exists.

downloadBytes.description: Size in bytes of exactly the file or build the add would fetch. Absent when Fab publishes no size, which is every pack: unknown, never zero.

downloadSizeKnown.description: False when downloadBytes is absent because Fab publishes no size for what the add would fetch.

canAddToProject.description: True when add_fab_asset_to_project can import this listing: it ships unreal-engine as an asset pack, or gltf, glb, fbx, obj or usdz. False for a complete project, a MetaHuman listing and a listing with no importable format (addBlockedCode says which). Megascans listings are importable: the add claims the listing itself. Check this rather than hasUnrealBuild before adding.

addBlockedCode.description: Present when canAddToProject is false: COMPLETE_PROJECT, METAHUMAN_FORMAT or NO_IMPORTABLE_FORMAT, the code the add would answer with.

addBlockedReason.description: Present when canAddToProject is false: why this listing cannot be imported.

addWarnings.description: What would surprise the caller about adding this listing: a pack with no build for the running engine, or a mesh file large enough that the add refuses it until combineMeshes is chosen.

downloads.description: Cached Fab downloads. Each entry carries assetId and cachedFile.

cacheDirectory.description: Directory the Fab plugin caches downloads in.

cacheDirectoryExists.description: False when nothing has been downloaded yet.

fabModuleAvailable.description: True when the plugin was built against the Fab module and read the cache through its own API rather than scanning the directory.

note.description: Guidance on what to do next given the current state.

entries.description: Library rows. Each entry maps column struct name to that column's properties, read by reflection. FabObjectColumn.AssetId is the listing id add_fab_asset_to_project takes.

unresolvedColumnTypes.description: Requested column paths that do not exist in this build — usually a Fab schema change.

syncTriggered.description: True when the table held no rows and Fab's library sync was run for this call.

syncWaitedSeconds.description: How long this call waited for rows after starting the sync. Present only when the sync ran.

syncSkipped.description: Why the sync was not run on an empty table: this editor registers no Fab sync command. Present only then.

listings.description: Matched listings: listingId, title, listingType, isFree (derived from price), tags, and, when the row carried them, seller, category, averageRating, ratingCount, price, currency, isCc0, publishedAt and formats (the format codes it ships). unresolvedPriceShape names the price field's keys when the price could not be read. The listing's own isFree flag is not reported.

assets.description: Indexed library entries, verbatim from uassetsData.json.

indexExists.description: False when Bridge has never written an index here.

importAvailable.description: True when this build links the MegascansPlugin module, so import_megascans_asset can run.

phase.description: queued, resolving, downloading, importing, cancelling, done or failed.

finished.description: True once phase is done or failed; stop polling.

queuePosition.description: 1-based place in the queue while phase is queued; absent otherwise.

queue.description: The import that is running, then every add waiting behind it in the order they start: operationId, listingId, title, phase, queuePosition, elapsedSeconds, and downloadedBytes and downloadPercent when known. Absent when nothing is running or queued.

queueLength.description: How many imports are running or queued.

elapsedSeconds.description: Seconds since the add was requested; frozen once the import finished.

formatCode.description: Format Fab was asked to import.

fileName.description: The file Fab downloads (source formats only).

engineExactMatch.description: False when no build of the pack declares the running engine; engineMatch says which build was taken instead.

engineVersion.description: The engine version that build declares, for example UE_5.4.

combinesMeshes.description: True when Fab's importer merges every mesh of a file into ONE static mesh for this listing.

combineMeshesApplied.description: Present only when the add passed combineMeshes=false for a listing Fab merges meshes for: true once Interchange's mesh combining was switched off before it ran, false while that has not happened yet or could not (the import then yields the single merged mesh).

downloadedBytes.description: Bytes fetched so far, when the download folder shows them. Absent when the download cannot be observed (a unreal-engine pack, or a download that has not begun).

downloadPercent.description: 0-100, as Fab's own download notification shows it, for a unreal-engine pack and a source format alike. Absent when that notification cannot be read: before the download starts, after it ends, or when Fab shows none.

cancellable.description: Present while the import is not finished: true when a cancel would stop it right now (queued, a unreal-engine pack that is downloading, or an import Interchange is translating); false for a source-format download, which Fab gives no cancel for.

assetsSoFar.description: New assets the asset registry has gained so far.

importedRoot.description: Where the content landed: the folder Fab chose (typically /Game/Fab/... or /Game/<PackName>), or the destinationPath the add asked for once the import was moved there. Present once finished and any landed.

sampleAssetPaths.description: Up to ten imported asset paths, the static and skeletal meshes first, at their final paths when the add asked for destinationPath or assetName.

relocated.description: Present when the add asked for destinationPath or assetName: true when assets were moved or renamed.

movedCount.description: Assets moved or renamed by that relocation.

relocationNote.description: What the relocation did not do, and why: a folder or name already taken (nothing moves then), an assetName with no single asset to name, or content left where Fab put it. Absent when everything asked for was done.

saved.description: Present once the import settled and any assets landed: true when every package the import left dirty was saved, false when some could not be (see unsavedPackages, and the message and note say so in capitals). Fab leaves what it imports unsaved in memory, so a Megascans add would otherwise be lost when the editor closes. The import is saved again 15 and 60 seconds after it ends, because Interchange marks packages dirty after the last asset has appeared; read again before saving by hand.

savedCount.description: Packages that were saved. A unreal-engine pack arrives on disk already and is not dirty, so it counts none.

unsavedPackages.description: Packages that could not be saved, by name; control_editor save_all writes them once whatever blocked the save is fixed.

failureCode.description: Present when phase is failed: FAB_IMPORT_FAILED (Fab logged that it gave up), IMPORT_TIMED_OUT (nothing appeared before the ceiling), IMPORT_PARTIAL (still streaming at the ceiling; what landed is reported), CANCELLED (cancel_fab_import stopped it; whatever had landed is listed and left unsaved), or the add's own refusal code (COMPLETE_PROJECT, METAHUMAN_FORMAT, LARGE_SCENE_FILE, QUALITY_NOT_AVAILABLE, NO_IMPORTABLE_FORMAT, NO_DOWNLOAD_URL).

failure.description: Present when phase is failed: why, in words.

fabErrors.description: Error lines Fab logged while the import ran, with URLs and anything credential-shaped masked.

examples.title: Query marketplace libraries: Fab listing details, Fab downloads, Fab library, Fab search, Megascans library, and the status of a Fab import that is running.

discovery.summary: Rename an asset or a folder in place (newName), or move it (destinationPath); a folder takes every asset under it along. Several unrelated assets in one call: maintain_content bulk_rename with renames.
whenToUse: An asset needs a new name in its own folder; settings that point at it (default map, game mode) follow.
A folder must get a new name and every asset under it must go along.
whenNotToUse: Many assets need new names by pattern, prefix, suffix or a list (use asset.maintain_content with maintenance=bulk_rename).
A copy under a new name is wanted, with the original kept (use asset.duplicate).

sourcePath.description: Source /Game asset path, or a folder: a folder is renamed with everything under it.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Rename an asset or a folder in place (newName), or move it (destinationPath); a folder takes every asset under it along. Several unrelated assets in one call: maintain_content bulk_rename with renames.

discovery.summary: Write package metadata on an asset (kind metadata: key/value pairs, numbers and booleans as text, objects and arrays as JSON text, null skipped; updatedKeys counts them) or tag it (tags: each tag becomes a metadata key set to true; appliedTags). The asset is marked unsaved, not saved (save_all keeps it). Package metadata is editor-only: cooking strips it, so the running game cannot read it.
whenToUse: kind=metadata: Key and value notes such as author or revision must be attached to an asset; the change stays unsaved until the asset is saved.
kind=tags: Simple labels such as Reviewed or Prop must be attached to an asset as package metadata; the change stays unsaved until the asset is saved.
whenNotToUse: kind=metadata: The stored values must be read back (use asset.inspect_asset).
kind=metadata: A property of the asset itself must change (use inspect.set_property).
kind=tags: Actors in a level need a tag (use control_actor.add_tag).

kind=tags: Assets must be found by the tag afterwards. asset.query_asset lookup=by_tag reads the asset registry, which carries a package-metadata tag only when its name is listed under Project Settings > Asset Manager > Metadata Tags For Asset Registry and the asset has been saved; otherwise it finds nothing.
kind=tags: The tags on an asset must be read back (use asset.inspect_asset lookup=metadata, which lists them under metadata at once).

tags.description: Tag names to set; each is written as package metadata with the value "true".

kind.description:
Which set metadata variant to run; omit for 'metadata'.
metadata: Set metadata key-value pairs on an asset.
tags: Set tags on an asset, stored as package metadata: each tag name is written with the value "true".

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Write package metadata on an asset (kind metadata: key/value pairs, numbers and booleans as text, objects and arrays as JSON text, null skipped; updatedKeys counts them) or tag it (tags: each tag becomes a metadata key set to true; appliedTags). The asset is marked unsaved, not saved (save_all keeps it). Package metadata is editor-only: cooking strips it, so the running game cannot read it.

discovery.summary: Revision control for the project, chosen by sourceControlOp: init makes a Git repository at the project root with an Unreal .gitignore and a first commit and turns the Git provider on; commit_all stages and commits every change (alreadyClean when there is none); enable turns a provider on or switches to it (Git, Perforce, Subversion); checkout and submit check assets out and in through the provider that is on, listing paths that name no asset (skipped). Git runs on a worker and every step comes back with its output.
whenToUse: sourceControlOp=checkout: Assets must be checked out of revision control before they are edited.
sourceControlOp=submit: Checked-out assets must be submitted to the revision-control server with a change description.
sourceControlOp=enable: A revision-control provider such as Git or Perforce must be selected before checkout or submit can work.
sourceControlOp=init: A project with no repository needs one, with an Unreal .gitignore and a first commit, in one call.
sourceControlOp=commit_all: A snapshot of every change in the project is wanted as one commit, for example after a batch of edits.
whenNotToUse: sourceControlOp=checkout: The checked-out or modified state of assets is wanted (use asset.query_asset for source control state).
sourceControlOp=submit|commit_all: Unsaved editor changes must reach disk first (use control_editor.save_all).
sourceControlOp=submit: Every change in the project is wanted as one Git snapshot, without listing assets (use sourceControlOp=commit_all).
sourceControlOp=enable: Only the state of particular assets is wanted (use asset.query_asset for source control state).
sourceControlOp=init: A Perforce or Subversion provider is wanted; init builds only a Git repository (select the provider with sourceControlOp=enable).
sourceControlOp=commit_all: Only chosen assets must go in, or the project uses Perforce or Subversion (use sourceControlOp=submit).

provider.description: Provider name as the editor registers it, e.g. Git or Perforce. Omit to report the current provider without changing it.

userName.description: Commit author name, written to the repository config only.

userEmail.description: Commit author email, written to the repository config only.

sourceControlOp.description:
Which source control variant to run.
checkout: Check out assets (paths, or assetPath) in the enabled revision-control provider so they can be edited and submitted. Paths that name no asset in the project are skipped and listed (skipped); none left is NO_VALID_ASSETS, and source control off is SOURCE_CONTROL_DISABLED (turn it on with sourceControlOp=enable). The reply gives checkedOut and assets.
submit: Submit (check in) saved assets (paths, or assetPath) to the enabled provider with description as the change description. Paths that name no asset are skipped and listed (skipped); none left is NO_VALID_ASSETS, a provider refusal SUBMIT_FAILED, and source control off SOURCE_CONTROL_DISABLED. The reply gives submitted.
enable: Turn revision control on with the provider named (Git, Perforce or Subversion, as the editor registers it), switching from another provider that is on; with that provider already on, or none named while one is on, it reports the current provider. A provider whose plugin is off or that cannot connect (Git needs a repository at the project root: sourceControlOp=init) is SOURCE_CONTROL_ENABLE_FAILED.
init: Put the project under Git: create a repository at the project root when there is none, write an Unreal .gitignore when there is none (Binaries, Intermediate, Saved, DerivedDataCache), stage everything, make the first commit (description, default "Initial commit") and turn the Git provider on. userName and userEmail go to the repository config only and cannot hold quotes or control characters. The reply gives committed, commit (short hash), provider and steps (each git command with its exit code and output); a failing step answers GIT_INIT_FAILED, GIT_ADD_FAILED or GIT_COMMIT_FAILED.
commit_all: Stage every change in the project (git add -A, honouring .gitignore) and commit it with description as the message; a clean tree answers success with alreadyClean true and committed false. Needs a repository (NO_REPOSITORY: sourceControlOp=init). userName and userEmail, when sent, go to the repository config and cannot hold quotes or control characters. The reply gives committed, commit and steps.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Revision control for the project, chosen by sourceControlOp: init makes a Git repository at the project root with an Unreal .gitignore and a first commit and turns the Git provider on; commit_all stages and commits every change (alreadyClean when there is none); enable turns a provider on or switches to it (Git, Perforce, Subversion); checkout and submit check assets out and in through the provider that is on, listing paths that name no asset (skipped). Git runs on a worker and every step comes back with its output.

discovery.summary: Show a page of a folder's assets as one numbered picture: each tile is the thumbnail the editor keeps for the asset (stored in its package when it was saved from the editor, or made this session), labelled with its number and name, three across; an asset with none shows a plain grey tile and thumbnail false in its row (none is rendered: that would load the asset; asset.process_asset process=thumbnail makes one). By default only assets without a caption are shown (uncaptionedOnly), so captioning a page with caption_assets and asking again brings the next ones. Rows give each number its assetPath and class; nextOffset is the next page. The picture is saved under Saved/Captures (file) and returned as an image.
whenToUse: An agent must see what a folder of assets holds (a pack whose names say little) before captioning or choosing them.
Captioning a library: show a page, caption it with caption_assets, show the next.
whenNotToUse: One asset's thumbnail must be made or refreshed: use asset.process_asset process=thumbnail.
Assets must be found by a description: use find_assets_like.

class.description: Only assets of this class, by its name (StaticMesh, Texture2D, MaterialInstanceConstant, SoundWave, Blueprint...).

uncaptionedOnly.description: Only assets with no caption yet (default true); false shows every asset.

offset.description: How many assets of the list to skip (default 0): the previous reply's nextOffset.

limit.description: Assets on the page (1-16, default 12).

number.description: The number on its tile (its place in the whole list, from 1).

thumbnail.description: False when the editor keeps no thumbnail for it (its tile is grey).

total.description: Assets in the whole list (after uncaptionedOnly).

nextOffset.description: The offset of the next page; absent on the last.

imageBase64.description: The picture as a PNG, base64, returned as an image; left out past 3 MB (the file has it).
