discovery.summary: Write gameplay logic into an Actor Blueprint in one call: health that takes damage and dies, damage on touch, a pickup that heals or counts (coins, keys), a sprint key for a Character, a key that shoots projectiles for a pawn, a pawn that chases the player or patrols a route, a turret that turns to the player and fires at them, an enemy the player defeats by jumping on it, a barrel that explodes when it dies, a moving platform or elevator, walk, look and jump controls for a Character, a pawn that respawns when it falls or dies (with checkpoints), a goal that ends the level when the player reaches it, a pad that launches a Character, a teleporter, a platform that falls when a pawn lands on it, a time limit, a spawner that keeps spawning an actor class, a dash key for a Character, the health of the player or a count such as coins or score on screen, a hint on screen while the player is in an area, or a game over screen that restarts the level when the player dies. Logic none of these covers is written with edit_graph.
whenToUse: behaviour=health: A player, enemy or breakable object must take damage and die; behaviour health_hud shows it on screen.
behaviour=damage_on_touch: Spikes, lava, an enemy body or a fire must hurt what touches it.
behaviour=pickup: A health pack, coin, key or ammo box must be collected by walking into it.
behaviour=sprint: The player must run faster while holding a key.
behaviour=shoot: The player (or any possessed pawn) must shoot projectiles with a key; a projectile from manage_combat create_combat_asset damages what it hits and never hits its shooter.

behaviour=chase: An enemy or creature must run after the player; with usePathfinding (default) the level needs a NavMeshBoundsVolume (manage_level_structure create_volume), without it the pawn heads straight for the player.
behaviour=patrol: An enemy or guard must walk a route, and may chase the player who comes close.

behaviour=turret: A tower, cannon or enemy must shoot at the player who comes close; a projectile from manage_combat create_combat_asset damages what it hits. With behaviour chase too, a pawn runs at the player and shoots.

behaviour=stomp: A platformer enemy must die when the player jumps on it, and hurt the player who walks into it. A damage_on_touch the actor has is taken over (it would hurt the stomping player too); its damage becomes sideDamage when none is given.
behaviour=explosive: A barrel, crate or mine must blow up when shot or hit, hurting what stands near; it needs the health behaviour, so damage from any source sets it off.
behaviour=moving_platform: A platform, lift or elevator must travel a route by itself, every placed copy of a Blueprint alike (each copy keeps its own PlatformPoints).
behaviour=controls: A Character made with manage_character create_character_blueprint (or any Character without input) must be playable: it has no input until this runs.
behaviour=respawn: A player pawn must not be lost for good when it falls off the level or dies.

behaviour=respawn: Checkpoints: tag a trigger actor (manage_interaction create_interactable trigger, or any actor that overlaps pawns) with checkpointTag; the pawn respawns where it stood when it touched it.
behaviour=goal: A level needs an end: a finish line, an exit door, a flag the player reaches.
behaviour=launch_pad: A jump pad, bounce pad, trampoline or boost pad for the player or any Character.
behaviour=teleporter: Portals, warp pads, or a pair of teleporters between two places.
behaviour=falling_platform: A ledge or bridge must give way under the player a moment after they land on it.
behaviour=countdown: A level or a run must be finished within a time limit.
behaviour=spawner: Enemies, pickups or obstacles must keep appearing while the game runs.
behaviour=dash: A player Character needs a quick burst of movement on a key: a dash, a dodge, an air dash.
behaviour=health_hud: The player must see their own health: a health bar on the HUD.
behaviour=counter_hud: The player must see a count: coins collected, score, keys, kills.
behaviour=hint: A sign, a tutorial area or a talking spot must tell the player something (Press Space to jump).
behaviour=game_over: The player death must end the run: a game over screen, then the level starts again.
whenNotToUse: behaviour=health: The project uses the Gameplay Ability System for attributes (use manage_gas).
behaviour=damage_on_touch: A whole area must hurt or kill (use manage_level_structure create_volume with a pain causing or kill Z volume).
behaviour=pickup: The item must go into an inventory system (use manage_inventory).
behaviour=sprint: The walk speed itself must change (use manage_character configure_character walkSpeed).
behaviour=shoot: A weapon actor the pawn holds must do the shooting (use manage_combat configure_projectile for its Fire function).
behaviour=chase: The pawn walks a route too (behaviour patrol, which chases with chaseRange; chase refuses a pawn that patrols).
behaviour=chase: Senses, cover or decisions beyond chasing (use manage_ai with a Behavior Tree or State Tree).
behaviour=patrol: Senses, cover or decisions beyond walking a route and chasing (use manage_ai with a Behavior Tree or State Tree).
behaviour=turret: The player shoots with a key (behaviour shoot).
behaviour=stomp: A hazard must hurt whatever touches it, from above too (behaviour damage_on_touch).
behaviour=explosive: Damage must happen on touch (behaviour damage_on_touch).
behaviour=moving_platform: One placed actor must spin or travel (control_actor edit_component with a RotatingMovement or InterpToMovement component).
behaviour=moving_platform: A pawn must walk a route (behaviour patrol).
behaviour=controls: Only one key or action must be added (use manage_networking configure_input for the asset and blueprint edit_graph for its node).
behaviour=respawn: A pawn that should stay dead, such as an enemy: give it the health behaviour with destroyOnDeath instead.
behaviour=goal: Something must happen on every touch, by any actor (use a trigger actor from manage_interaction create_interactable).
behaviour=launch_pad: A Character must jump higher by itself (manage_character set_movement_property JumpZVelocity).
behaviour=teleporter: Moving an actor from the editor or a test (control_actor set_transform).
behaviour=falling_platform: A platform must keep moving on its own (add an InterpToMovement component with its control points).
behaviour=countdown: Something must happen once after a delay (edit_graph with a Delay or a timer node).
behaviour=spawner: Actors must be placed once, before play (use control_actor spawn).
behaviour=dash: It must run faster while a key is held (use behaviour sprint).
behaviour=health_hud: A bar floating over an actor in the world, such as over an enemy.
behaviour=counter_hud: Health as a bar (behaviour health_hud).
behaviour=hint: A value such as coins or a timer must stay on screen (behaviour counter_hud).
behaviour=game_over: The player must come back where it died or at a checkpoint (behaviour respawn; a pawn that respawns when it dies is refused here).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

destroyOnDeath.description: Destroy the actor when its health reaches 0 (default false; OnDied fires either way).

invulnerableTime.description: Seconds after a hit during which further damage is ignored, so one touch costs one hit (default 0, none); heals still count.

damage.description: Damage on each touch (default 10; negative heals).

knockback.description: Speed a touching Character is launched away from the actor at, in units per second (default 0, none).

heal.description: Health given to the pawn that collects it; it reaches an actor with health (add_health) as negative damage.

collectorClass.description: Instead of heal: the class that collects it (a Blueprint path such as /Game/Blueprints/BP_Player), whose variableName goes up by amount.

variableName.description: With collectorClass: the collector's Int or Float variable (Coins).

soundPath.description: Sound asset played at the actor: where a pickup was collected, a goal when the player reaches it, a pad on each launch, where a teleported pawn arrives, or an explosive blows up.

key.description: The key that drives it: held to sprint (default LeftShift), pressed to shoot (default LeftMouseButton) or to dash (default Q). Any key name works: SpaceBar, Gamepad_RightTrigger, Gamepad_FaceButton_Right.

inputActionPath.description: An Input Action to use instead of the one the behaviour makes next to the Blueprint (IA_Sprint, IA_Shoot, IA_Dash).

mappingContextPath.description: The Input Mapping Context its keys go in (the project's own); default the one the pawn already registers, else /Game/Input/IMC_MCP.

projectileClass.description: The projectile it shoots: a Blueprint path (/Game/Weapons/BP_Fireball) or class path.

fireRate.description: Most shots a minute (default 300 for shoot, 60 for turret).

chaseRange.description: Distance within which the pawn chases the player, in units: chase defaults to 2000, and a patrol chases only when given one (default 0, or the range of a chase it takes over).

stopDistance.description: How close it gets to the player before it stops, in units (default 100).

usePathfinding.description: Follow the navigation mesh (default true; the level needs a NavMeshBoundsVolume, from manage_level_structure create_volume); false heads straight for the player or the next point.

points.description: The route: [x, y, z] offsets from where the actor starts, in world axes, visited in turn and looped (default [[500, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0]], back and forth). Each placed copy keeps its own route (PatrolPoints or PlatformPoints is instance editable).

waitTime.description: Seconds it waits at each point (default 1).

range.description: Distance within which it turns to the player and fires, in units (default 2000).

bounceSpeed.description: Upward speed the stomping Character bounces off at, units per second (default 600).

sideDamage.description: Damage to a player Character that bumps it from the side or below, at most once a second (default 0, none, or the damage of a damage_on_touch it takes over).

explosionDamage.description: Damage at the centre of the blast, less toward its edge (default 50).

explosionRadius.description: Radius of the blast in units (default 400); walls between it and an actor shield that actor.

effectPath.description: A Niagara system played at the blast (none by default).

speed.description: Units per second it travels between points (default 200).

look.description: Also turn the view with the mouse and the right stick (default true); false for a fixed camera.

fallHeight.description: How far below its respawn point the pawn may fall before it respawns, in units (default 2000).

checkpointTag.description: Actor tag that marks a checkpoint (default Checkpoint).

nextLevel.description: Level opened once the goal is reached, by name or /Game path (a path must exist). Omitted: the game stays in this level, and OnGoalReached is left for other logic.

delay.description: Seconds between reaching the goal and opening nextLevel (default 2).

launchVelocity.description: Launch velocity [x, y, z] in units per second, world axes (default [0, 0, 1200], straight up).

overrideXY.description: Replace the horizontal speed of the Character instead of adding to it (default false).

cooldown.description: Seconds before it works again: before a Character can dash again, or before a teleporter takes a pawn after one arrived on it (default 1).

fallDelay.description: Seconds it shakes before it drops (default 0.5).

respawnTime.description: Seconds after it starts to drop until it is back in place (default 3); 0 never: it is destroyed 5 seconds into its fall.

seconds.description: The time limit in whole seconds (default 60).

killAtZero.description: Kill the actor when the time is up (default true; it needs the health behaviour to die). False only fires OnTimeUp.

spawnClass.description: The actor it spawns: a Blueprint path (/Game/Enemies/BP_Slime) or class path; not the spawner itself.

maxAlive.description: Most of its spawned actors alive at once (default 5); a destroyed one frees its place.

radius.description: How far across from the spawner an actor may appear, in units (default 0: on the spawner).

dashSpeed.description: Launch speed along the facing, units per second (default 1500).

widgetPath.description: A Widget Blueprint to show instead of the one made next to the Blueprint under UI/ (WBP_HealthBar, WBP_<variable>Counter, WBP_GameOver, WBP_Hint). One without the bar or the text gets it: the health bar HUD piece (add_game_widget), a text at the top right, a full-screen shade with the message, or a dark box at the bottom with the hint.

barName.description: The ProgressBar in the widget that shows the health (default HealthBar_Bar, the bar of the health bar piece). A bar named here must already be in the widget.

label.description: Text before the number (default the variable name; empty for the number alone).

textName.description: The TextBlock in the widget that the behaviour writes: the count of counter_hud (default <variable>Counter), or the message of game_over (default GameOver_Text) or of a hint (default Hint_Text). A text named here must already be in the widget.

message.description: The text shown: a game over's message (default GAME OVER), or the hint itself (required for hint).

hideAfter.description: Seconds the hint stays once shown (default 0: while the pawn stays in the area).

restartDelay.description: Seconds before the level opens again (default 3); 0 never restarts it.

behaviour.description:
Which add behaviour variant to run.
health: Give an actor health: Health and MaxHealth variables, damage from any source (ApplyDamage, a pain causing volume, a projectile) lowers it and negative damage heals, a Heal function, OnHealthChanged and OnDied dispatchers, and optional destroy on death.
damage_on_touch: Make an actor damage whatever touches it: ApplyDamage with TouchDamage on each overlap, which an actor with health loses (a negative amount heals); with knockback a touching Character is also launched away from it. It fires on overlap, so the actor needs a component that overlaps pawns (a sphere or box with the Trigger or OverlapAllDynamic profile).
pickup: Make an actor a pickup: a pawn that touches it collects it, which heals the pawn (heal) or adds to a number variable of the collector class (coins, keys, ammo), plays a sound and destroys the pickup. It fires on overlap, so the actor needs a component that overlaps pawns (a sphere or box with the Trigger or OverlapAllDynamic profile).
sprint: Give a Character a sprint: while the key is held its MaxWalkSpeed is sprintSpeed, and on release the walk speed it had at BeginPlay comes back. The key gets an Input Action and a mapping, registered when the character is possessed.
shoot: Give a pawn a key that shoots: each press spawns projectileClass in front of it, facing its way and owned by it, and launches it at projectileSpeed, at most fireRate shots a minute. The key gets an Input Action and a mapping, registered when the pawn is possessed.
chase: Make a pawn chase the player: every quarter second, while the player is within chaseRange, its AI controller moves it toward the player and stops stopDistance away; out of range it stops. The pawn is set to be possessed by an AI controller when placed or spawned.
patrol: Make a pawn patrol: its AI controller walks it to each of points in turn (offsets from where it starts), it waits waitTime at each and the route loops; with chaseRange it chases the player who comes that close and goes back to its route after. A chase the pawn already has is taken over. The pawn is set to be possessed by an AI controller when placed or spawned.
turret: Make an actor a turret: every frame, while the player is within range, it turns about its vertical axis to face the player and fires projectileClass at them at projectileSpeed, at most fireRate shots a minute; each projectile is owned by the actor, so it never hits it. Nothing checks line of sight: a wall between them stops the shots.
stomp: Make an enemy the player defeats by landing on it: a player-controlled Character that lands on top of the actor bounces up at bounceSpeed and the actor dies (with the health behaviour it takes damage enough to die, else it is destroyed); one that bumps it from the side or below takes sideDamage, at most once a second.
explosive: Make an actor with health explode when it dies: every actor within explosionRadius with a clear line to it takes up to explosionDamage (less with distance), effectPath plays and soundPath sounds at the spot, and the actor is gone. An explosive the blast kills explodes in turn.
moving_platform: Make an actor a moving platform or an elevator: it travels to each of points in turn (offsets from where it starts) at speed, waits waitTime at each, and loops; a Character standing on it rides along. Its root must be movable (a Blueprint made with manage_blueprint create is).
controls: Give a Character the controls a player steers it with: WASD or the left stick walk it relative to where the controller faces, the mouse or the right stick turn the view, and the jump key jumps (held longer, higher). It makes IA_Move and IA_Look (Axis2D) and IA_Jump next to the Blueprint, maps the keys and registers the context when the character is possessed.
respawn: Make a pawn come back when it falls off the level or dies: to its start, or to where it last touched an actor tagged checkpointTag (a checkpoint), once it falls fallHeight below that point, and when it dies (back at full health) if it has the health behaviour. Respawn, SetRespawnPoint and OnRespawned are left for other logic.
goal: Make an actor the goal of a level: the first time the player touches it, OnGoalReached fires and soundPath plays there, and with nextLevel that level opens delay seconds later. It fires on overlap, so the actor needs a component that overlaps pawns (a sphere or box with the Trigger or OverlapAllDynamic profile).
launch_pad: Make an actor launch a Character that touches it: LaunchCharacter with launchVelocity, replacing its vertical speed so every bounce reaches the same height (overrideXY replaces its horizontal speed too), and soundPath plays at the pad. It fires on overlap, so the actor needs a component that overlaps pawns (a sphere or box with the Trigger or OverlapAllDynamic profile).
teleporter: Make an actor a teleporter: a pawn that touches it is moved to TeleportTarget, keeping its rotation, and soundPath plays where it arrives. Set TeleportTarget on each placed teleporter to the actor to arrive at (control_actor spawn variables, or set_blueprint_variables, with that actor name); a target that is a teleporter of the same class ignores pawns for cooldown seconds first, so a pair of pads does not send the pawn straight back. It fires on overlap, so the actor needs a component that overlaps pawns (a sphere or box with the Trigger or OverlapAllDynamic profile).
falling_platform: Make an actor a falling platform: the first pawn that lands on top of it starts it shaking, fallDelay seconds later it drops with gravity, and respawnTime seconds after the drop began it is back in place and ready again. A bump from the side or below does not set it off. The actor must block pawns, and its root must be movable (a Blueprint made with manage_blueprint create is).
countdown: Give an actor a time limit: at BeginPlay TimeLeft starts at seconds and drops by one every second; at zero OnTimeUp fires and, with killAtZero, the actor takes damage enough to die, so a pawn with the health behaviour dies and its game over or respawn follows. Show the time with behaviour counter_hud variableName TimeLeft.
spawner: Make an actor a spawner: every interval seconds, while fewer than maxAlive of the actors it spawned are alive, it spawns spawnClass at a random point up to radius across from itself, counts each until it is destroyed, and fires OnSpawned with it. A pawn class set to be possessed by AI when spawned (the chase behaviour sets that) moves on its own.
dash: Give a Character a dash: each press of the key launches it dashSpeed along where it faces, with a small lift so the dash carries before the ground slows it, at most once every cooldown seconds. The key gets an Input Action and a mapping, and the context is registered when the character is possessed.
health_hud: Show the health of a pawn on screen: while a local player controls it, a widget is on the screen with a bar filled to Health / MaxHealth, refilled whenever OnHealthChanged fires, and taken off when the pawn loses that player or is destroyed. Needs the health behaviour. With no widgetPath it makes UI/WBP_HealthBar next to the Blueprint.
counter_hud: Show a number of a pawn on screen (Coins, Score): while a local player controls it, a text at the top right reads label: value, the variable rounded to a whole number and refreshed every 0.1 seconds, taken off when the pawn loses that player or is destroyed. With no widgetPath it makes UI/WBP_<variable>Counter next to the Blueprint; each further counter sits a row lower.
hint: Show a message on the player's screen while the player is in the actor's area: when a locally controlled pawn starts to overlap the actor, a widget shows message at the bottom of that player's view, and it goes when the pawn leaves, or hideAfter seconds later. Each placed copy can say its own text (HintMessage is instance editable). It fires on overlap, so the actor needs a component that overlaps pawns (a sphere or box with the Trigger or OverlapAllDynamic profile).
game_over: Give the player a game over: when the pawn dies (health behaviour) while a local player controls it, that player input stops, a widget shows message over a dark shade, and the current level opens again restartDelay seconds later. The pawn stays when it dies, so the restart can run. With no widgetPath it makes UI/WBP_GameOver next to the Blueprint.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

compiled.description: The Blueprint compiled with the behaviour.

saved.description: The Blueprint was saved.

variables.description: The variables it uses: {name, status added, redefaulted or kept}.

dispatchers.description: Event dispatchers it added, which other logic can bind.

discovery.summary: Add a function or an event to a Blueprint; an event can be bound to a component's or a Widget Blueprint widget's delegate (OnClicked), and a function named after one the parent lets a Blueprint override (a widget's OnKeyDown) is made as that override.
whenToUse: kind=function: A new callable function must be created on the Blueprint.
kind=function: A parent function with a return value must be overridden, such as a widget's OnKeyDown to handle a key.
kind=event: An event handler node must be created in the EventGraph.
kind=event: A component event such as OnComponentBeginOverlap or OnComponentHit must be handled.
kind=event: A Widget Blueprint button, slider or other widget event such as OnClicked must be handled.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

functionName.description: Function name to add or remove.

inputs.description: Function inputs, each {name, type}, with the types add_event parameters take (Float, Vector, Actor, Array<Int> ...). A nameless entry or a type no pin takes is refused (TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED) before anything changes.

outputs.description: Function outputs (its return values), each {name, type}, with the types inputs take.

isPublic.description: Access specifier: true public (the default), false private (callable only from this Blueprint).

pure.description: Pure function (the Details panel's Pure checkbox): its call nodes have no exec pins. Default false.

posX.description: X position of the new node in the graph (default 0, the origin). add_node and create_node move a node given no position right past any node at the origin, and refuse a given spot another node covers (NODE_OVERLAP, with a suggestedPosition).

posY.description: Y position of the new node in the graph (default 0).

parameters.description: Event parameters, each {name, type}. Types: bool, byte, int, int64, float, double, string, name, text, vector, vector2d, rotator, transform, color, linearcolor, object, class, a class, struct or enum name (Actor, HitResult), Object:/Script/Engine.Actor, Struct:<path>, Enum:<path>, and Array<T>, Set<T> or Map<Key,Value>. A nameless entry or a type no pin takes is refused (TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED) before anything changes.

graphName.description: Event graph page to add the event to; omitted, the main EventGraph.

eventName.description: Custom event name; with componentName, the delegate to bind: a component's (OnComponentBeginOverlap, OnComponentHit, ...) or a widget's (OnClicked, OnHovered, OnValueChanged, ...).

componentName.description: Component whose delegate fires the event, added by the Blueprint or inherited (a Character's CapsuleComponent), or in a Widget Blueprint a widget of its tree that is a variable (every widget the widget handlers add is), e.g. PlayButton with eventName OnClicked. Makes a component-bound event (K2Node_ComponentBoundEvent) named by eventName.

kind.description:
Which add function variant to run; omit for 'function'.
function: Add a new function graph to a Blueprint with optional inputs and outputs; an existing function of that name is reused only when it matches the pure, inputs and outputs given. A name the parent class lets a Blueprint override (a widget's OnKeyDown) makes that override with its own signature, so leave inputs, outputs, pure and isPublic out.
event: Add an event node to a Blueprint event graph: built-in, custom, or bound to a component delegate (componentName plus eventName, e.g. OnComponentBeginOverlap on a BoxComponent) or to a Widget Blueprint widget's event (componentName the widget, e.g. PlayButton with OnClicked).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

functionName.description: Function name to add or remove.

nodeGuid.description: Node guid: the function's entry node, or the event node. A built-in event that already exists in the graph may be bound without one.

resultNodeGuid.description: The function's return node, present when the function has one (it is made when outputs are declared).

overrides.description: The parent function the new one overrides (UserWidget::OnKeyDown), when functionName names one.

examples.title: Add a function or an event to a Blueprint; an event can be bound to a component's or a Widget Blueprint widget's delegate (OnClicked), and a function named after one the parent lets a Blueprint override (a widget's OnKeyDown) is made as that override.

widgetKind=ammo_counter: A HUD needs a ammo counter without assembling it widget by widget.
widgetKind=crosshair: A HUD needs a crosshair without assembling it widget by widget.
widgetKind=minimap: A HUD needs a minimap without assembling it widget by widget.

widgetKind=damage_indicator: A HUD needs a damage indicator without assembling it widget by widget.

keyLabel.description: Key shown in the interaction prompt badge, such as E.

title.description: Objective tracker heading (default OBJECTIVES) or the quest name (default Quest Name).

items.description: Rows the objective or quest tracker lists, top to bottom.

slotName.description: Slot name for a child widget inside its parent.

widgets.description: Every widget created, root first; bind or restyle them by these names.

discovery.summary: Add a panel widget to a Widget Blueprint: canvas, overlay, boxes, grids, border, scroll/size/scale box, spacer, safe zone, switcher, wrap box, or a whole layout of panels, text and images with their looks in one call (widget_tree).
whenToUse: widgetKind=canvas_panel: A new canvas panel must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=overlay: A new overlay must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=vertical_box: A new vertical box must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=horizontal_box: A new horizontal box must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=grid_panel: A new grid panel must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=uniform_grid: A new uniform grid must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=wrap_box: A new wrap box must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=border: A new border must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=scroll_box: A new scroll box must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=size_box: A new size box must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=scale_box: A new scale box must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=spacer: Fixed empty space must separate sibling widgets in a box or panel.
widgetKind=safe_zone: HUD content must stay inside the title-safe area on console or TV output.
widgetKind=widget_switcher: Several pages or tabs must occupy one region with only one visible at a time.

whenNotToUse: widgetKind=canvas_panel|overlay|vertical_box|horizontal_box|grid_panel|uniform_grid|wrap_box|border|scroll_box|size_box|scale_box: A content widget (button, text, etc.) is needed instead.
widgetKind=spacer: The gap should belong to an existing widget (set its padding instead).
widgetKind=safe_zone: The layout is desktop-only and no safe-area inset applies.
widgetKind=widget_switcher: All children should be visible together (use an overlay or a box).
widgetKind=widget_tree: One widget must be added (use the matching widgetKind).
widgetKind=widget_tree: A widget already in the tree must change (use set_widget_layout).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

slotName.description: Slot name for a child widget inside its parent.

parentSlot.description: Parent slot to add the widget to.

positionX.description: Canvas slot X position, applied only when the parent is a canvas panel.

positionY.description: Canvas slot Y position, applied only when the parent is a canvas panel.

columnCount.description: Columns given an equal share of the width (0-64).

rowCount.description: Rows given an equal share of the height (0-64).

contentColorAndOpacity.description: Tint (0-1 values) a border applies to its content.

maxDesiredWidth.description: Maximum desired width of a size box.

maxDesiredHeight.description: Maximum desired height of a size box.

activeIndex.description: Index shown first by a widget switcher.

tree.description: The layout as one nested node {type, name, children[], slot{}, ...props}. type: a UMG class short name (CanvasPanel, Overlay, VerticalBox, HorizontalBox, Border, SizeBox, ScaleBox, UniformGridPanel, Spacer, TextBlock, RichTextBlock, Image, ProgressBar, Button). name: the widget name, unique in the Widget Blueprint (each becomes a variable a graph can read). Props: text, fontSize, color [r,g,b,a] (text colour, border brush, image tint, bar fill), justify left|center|right, autoWrap, opacity, visibility, padding (number or [l,t,r,b]: a border's inner padding), radius (rounded border, image or button) with outlineColor and outlineWidth, imageSize [w,h], texture (an image's texture path), material (an Image's or Border's brush: a UI material or instance that draws the whole widget, such as a rounded panel with its rim and gradient), percent (progress bar), width, height, maxHeight (size box). Text blocks also take typeface (Bold, Regular, Light, Italic), fontFamily, letterSpacing, outline with outlineColor, and shadowOffset [x,y] with shadowColor. slot places the node in its parent: in a canvas anchors [minX,minY,maxX,maxY], alignment [x,y], position [x,y], size [w,h], autoSize, z; in a box padding, hAlign (left|center|right|fill), vAlign (top|center|bottom|fill) and fill (a share of the free space). A Widget Blueprint with no root yet gets a canvas, and a tree root with no slot (and no positionX/Y or sizeX/Y) fills it. An unknown field is refused, not ignored; at most 200 widgets.

dryRun.description: Check the tree without adding a widget (default false): types, properties and slots, names the Widget Blueprint already holds (SLOT_EXISTS) and the parent panel (PARENT_NOT_FOUND). Nothing is added or saved.

border: Add a Border widget to a Widget Blueprint for framed/decorative child layout.

topics: place widgets relative to each other
discovery.summary: Place the children of a Canvas Panel by how they relate instead of by coordinates: one left of, right of, above or below another (gap: exactly that far apart, else at least 0), edges or centre lines lined up (alignLeft, alignRight, alignTop, alignBottom, alignCenterX, alignCenterY over widgets), the same width or height, a width or height, an inset from an edge of the panel, or centred in it. Each relation is required, or preferred with a strength (strong, medium, weak) and kept as far as the required ones allow (Cassowary); besides them every widget stays inside the panel and no narrower than its text (strong), and otherwise as large as it is and then where it is (weak): set in from an edge, it moves there rather than stretching. The boxes are solved at the reference resolution (default 1920x1080, the project's DPI scaling applied) and each widget's anchors follow what holds it (an inset from the right anchors it right, centred anchors it at the centre, insets from both sides stretch it, a widget tied to another follows that one), so the layout holds at other sizes; every relation is then measured again at each of resolutions (default 1920x1080, 1280x720 and 3440x1440) and the reply says where it holds. One undo step; compiled and saved; dryRun reports the boxes and anchors and changes nothing. A required relation that cannot hold with the required ones before it is UNSATISFIABLE (which one) and nothing changes; a widget not in a Canvas Panel, or in another one than the rest, is NOT_A_CANVAS.
whenToUse: Laying out a menu or HUD: a title centred near the top, buttons stacked under it with even gaps and the same width, a score 24 in from the top right corner, held there at every screen size.
whenNotToUse: One widget moved to exact coordinates (set_widget_layout position).
Children of a Vertical or Horizontal Box, which lay themselves out (set_widget_layout padding).

relations.description: How the widgets relate, each one an object; the widgets named must be children of one Canvas Panel.

widget.description: The widget the relation is about (every type but the align and same ones).

of.description: leftOf, rightOf, above, below: the widget it is placed against (widget leftOf of).

widgets.description: align and same types: the widgets lined up or sized alike.

gap.description: leftOf, rightOf, above, below: exactly this far apart, in Slate units (left out: at least 0 apart).

value.description: width, height: the size; inset: the distance from the edge; in Slate units.

edge.description: inset: the edge of the panel.

axis.description: center: across (x), up and down (y) or both (default both).

strength.description: required (default) holds exactly or the call is refused; the others are kept as far as the required ones allow, stronger first.

resolution.description: Screen size the boxes are solved at, "WxH" (default 1920x1080).

resolutions.description: Screen sizes the relations are checked at afterwards, each "WxH" up to 3840x2160 (default 1920x1080, 1280x720 and 3440x1440).

dryRun.description: Report the boxes and anchors without changing the Widget Blueprint.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

box.description: [left, top, width, height] in the panel at the reference resolution, Slate units.

anchors.description: What it holds on to, across then up and down: left, centre, right or stretch; top, middle, bottom or stretch.

relations.description: Each relation as checked at the sizes.

metAt.description: The sizes it holds at (within 1 Slate unit).

worstMiss.description: Its largest miss over the sizes, in Slate units.

saved.description: Whether the Widget Blueprint was saved.

undo.description: What editor undo takes back: {undoable, transactionScope, steps}; all the moves are one step. Absent under dryRun.

auditCall.description: The audit_widget call that checks the result at the same sizes (cut-off text, overlaps, safe area, contrast).

discovery.summary: Check a Widget Blueprint the way a UI reviewer would, at several screen sizes: it is laid out offscreen as the game creates it (as preview_widget draws it) at each of resolutions, and every visible widget is judged. Findings: off_screen (part or all of a widget past the screen edge), clipped_text (a text needing more room than its box gives, without wrapping), overlap (buttons on buttons, text on text, text across a button it is not part of; images are backdrops and not judged), unsafe (text or a button inside the margin outside the title-safe area, safeZone), small_target (with touch: a button, check box, slider or text box under 44 Slate units on its short side), low_contrast (the WCAG 2.x ratio of a text's colour to what is drawn behind it, under 4.5:1, or 3:1 for text of 18 pt or 14 pt bold; where nothing is drawn behind it, the preview's dark backdrop stands in for the game), misaligned (two neighbouring widgets whose edges miss each other by 1-4 px, unless another edge or the centre of that direction lines them up exactly). Each finding names its widget (and the other one), the sizes it shows at, its rect at the first of them and what is wrong; the most severe come first, 100 at most. Reads only.
whenToUse: After building or changing a menu or HUD: is anything cut off, on top of something else, off the screen at another size, hard to read or out of line?
whenNotToUse: Only the picture is wanted (use preview_widget).
The running game's screen, runtime texts included, must be judged (play, then inspect analyze_view).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

resolutions.description: Screen sizes to lay it out at, each "WxH" (up to 3840x2160), the project's DPI scaling applied as in the game (default 1920x1080, 1280x720 and 3440x1440).

safeZone.description: Share of each side of the screen that is title-safe (default 0.9: a 5% margin on every side); 1 turns the check off.

touch.description: The UI is touched: also flag interactive widgets under 44 Slate units on their short side (default false).

image.description: Also return the first size's picture with each finding outlined (red, orange, yellow, grey from most to least severe).

waitForShaders.description: true: when the drawing would find shaders still compiling (a material's UI shaders compile the first time it is drawn), wait for them, at most 25 seconds, before judging: until then a material draws blank and its contrast reads wrong. Default false: judge at once and report shadersCompiling.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

widget.description: The widget, by its name in the tree.

other.description: overlap and misaligned: the other widget.

rect.description: [x, y, width, height] in pixels at the first of those sizes (both widgets, for a pair).

widgetsChecked.description: Visible widgets laid out at the first size.

imageBase64.description: With image: the first size's picture with the findings outlined, PNG, base64.

shadersCompiling.description: Shader compile jobs outstanding when it was drawn: above 0, a material may have drawn blank (contrast then reads wrong); pass waitForShaders.

shaderWait.description: With waitForShaders while shaders compiled: waitedSeconds, jobsLeft and timedOut.

discovery.summary: Bind a widget property to a variable or pure function (text, color, enabled, visibility, progress bar percent or slider value; the converting getter is generated), wire an event to a function (on-clicked, hovered, value-changed; the function is created when missing), or bind localized text or a localization key.
whenToUse: bindingKind=text: A widget's text must follow a Blueprint variable or function at runtime.
bindingKind=color: A widget's color must follow a Blueprint variable or function at runtime.
bindingKind=enabled: A widget's enabled must follow a Blueprint variable or function at runtime.
bindingKind=percent: A widget's percent must follow a Blueprint variable or function at runtime.
bindingKind=visibility: A widget's visibility must follow a Blueprint variable or function at runtime.
bindingKind=on_clicked: A widget's OnClicked event must run a Blueprint function.
bindingKind=on_hovered: A button must react when the pointer moves onto or off it.
bindingKind=on_value_changed: A widget's OnValueChanged event must run a Blueprint function.
bindingKind=localized_text: Displayed text must come from a string table rather than a literal.
bindingKind=localization_key: A Text Block must carry an explicit localization key for translators.
whenNotToUse: bindingKind=text|color|enabled|percent|visibility|on_clicked|on_value_changed: The widget should be set directly rather than bound.
bindingKind=on_hovered: Only a hover sound is wanted (set_style hoverSoundPath).
bindingKind=localized_text: The text is authored inline and never localized (set it directly instead).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

slotName.description: Slot name for a child widget inside its parent.

bindingSource.description: For bind_text, bind_color, bind_enabled, bind_percent and bind_visibility: the variable (a getter converting it is generated) or pure no-input function the property reads. For bind_on_clicked and bind_on_value_changed: the function the event calls, created with the event inputs when it does not exist.

onHoveredFunction.description: Function the Button calls when the pointer moves onto it; created when it does not exist.

onUnhoveredFunction.description: Function the Button calls when the pointer leaves it; created when it does not exist.

stringTableId.description: String table asset backing a localized text binding.

stringKey.description: Key looked up within the string table.

key.description: Localization key assigned to the text widget.

bindingKind.description:
Which bind widget variant to run.
text: Bind the Text of a widget to a Blueprint variable (any type that converts to text) or pure function.
color: Bind the tint of a widget (text or image color, progress fill, border brush) to a Blueprint variable or pure function.
enabled: Bind whether a widget is enabled to a Blueprint bool variable or pure function.
percent: Bind the fill Percent of a Progress Bar (or the Value of a Slider or SpinBox) to a Blueprint float variable or pure function, so a health or loading bar follows it at runtime.
visibility: Bind the Visibility of a widget to a Blueprint variable (a bool maps true to Visible, false to Collapsed) or pure function.
on_clicked: Wire the OnClicked event of a Button to a Blueprint function (bindingSource), creating the function when missing.
on_hovered: Wire the OnHovered (and optionally OnUnhovered) event of a Button to Blueprint functions, creating them when missing.
on_value_changed: Wire the value-changed event of a Slider, SpinBox, CheckBox or ComboBoxString to a Blueprint function (bindingSource) that receives the new value; the function is created when missing.
localized_text: Point a Text Block at a string-table entry so its text follows the active localization.
localization_key: Assign the localization namespace and key a Text Block resolves its text through.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

slotName.description: The widget that was bound.

property.description: Property binds: the widget property now bound (Text, Visibility, ColorAndOpacity, bIsEnabled, ...).

functionName.description: The function now bound or called: the generated Get_<Widget>_<Property> getter, or the event handler.

generatedGetter.description: Property binds: true when a converting getter was generated for a variable.

bindings.description: Event binds: per event, its name, functionName, createdFunction, createdEvent, nodeId and callNodeId.

saved.description: Whether the Widget Blueprint was saved.

stringTableId.description: String table asset backing a localized text binding.

stringKey.description: Key looked up within the string table.

note.description: Why the binding was not applied; present only when success is false.

key.description: Localization key assigned to the text widget.

examples.title: Bind a widget property to a variable or pure function (text, color, enabled, visibility, progress bar percent or slider value; the converting getter is generated), wire an event to a function (on-clicked, hovered, value-changed; the function is created when missing), or bind localized text or a localization key.

discovery.summary: Compile a Blueprint asset, optionally saving after compile, or every Blueprint under a folder at once, answered with the ones the compiler or the graph checks flag.
whenToUse: Blueprint changes must be compiled to take effect.
A project or a folder must be audited for compile errors and graph-check warnings (after an engine upgrade, before a release): folder compiles every Blueprint under it in one call.
whenNotToUse: The Blueprint has no pending changes.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

discovery.summary: Create a Blueprint asset, chosen by createMode (ensure checks first), named name in savePath (default /Game) and save it (saved). parentClass is a native class as /Script/Module.Class or a short name (Actor, Pawn, Character, PlayerController), or a Blueprint class path ending in _C; blueprintType Actor, Pawn, Character or FunctionLibrary stands in for a missing parentClass, and Interface without one makes a Blueprint Interface. A parent that resolves to nothing is CLASS_NOT_FOUND, naming classes of that name. properties sets class defaults, Component.Property and struct members by dotted path, reported as appliedProperties and failedProperties (the create stands either way). A Blueprint already at the path is answered with alreadyExists and left unchanged; one with another parent class is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS.
whenToUse: createMode=create: A new Blueprint of a known parent class is needed.
createMode=create: A pickup or hazard is needed; its parts come from edit_scs, its logic from add_behaviour.
createMode=blueprint: A Blueprint must be created with a specific type hint.
createMode=ensure: Idempotent setup requires a Blueprint to exist without failing on duplicates.
whenNotToUse: createMode=create: An existing Blueprint should be opened or modified instead.
createMode=ensure: A fresh Blueprint is always required even if one exists.

properties.description: Property bag applied to the CDO, component template, or node: name to value. An object or class reference takes a path (a Blueprint class path ends in _C); null or "None" clears it.

blueprintType.description: Picks the parent class when parentClass is absent: Actor, Pawn, Character or FunctionLibrary; Interface makes a Blueprint Interface (its functions with add_function, taken on with implement_interface).

createIfMissing.description: Create the Blueprint when savePath/name does not exist (default true); false only reports whether it exists.

createMode.description:
Which create variant to run; omit for 'create'.
create: Create a Blueprint asset named name in savePath (default /Game) and save it (saved). parentClass is a native class as /Script/Module.Class or a short name (Actor, Pawn, Character, PlayerController), or a Blueprint class path ending in _C; blueprintType Actor, Pawn, Character or FunctionLibrary stands in for a missing parentClass, and Interface without one makes a Blueprint Interface. blueprint: Same as create: a Blueprint named name in savePath from parentClass, or from blueprintType when parentClass is left out.
ensure: Make sure a Blueprint of parentClass is at savePath/name: one already there is answered with alreadyExists and left unchanged (another parent class is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS); otherwise it is created as create does, unless createIfMissing is false, which only reports whether it exists.

appliedProperties.description: The properties names set on the class defaults; a subobject property reads Holder.Property.

failedProperties.description: Each properties name that was not set, as "Name: reason"; the Blueprint is created anyway.

saved.description: Whether the new Blueprint reached disk.

alreadyExists.description: True when a Blueprint of that parent class was already at the path; it is answered unchanged.

parentClass.description: Path of the Blueprint's parent class.

discovery.summary: Create a new Widget Blueprint holding a ready-made screen: main menu, pause menu, settings menu, loading screen, HUD, dialog box, inventory, radial menu, credits or shop.
whenToUse: screen=main_menu: A game needs a main menu and none exists yet.
screen=pause_menu: A game needs a pause menu and none exists yet.
screen=settings_menu: A game needs a settings menu and none exists yet.
screen=loading_screen: A game needs a loading screen and none exists yet.

screen=dialog: A game needs a dialog widget and none exists yet.

path.description: Destination /Game folder for a new Widget Blueprint.

buttons.description: Button labels, top to bottom: a menu's buttons, or a dialog's responses (at most 6, in place of responseCount); each becomes <Label>Button.

settingsType.description: Which settings sections the menu holds (default all).

includeProgressBar.description: Whether the loading screen has a progress bar (default true).

fadeTime.description: Seconds of the fade: the damage flash (default 0.6) or the loading screen FadeIn animation (0 makes none).

elements.description: HUD pieces the new HUD starts with (default health_bar, crosshair, ammo_counter; [] for an empty canvas).

showSpeakerName.description: Whether the dialog shows the speaker name line (default true).

responseCount.description: Placeholder response buttons under the dialog line when buttons names none (0-6, default 3).

title.description: Role or section, such as Music.

name.description: Name credited.

entries.description: Credits entries in order; default is four placeholder sections.

itemCount.description: Placeholder shop item cards when items names none (1-48, default 8).

name.description: Item name shown on its card.

items.description: Shop items in order (1-48, in place of itemCount): each card shows its name and price, and its button is Item_<n>_Buy, n counting from 1.

currency.description: Currency name in the shop header, shown as "<currency>: 0" (default Gold).

screen.description:
Which create widget template variant to run.
main_menu: Create a main menu Widget Blueprint: backdrop, title and a column of buttons (default Play, Settings, Quit).
pause_menu: Create a pause menu Widget Blueprint: dimmed backdrop, PAUSED title and buttons (default Resume, Settings, Main Menu).
settings_menu: Create a settings menu Widget Blueprint: graphics, audio and controls rows with real combo boxes, check boxes and sliders, plus Apply and Back.
loading_screen: Create a loading screen Widget Blueprint: backdrop, Loading text, optional progress bar and optional FadeIn animation.
hud: Create a HUD Widget Blueprint on a canvas holding ready-made pieces (default health bar, crosshair, ammo counter).
dialog: Create a dialog box Widget Blueprint: speaker name, wrapped dialog line, response buttons and a continue hint.
inventory: Create an inventory Widget Blueprint: titled panel with a grid of item slots (default 6 by 4).
radial_menu: Create a radial menu Widget Blueprint: a ring of round buttons around a centre label (default 8 segments).
credits: Create a credits Widget Blueprint: centred scrolling list of role and name pairs with a Back button.
shop: Create a shop Widget Blueprint: header with currency, a scrolling grid of item cards each with a Buy button, and Close.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

buttons.description: Every Button created; wire them with bind_widget on_clicked.

animationName.description: Animation created with the screen (the loading screen FadeIn, the HUD damage flash).

compiled.description: Whether the new Widget Blueprint compiled.

saved.description: Whether the new Widget Blueprint was saved.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

discovery.summary: Delete Blueprint graph nodes (deleteScope node, the default), or disconnect every wire of one pin (pin_links). node deletes nodeId, or every node in nodeIds (up to 500), all or nothing: an id that matches no node is NODE_NOT_FOUND and a function entry or result node is PROTECTED_NODE, with nothing deleted; their wires go with them, and the reply lists the removed guids. pin_links breaks the links of pinName on nodeId (PIN_NOT_FOUND lists the pins the node has) and names the pins it was wired to under disconnectedFrom; a pin with no links changes nothing. Either is one undo step, then the Blueprint compiles (diagnostics when it no longer compiles) and is saved. A pinName sent with deleteScope node is refused (CONTRADICTORY_SCOPE) rather than deleting the whole node.
whenToUse: deleteScope=node: A graph node must be permanently removed.
deleteScope=node: A whole dead chain of nodes must be removed in one call.
deleteScope=pin_links: All links from a specific pin must be removed (disconnect or unlink a wire).
whenNotToUse: deleteScope=node: The node should be moved rather than deleted.
deleteScope=pin_links: A single link should be redirected (use connect_pins after breaking).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

graphName.description: Target graph name (Event Graph, Construction Script, etc.).

nodeId.description: Id of an existing node: the nodeGuid edit_graph returned when it made the node, or a nodeId inspect_graph lists.

nodeGuid.description: Node GUID accepted in place of nodeId.

nodeIds.description: Several node ids or guids to delete in one call, in place of nodeId. Every id must resolve to a deletable node or nothing is deleted.

pinName.description: Pin name on a graph node.

deleteScope.description:
Which delete node variant to run; omit for 'node'.
node: Delete a node from a Blueprint graph by its nodeGuid, or many nodes at once with nodeIds (one consent, one compile, all or nothing).
pin_links: Break (disconnect) every link of one pin on a graph node, leaving the pin unwired.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

removed.description: Guids of the nodes that were deleted.

brokenLinks.description: How many wires of the pin were broken (0 when it had none, and nothing changed).

disconnectedFrom.description: The pins it was wired to, each as nodeGuid.pinName.

Every widget under it is copied as <its own name>_Copy, made unique the same way: copying QuitButton gives QuitButton_Copy and its label QuitButtonText_Copy. copiedWidgets lists the pairs.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

slotName.description: Name of the copy, for later calls.

index.description: Where the copy sits among the children of that panel (0 = first).

discovery.summary: Write Blueprint logic of any kind, or edit a graph: add or create nodes (including reroute and struct make/break nodes), connect pins, set node properties and pin defaults, add a construction script, arrange nodes beside what they are wired to, or run many of those edits, variables included, in one batch.
whenToUse: edit=add_node: A node must be added using a friendly type alias (e.g. Branch, Cast, GetVariable).
edit=create_node: A new node must be placed in a Blueprint event or function graph.
edit=create_node: An animation node (Two Bone IK, Modify Bone, Blend Space Player, Look At ...) must be placed by class in an Animation Blueprint's AnimGraph or a state's graph.
edit=create_reroute_node: Wire paths need a reroute node for cleaner layout.
edit=create_struct_make_break_nodes: A MakeStruct or BreakStruct node must be placed for a known struct type.
edit=connect_pins: An exec or data link between two existing nodes must be created.
edit=set_node_property: A node-level property (e.g. comment, position) must be updated.
edit=set_pin_default_value: A pin's default literal value must be set when it has no incoming link.
edit=set_pin_default_value: A read-only text, string, name or number pin (TextRender Set Text's Value) needs a literal.
edit=add_construction_script: The Construction Script graph must be created or opened for editing.
edit=arrange_nodes: Nodes of a chain sit far from each other or from the event they hang off, and should be laid out beside what they are wired to.
edit=batch: More than a couple of nodes or links must be added to one Blueprint graph.
edit=batch: A new function and the nodes inside it must be built in one call.
edit=batch: A long batch should be checked before it runs (dryRun: every problem at once, nothing changed).
whenNotToUse: edit=connect_pins: Links must be broken (use break_pin_links).
edit=arrange_nodes: Every listed node is wired only to other listed nodes: nothing anchors them, so none moves; leave the head of the chain (its event) out of nodeIds.
edit=batch: Nodes or links must be deleted (use delete_node; destructive edits are not batched).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

graphName.description: Target graph name (Event Graph, Construction Script, etc.).

nodeType.description: The node to create: CallFunction (memberName, plus memberClass for a function of another class), Event (eventName: BeginPlay, Tick), CustomEvent (customEventName), VariableGet or VariableSet (memberName), Cast (targetClass), InputAxisEvent (inputAxisName), Branch, Sequence, Select, Switch, SwitchOnInt, SwitchOnEnum (enumPath: one exec output per value, named after it), SwitchOnString, DoOnce, DoN, FlipFlop, Gate, MultiGate, ForLoop, ForEachLoop, WhileLoop (each also WithBreak), MakeArray, GetArrayItem (an array's Get: pins Array, Dimension 1 for the index, Output), MakeStruct and BreakStruct (structPath), SpawnActorFromClass, GetAllActorsOfClass, Self, CallDelegate (memberName: an event dispatcher, memberClass: another class's), BindEvent (the same, plus eventName: a Bind Event node and a custom event with the dispatcher's inputs wired to it, eventNodeGuid in the reply),Timeline (timelineName; edit_timeline keys its tracks), Reroute, Comment, MathExpression (its formula goes in set_node_property Expression) (a Switch on Int is made with only Default: wire a case by its number, from "$id.0", "$id.1"..., and the case pin is added; a Sequence or a commutative math node grows its inputs the same way); a common function by name (PrintString, Delay, SetActorLocation, GetPlayerPawn, GetActorOfClass, IsValid, PlaySound2D; IsValid is the pure function, K2Node_IsValid the Is Valid macro with exec pins exec, InputObject, Is Valid and Is Not Valid); or a K2Node class name that inspect_graph info=node_types lists. In an Animation Blueprint's AnimGraph or a state's graph (graphName), any animation node by class: AnimGraphNode_TwoBoneIK, TwoBoneIK or Two Bone IK (info=node_types with filter IK lists them; animation_physics configure_anim_graph_node set_value sets its settings); a node the graph cannot hold is refused (NODE_NOT_ALLOWED_IN_GRAPH). For create_struct_make_break_nodes: make or break.

posX.description: X position of the new node in the graph (default 0, the origin). add_node and create_node move a node given no position right past any node at the origin, and refuse a given spot another node covers (NODE_OVERLAP, with a suggestedPosition).

posY.description: Y position of the new node in the graph (default 0).

memberName.description: The function, variable or event the node uses (PrintString, GetGameTimeInSeconds). A function whose name is not known: inspect_graph info functions finds it by what it does. A variable Blueprints cannot read, or for VariableSet write (not Blueprint-visible, read-only), is refused with VARIABLE_NOT_ACCESSIBLE.

functionName.description: Function a CallFunction node calls (the same as memberName), e.g. PrintString.

targetClass.description: Target class for a node that carries one: a Cast target, a CreateWidget or SpawnActor class, the subsystem a Get Subsystem node returns, or the class GetAllActorsOfClass and GetActorOfClass look for (their result is then typed to it, so a ForEach element wires to its functions). Required for cast and subsystem nodes, whose type is stored on the node itself and cannot be set afterwards.

timelineName.description: For nodeType Timeline: the timeline it plays, which edit_timeline keys; a name the Blueprint lacks makes one (omitted, a new Timeline_N). One node plays a timeline, in the event graph of an Actor Blueprint.

menuId.description: In place of nodeType: any node by its action-menu id, Category|Title with spaces removed, as read_graph_as_code prints it (Development|PrintString, Utilities|FlowControl|Branch, Variables|GetHealth, Utilities|Operators|Add); AddEvent|Custom|Name makes a custom event named Name. An id this graph's menu does not offer is refused (MENU_ID_NOT_FOUND) with the ids it offers for that title.

pure.description: Build a Cast node pure (no exec pins, as in the editor's Convert to pure cast); default false.

memberClass.description: The class that declares the function (KismetMathLibrary, Character, or a Blueprint path); inspect_graph info functions names it. Omitted: the Blueprint itself and the common libraries are searched.

actorName.description: For nodeType K2Node_ActorBoundEvent or K2Node_Literal, which belong in a level Blueprint: the placed actor of its level (label, name or object path) the event fires for, with eventName one of its event dispatchers (OnActorBeginOverlap), or the node references. Without it, or outside a level Blueprint, the node is refused.

inputAxisName.description: Axis name for an InputAxis event node.

inputActionPath.description: Enhanced Input action asset path for an EnhancedInputAction node.

inputActionAssetPath.description: Enhanced Input action asset path accepted in place of inputActionPath.

actionPath.description: Enhanced Input action asset path accepted in place of inputActionPath.

structPath.description: For MakeStruct or BreakStruct: the struct, a Blueprint Struct asset (/Game/Data/F_Item) or a native one (/Script/SlateCore.SlateColor, /Script/CoreUObject.Vector); without it the node is refused.

enumPath.description: For SwitchOnEnum, ForEachElementInEnum, GetNumEnumEntries, EnumLiteral and CastByteToEnum: the enum whose values become the node's pins (a Switch on Enum's outputs are named after them), a Blueprint enum asset (/Game/Data/E_Phase) or a native one (/Script/Engine.ECollisionChannel); without it the node is refused.

parameters.description: CustomEvent inputs, each {name, type}: float, double, int, int64, bool, byte, string, name, text, object, class, softobject, an enum or struct name (Vector, Rotator, Transform, /Script/CoreUObject.Vector) or a class name (Actor) for an object of that class. An array, set or map parameter needs add_event. A nameless entry or another type is refused (TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED) before anything changes.

fromNodeId.description: Node the wire leaves (its nodeGuid, an 8+ hex prefix of it, or its node name); required, or send sourceNode.

fromPinName.description: Output pin it leaves from; required, or send sourcePin.

toNodeId.description: Node the wire enters; required, or send targetNode.

toPinName.description: Input pin it enters; required, or send targetPin.

sourceNode.description: Source node id accepted in place of fromNodeId.

targetNode.description: Target node id accepted in place of toNodeId.

sourcePin.description: Output pin name accepted in place of fromPinName.

targetPin.description: Input pin name accepted in place of toPinName.

nodeId.description: Id of an existing node: the nodeGuid edit_graph returned when it made the node, or a nodeId inspect_graph lists.

propertyName.description: Property name to set on the CDO or component.

nodeGuid.description: Node GUID accepted in place of nodeId.

propertyValue.description: set_node_property: text for NodeComment, a number for NodePosX or NodePosY, true or false for bCommentBubbleVisible or bDisabled, Enabled, Disabled or DevelopmentOnly for EnabledState, the text of a Math Expression node's Expression (each other name becomes a number input pin, except one the Blueprint has a variable of, which reads that variable; a number input is never a vector, so add to a location as VECT(x, y, z + 20) from its parts; a comparison used as a number is refused: write SelectFloat(1, 0, A > B); an input pin is never true/false, so join true/false values from other nodes with BooleanAND, BooleanOR or BooleanXOR nodes), an asset path for a reflected field. set_pin_default_value: the pin's new default as text: a number, true or false, an enum value name, a vector as X,Y,Z (0,150,110), a rotator as P,Y,R, or an asset path.

pinName.description: Pin name on a graph node.

nodeIds.description: The nodes to move, by nodeId or nodeGuid. Nodes left out stay where they are and anchor the ones listed; a node wired to nothing left in place goes back where it was and is listed under unmoved.

layout.description: beside (default): each listed node to the nearest free slot beside a node left in place that it is wired to. layered: the listed nodes in columns along the links among them, left to right as the flow runs, a pure value in the column before its first reader, crossings reduced; the first listed node stays where it is and nodes left out are ignored (for a whole event, list the event first, then its nodes).

operations.description: Steps run in order, 1-200. Each is {edit, ...that edit's own params}. Member steps come before the nodes that use them: add_variable (variableName, variableType as add_variable takes it: basic, class, struct, enum and container types, defaultValue, isPublic, exposeOnSpawn, category), add_function (functionName, inputs, outputs, pure, isPublic; the create steps of its body set graphName to the function name, and a connect or pin step that leaves graphName out runs in the graph of the node it names; with an id, "$id" is its entry node and "$id_return" its return node, which exists when outputs are declared), add_event (customEventName and parameters, or componentName plus eventName for a component or Widget Blueprint widget delegate, e.g. PlayButton with OnClicked) and add_event_dispatcher (dispatcherName, parameters [{name, type}]). Node steps: create_node, connect_pins, set_pin_default_value, set_node_property, create_reroute_node. create_node also takes nodeType CallDelegate (memberName: a dispatcher, memberClass: another class's), BindEvent (the same: a Bind Event node and a custom event, eventName, wired to it; with an id, "$id_event" is that event, whose then pin runs when the dispatcher fires, and the object bound goes to "$id.self"), Message (memberClass: an interface, memberName: its function), AsyncTask (memberClass: the task or async-action class, memberName: its static factory; event graphs only), FunctionResult (one more return node in a function graph) and MathExpression with expression (the formula, checked and set as set_node_property Expression sets it, before pinDefaults, which can then name its inputs; a name in the formula that is one of the Blueprint's variables reads that variable and gets no input pin, any other name becomes an input pin). Optional per step: id (names the created node; later steps use "$id" in fromNodeId, toNodeId and nodeId), from and to ("$id.PinName" shorthand for connect_pins), pinDefaults (create_node only: {PinName: value} applied to the new node; a read-only pin such as Set Text's Value gets a MakeLiteral node wired into it). "$entry" is the graph's own entry node (a Construction Script or function graph starts there: from "$entry.then"). A pure node (math, a getter) runs again for each node that reads it, so after a Set node read the new value from the Set node's Output_Get pin, not from the math that computed it. A create step without posX and posY is auto-placed, and once every step ran it moves beside a node it is wired to (right of what runs it, below-left of what reads it); one whose posX and posY overlap an existing node is placed at the nearest free position instead, and its result says where in placementWarning, so a crowded row never stops the batch (a single create_node call still refuses an overlap). Every function, variable, dispatcher and async factory a step names is checked before any step runs, so a misspelled one fails the batch with nothing applied; any other failure stops the batch at that step and undoes the steps before it (members, nodes, links and pin defaults, in every graph), so a failed batch leaves the Blueprint as it was: fix that step and send the whole batch again. Only a set_node_property on a node that was already there stays, and the error names it.

dryRun.description: Check the batch without running any step (default false): the members, functions, variables and expressions the steps name, every "$id" against the ids of the steps before it, and every node named by guid. Every problem comes back at once in problems, and the reply fails with the first one's code; the pins of the nodes the batch would create are checked only when it runs. Nothing is changed, compiled or saved.

edit.description:
Which edit graph variant to run.
add_node: Add a node to a Blueprint graph (alias of edit=create_node with simplified type resolution).
create_node: Create a graph node (function call, event, variable, branch, etc.) in a Blueprint graph.
create_reroute_node: Create a reroute node for organizing exec/data wire paths in a Blueprint graph.
create_struct_make_break_nodes: Create a Make or Break Struct node in a Blueprint graph from a UserDefinedStruct or native UScriptStruct.
connect_pins: Connect two graph pins (exec or data) by nodeGuid and pin name. A pin the editor adds on demand is added: a Sequence's then_2, a Make Array's [2], a Switch on Int's case 7 (a new switch has only Default).
set_node_property: Set a property on a graph node by nodeGuid.
set_pin_default_value: Set the default value of a data pin on a graph node; a read-only (const reference) pin gets it through a MakeLiteral node wired into it.
add_construction_script: Add or open the Construction Script graph for a Blueprint.
arrange_nodes: Tidy a graph: move the listed nodes beside the nodes they are wired to (right of what runs them, below-left of what reads them), each to the nearest free slot; the nodes left out stay put and anchor them. layout layered instead lays the listed nodes out in columns along their links (a layered, Sugiyama-style layout), the first listed staying where it is. An unknown nodeId is refused before anything moves. The Blueprint then compiles and is saved; that compile clears the editor's undo history whenever the history holds the Blueprint (undoBufferReset, and undo.undoable false with UNDO_CLEARED_BY_COMPILE), so the move usually cannot be undone: run edit=arrange_nodes again or set positions back with edit=set_node_property.
batch: Run many graph edits in one call: add variables, functions (with their bodies), events and event dispatchers, create nodes, connect pins, set pin defaults and node properties, with $id references between steps. dryRun checks a batch without running any step.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

nodeGuid.description: Unique node identifier for subsequent graph operations.

graphName.description: Target graph name (Event Graph, Construction Script, etc.).

timelineName.description: For a Timeline node: the timeline it plays, the name edit_timeline takes.

posX.description: X coordinate the node was placed at.

posY.description: Y coordinate the node was placed at.

estimatedWidth.description: Approximate node width. Slate computes the real size at draw time, so this is derived from title length and is an estimate, not a measurement.

estimatedHeight.description: Approximate node height, derived from pin-row count. Offset the next node by at least this much to avoid overlap.

overlappingNodes.description: Titles of existing nodes whose estimated bounds intersect this one. Empty or absent when placement is clear.

placementWarning.description: Human-readable overlap warning, present only when overlappingNodes is non-empty.

pinTypes.description: Per-pin objects: { name, direction, type, category, subCategory }.

compilerStatus.description: Blueprint status after compile (UpToDate, UpToDateWithWarnings, Error, Dirty, BeingCreated).

compiled.description: True when the Blueprint is up-to-date (warnings allowed).

assetPath.description: Asset path of the created node (verification).

existsAfter.description: Whether the node exists after creation (verification).

connected.description: Whether the two pins are linked after the call, directly or through the conversion node the engine inserted between differing pin types (conversionInserted), read back from the graph rather than inferred from the schema call.

sourcePinName.description: Source pin that was actually used — the first output pin when fromPinName named none.

targetPinName.description: Target pin that was actually used.

sourcePinType.description: Pin category of the source pin (exec, object, real, ...).

targetPinType.description: Pin category of the target pin.

blueprintPath.description: Normalized blueprint path the link was written to.

saved.description: Whether the blueprint asset was saved after the link was made.

replacedLinks.description: Links the new one replaced, each {nodeId, nodeTitle, pinName}: a pin that holds one link (an exec output, a data input) drops its old link to take the new one. Absent when nothing was replaced.

inputPins.description: Expression: the input pins the parsed expression made, the names to wire.

boundToMembers.description: Expression: names that read the Blueprint's own variable of that name instead of making a pin; rename the input to get a pin.

nodeId.description: Id of an existing node: the nodeGuid edit_graph returned when it made the node, or a nodeId inspect_graph lists.

pinName.description: Pin name on a graph node.

appliedValue.description: Literal actually stored on the pin (or the resolved object path for object/class pins).

literalNodeId.description: Guid of the MakeLiteral node carrying the value when the pin itself takes no literal; setting the pin again updates that node.

moved.description: Each node that moved: nodeId, nodeTitle and its new x and y.

unmoved.description: Ids of listed nodes that stayed where they were: wired to no node left in place, or no free slot near one.

alreadyInPlace.description: Ids of listed nodes already beside what they are wired to: nothing moved them, so there is nothing to undo for them.

results.description: Per-step outcome: index, edit, id, success, error, nodeGuid, resultNodeGuid (add_function), pins (for created nodes), connected, appliedValue, placementWarning (a create step that was moved off an overlapping position, or placed where it still overlaps), inputPins and boundToMembers (a Math Expression's Expression step: the pins it made, and the names that read member variables instead). A step that ran and has nothing more to say (a plain connect_pins, an add_variable) is counted in succeeded, not listed; a failed batch lists only the step that failed, with its error.

nodeIds.description: Step id -> node guid for every node the batch created or reused; an add_function step with an id also adds "<id>_return" for its return node. Absent when a step failed: its nodes were removed.

succeeded.description: Steps that completed; 0 when a step failed, since the steps before it were undone.

failedIndex.description: Index of the step that stopped the batch (failures only).

dryRun.description: True when nothing ran (dryRun).

wouldCreate.description: dryRun: the nodes the batch would create.

problems.description: dryRun: every step that would fail a check, each with index, edit, errorCode and error.

examples.title: Write Blueprint logic of any kind, or edit a graph: add or create nodes (including reroute and struct make/break nodes), connect pins, set node properties and pin defaults, add a construction script, arrange nodes beside what they are wired to, or run many of those edits, variables included, in one batch.
