discovery.summary: Change the components a Blueprint adds (its Simple Construction Script), chosen by edit; each edit saves the Blueprint unless save is false. add_scs_component (add_component is the same) adds componentName of componentClass under parentComponent (its own part, a parent Blueprint's, or the native root; by default the root), with meshPath and materialPath (refused when they do not load or the class shows no mesh or material), location, rotation, scale and properties, and compiles; a taken name is refused, as is an add during Play. modify applies operations in order (add, modify, attach) or edits one component, naming each failed one in warnings (the call fails when none applied), and compiles only with compile or applyAndSave true; reparent moves a component under another; set_property and set_transform change one template and compile, and placed copies that kept the old value follow (instancesUpdated).
whenToUse: edit=add_scs_component: A component template must be owned by the SCS tree for instanced property overrides.
edit=add_component: A component must be added to a Blueprint under the add_component verb.
edit=modify: An SCS-owned component template needs property or transform updates.
edit=reparent: An SCS component must move under a different parent node.
edit=set_property: One property on an SCS component template must be changed.

edit=set_property: Collision of the template, for every placed copy: CollisionProfileName (a preset such as OverlapAllDynamic), CollisionEnabled, or CollisionResponses ({"Pawn": "Ignore"} lets a character walk through) go through the component setters, as does PhysMaterialOverride (a physical material path).
edit=set_transform: An SCS component template transform must be updated.
whenNotToUse: edit=add_scs_component: One placed actor needs the component, not every copy of the Blueprint (use control_actor.edit_component with edit=add).
edit=reparent: The component hierarchy does not need restructuring.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

componentClass.description: Component class path for SCS node creation.

componentName.description: Name for the SCS component node.

parentComponent.description: Parent component to put the component under: one of this Blueprint's own, a parent Blueprint's scene component, or a native one (Mesh, CapsuleComponent).

attachTo.description: Socket or parent component to attach to: one of this Blueprint's own, a parent Blueprint's part, or a native one (Mesh, CapsuleComponent).

meshPath.description: Static/Skeletal mesh asset path for a mesh component.

materialPath.description: Material asset path for a component.

location.description: Relative location {x, y, z} for an SCS component template.

rotation.description: Relative rotation {pitch, yaw, roll} for an SCS component template.

scale.description: Relative scale {x, y, z} for an SCS component template, or {x, y} for a widget render transform.

properties.description: Property bag applied to the CDO, component template, or node: name to value. A dotted name reaches a member of a component or struct (CapsuleComponent.CapsuleRadius, BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled); on a Blueprint's class defaults a native component also answers to its object name (CollisionCylinder.CapsuleRadius, CharMoveComp.MaxWalkSpeed). An object or class reference takes a path (a Blueprint class path ends in _C); null or "None" clears it.

save.description: Save the Blueprint after the edit (default true, so it survives an editor restart). false leaves it compiled in memory and unsaved: a trial change to put back, or to save later with control_editor save_all.

compile.description: Compile the Blueprint after the operations (default false; applyAndSave also compiles).

operations.description: SCS operations applied in order. Each entry is an object with `type` plus that operation's own fields; `type: "add_component"` also takes componentName, componentClass (or componentType), attachTo, transform, meshPath, materialPath and a nested properties bag; `type: "modify_component"` takes the same transform, meshPath, materialPath and properties for a component that already exists (its own, or a parent Blueprint's part, edited through this Blueprint's override of it); transform is {location:{x,y,z}, rotation:{pitch,yaw,roll}, scale:{x,y,z}} (or those three directly on the operation), and a part left out keeps its current value, while a transform that cannot be applied (a part that is not an {x,y,z} or {pitch,yaw,roll} object or a three-number array, or a component with no transform) is named in warnings, not skipped, as is a meshPath or materialPath that does not load or that its component cannot take; `type: "attach_component"` (or "reparent") moves componentName under parentComponent (or attachTo/newParent). A failed operation is named in warnings, and the call fails when none applied. Each result carries instancesUpdated (placed copies that took the change, 0 included) with up to three of their paths, and a hint, repeated in warnings, when a mesh or material lands on a hidden component.

applyAndSave.description: Whether to save the Blueprint after applying SCS changes.

propertyName.description: Property name to set on the CDO or component.

propertyValue.description: Value to assign to the property. An object or class reference takes a path (a Blueprint class path ends in _C); null or "None" clears it.

edit.description:
Which edit scs variant to run.
add_scs_component: Add a component named componentName of componentClass (a component class name such as StaticMeshComponent, or its /Script path) to a Blueprint, under parentComponent (attachTo): its own part, a parent Blueprint's, or the native root, by default the root. meshPath and materialPath give a mesh component its mesh and first material and are refused, adding nothing, when they do not load or the class shows none; location, rotation, scale and properties set the template, and a property that does not take fails the call. A taken name is refused. The Blueprint compiles and saves unless save is false (compiled, saved); the reply names the parent the component got, and mesh_applied and material_applied.
add_component: Add a component to a Blueprint (the same SCS template edit=add_scs_component adds), optionally attached, placed, meshed and configured.
modify: Modify an existing SCS component template node (properties or transform).
reparent: Reparent an SCS component node to a new parent node in the SCS tree.
set_property: Set a single property on an SCS-owned component template; placed actors that still had the old value take the new one (instancesUpdated), one changed by hand keeps its own. For RelativeScale3D/RelativeLocation, note that a child inherits its parent's scale: Unreal multiplies parent and child scale COMPONENT-WISE in the child's own local axes, and rotation does NOT permute which axis each factor lands on. World size = ParentScale * ChildScale * MeshExtent per local axis, and world offset = ParentScale * RelativeLocation. Under a parent scaled non-uniformly, divide the offset you want by the parent scale on that axis.
set_transform: Set the transform (location, rotation, scale) of an SCS-owned component template. Placed actors that still had the old transform take the new one (instancesUpdated); an actor whose component was changed by hand keeps its own. instancesUpdated counts copies in loaded levels only: a copy in a level that is not loaded keeps the transform saved with it, so move it with control_actor.edit_component once its level is open.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

componentName.description: Name for the SCS component node.

componentClass.description: Component class path for SCS node creation.

parent.description: Parent component to put the component under: one of this Blueprint's own, a parent Blueprint's scene component, or a native one (Mesh, CapsuleComponent).

saved.description: Whether the action succeeded.

appliedProperties.description: The names in properties that took their value; one that did not apply fails the call and is named in the error.

partWarnings.description: Mesh parts this edit left sunk or buried, worst first (at most 8, each also a warnings[] sentence): componentName, kind (sunk: below the actor's ground, a Character's capsule bottom; buried: inside otherComponent), depth in cm, insideShare (0-1, how much of the part's surface is inside the other) and issue. Measured on the real triangles of a preview instance, not on bounds. A part tagged mcp.placement.ok (set ComponentTags to ["mcp.placement.ok"]) is a deliberate embed, such as an eyeball in its socket, and is left out; mcp.placement.ok:<component> accepts the embed in that one part only (a neck in its collar, a hand round a handle) and keeps every other check. control_actor.audit_placement with blueprintPath lists every part of the Blueprint.

verifiedValue.description: Value to assign to the property. An object or class reference takes a path (a Blueprint class path ends in _C); null or "None" clears it.

examples.title: Change the components a Blueprint adds (its Simple Construction Script), chosen by edit; each edit saves the Blueprint unless save is false. add_scs_component (add_component is the same) adds componentName of componentClass under parentComponent (its own part, a parent Blueprint's, or the native root; by default the root), with meshPath and materialPath (refused when they do not load or the class shows no mesh or material), location, rotation, scale and properties, and compiles; a taken name is refused, as is an add during Play. modify applies operations in order (add, modify, attach) or edits one component, naming each failed one in warnings (the call fails when none applied), and compiles only with compile or applyAndSave true; reparent moves a component under another; set_property and set_transform change one template and compile, and placed copies that kept the old value follow (instancesUpdated).

discovery.summary: Make or change a Blueprint timeline, what a Timeline node plays: its length, autoplay and loop, and its float, vector, color and event tracks with their keys. The Timeline node gets a pin per track, and its Update pin fires every frame while it plays.
whenToUse: Something must change smoothly over a set time from a Blueprint (a door swinging open, a platform sliding, a light fading): key a float track from 0 to 1 and feed it to a Lerp on the Timeline node's Update.
whenNotToUse: A cinematic or a camera move is needed (use a level sequence).
A widget must animate (use edit_widget_animation).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

timelineName.description: The timeline, as its node is titled. A name the Blueprint lacks makes one; the node that plays it comes from edit_graph create_node nodeType Timeline with this timelineName, made before or after (either way it shows a pin per track).

length.description: How long it plays, in seconds (a new timeline: 5).

useLastKeyframe.description: End at the last key instead of at length.

autoPlay.description: Start when the game starts, without a Play call.

loop.description: Start over at the end, again and again.

ignoreTimeDilation.description: Play at real speed while the game is slowed down or sped up.

tracks.description: Tracks to add, or whose keys to replace (a track keeps its type): each {name, type, keys, interpolation}. name is the node pin its value comes out of; type float (default), vector, color or event (an exec pin that fires at each key time); keys [{time in seconds, value}], value a number, {x, y, z} or {r, g, b, a} by type and none for an event; interpolation auto (smooth, default), linear or constant. Every track is checked before anything changes; a bad one is named by its index (tracks[1].keys[0]).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

created.description: True when this call made the timeline.

useLastKeyframe.description: Whether it ends at its last key.

autoPlay.description: Whether it starts on its own.

tracks.description: Every track: name (its node pin), type and keys (the key count).

nodeGuid.description: The Timeline node that plays it; absent until one is made.

examples.title: Make or change a Blueprint timeline, what a Timeline node plays: its length, autoplay and loop, and its float, vector, color and event tracks with their keys. The Timeline node gets a pin per track, and its Update pin fires every frame while it plays.

discovery.summary: Change a Blueprint's variables, chosen by edit. add_variable adds variableName of variableType with defaultValue, category and the isPublic, isReplicated and exposeOnSpawn flags (a taken name is VARIABLE_NAME_CONFLICT, a type that resolves to nothing TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED, a default the type refuses DEFAULT_NOT_APPLIED; nothing is added then); rename_variable renames a variable or a component and its graph nodes follow; set_variable_metadata sets a variable's tooltip, category or replication; set_metadata sets metadata pairs on the class or one variable; set_default writes a class default value, an inherited property included.
whenToUse: edit=add_variable: A Blueprint needs a new member variable with a type and default.
edit=rename_variable: A member variable needs a new name.
edit=rename_variable: A component (Simple Construction Script node) needs a new name.
edit=set_variable_metadata: Variable metadata such as tooltip or category must be updated.
edit=set_metadata: Freeform metadata must be attached to a Blueprint or its members.
edit=set_default: A default property must be set on the CDO; if the property denotes a component, the component CDO is targeted.
whenNotToUse: edit=add_variable: A graph-local variable is needed (use create_node with a local variable).
edit=rename_variable: The variable should be removed rather than renamed.
edit=set_default: An SCS component template property is the target (use set_scs_property).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

variableName.description: Variable name to add, remove, rename, or modify.

variableType.description: Variable type, any case. Basic: Boolean, Byte, Integer, Int64, Float, Double, String, Name, Text, Vector, Vector2D, Vector4, Rotator, Transform, Color, LinearColor. References: Object or Class (any UObject), or Object:<class>, Class:<class>, SoftObject:<class>, SoftClass:<class> with a class name or path (Actor, /Script/UMG.Widget, /Game/Blueprints/BP_Door); a bare class name or path is an object reference to that class. Structs: struct:<path> (struct:/Game/Data/F_Item), a /Script path (/Script/Engine.HitResult) or a struct name (HitResult). Enums: enum:<object path> (enum:/Script/Engine.ECollisionChannel, enum:/Game/Enums/E_State.E_State). Containers: Array<T>, Set<T> or Map<Key,Value> (also Array:T, Set:T, Map:Key,Value); a map key is Byte, Integer, Int64, Name, String or an enum. Example: Array<Object:/Script/UMG.Widget>. An unknown spelling is refused with TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED and the reason.

defaultValue.description: Default value for the variable, in the form get_property reads back: a number, string or bool, {"x": 0, "y": 0, "z": 100} for a Vector, an array for an Array or Set, and a JSON object of key: value for a Map ({"Apple": 3}). A value its type cannot take is refused with DEFAULT_NOT_APPLIED and the variable is not added.

isPublic.description: Instance Editable (the editor's eye toggle): true, the default when left out, shows the variable on placed instances in the Details panel; false keeps it to the Blueprint itself.

exposeOnSpawn.description: Expose on Spawn: the variable becomes an input pin on SpawnActor and Create Widget nodes for this class, set as the actor is made (before its BeginPlay). Makes it instance-editable too, as the editor does.

oldName.description: Current name of the variable or component.

newName.description: New name for a renamed variable, function, or component.

variableNames.description: Several variables to give the same metadata in one call (one compile and save), in place of or besides variableName.

propertyName.description: A member variable to put the metadata on (as set_variable_metadata does); omitted, the keys go on the Blueprint class.

propertyValue.description: Value to assign to the property. An object or class reference takes a path (a Blueprint class path ends in _C); null or "None" clears it.

edit.description:
Which edit variable variant to run.
add_variable: Add a member variable named variableName of variableType (basic types, object and class references, structs, enums, arrays, sets and maps, as variableType lists) with defaultValue, category, and the isPublic (instance editable), isReplicated and exposeOnSpawn flags, then compile and save the Blueprint (saved). A name the Blueprint or a parent class already uses is VARIABLE_NAME_CONFLICT, a type that resolves to nothing TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED, and a default its type refuses DEFAULT_NOT_APPLIED; nothing is added then.
rename_variable: Rename a member variable or a component in a Blueprint; its graph nodes follow.
set_variable_metadata: Set metadata (tooltip, category, replication) on a Blueprint member variable.
set_metadata: Set arbitrary metadata key-value pairs on a Blueprint class, or on one member variable.
set_default: Set a default property value on the Blueprint CDO (Class Default Object).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

variableName.description: Variable name to add, remove, rename, or modify.

variableNames.description: Every variable that took the metadata.

value.description: Property value re-read from the Class Default Object after the write. Emitted on the literal path only and omitted when the value cannot be exported to JSON.

instancesUpdated.description: Placed actors (in loaded levels) that still held the old default and took the new value, as the Details panel propagates a class default; an actor that overrides the value keeps it. Save the level to keep them.

examples.title: Change a Blueprint's variables, chosen by edit. add_variable adds variableName of variableType with defaultValue, category and the isPublic, isReplicated and exposeOnSpawn flags (a taken name is VARIABLE_NAME_CONFLICT, a type that resolves to nothing TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED, a default the type refuses DEFAULT_NOT_APPLIED; nothing is added then); rename_variable renames a variable or a component and its graph nodes follow; set_variable_metadata sets a variable's tooltip, category or replication; set_metadata sets metadata pairs on the class or one variable; set_default writes a class default value, an inherited property included.

discovery.summary: Build a widget animation, chosen by edit, each saved: create makes a named animation of a given length (a taken name is refused), add_track gives one widget an opacity, color or render-transform track, add_keyframe keys a value at a time on a widget (adding the track and binding when missing) or a whole animation across several widgets in one call (keys, all checked before any is written). get_widget_animation reads it back.
whenToUse: edit=create: A new UMG widget animation must be created for property keyframing.
edit=add_track: A widget needs an empty property track in a widget animation before keys are added.
edit=add_keyframe: A property value must be keyframed at a specific time in a widget animation.
edit=add_keyframe: A whole widget animation (a logo popping in, a menu sliding up, a pulse) must be keyed in one call (keys).
whenNotToUse: edit=create: A Blueprint graph animation is needed (use animation_physics).
edit=create: An animation must be seen playing in PIE: write the value that sets it off with inspect.set_property and watch (a short pop ends before a later call can read it).
edit=add_keyframe: The track should be removed rather than keyframed.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

trackType.description: Animation track type: opacity/renderOpacity (RenderOpacity), color (ColorAndOpacity), translation/scale/angle/shear or transform (RenderTransform).

slotName.description: Name of the widget in the widget tree that the track animates.

propertyValue.description: The key value, by trackType: opacity a number 0-1; color {r,g,b,a} or [r,g,b,a]; translation, scale or shear {x,y} or [x,y]; angle a number in degrees; transform any of {translation:{x,y}, scale:{x,y}, angle, shear:{x,y}}. A value of the wrong shape is refused before anything is added.

value.description: A plain number for an opacity or angle key, in place of propertyValue.

keys.description: Many keyframes in one call, in place of time: each {time, propertyValue or value, and any of slotName, trackType, interpolation that differ from the call's own}. Every key is checked before any is written: a refused one is named by its index (keys[3]) and nothing is added. The Widget Blueprint is saved once.

edit.description:
Which edit widget animation variant to run.
create: Create a widget animation named animationName in a Widget Blueprint and save it: duration seconds long (default 1, at least 0.01), 20 frames a second, with no tracks yet; a name the Blueprint already has is refused (ALREADY_EXISTS). The Blueprint is compiled, so a graph can play it at once (Play Animation on the animation variable); edit=add_keyframe keys it.
add_track: Add a track for one widget (slotName, its name in the widget tree) to a widget animation and save: trackType opacity (RenderOpacity), color (ColorAndOpacity), or translation, scale, angle, shear or transform (all RenderTransform). A track the widget already has is kept (createdTrack false) and its binding reused; a widget not in the tree is WIDGET_NOT_FOUND. edit=add_keyframe adds the track itself, so this is needed only for an empty track.
add_keyframe: Add a keyframe at a specific time on a widget animation track, or a whole animation across several widgets in one call (keys).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

duration.description: Length of the new animation in seconds.

saved.description: Whether the Widget Blueprint was saved.

slotName.description: Widget the track animates.

propertyName.description: Widget property driven by the track (RenderOpacity, ColorAndOpacity, RenderTransform).

trackClass.description: MovieScene track class that owns the section.

createdTrack.description: Whether the property track was created by this call.

createdBinding.description: Whether the widget binding was created by this call.

bindingGuid.description: MovieScene possessable GUID bound to the widget.

keysAdded.description: With keys: how many keyframes were added; the other fields describe the last one.

frameNumber.description: Key position in MovieScene tick-resolution frames.

keyCount.description: Keys on the last channel written after this call.

examples.title: Build a widget animation, chosen by edit, each saved: create makes a named animation of a given length (a taken name is refused), add_track gives one widget an opacity, color or render-transform track, add_keyframe keys a value at a time on a widget (adding the track and binding when missing) or a whole animation across several widgets in one call (keys, all checked before any is written). get_widget_animation reads it back.

discovery.summary: Create or restructure a Widget Blueprint, chosen by edit. create makes one named name in path (default /Game/UI), or at widgetPath, from parentClass (default UserWidget; a native widget class or a Widget Blueprint class path, anything else INVALID_PARENT_CLASS), with an empty widget tree, then compiles and saves it (compileSucceeded, saveSucceeded); a taken path is ALREADY_EXISTS. set_parent_class reparents it to a UserWidget class or Widget Blueprint, refreshes, compiles and saves (INVALID_CLASS, CYCLIC_PARENT). rename_widget renames slotName to newName and carries graph references, bindings, animations and navigation along (ALREADY_EXISTS, NAME_CONFLICT). reparent_widget moves slotName under the panel newParent at index (default last; the same parent reorders), keeping its slot layout; a move under its own child is INVALID_PARENT.
whenToUse: edit=create: A new UMG Widget Blueprint must be created.
edit=set_parent_class: A Widget Blueprint must inherit from a specific UserWidget subclass.
edit=rename_widget: A widget name must change so bindings and lookups can address it.
edit=reparent_widget: An existing widget must move into another panel without being recreated.
edit=reparent_widget: Children of a panel must be reordered (same newParent, with index).
whenNotToUse: edit=create: A non-widget Blueprint is needed (use create or create_blueprint).
edit=set_parent_class: The Widget Blueprint already has the correct parent.
edit=rename_widget: A Blueprint or Widget Blueprint asset itself should be renamed (use asset.rename).
edit=reparent_widget: The widget is being added for the first time (use the matching add action).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

name.description: Name for the new Blueprint or asset.

path.description: Destination /Game folder for a new Widget Blueprint.

folder.description: Destination /Game folder for a Widget Blueprint.

widgetPath.description: Full asset path of the new Widget Blueprint (/Game/UI/WBP_Title), in place of name and path.

parentClass.description: Parent class path for Blueprint creation (e.g. /Script/Engine.Actor).

slotName.description: Slot name for a child widget inside its parent.

newName.description: New name for a renamed variable, function, or component.

index.description: Position among the children of the new parent after the move (0 = first). Without it the widget goes last.

edit.description:
Which edit widget blueprint variant to run.
create: Create a new Widget Blueprint (UMG) asset with an optional parent class, named by name and path or by its full widgetPath.
set_parent_class: Reparent a Widget Blueprint to parentClass, a UserWidget class path or another Widget Blueprint, refresh its nodes, compile and save, as the editor's Reparent does; the reply names parentClass and previousParentClass. A class that is no UserWidget or does not load is INVALID_CLASS, and the widget itself or one deriving from it CYCLIC_PARENT.
rename_widget: Rename a widget (slotName) in a Widget Blueprint's tree to newName, compile and save, carrying along what names it as the editor's rename does: graph references to its variable, property bindings, animations bound to it (animationBindingsRenamed), navigation rules and, from UE 5.6, the desired focus. A name another widget has is ALREADY_EXISTS; one a member of the class holds (DisplayLabel and the like) is NAME_CONFLICT with a free name suggested.
reparent_widget: Move a widget under a different parent widget inside a Widget Blueprint, or to another position in its own parent, keeping its slot layout.

animationBindingsRenamed.description: Animation bindings that now name the widget by newName.

slotName.description: Slot name for a child widget inside its parent.

index.description: Where the widget now sits among the children of the new parent (0 = first).

applied.description: The widget as it is now: visibility, renderOpacity, renderTransform, slotClass, and the canvas anchors, alignment, position, size, zOrder and autoSize or the box padding and horizontal and vertical alignment.

saved.description: Whether the Widget Blueprint was saved.

examples.title: Create or restructure a Widget Blueprint, chosen by edit. create makes one named name in path (default /Game/UI), or at widgetPath, from parentClass (default UserWidget; a native widget class or a Widget Blueprint class path, anything else INVALID_PARENT_CLASS), with an empty widget tree, then compiles and saves it (compileSucceeded, saveSucceeded); a taken path is ALREADY_EXISTS. set_parent_class reparents it to a UserWidget class or Widget Blueprint, refreshes, compiles and saves (INVALID_CLASS, CYCLIC_PARENT). rename_widget renames slotName to newName and carries graph references, bindings, animations and navigation along (ALREADY_EXISTS, NAME_CONFLICT). reparent_widget moves slotName under the panel newParent at index (default last; the same parent reorders), keeping its slot layout; a move under its own child is INVALID_PARENT.

discovery.summary: Inspect a Blueprint graph: its nodes (every one, those whose title, pin default, text or object path matches a filter, or the unused ones), node details, pin details, the available node types, or the functions a node can call found by what they do in plain words (game time, random number in range), with the memberName, memberClass and pins create_node takes.
whenToUse: info=graph: The full node list of a graph must be inspected in one call.
info=graph: A large graph must be read in parts: filter by node title or by what a pin holds, page with offset/limit.
info=graph: The node that builds or uses a given asset, class or literal must be found, e.g. the Create Widget node for WBP_MainMenu.
info=graph: Leftovers must be found after an edit: unusedOnly lists the nodes that do nothing, to delete them.
info=graph: A level Blueprint's nodes must be read: blueprintPath takes the path of a level open in the editor (/Game/Maps/L_Main).
info=node: A single node's pins, type, and links must be inspected.
info=node: What an event or function does must be read: followExec on its entry node lists every node its exec wires reach, with their inputs, in one call.
info=pins: Pin-level details including linkedTo connections must be inspected for a single node.
info=node_types: The set of creatable node types must be enumerated before node creation.
info=node_types: An animation graph node class must be found by part of its name (filter IK, Blend, Bone) before create_node places it in an AnimGraph.
info=functions: A graph needs a node whose function name or class is not known: get memberName, memberClass and the pin names before create_node or a batch.
info=functions: A create_node or batch step failed with FUNCTION_NOT_FOUND: find the function by what it does.
info=functions: What an object of a class can do must be listed (memberClass Character, words jump).
whenNotToUse: info=node_types: A specific node type is already known.
info=functions: The function name and class are already known (create_node directly).
info=functions: The node is not a function call (Branch, Cast, a loop, an array's Get, which is nodeType GetArrayItem, a timeline): node_types lists those.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

graphName.description: Target graph name (Event Graph, Construction Script, etc.).

includePins.description: When true, graph details include per-node pins and links.

filter.description: Only nodes whose title or name, or whose pin default value or default object path, contains this text (case-insensitive, spaces ignored), e.g. "IA_Move", "Set bLocked", or "WBP_MainMenu" for the Create Widget node whose Class pin holds /Game/UI/WBP_MainMenu.WBP_MainMenu_C; or whose input is wired from a variable or component of that name, so "Arm" lists every node that reads or moves the Arm component (find each writer before driving it from Tick).

unusedOnly.description: Only nodes that do nothing: a call no exec wire reaches, or a getter, math or other pure node whose result nothing reads (what is left behind when the node that read it was deleted; the compiler says nothing). Events, input actions and function entries never count. Combines with filter.

offset.description: Skip this many matching nodes (paging).

limit.description: Return at most this many nodes; totalCount and hasMore say what is left. Use it with includePins on a big graph.

nodeId.description: Id of an existing node: the nodeGuid edit_graph returned when it made the node, or a nodeId inspect_graph lists.

nodeGuid.description: Node GUID accepted in place of nodeId.

followExec.description: Also walk this many nodes (1-50) along the exec wires leaving the node, depth-first (a Branch's then side before its else), and list each under chain with its inputs.

pinName.description: Report only this pin; omitted, every pin on the node.

words.description: A few plain words for what the node does (game time, random number in range, distance between actors); a function matches on its name, keywords, category and description, best first, at most 10.

memberClass.description: Only functions an object of this class calls on itself (Character, or a Blueprint path), no library functions.

node_types: List the Blueprint node types create_node can make, animation graph nodes included: all of them, or those whose class or display name contains filter.
functions: Find the functions a Blueprint node can call by what they do, in plain words (game time, random number in range, distance between actors): each with the memberName and memberClass create_node takes, its input and output pins, and the class it acts on.

discovery.summary: Read every graph of a Blueprint for the mistakes that show in Play, each with the node to fix: tick_heavy (Event Tick reaches a level search such as Get All Actors Of Class, or a spawn, every frame), unreachable (no event or function leads to a node, so it never runs), random_fanout (one pure Random node read by several nodes rolls once per read), infinite_while (a While Loop whose Condition is always true), never_assigned (an object variable read but never set, neither Instance Editable nor Expose on Spawn, with no default: every read is None), unguarded_read (an object variable set from a cast, a call or nothing, used as the target of a call or property where not every path to it checks it first with Is Valid, a validated get or a cast: a None there is an Accessed None). Nothing compiles or changes, and a function library is read too.
whenToUse: A Blueprint should be checked before Play, or after an edit, for mistakes that only show while the game runs.
A game runs slowly and a Blueprint's Event Tick may search the level every frame.
An Accessed None should be found before it fires (never_assigned, unguarded_read).
whenNotToUse: An error already fired in Play: inspect runtime_report lists it, with the cause of an Accessed None.
The Blueprint does not compile: compile it and read its messages (manage_blueprint compile).

discovery.summary: Read a Blueprint's event graphs and functions as text, in the S-expression grammar of Epic's UE 5.8 Blueprint DSL (read_graph_dsl / write_graph_dsl), on every UE 5.x: one (event Name (Params) ...) or (fn Name (Params) ...) per event or function; a statement per node that runs, (Category|Title args...) named by the node's action-menu id (Development|PrintString, Variables|Default|SetHealth), with trailing arguments still at their defaults left out; (bind var (Call ...)) where an output is read later (by output position, _ for one not read); (if cond ... (elif cond ...) (else ...)), (for i (range n) ...), (for elem array ...), (while cond ...), (break), (switch Type value (:Case ...)), (return ...); pure nodes inline: (+ a b), (== a b), (and a b), (not x), (select cond a b), (.x vector), (.yaw rotator), (.location transform), self, literals ("text", 5, true); a node with named exec outputs takes (:Pin ...) continuations (pin names with spaces quoted). Every statement ends with a ; comment naming its node by id: n and the first hex digits of the node's GUID (6, more where two nodes read together share them), so ids do not change between reads; nodes gives each id its nodeId (the full GUID other graph actions take) and type, links every wire as "id.Pin -> id.Pin". Where a path runs on into a node already printed, (goto id) says so (Epic's own reader leaves that path out); a pure value two statements read is bound once at the top, tagged "pure, runs at each read" (Blueprint works it out again at each read). Reads only: nothing is created, compiled or changed. The first read after the editor starts takes several seconds while the editor builds its node menu.
whenToUse: What a Blueprint does must be read or reviewed in one call, instead of node by node.
Before editing a graph: the code shows what runs and in what order, and the node ids to edit.
A Blueprint's logic should be explained, compared with another, or checked against what it is meant to do.
whenNotToUse: One node's pins, defaults or position are needed: get_node_details.
Mistakes that show only in Play should be found: lint_blueprint.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

graphName.description: One graph: EventGraph, a function's name, or a macro or collapsed graph by name (GRAPH_NOT_FOUND lists the graphs). Default: every event graph and function.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

code.description: The text: each graph after a "; graph Name" comment line, its events and functions top to bottom.

graphs.description: One row per graph read: name, kind (event_graph, function, macro or graph), nodes, and notInCode (the ids of nodes no event or function reaches, so the code leaves them out; reroutes are never printed).

nodes.description: Every node: id (as the code names it), nodeId (its GUID) and type (its action-menu id). At most 500.

examples.title: Read a Blueprint's event graphs and functions as text, in the S-expression grammar of Epic's UE 5.8 Blueprint DSL (read_graph_dsl / write_graph_dsl), on every UE 5.x: one (event Name (Params) ...) or (fn Name (Params) ...) per event or function; a statement per node that runs, (Category|Title args...) named by the node's action-menu id (Development|PrintString, Variables|Default|SetHealth), with trailing arguments still at their defaults left out; (bind var (Call ...)) where an output is read later (by output position, _ for one not read); (if cond ... (elif cond ...) (else ...)), (for i (range n) ...), (for elem array ...), (while cond ...), (break), (switch Type value (:Case ...)), (return ...); pure nodes inline: (+ a b), (== a b), (and a b), (not x), (select cond a b), (.x vector), (.yaw rotator), (.location transform), self, literals ("text", 5, true); a node with named exec outputs takes (:Pin ...) continuations (pin names with spaces quoted). Every statement ends with a ; comment naming its node by id: n and the first hex digits of the node's GUID (6, more where two nodes read together share them), so ids do not change between reads; nodes gives each id its nodeId (the full GUID other graph actions take) and type, links every wire as "id.Pin -> id.Pin". Where a path runs on into a node already printed, (goto id) says so (Epic's own reader leaves that path out); a pure value two statements read is bound once at the top, tagged "pure, runs at each read" (Blueprint works it out again at each read). Reads only: nothing is created, compiled or changed. The first read after the editor starts takes several seconds while the editor builds its node menu.

discovery.summary: Write a Blueprint's logic from text, on every UE 5.x: each (event Name ...) or (fn Name (Params) ...) form replaces that event's or function's body with nodes made from its statements, in the grammar read_graph_as_code prints (Epic's UE 5.8 Blueprint DSL), so the way to edit is read, change the text, write it back. A statement is (Category|Title args... :Pin value (:ExecPin stmts...)), the node named by its action-menu id as read_graph_as_code prints it (positional arguments fill the data inputs in order, :Pin names one, a (:Pin ...) continuation runs from that exec output and sees the node's outputs as _pin_name); (bind name (Call ...)) or (bind (first _ third) (Call ...)) names outputs for later statements (a name is bound once); (if cond ... (elif cond ...) (else ...)), (for i (range n) ...), (for i (range a b) ...), (for item array ...), (while cond ...), (break), (switch int|string|name value (:Case ...) (:Default ...)), (return values...), (goto id [Pin]) on to the node with that id (a statement of this code by its ; comment, or a node the write leaves in the graph, so one event can be rewritten alone). Values: names, literals ("text", 5, 1.5, true), (+ - * / % == != < <= > >= and or xor a b), (not x), (- x), (select cond a b), (.x .y .z .pitch .yaw .roll .location .rotation .scale value), self. An entry's inputs are names by their pin names, as read_graph_as_code lists them (an (fn) head must list only names the function has; an (event) head's list is optional): code names inputs, add_function or add_event makes them. An event the graph lacks is made (a custom event as Custom|Name); a function must exist (FUNCTION_NOT_FOUND). A form with no statements leaves that body as it is. What goes: the nodes only that event or function reached (its flow and the values that flow read); a node another event also runs stays, and events and functions the code does not name are not touched; a function keeps its return nodes when the new body makes none. A statement whose ; comment names a node of the old body by its id (as read_graph_as_code tags every statement) keeps that node when it is of the same kind (its GUID, position and comment stay; its links and inputs are set afresh), so read, edit, write changes only what was edited; new nodes then go beside the nodes they are wired to. Code without such ids makes every node new, laid out in columns from its event, a new event below the graph. All or nothing: a parse error, an unknown node id (the reply lists the ids the menu offers for that title), an undefined name, too many arguments, a pin the node lacks, or code that leaves a Blueprint that compiled not compiling is refused with its line and nothing changes (CODE_PARSE_ERROR, CODE_INVALID, CODE_BREAKS_COMPILE with compileMessages). The reply reads the written graphs back as code with the new nodes' ids. Refused during Play In Editor (PIE_ACTIVE). The first call after the editor starts takes several seconds while the editor builds its node menu.
whenToUse: An event's or function's logic should be written or rewritten in one call instead of node by node.
A graph read with read_graph_as_code should be changed: edit the text and write it back.
whenNotToUse: One node, link or pin default should change and the rest stay exactly as it is (node GUIDs included): create_node, connect_pins, set_pin_default_value.
Variables, functions or event inputs must be added: add_variable, add_function, add_event.

discovery.summary: Create or update a foliage type asset, place explicit instances/transforms, or paint instances over a brush disc or a box area, dropped onto the ground. Placing and painting are one undo step each.
whenToUse: Foliage must be added, configured, or removed in the level.
whenNotToUse: foliageOp=scatter: A procedural foliage volume should be used for large areas.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

count.description: How many instances to place over the brush disc (location + radius) or the area; overrides density.

name.description: Name for the new actor, asset, or volume.

path.description: Folder the new foliage type asset goes in (type creation only; default /Game/Foliage).

density.description: Type creation: instances per 1000x1000 units. Scatter: brush fill 0-1 (count overrides it).

location.description: World-space location {x, y, z}.
Location.

rotation.description: Rotation.

area.description: A box min..max. Painting: instances spread evenly over min..max in X and Y, and each drops onto the ground found between 500 above max.z and 1000 below min.z. Removing: only the instances whose location lies inside min..max on all three axes (a pit or a path), every type unless foliageType names one.

snapToSurface.description: Drop each point onto the first static surface below it (default true). Points with no surface below - over a pit or off the level - are skipped and reported as skippedNoSurface.

foliageOp.description:
Which add foliage variant to run; omit for 'scatter'.
scatter: Add foliage: with only meshPath (+ name) create or update a foliage type asset; with a foliage type or a placement (locations, position, location + radius + count) scatter instances onto the ground, a bare meshPath standing in for its auto foliage type.
instances: Add explicit foliage instances: full transforms, or bare locations varied by minScale/maxScale/randomYaw. One undo step removes them all; the reply's undo block says so.
paint: Paint foliage over a brush disc (location + radius) or a box area: count instances dropped onto the ground, each with a random scale and yaw. One undo step removes the whole stroke; NO_SURFACE (no ground below any point) adds nothing.

setting.description:
Which configure lighting variant to run.
shadows: Set shadows. Engine-wide values go to console variables for this editor session only (not saved to the project): shadowQuality Low, Medium, High, Epic or Cinematic (sg.ShadowQuality), shadowDistance (r.Shadow.DistanceScale), contactShadows, rayTracedShadows and virtualShadowMaps, each set as a console command would set it and read back: one that did not take is listed under notSet with why (read-only, or missing in this engine version), and a call where none took is refused. With actorName, that light's own castShadows, shadowBias, shadowSlopeBias and shadowResolutionScale change, saved with the level. settings may carry the same keys nested; a value there wins.
ambient_occlusion: Set ambient occlusion on a post-process volume: actorName names a post-process volume, else the level's one unbound volume is used (several are AMBIGUOUS; with none, an unbound one is spawned). intensity, radius and quality (Low 25, Medium 50 or High 100 percent) each turn on their override; enabled true sets intensity 0.5 and false sets 0, unless intensity is sent too. A call that sets none is NO_SETTING_SUPPLIED. The reply gives intensity, radius and qualityPercent; one undo step, a spawned volume included.
exposure: Set auto-exposure on a post-process volume: actorName names a post-process volume, else the level's one unbound volume is used (several are AMBIGUOUS; with none, an unbound one is spawned). method (Manual, AutoExposureHistogram or AutoExposureBasic), compensationValue (the exposure bias), minBrightness and maxBrightness each turn on their override; a call that sets none is NO_SETTING_SUPPLIED. The reply lists appliedSettings; one undo step, a spawned volume included.
global_illumination: Switch the dynamic global illumination method (method: LumenGI, which also turns on Lumen reflections, ScreenSpace, None or Lightmass for baked lighting only; RayTraced only before UE 5.4) through r.DynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod, set as a console command would set it and read back (GI_METHOD_NOT_APPLIED names what held it). That lasts for this editor session; saveToProject true also writes it to Project Settings > Rendering (DefaultEngine.ini), so the project and its packaged game keep it (savedToProject). quality sets the GI scalability level for the session (sg.GlobalIlluminationQuality; one that did not take is listed under notSet), indirectLightingIntensity a post-process volume's override (actorName names a post-process volume, else the level's one unbound volume is used (several are AMBIGUOUS; with none, an unbound one is spawned)), bounces the level's Lightmass bounces.
volumetric_fog: Turn volumetric fog on or off (enabled) and set how far it reaches (viewDistance) on the level's first Exponential Height Fog, spawning one at the origin when there is none. What is left out keeps its value; a call that sets neither is NO_SETTING_SUPPLIED. The reply reads both back; one undo step.

discovery.summary: Static (baked) lighting, chosen by setting. settings writes the level's Lightmass settings (World Settings) from settings, keyed by engine field name (NumIndirectLightingBounces, IndirectLightingQuality, StaticLightingLevelScale, bUseAmbientOcclusion), which the next build uses; build_quality bakes the lighting at quality (default Production; Preview, Medium, High, or 0 to 3) and answers when the bake ends, refused when the level forces no precomputed lighting; indirect_lighting_cache sets how an actor's primitive components sample the indirect lighting cache (enabled: point sampling or off) or other primitive fields (settings). A key the target lacks is listed in unsupportedSettings and a call where none applies is refused; settings and indirect_lighting_cache are one undo step, and nothing is saved.
whenToUse: Render or lighting quality settings must be configured.
whenNotToUse: Default rendering settings are sufficient.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

settings.description: Action-specific settings key-value pairs.

quality.description: Lightmap bake quality (Preview, Medium, High, Production).

actorName.description: Actor name in the current level.

enabled.description: Indirect lighting cache on (point sampled) or off for each primitive.

setting.description:
Which configure lightmass variant to run.
settings: Set the level's Lightmass settings (World Settings > Lightmass) from settings, keyed by FLightmassWorldInfoSettings field names such as NumIndirectLightingBounces or IndirectLightingQuality; the next lighting build uses them. A key the struct lacks is listed in unsupportedSettings, a call where none applies is refused naming the fields it comes close to; one undo step, and the level is left unsaved.
build_quality: Bake the level's static lighting at quality (default Production; Preview, Medium, High, or 0 to 3), as build_lighting does: it answers when the bake ends, rebuilds no reflection captures and saves nothing; a level whose World Settings force no precomputed lighting is refused (PRECOMPUTED_LIGHTING_DISABLED), an unknown quality is UNKNOWN_QUALITY, and a failed build lists its reasons.
indirect_lighting_cache: Set how every primitive component of actorName samples the indirect lighting cache (the baked light a movable or unbuilt object receives): enabled true is point sampling, false off; settings writes other primitive component fields by engine name. One undo step; componentCount says how many components took it.

topics: add bloom or depth of field
discovery.summary: Set post-process values on a PostProcessVolume, chosen by setting: bloom, exposure, depth of field, motion blur, tonemapper, color grading, LUT, white balance, vignette, grain, chromatic aberration, lens flare, SSAO/GTAO, screen-space and Lumen reflections, blend (screen_percentage sets r.ScreenPercentage instead). The volume is actorName, else the level's unbound (whole level) volume, the persistent level's first; a level with none gets one, named actorName when given. A name no volume has is ACTOR_NOT_FOUND listing the volumes, several unbound volumes AMBIGUOUS. Each value is the FPostProcessSettings field it names and turns that field's override on; settings takes any field by engine name. A value outside the engine's limits, an unknown name and a call that sets nothing are refused, and nothing is written unless every value is taken. One undo step; the level is left unsaved. blendWeight (0-1) and infiniteUnbound set the volume itself with any variant.
whenToUse: setting=configure_bloom|set_bloom_intensity|set_bloom_threshold|configure_exposure|set_exposure_method|configure_dof|set_dof_method|set_focal_distance|set_aperture|configure_bokeh|configure_motion_blur|set_motion_blur_amount|set_motion_blur_max|configure_tonemapper|set_tonemapper_type|set_pp_color_grading|set_pp_lut|set_pp_white_balance|configure_lens_flare|configure_ssr_settings|configure_lumen_reflection_settings|configure_pp_blend: Post-process, exposure, or screen effect settings must be configured.

setting=set_exposure_compensation|set_exposure_min_max|configure_vignette|configure_grain|configure_chromatic_aberration|configure_ssao|configure_gtao|configure_screen_percentage: Exposure, ambient occlusion, screen, or capture settings must be configured.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: Actor name in the current level.

infiniteUnbound.description: Whether the volume is infinite and unbound.

settings.description: FPostProcessSettings fields by engine name, e.g. {"ColorSaturation": {"x": 1.1, "y": 1.1, "z": 1.1, "w": 1}, "VignetteIntensity": 0.3}; each field's bOverride_ flag is set for you. A key that is not a field is listed under unsupportedSettings, and when no key is one the call fails naming the closest fields.

amount.description: Bloom intensity, 0 or more (0.675 by default; 8 is the top of the editor slider).

threshold.description: Brightness a pixel needs to bloom: -1 (the default) blooms everything, 0 or more only brighter pixels.

compensationValue.description: Exposure bias in stops (+1 is twice as bright).

minBrightness.description: Lowest auto exposure (EV100 with the extended luminance range).

maxBrightness.description: Highest auto exposure (EV100 with the extended luminance range).

method.description: Auto-exposure method: Manual (fixed; camera settings), Histogram (the default) or Basic.

distance.description: Focal distance in cm, 0 or more.

enabled.description: false sets LensFlareIntensity 0; true sets it back to 1 unless settings gives it.

setting.description:
Which configure post process variant to run.
configure_bloom: Set bloom: amount (BloomIntensity) and threshold (BloomThreshold), written after settings, which takes any other bloom field by engine name (BloomSizeScale, BloomMethod). Send at least one.
set_bloom_intensity: Set BloomIntensity to amount: 0 or more, 0.675 by default, 8 at the top of the editor slider; 0 turns bloom off.
set_bloom_threshold: Set BloomThreshold to threshold, the brightness a pixel needs to bloom: -1 (the default) blooms everything, 0 or more only brighter pixels.
configure_exposure: Set exposure: method (Manual, Histogram, the default, or Basic), compensationValue (AutoExposureBias, in stops), minBrightness and maxBrightness (the auto exposure range), then settings for any other exposure field (AutoExposureSpeedUp, AutoExposureSpeedDown). The range is in EV100 when the project extends the default luminance range, as UE 5 projects do, and in luminance otherwise. Send at least one.
set_exposure_compensation: Set AutoExposureBias to compensationValue, in stops: +1 is twice as bright, -1 half; it applies with every exposure method.
set_exposure_method: Set AutoExposureMethod: Manual (no adaptation: exposure from compensation and camera settings), Histogram (the default, adapting from the scene's brightness) or Basic (a cheaper adaptation). Anything else is INVALID_SETTING.
set_exposure_min_max: Set the auto exposure range, AutoExposureMinBrightness and AutoExposureMaxBrightness (-10 or more): in EV100 when the project extends the default luminance range, as UE 5 projects do, in luminance otherwise. Equal values fix the exposure. A bound left out keeps its value; send at least one.
configure_dof: Set depth of field from settings, by engine field name: DepthOfFieldFocalDistance (cm to the sharp plane; at 0, the default, there is no depth of field), DepthOfFieldFstop (1-32; lower blurs more), DepthOfFieldSensorWidth (mm), DepthOfFieldDepthBlurRadius and the rest of the Lens|Depth of Field fields.
set_dof_method: Choose the depth of field the volume renders with method: UE 5 desktop and console renderers always use the cinematic one, so this picks what mobile renders, Gaussian (bMobileHQGaussian on: the high quality Gaussian blur) or Cinematic (off: mobile's own). CircleDOF and BokehDOF are taken as Cinematic, GaussianDOF as Gaussian.
set_focal_distance: Set DepthOfFieldFocalDistance, the distance in cm from the camera to the sharp plane, 0 or more; depth of field shows only while it is above 0 (0 is the default).
set_aperture: Set DepthOfFieldFstop to aperture, 1 to 32 (4 by default): a lower f-stop gives a shallower, blurrier depth of field. Shows once a focal distance is set.
configure_bokeh: Set the shape of out-of-focus highlights from settings, by engine field name: DepthOfFieldBladeCount (aperture blades), DepthOfFieldMinFstop, DepthOfFieldSensorWidth (mm), DepthOfFieldSqueezeFactor (anamorphic).
configure_motion_blur: Set motion blur from settings, by engine field name: MotionBlurAmount (0-1, 0.5 by default; 0 turns it off), MotionBlurMax (0-100, percent of the screen width, 5 by default), MotionBlurTargetFPS, MotionBlurPerObjectSize.
set_motion_blur_amount: Set MotionBlurAmount to amount, 0 to 1 (0.5 by default); 0 turns motion blur off.
set_motion_blur_max: Set MotionBlurMax to amount: the longest blur streak, 0 to 100 percent of the screen width (5 by default).
configure_tonemapper: Set the filmic tonemapper's curve on a post-process volume from settings, by FPostProcessSettings field: FilmSlope, FilmToe, FilmShoulder, FilmBlackClip, FilmWhiteClip, ToneCurveAmount, ExpandGamut (each turns its override on).
set_tonemapper_type: Choose the tonemapper look on a post-process volume: method Filmic (default: the engine's filmic tone curve, ToneCurveAmount and ExpandGamut 1) or Linear (the curve off, both 0); anything else is refused, nothing changed.
set_pp_color_grading: Set color grading on the volume from settings, by engine field name: ColorSaturation, ColorContrast, ColorGamma and ColorGain as {x, y, z, w} (1 is neutral; w scales all three), ColorOffset (0 neutral), each also in a Shadows, Midtones or Highlights form (ColorSaturationShadows), and ColorGradingIntensity (0-1).
set_pp_lut: Grade the volume with a color lookup table: lutPath is a texture in the 256x16 strip LUT format, which becomes ColorGradingLUT with its override on (ColorGradingIntensity sets how strongly it applies). A path that loads no texture is ASSET_NOT_FOUND.
set_pp_white_balance: Set white balance on the volume from settings, by engine field name: WhiteTemp (Kelvin; 6500, the default, is neutral, lower is warmer) and WhiteTint (-1 to 1, green to magenta).
configure_vignette: Set VignetteIntensity to amount: how much the screen edges darken, 0 (off) to 1 on the editor slider, 0.4 by default.
configure_grain: Set film grain: amount (FilmGrainIntensity, 0 by default, 1 at the top of the slider) written after settings, which takes other grain fields by engine name (FilmGrainIntensityShadows, FilmGrainTexelSize, FilmGrainTexture). Send at least one.
configure_chromatic_aberration: Set chromatic aberration: amount (SceneFringeIntensity, 0 by default, 5 at the top of the slider) written after settings, which takes other fields by engine name (ChromaticAberrationStartOffset 0-1). Send at least one.
configure_lens_flare: Set lens flares from settings, by engine field name (LensFlareIntensity 0-16, 1 by default; LensFlareThreshold; LensFlareBokehSize; LensFlareTint). enabled false sets LensFlareIntensity 0; enabled true puts it back to 1 unless settings gives it.
configure_ssao: Set screen-space ambient occlusion: amount (AmbientOcclusionIntensity, 0-1, 0.5 by default) written after settings, which takes other fields by engine name (AmbientOcclusionRadius in cm, AmbientOcclusionPower, AmbientOcclusionQuality 0-100). With Lumen on, its own occlusion replaces this. Send at least one.
configure_gtao: Set ambient occlusion fields from settings, by engine field name (AmbientOcclusionQuality 0-100, AmbientOcclusionRadius, AmbientOcclusionIntensity); ground truth AO itself is chosen by r.AmbientOcclusion.Method, which this does not change.
configure_ssr_settings: Set screen-space reflections on the volume from settings, by engine field name: ScreenSpaceReflectionIntensity and ScreenSpaceReflectionQuality (0-100; 100 and 50 by default) and ScreenSpaceReflectionMaxRoughness (0-1).
configure_lumen_reflection_settings: Set Lumen reflections on the volume from settings, by engine field name, such as LumenReflectionQuality and LumenMaxRoughnessToTraceReflections (0-1); they show only where the project renders reflections with Lumen.
configure_screen_percentage: Set screen percentage for rendering (the r.ScreenPercentage console variable; no volume involved).
configure_pp_blend: Set the volume's own fields: enabled, blendWeight (0-1, how much of the volume applies) and infiniteUnbound (true: the whole level, false: only inside its bounds). Send at least one.

discovery.summary: Turn a ray-tracing feature on or off and tune it through its console variables for this editor session: shadows, global illumination, reflections, ambient occlusion, path tracing. settings takes only the keys that feature reads (another is refused); with hardware ray tracing off for the project the values draw nothing and the reply warns.
whenToUse: Render or lighting quality settings must be configured.
whenNotToUse: Default rendering settings are sufficient.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

settings.description: Console values by key, only these (any other key is refused and nothing is set): Radius (0-10000 world units).

enabled.description: Turn the feature on (default true) or off: its console variable is set to 1 or 0 even when only settings are sent.

intensity.description: Occlusion intensity 0-10 (r.RayTracing.AmbientOcclusion.Intensity); out of range is refused.

feature.description:
Which configure ray tracing variant to run.
ao: Turn ray-traced ambient occlusion on or off (r.RayTracing.AmbientOcclusion) and set its intensity and radius. Values are set as a console command would set them (console_command and this call replace each other, last one wins) and last for this editor session, not saved to the project. With hardware ray tracing off for the project (r.RayTracing 0, fixed at startup) they are stored, draw nothing, and the reply warns (rayTracingEnabled false). A variable that did not take is listed under unsupportedCVars with why: missing in this engine version, read-only, or reset by the engine; refused with CVAR_UNAVAILABLE when none took.
gi: Turn ray-traced global illumination on or off (r.RayTracing.GlobalIllumination) and set its samples and bounces. Values are set as a console command would set them (console_command and this call replace each other, last one wins) and last for this editor session, not saved to the project. With hardware ray tracing off for the project (r.RayTracing 0, fixed at startup) they are stored, draw nothing, and the reply warns (rayTracingEnabled false). A variable that did not take is listed under unsupportedCVars with why: missing in this engine version, read-only, or reset by the engine; refused with CVAR_UNAVAILABLE when none took.
reflections: Turn ray-traced reflections on or off (r.RayTracing.Reflections) and set their samples and roughness cutoff. Values are set as a console command would set them (console_command and this call replace each other, last one wins) and last for this editor session, not saved to the project. With hardware ray tracing off for the project (r.RayTracing 0, fixed at startup) they are stored, draw nothing, and the reply warns (rayTracingEnabled false). A variable that did not take is listed under unsupportedCVars with why: missing in this engine version, read-only, or reset by the engine; refused with CVAR_UNAVAILABLE when none took.
shadows: Turn ray-traced shadows on or off (r.RayTracing.Shadows) and set their samples per pixel. Values are set as a console command would set them (console_command and this call replace each other, last one wins) and last for this editor session, not saved to the project. With hardware ray tracing off for the project (r.RayTracing 0, fixed at startup) they are stored, draw nothing, and the reply warns (rayTracingEnabled false). A variable that did not take is listed under unsupportedCVars with why: missing in this engine version, read-only, or reset by the engine; refused with CVAR_UNAVAILABLE when none took.
path_tracing: Set the path tracer's samples per pixel and bounces. Its switch r.PathTracing is read-only, fixed at startup by the project's config, so enabled cannot turn it on or off here (the reply lists it under unsupportedCVars); to see the path tracer, set_view_mode PathTracing. Values are set as a console command would set them (console_command and this call replace each other, last one wins) and last for this editor session, not saved to the project. With hardware ray tracing off for the project (r.RayTracing 0, fixed at startup) they are stored, draw nothing, and the reply warns (rayTracingEnabled false). A variable that did not take is listed under unsupportedCVars with why: missing in this engine version, read-only, or reset by the engine; refused with CVAR_UNAVAILABLE when none took.

discovery.summary: Configure a capture actor: render target, capture source, resolution, offset, planar-reflection settings, reflection capture resolution, or trigger a (re)capture.
whenToUse: setting=render_target|source|capture: Exposure, ambient occlusion, screen, or capture settings must be configured.
setting=resolution|offset|planar_reflection|reflection_resolution|recapture: Render or lighting quality settings must be configured.
whenNotToUse: setting=render_target|source|capture: Default settings are sufficient.
setting=resolution|offset|planar_reflection|reflection_resolution|recapture: Default rendering settings are sufficient.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: Actor name in the current level.

captureSource.description: What the capture renders: FinalColorLDR, SceneColorHDR, SceneDepth, BaseColor, Normal or an SCS_ value. Required.

resolution.description: Width and height in pixels, 1 to 4096.

captureOffset.description: Offset in cm from the capture actor.

settings.description: Action-specific settings key-value pairs.

setting.description:
Which configure scene capture variant to run.
render_target: Assign a render target to a scene capture.
source: Configure scene capture source.
resolution: Resize the render target a SceneCapture2D draws into to resolution x resolution (1-4096; the reply reads the size back). It is the render target asset that changes, for every capture drawing into it, in one undo step, and it is left unsaved. A cube capture is UNSUPPORTED_TARGET, a capture with no render target RENDER_TARGET_NOT_ASSIGNED; without actorName the level's one scene capture is used.
offset: Move the point a sphere or box reflection capture captures from by captureOffset (cm from the actor, {x, y, z} or [x, y, z]; a component left out keeps its value), then mark it for recapture. One undo step; the reply reads the offset back. Without actorName the level's one reflection capture is used; several is AMBIGUOUS.
planar_reflection: Configure planar reflection settings.
reflection_resolution: Set reflection capture resolution (project-wide CVar; marks the named capture, or every capture, for recapture).
capture: Trigger a scene capture on an actor.
recapture: Recapture a reflection or scene capture.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Configure a capture actor: render target, capture source, resolution, offset, planar-reflection settings, reflection capture resolution, or trigger a (re)capture.

discovery.summary: Configure meshes along a spline: mesh asset, material, forward axis, spacing, randomization, or scatter meshes along it.
whenToUse: A spline actor or spline mesh must be created or modified.
whenNotToUse: setting=mesh_asset: The mesh should be recreated.
setting=material: Default material is sufficient.
setting=axis: Default axis is sufficient.
setting=spacing: Default spacing is sufficient.
setting=randomization: Uniform placement is desired.
setting=scatter: Manual placement is sufficient.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: Actor name in the current level.

actorPath.description: Object path of the spline actor; used when actorName is omitted.

componentName.description: Component name.

forwardAxis.description: Mesh axis laid along the spline: X (the default), Y or Z, any case; another name is refused.

useRandomOffset.description: Apply a random offset to scattered meshes.

setting.description:
Which configure spline meshes variant to run.
mesh_asset: Set the static mesh asset for a spline mesh component.
material: Set the material on a spline mesh component.
axis: Set which local axis of its mesh a spline mesh component lays along the spline (forwardAxis X, the default, Y or Z, any case; another name is refused before anything changes). The reply gives the axis the component holds; the level is left unsaved.
spacing: Store the spacing setting=scatter uses for a spline actor (actorName; with none, for every spline in the level): spacing in cm between meshes (default 100), useRandomOffset and randomOffsetRange (cm). Nothing is placed until scatter runs, and a value sent to scatter wins over the stored one. Only the fields sent are stored, a call with none is refused, and the reply gives what scatter will read.
randomization: Store the randomization setting=scatter uses for a spline actor (or, with no actorName, for every spline in the level): randomizeScale between minScale and maxScale (defaults 0.8 and 1.2), randomizeRotation within rotationRange degrees (default 360). Nothing is placed until scatter runs; only the fields sent are stored (a scale sent alone is checked against the stored other), a call with none is refused, and the reply gives what scatter will read.
scatter: Scatter static meshes along a spline path.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Configure meshes along a spline: mesh asset, material, forward axis, spacing, randomization, or scatter meshes along it.

discovery.summary: Change a water body, chosen by setting: the one named by waterBodyName, targetActor or actorName, else the level's first. waves gives it Gerstner waves (waveHeight, waveLength, steepness, direction) that its surface and anything floating on it follow, and fails when the body does not keep them; material sets the material that draws its surface (its WaterMaterial, read back as waterMaterial; a material without the Used with Water usage gains it and is left unsaved); collision turns collision on its components on or off (collisionEnabled); settings writes water body actor properties by engine name. material and collision are one undo step; a call with nothing to set, or whose settings name nothing the body has, is refused, and a material that does not load fails the call.
whenToUse: A water body or water simulation must be created or configured.
whenNotToUse: setting=waves: Default waves are sufficient.
setting=material: Default water material is sufficient.
setting=collision: Default collision is sufficient.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

waveHeight.description: Height (amplitude) of the largest wave in cm; the body's other waves shrink to 15% of it, as a real sea's do. A calm harbour is about 5-10, open sea 50 or more.

waveLength.description: Wavelength of the longest wave in cm, crest to crest; the shortest waves are 13% of it (a harbour is about 1500-2500).

amplitude.description: Same as waveHeight; waveHeight wins when both are given.

steepness.description: Crest sharpness of the short waves, 0 (smooth swell) to 1 (peaked); the long waves take about half. Keep it under about 0.3: steep crests from many waves fold the surface over itself.

direction.description: Wind direction: its yaw sets where the waves travel.

waterBodyName.description: Water body to configure; the first ocean, lake, river or custom body when omitted.

settings.description: Action-specific settings key-value pairs.

setting.description:
Which configure water variant to run.
waves: Give a water body Gerstner waves, the swell its surface and anything floating on it follow: height, wavelength, steepness and wind direction. The call fails when the body does not end up holding the waves.
material: Set the material that draws a water body's surface: its WaterBodyComponent's WaterMaterial, read back as waterMaterial; a material without the Used with Water usage gains it, as in the editor, and is left unsaved (a slot material on the body's components never reached the water). One undo step; a material that does not load fails the call, and a call with nothing to set is refused. settings also writes water body actor properties by engine name.
collision: Turn collision on every primitive component of a water body on (query and physics) or off with collisionEnabled; settings also writes water body actor properties by engine name. One undo step; a call with nothing to set is refused.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Change a water body, chosen by setting: the one named by waterBodyName, targetActor or actorName, else the level's first. waves gives it Gerstner waves (waveHeight, waveLength, steepness, direction) that its surface and anything floating on it follow, and fails when the body does not keep them; material sets the material that draws its surface (its WaterMaterial, read back as waterMaterial; a material without the Used with Water usage gains it and is left unsaved); collision turns collision on its components on or off (collisionEnabled); settings writes water body actor properties by engine name. material and collision are one undo step; a call with nothing to set, or whose settings name nothing the body has, is refused, and a material that does not load fails the call.

discovery.summary: Create the sky lighting rig (kind sky_sphere: a Sky Atmosphere, a sun and a Sky Light), an Exponential Height Fog (fog_volume), or one actor carrying its own sun, sky light and atmosphere at noon (time_of_day_system; nothing animates it, set_time_of_day moves the sun). Each reuses an actor already carrying its label, but one labelled otherwise is not seen, so mixing sky_sphere and time_of_day_system, or a sun of another label, doubles the sun.
whenToUse: Atmosphere, sky, fog, or time-of-day must be configured.
whenNotToUse: kind=sky_sphere: A sky atmosphere or sun is already present under another label: configure it (configure_sky_atmosphere, configure_directional_light_atmosphere) instead of adding a second.
kind=fog_volume: The level has a height fog under another label: configure_exponential_height_fog finds the first one.
kind=time_of_day_system: The level already has a sun and sky atmosphere: set_time_of_day moves its sun.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

name.description: Name for the new actor, asset, or volume.

location.description: World-space location {x, y, z}.

rotation.description: Rotation {pitch, yaw, roll}.

density.description: Fog density, the height fog's FogDensity (0.02 a light haze, 0.05 and up a thick fog).

settings.description: Property values for the actor or its component, keyed by the Unreal property name (case-insensitive): {"Intensity": 2, "LightColor": {"R": 0.6, "G": 0.7, "B": 1}} for a light, {"FogDensity": 0.02} for fog. A key neither declares is named in configurationErrors and fails the call.

kind.description:
Which create atmosphere actor variant to run.
sky_sphere: Create the sky lighting rig in the level being edited: a Sky Atmosphere, a sun (Directional Light) and a Sky Light, labelled <name>_Atmosphere, <name>_Sun and <name>_SkyLight (SkyAtmosphere, DirectionalLight and SkyLight without a name). An actor already carrying one of those labels is reused and set up rather than doubled, but a sun or atmosphere labelled otherwise is not found, so the level gets a second one. No sky sphere mesh, clouds or fog: add those with configure_volumetric_cloud and kind=fog_volume. Replies createdActorCount (0 when all three existed) and the three actor names.
fog_volume: Create an Exponential Height Fog actor in the level being edited, or set up the one already labelled name (default ExponentialHeightFog), with density and settings (properties of its fog component). It is height fog over the whole level, not a local volume, and a fog labelled otherwise is not found, so the level gets a second one.
time_of_day_system: Create one actor, TimeOfDaySystem (or name), carrying its own sun (a directional light at intensity 10, the atmosphere sun), sky light (intensity 1) and sky atmosphere, all movable, with the sun at noon; an actor already labelled so gets the missing parts. Nothing animates it, no curves and no day cycle: move the sun with set_time_of_day. A level that already has a sun or sky atmosphere (kind=sky_sphere, the default level template) ends up with two of each, so use one rig or the other.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Create the sky lighting rig (kind sky_sphere: a Sky Atmosphere, a sun and a Sky Light), an Exponential Height Fog (fog_volume), or one actor carrying its own sun, sky light and atmosphere at noon (time_of_day_system; nothing animates it, set_time_of_day moves the sun). Each reuses an actor already carrying its label, but one labelled otherwise is not seen, so mixing sky_sphere and time_of_day_system, or a sun of another label, doubles the sun.
