discovery.summary: Create foliage assets, chosen by kind. type makes a static mesh foliage type named name in path (default /Game/Foliage) that places meshPath, with density (instances per 1000 x 1000 units, default 100), minScale and maxScale (default 1), alignToNormal and randomYaw (default true) and cullDistance. A foliage type already there is updated instead, keeping the settings not sent (created false); another kind of asset under the name is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS). procedural places a procedural foliage volume and a spawner asset named <name>_Spawner (refused when it exists) with one foliage type per foliageTypes entry ({meshPath, density}), simulated with seed over bounds; a simulation that places nothing fails.
whenToUse: kind=type: A new foliage type asset is needed.
kind=procedural: Large-area procedural foliage scatter is needed.
whenNotToUse: kind=type: An existing foliage type should be reused.
kind=procedural: Manual foliage placement is sufficient.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

name.description: Name for the new actor, asset, or volume.

path.description: Canonical /Game asset or directory path.

volumeName.description: Label of the procedural foliage volume (name is accepted too).

items.description: Foliage type with mesh and density.

foliageTypes.description: At least one {meshPath, density}: the static mesh to scatter and its density, the seeds per 10 m x 10 m the simulation starts from (default 10). Its steps then spread, age and thin them (instances keep a collision radius apart), so the count placed differs; get_foliage_instances reads it.

bounds.description: The area {location, size}: a box of size (default 1000 on each axis) centred on location (default the origin); it must enclose a surface to place on.

location.description: Bounds location.

seed.description: Random seed of the scatter (default 12345); the same seed gives the same placement.

tileSize.description: Side of one simulated tile in world units (default 1000); the scatter repeats 10 unique tiles across the area.

kind.description:
Which create foliage type variant to run; omit for 'type'.
type: Create a foliage type asset from a static mesh.
procedural: Scatter foliage over an area in one call: make a Procedural Foliage Spawner (and one foliage type per foliageTypes entry) in path, place a Procedural Foliage Volume over bounds (a box of size, default 1000 on each axis, centred on location) and run the simulation as the Resimulate button does, which traces the instances onto the landscape, static mesh and BSP surfaces inside the volume. A mesh that does not load (MESH_NOT_FOUND) or an empty foliageTypes is refused before anything is created; a run that places no instance is NOTHING_SPAWNED (the assets and volume stay).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Create foliage assets, chosen by kind. type makes a static mesh foliage type named name in path (default /Game/Foliage) that places meshPath, with density (instances per 1000 x 1000 units, default 100), minScale and maxScale (default 1), alignToNormal and randomYaw (default true) and cullDistance. A foliage type already there is updated instead, keeping the settings not sent (created false); another kind of asset under the name is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS). procedural places a procedural foliage volume and a spawner asset named <name>_Spawner (refused when it exists) with one foliage type per foliageTypes entry ({meshPath, density}), simulated with seed over bounds; a simulation that places nothing fails.

discovery.summary: Create a new landscape in the world (its current level), or a grass type for one, chosen by kind. landscape spawns a flat Landscape actor labelled name (or landscapeName; an actor already under it is refused, NAME_TAKEN), its corner at location: componentCount {x, y} components (default 8 x 8), or the fewest that cover sizeX and sizeY (vertices like the editor Overall Resolution, or quads). Each component holds sectionsPerComponent (1 or 2) squared sections of quadsPerSection quads (7, 15, 31, 63 by default, 127 or 255). materialPath goes on it (default the engine grid material; one that does not load is refused, ASSET_NOT_FOUND). builtComponents, resolutionX/resolutionY and extentX/extentY (half the built size; a quad is 100 units) are measured from what was built, a build that makes no components fails (LANDSCAPE_BUILD_FAILED), and the level is left unsaved. grass_type saves a landscape grass type asset named name in path (default /Game/Landscape) that grows meshPath at density 1 per 10 square metres, scaled 0.8 to 1.2, randomly turned and aligned to the surface; a grass type already there is kept unchanged (alreadyExists) and another asset there is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS).
whenToUse: kind=landscape: A landscape must be created or modified in the current level.
kind=grass_type: A grass type asset is needed for landscape grass rendering.
whenNotToUse: kind=landscape: A landscape already exists and should be modified.
kind=grass_type: Foliage instances should be placed manually.

location.description: World-space location {x, y, z}.

sizeX.description: Landscape size along X, in vertices like the editor Overall Resolution (1009 is 16 components of 63 quads) or in quads; it becomes the fewest whole components that cover it.

sizeY.description: Landscape size along Y, in vertices like the editor Overall Resolution (1009 is 16 components of 63 quads) or in quads; it becomes the fewest whole components that cover it.

quadsPerSection.description: Quads per section: 7, 15, 31, 63 (default), 127 or 255. A component spans sectionsPerComponent sections.

sectionSize.description: Quads per section (same as quadsPerSection): 7, 15, 31, 63 (default), 127 or 255.

sectionsPerComponent.description: Sections per component side: 1 (default) or 2, for 2x2 sections per component.

path.description: Canonical /Game asset or directory path.

Which create landscape variant to run; omit for 'landscape'.

discovery.summary: Create a light actor in the level being edited: point, spot, directional, rect or sky (or any light class), at location (default 0, 0, 300), made Movable, with intensity, color and, in properties, shadow, radius and cone settings. The reply lists what was applied, refused (a setting this kind of light lacks) or adjusted; the spawn is one undo step and the level is left unsaved. During Play it still goes into the edited level, not the running game.
whenToUse: A point, spot, directional, rect or sky light must be added to the level being edited, with its intensity, color or shadow settings.
whenNotToUse: An existing light should be reconfigured: control_actor.edit_component sets its component values.
The light must exist in the running PIE world: manage_effect.create_dynamic_light spawns into the active world, this one into the level being edited.
manage_level.create_light runs this same handler; use this one, which documents every property.
The light is always created Movable; a static or stationary light needs its mobility changed afterwards with control_actor.edit_component.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

lightType.description: Light kind: point, spot, directional, rect or sky (any case), or the class name PointLight, SpotLight, DirectionalLight, RectLight or SkyLight. A light class of your own goes in lightClass.

lightClass.description: Light class name or path, for a class lightType does not name, including a Blueprint light (/Game/Lights/BP_Lamp.BP_Lamp_C); build_environment list_light_types lists the loaded ones. Wins over lightType.

name.description: Name for the new actor, asset, or volume.

location.description: World location {x, y, z}; 0, 0, 300 when omitted.

rotation.description: Rotation {pitch, yaw, roll} in degrees. A spot or directional light shines along its forward axis, so pitch -90 points it straight down.

intensity.description: Brightness: the light component's Intensity, set as given, in the component's own units (a directional light is in lux). Left out, the engine default stays. properties.intensity wins over it.

color.description: Light color {r, g, b, a}. Linear 0-1 channels, stored by the engine as the 8-bit sRGB color: {r: 1, g: 0.7, b: 0.42} reads back as (255, 218, 173). A missing channel reads 0 (alpha 1). properties.color wins over it.

properties.description: Light component settings, applied to the lights they fit; the reply lists what went in as details.applied, what did not as details.refused ("name: why") and any value replaced for being out of range as details.adjusted. Keys: intensity (0 or more; a negative reads 0), color (as above), castShadows (true or false), useAsAtmosphereSunLight (true or false; a directional light given properties is the atmosphere sun unless this says false), attenuationRadius (above 0, point and spot lights; an invalid value reads 1000), innerConeAngle and outerConeAngle (0 to 180 degrees, spot lights; clamped), sourceWidth and sourceHeight (above 0, rect lights; an invalid value reads 100). A sky light takes only the top-level intensity and color. Any other key, or one that does not fit the light, is refused by name.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Create a light actor in the level being edited: point, spot, directional, rect or sky (or any light class), at location (default 0, 0, 300), made Movable, with intensity, color and, in properties, shadow, radius and cone settings. The reply lists what was applied, refused (a setting this kind of light lacks) or adjusted; the spawn is one undo step and the level is left unsaved. During Play it still goes into the edited level, not the running game.

kind.description:
Which create lighting setup variant to run.

discovery.summary: Edit a landscape (landscapeName or landscapePath, else the first in the level), chosen by edit. paint_landscape paints a layer over a brush disc, a vertex region or the whole landscape, and paint_landscape_layer at one weight over a region; import_heightmap writes a raw 16-bit heightmap into its heights. Those three go into the edit layer being edited (else the first), are one undo step and are merged before the reply, so the drawn landscape and its collision show them. configure_landscape_lod sets LOD properties by name and reads them back; configure_landscape_material assigns its material; configure_landscape_splines replaces its splines with one through points that can deform the terrain and paint a layer; generate_lods gives static meshes simplified LODs.
whenToUse: edit=paint_landscape|paint_landscape_layer: A landscape must be created or modified in the current level.
edit=import_heightmap: A heightmap file must be imported to create or update a landscape.

edit=import_heightmap: The heightmap should be generated procedurally.
edit=configure_landscape_splines: Standalone spline actors should be used instead.

edit.description:
Which edit landscape variant to run.
paint_landscape: Paint a landscape layer (layerName) at strength over a brush disc (location + radius), a vertex region, or the whole landscape. The edit goes into the landscape's edit layer (the one being edited in Landscape mode, else the first; other layers still add on top), is one undo step (undo), and the layers are merged before the reply, so the drawn landscape and its collision show it.
paint_landscape_layer: Paint a landscape layer (layerName) at one weight (strength) over a vertex region, or the whole landscape. The edit goes into the landscape's edit layer (the one being edited in Landscape mode, else the first; other layers still add on top), is one undo step (undo), and the layers are merged before the reply, so the drawn landscape and its collision show it.
import_heightmap: Write a raw 16-bit heightmap file (heightmapPath, project-relative, no header, machine byte order, as export_heightmap writes it) into a landscape's heights, over its whole extent or region; the file must hold at least one sample per vertex of that area, row by row. The edit goes into the landscape's edit layer (the one being edited in Landscape mode, else the first; other layers still add on top), is one undo step (undo), and the layers are merged before the reply, so the drawn landscape and its collision show it.
configure_landscape_lod: Tune how a landscape lowers its detail with distance: settings sets its LOD properties by name, such as LOD0ScreenSize (where full detail ends, default 0.5), LOD0DistributionSetting (default 1.25) and LODDistributionSetting (the spacing of the other LODs, default 3; higher keeps detail farther), MaxLODLevel (-1 for no cap) and StaticLightingLOD; from UE 5.4 also bUseScalableLODSettings with the per-quality Scalable versions and LODBlendRange. It is one undo step, reaches the landscape's World Partition streaming proxies as an edit in the Details panel does, and reads back what was set (values). Nothing set is NO_SETTING_SUPPLIED; an unknown or bad value is CONFIGURATION_FAILED, listed in configurationErrors.
configure_landscape_material: Assign the material a landscape renders with (materialPath: a material or material instance; its layer blend nodes name the layers that can be painted), as one undo step. A path outside the project is refused, one that loads nothing is ASSET_NOT_FOUND and another kind of asset LOAD_FAILED. The reply gives landscapeName and landscapePath. Painting a layer creates its layer info when the landscape has none.
configure_landscape_splines: Replace a landscape's splines with one through the given points (width, loop, terrain deform, painted layer).
generate_lods: Give static mesh assets (foliage meshes included) numLODs LODs in all (default 4, LOD 0 included): each LOD keeps half the triangles of the one before, LODs past the count and hand-tuned LOD settings are replaced, and each mesh is rebuilt and saved. Engine meshes are not changed (engineContentPaths; ENGINE_CONTENT when nothing else was given): duplicate one into /Game first. The reply counts processed out of requested and lists notFoundPaths and notMeshPaths.

discovery.summary: Change the points of an actor's first spline component, chosen by edit; positions, rotations and tangents are in the spline actor's local space (subtract its location from a world point), and each edit is one undo step. add_point appends position, or inserts it at index, with pointType (default Curve) and optional tangents; set_point_position, set_point_rotation, set_point_scale and set_point_tangents change the point at pointIndex, which they require with their value (a lone arriveTangent sets both tangents); set_type sets splineType on pointIndex, or on every point when it is left out. An index past the last point is INVALID_INDEX and an unknown point type is refused.

actorName.description: Actor name in the current level.

actorPath.description: Object path of the spline actor; used when actorName is omitted.

index.description: Insert the point before this index; appended when omitted or out of range.

edit.description:
Which edit spline variant to run.
add_point: Add a point at position, in the spline actor's local space (subtract its location from a world point), to an actor's first spline component: appended, or inserted at index. pointType (default Curve) and arriveTangent and leaveTangent shape it; an unknown point type or a missing position is refused. One undo step.
set_point_position: Move the point at pointIndex of an actor's first spline component to position, in the spline actor's local space (subtract its location from a world point). Both are required; an index past the last point is INVALID_INDEX. One undo step.
set_point_rotation: Set the rotation of the point at pointIndex to pointRotation, in the spline actor's local space; both are required. One undo step.
set_point_scale: Set the scale (pointScale) of the point at pointIndex, which a spline mesh along it follows; both are required. One undo step.
set_point_tangents: Set the arrive and leave tangents of the point at pointIndex, in the spline actor's local space (subtract its location from a world point): a lone arriveTangent sets both, a lone leaveTangent keeps the arrive one. One undo step.
set_type: Set the type of the point at pointIndex, or of every point when pointIndex is left out: Linear, Curve (default), Constant, CurveClamped or CurveCustomTangent; another name is refused. The reply names the type set and pointsAffected. One undo step.

discovery.summary: Wear a landscape down the way water wears ground, so that every cell drains: fillDepressions (default true) raises each pit to where it would spill (its basin becomes a flat lake bed), valleys cuts valleys by stream power, droplets wash gullies into the slopes, talusAngle slumps what is steeper, and the pits that leaves are filled again. region limits it to some of the landscape's vertices (default all), its border held so the result joins the ground around it. Written into the landscape's edit layer (the one being edited, else the first, as sculpt writes) as one undo step and merged before the reply; dryRun computes all of it and writes nothing. The reply gives drains (every cell has a path to the border that never climbs, judged on the heights written; undrainedCells when not), depressionsFilled, maxLoweredCm, maxRaisedCm, changedCells, dropletsRun (the same seed and droplets give the same ground), editLayers (with more than one, the others still add on top of this one) and rivers: up to 20, largest catchment first, each {catchmentM2, lengthM, points} with its course in world cm from source to mouth (at most 64 points; a river crossing a filled lake runs straight over it), for water bodies, splines and roads. Refused, changing nothing: LANDSCAPE_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_REGION (outside the landscape, or under 5 vertices a side), INVALID_ARGUMENT (more than 4,194,304 vertices at once: name a region).
whenToUse: Sculpted, imported or noise terrain should look worn by water, with valleys, gullies and rivers, and no hollow that would hold water by accident.
Rivers are needed for water bodies, bridges or roads: their courses come back in world space.
whenNotToUse: One spot should rise, sink or flatten: sculpt or modify_heightmap.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

landscapeActorPath.description: Landscape actor path in the level.

region.description: Vertices to erode, {minX, minY, maxX, maxY} in the landscape's vertex grid (default all). Its border stays as it is.

fillDepressions.description: Raise every pit to where it would spill, so all ground drains (default true). false keeps basins: rivers then end in them, and drains is false.

valleys.description: How deep valleys cut, 0 to 1 (default 0.3; 0 skips): how far an erosion front travels up the largest river, as a share of the region's longer side, the same at any landscape size or resolution. Smaller rivers cut less (by the square root of their catchment).

droplets.description: Rain droplets that wash gullies into the slopes (default a quarter of the vertices, at most 200,000; 0 skips).

talusAngle.description: Degrees: slopes steeper than this slump until they are not (default 0, off). 30 to 40 is loose rock and soil.

riverAreaM2.description: Catchment in square metres that makes a river (default 1% of the region).

seed.description: Seed for the droplets (default 1): the same seed and droplets give the same ground.

dryRun.description: Compute and report, writing nothing (default false).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

region.description: The vertices eroded, {minX, minY, maxX, maxY}.

drains.description: Every cell has a path to the region's border that never climbs.

undrainedCells.description: Cells with no such path (fillDepressions false).

dropletsRun.description: Droplets run (fewer than asked only when a time guard stopped them).

editLayers.description: The landscape's edit layers (0 without them).

rivers.description: Up to 20 rivers, largest catchment first.

items.description: {catchmentM2, lengthM, points: [{x, y, z}] from source to mouth, world cm}.

undo.description: What editor undo takes back: {undoable, transactionScope}.

examples.title: Wear a landscape down the way water wears ground, so that every cell drains: fillDepressions (default true) raises each pit to where it would spill (its basin becomes a flat lake bed), valleys cuts valleys by stream power, droplets wash gullies into the slopes, talusAngle slumps what is steeper, and the pits that leaves are filled again. region limits it to some of the landscape's vertices (default all), its border held so the result joins the ground around it. Written into the landscape's edit layer (the one being edited, else the first, as sculpt writes) as one undo step and merged before the reply; dryRun computes all of it and writes nothing. The reply gives drains (every cell has a path to the border that never climbs, judged on the heights written; undrainedCells when not), depressionsFilled, maxLoweredCm, maxRaisedCm, changedCells, dropletsRun (the same seed and droplets give the same ground), editLayers (with more than one, the others still add on top of this one) and rivers: up to 20, largest catchment first, each {catchmentM2, lengthM, points} with its course in world cm from source to mouth (at most 64 points; a river crossing a filled lake runs straight over it), for water bodies, splines and roads. Refused, changing nothing: LANDSCAPE_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_REGION (outside the landscape, or under 5 vertices a side), INVALID_ARGUMENT (more than 4,194,304 vertices at once: name a region).

discovery.summary: Find a road between from and to that a vehicle could drive: no grade over maxGradePercent anywhere along it (default 10), every obstacle and gap kept half its width away (width, default 600 cm), and no corner tighter than turnRadius (default 1500 cm), so a slope too steep to take straight is climbed in turns and switchbacks (up a cone-shaped hill whose sides pass about three times the limit its straight runs may find no way to the top: NO_ROUTE then says how steep a route would be). The ground under a grid turned so both ends sit on its points (a margin of half their distance, or of half the road their difference in height needs at that grade, at least 50 m; cells of about half the turn radius, at most 400 a side) is read by vertical traces: a landscape is ground, or the actors in groundActors (with neither, the actor under from); anything else solid standing anywhere in a cell up to 3.3 m above the ground is an obstacle (a post or a thin wall included), and a place with no collision at all is a gap (a create_primitive mesh has none until configure_mesh_collision). The route is searched over every cell and the heading it is entered by (16 headings), then straightened wherever grade, clearance and radius still hold and the straight road stays within 25 cm of the ground. Reads only. The reply gives points (world cm, 10 cm above the ground, the first at from and the last at to), lengthM, climbM, and maxGradePercent and minTurnRadiusM measured on those points, switchbacks, groundGapCm (the farthest the straight road between two points strays from the ground), and two ready calls: nextCall lays the road with create_road_spline (a road slab named Road; rename it there), and on a landscape landscapeSplineCall makes the same route a landscape spline. Refused: POINT_BLOCKED (from or to on an obstacle or a gap), NO_ROUTE (only a route steeper than the limit reaches, with how steep; obstacles and gaps cut the ends apart; or the search ran out of time), ACTOR_NOT_FOUND (a groundActors name), INVALID_ARGUMENT.
whenToUse: A road, track or path must reach a place uphill or past buildings at a grade a vehicle can drive.
A road should look engineered: gentle grades, wide curves, switchbacks on a steep slope.
whenNotToUse: The route is already known: create_road_spline or configure_landscape_splines with its points.
A character's walking path: get_ai_info info path reads the nav mesh.

width.description: Road width in cm (default 600): obstacles and gaps stay half of it away, and the ready calls lay it this wide.

turnRadius.description: Tightest corner in cm (default 1500, a car; 600 a cart track, 3000 a fast road). It also sets the grid: cells of about half of it.

groundActors.description: Actors a road may run on (labels or names) instead of the landscape: a floor, a deck, a bridge.

minTurnRadiusM.description: Tightest corner on the points, in m (absent on a straight road).

switchbacks.description: Times the road turns back by more than 90 degrees.

groundGapCm.description: The farthest the straight road between two points strays from the ground, in cm.

nextCall.description: create_road_spline with the points and width, ready to send.

landscapeSplineCall.description: configure_landscape_splines with the points and the landscape, ready to send (on a landscape).

discovery.summary: Shape a landscape, chosen by sculptOp: sculpt raises, lowers or flattens the ground under a round brush at a world location; heightmap sets, raises, lowers, flattens or smooths a region of its vertices (raw heights or centimetres); material sets the material it renders with. sculpt and heightmap count the vertices that changed, write the landscape's edit layer (the one being edited, else the first) as one undo step, and merge the layers before the reply so rendering and collision follow; an unknown tool or operation is refused.
whenToUse: sculptOp=sculpt|heightmap: A landscape must be created or modified in the current level.
sculptOp=material: A landscape needs a different material assignment.
whenNotToUse: sculptOp=sculpt: The landscape should be modified via raw heightmap data.

sculptOp=material: The material should be configured with layer blends.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

landscapeActorPath.description: Landscape actor path in the level.

tool.description: Sculpt tool: Raise (default), Lower or Flatten (towards the location's z). Any other name is refused.

location.description: World-space location {x, y, z}.

skipFlush.description: Do not wait for the GPU (default false): the upload and the edit layer merge finish on a later editor tick, so read heights, paint or collision back only after that. Faster for many edits in a row.

operation.description: set (default), raise (add), lower (subtract), flatten or smooth.

heightData.description: Raw heights, 0-65535: 32768 sits at the landscape's own Z and 128 units are one landscape Z-scale step (ScaleZ cm). set takes one for the whole region or one per vertex; flatten takes the first (default 32768).

amount.description: raise and lower: the centimetres to move every vertex in the region, above 0.

sculptOp.description:
Which sculpt variant to run; omit for 'sculpt'.
sculpt: Sculpt a landscape at location (world space) with a round brush: tool Raise (default) or Lower moves the ground strength x 100 cm at the brush centre (strength default 0.1), Flatten pulls it toward location.z by the strength fraction. radius is in world units (default 1000) and falloff (default 0.5) is the outer share of it that fades out. modifiedVertices counts the vertices that moved (0 when all were clamped); an unknown tool, or a location off the landscape (OUT_OF_BOUNDS), is refused. The edit goes into the landscape's edit layer (the one being edited in Landscape mode, else the first; other layers still add on top), is one undo step (undo), and the layers are merged before the reply, so the drawn landscape and its collision show it.
heightmap: Change a landscape's heights over a region of its vertices (minX..maxX and minY..maxY, or region; default the whole landscape) by operation: set (default) writes heightData raw heights, one for the whole region or one per vertex row by row; raise and lower (add, subtract) move it by amount cm; flatten sets it to heightData[0]; smooth runs one 3x3 averaging pass. An unknown operation, a heightData count that fits neither form, or raise/lower without amount is refused; modifiedVertices counts the vertices that changed. The edit goes into the landscape's edit layer (the one being edited in Landscape mode, else the first; other layers still add on top), is one undo step (undo), and the layers are merged before the reply, so the drawn landscape and its collision show it.
material: Set the material a landscape renders with, in one undo step: materialPath must load as a material or material instance (ASSET_NOT_FOUND when nothing is there, LOAD_FAILED for another asset type). paint_landscape_layer then paints the layers its Landscape Layer Blend names.

discovery.summary: Move actors until the relations stated hold, overlapping nothing, in one undo step: say where things go (["Lamp on Table", "Chair_1 nextTo Table", "Chair_1 facing Table", "Shelf against Wall"]) instead of computing coordinates. The relations are those execute's expect judges: A on B (resting on its top), A inside B, A nextTo B (side by side, touching), A against B (touching, its back to B, its front away), A facing B (the line ahead of its front, its X axis, meets B or points within 20 degrees of the centre of B; beside a side of B it turns square to it) and A near B within d (cm, default 100). A solver plans from where the actors stand now, keeping a rough placement wherever it already fits: each actor is a box turned about Z (what it draws), and their places and turns are annealed over how far each relation misses, how deep they overlap each other or the scene around them, and how far they wander; then each contact is snapped exact. What rests on a moved actor moves with it. Each relation is then judged by the engine as expect judges it.
whenToUse: Furnishing or dressing a scene from a description: the lamp on the table, chairs beside it facing it, the shelf against the wall.
Fixing a rough layout so its pieces touch, rest and face as intended, without reading or computing coordinates.
Checking a layout plan first with dryRun, which moves nothing.
whenNotToUse: Moving one actor to known coordinates: use set_transform.
Only resting sunk or floating actors on the surface under them, or pushing intersecting ones apart: use fix_placement.
Reading how a level is arranged now: use describe_relations.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

relations.description: What should hold, one relation per entry between two actors by name (names with spaces in double quotes): A on B, A inside B, A nextTo B, A against B, A facing B, or A near B within d. Anything else (a comparison, exists, not, and, or) is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT, as is a relation from an actor to itself; a name that matches no actor refuses with ACTOR_NOT_FOUND (missing lists them) and nothing moves.

actorNames.description: The actors that may move; omit to move every relation's left-hand actor. A floor or landscape, an actor with Lock Actor Movement and an attached actor never move: they come back under skipped with the reason. What is not named stays put and is kept clear of.

dryRun.description: Plan only: moved lists where each would go and relations says whether the plan meets each, judged on the plan's boxes; nothing moves (default false).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

moved.description: Each actor moved (or that would move under dryRun) as {actorName, from [x, y, z], to [x, y, z], turned (degrees about Z)}.

relations.description: Each relation as {relation, verdict (ok or failed), actual}: judged by the engine after the move as expect judges it (actual says what was found: "touching its -Y side, its back to it", "it rests on 'Book' instead"); under dryRun judged on the plan.

unmet.description: How many relations do not hold: 0 when every one does. Relations that contradict each other or leave no free place stay unmet.

steps.description: Annealing steps run (it stops at a fixed count or after 8 seconds).

skipped.description: Actors that would move but never do, as {actorName, reason}.

dryRun.description: Present and true when nothing moved because dryRun was set.

discovery.summary: Sweep every actor in the level and report the ones that interpenetrate another actor, sit sunk below the surface under them, float above it, lean off vertical, or have a face in the same plane as another surface (z-fighting flicker), and the unfinished content they show (a slot on the engine's default grid material, a text still reading "Text", a copy pasted onto the original); or, with blueprintPath, the mesh parts of one actor Blueprint that are buried in each other or sunk below its capsule.
whenToUse: A level was assembled programmatically and needs checking before anyone looks at it.
Actors appear to clip through each other, stand in the ground, or lie on their side.
A placement pass should be verified without flying the viewport around to eyeball it.
Judging what was already in the level, or what an import, a merge or a script outside the MCP left: a call's own warnings cover only the actors that call changed.
A level must be checked for slop before anyone plays it: default_material, placeholder_text and duplicate name what was left unfinished.

Surfaces flicker, or another material shows through in ragged patches (z-fighting): the coplanar face pairs responsible are listed under coplanarFaces, with the direction to push each one; control_actor fix_coplanar fixes them all in one call.

A character, vehicle or prop is assembled from mesh components in a Blueprint (a driver in a seat, legs on a body): blueprintPath checks every part against every other on their real triangles and against the capsule bottom, so a leg sunk into the seat or a foot through the floor is named with its depth.
whenNotToUse: Checking only what one call just did: every call that spawns, moves, duplicates or re-meshes actors already runs these checks on the actors it changed (spawn and set_transform answer placementWarning; every other call lists what it finds in its reply's warnings).

A finding is a deliberate composition (a keep bedding its towers into its platform, an island meant to hang in the air, a signpost leaning by design): tag that actor mcp.placement.ok with control_actor.add_tag and it drops out of the sweep entirely -- as tilt subject, and as both subject and target for overlap -- rather than being re-reported every time. Coplanar faces are still reported for tagged actors, because they flicker whatever the intent.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

nameFilter.description: Only examine actors whose label or object name contains this text (an actor that shares its label with another is reported by object name, e.g. StaticMeshActor_75). Omit to sweep the whole level.

limit.description: Maximum problem entries to return (1-200, default 25). Entries come worst-first, so a small limit still shows the placements that matter; flagged is always the true total.

minSeverity.description: Drop findings whose severity (worst penetration, ground error, tilt displacement, or the side of the largest z-fighting patch, in world units) is below this. Use it to skip cosmetic grazes on a large level.

kinds.description: Report only these problem kinds, e.g. ["coplanar"] to list z-fighting alone in a platformer full of platforms that float on purpose. default_material: a visible mesh slot drawing the engine's default grid (no material, or one made from it). placeholder_text: a text render still reading the engine default "Text" (give it its label, or an empty text when a script writes it in play). duplicate: an actor that is a copy of another in the same place with the same meshes, drawn twice. An actor whose worst problem is another kind still counts for these, as for coplanar, when its contentIssues hold them. An actor whose worst problem is another kind still counts for coplanar when it has coplanarFaces. An actor whose bounds touch or overlap another actor's vertical face (a window band on a hall, an awning on a facade) is mounted, never floating or unsupported. Two faces pointing down with something solid right below them (pieces lying on a floor) are not reported as coplanar: no camera sees them. Omit for every kind.

maxTilt.description: Degrees off vertical an actor may lean before it is reported as tilted (1-90, default 30). Lean is the angle between the up vector of the actor and world up, so yaw never counts and a fully inverted actor reads 180. Raise it for a level whose props are deliberately strewn about; lower it to catch subtler leans.

blueprintPath.description: Audit the mesh parts of this actor Blueprint instead of the level: a preview instance (the level is untouched) has every visible static mesh part measured against every other and against its ground (a Character's capsule bottom). problems[] then lists componentName, kind (buried: inside otherComponent; sunk: below the ground), depth and severity in cm, insideShare and the issue; minSeverity is the tolerance (default 0.5 cm), and kinds, nameFilter and maxTilt are refused (INVALID_ARGUMENT). A part tagged mcp.placement.ok in its ComponentTags is a deliberate embed (an eyeball in its socket) and is left out; mcp.placement.ok:<component> accepts the embed in that one part only and keeps every other check. Blueprint component edits report the same for the parts they touch, as partWarnings.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

flagged.description: Actors with a placement problem (part findings, with blueprintPath), before the limit.

byKind.description: Count of flagged actors per problem kind: sunk, floating, overlapping, unsupported, tilted, coplanar, default_material, placeholder_text, duplicate.

problems.description: Findings worst-first: actorName, kind, severity in world units, the issue in words, suggestedZ when a resting height can be computed, overlappingActors when it intersects others (up to 8, each with actorName, actorClass and penetrationDepth), and coplanarFaces when faces z-fight: one entry per pair with direction (the axis both faces point along, e.g. -Y), component, otherActor, otherComponent, gap and overlapU x overlapV. Fix a pair by moving the face about 2 units along direction (this piece shows) or against it (the other shows, right for a piece sunk into it, such as a ramp in the floor), by moving or scaling the actor. contentIssues lists the unfinished content it shows: kind (default_material, placeholder_text, duplicate), component and the issue; their severity is the size in cm of what shows them.

truncationNote.description: Present when the limit cut the list short; says how to reach the rest.

blueprintPath.description: With blueprintPath: the Blueprint whose parts were measured.

groundZ.description: With blueprintPath: the ground the parts were measured against (the capsule bottom of the preview instance); absent when the root is not a capsule.

actorNames.description: Actor names to act on (batch delete).

discovery.summary: Read the level back as relations between its actors, the way one describes a room: what rests on what (on), what hangs on a wall (mounted), what stands inside what (inside), what touches what side by side (nextTo) and what each actor's front points at (faces); which actors stand together (groups), which copies of one prop line up in rows or grids or stand in a ring; and the scene's roles: the ground, the sun's elevation and azimuth, the sky actors, player starts, cameras and the navigation area. Read only.
whenToUse: Checking that a layout reads as intended (the lamp on the table, the chairs facing it, the shelf against the wall) without reading coordinates.
Learning how an existing level is arranged before adding to it: what stands on the floor, what forms a row or a ring, where the player starts.
After moving or spawning props, confirming what each now rests on or touches.
whenNotToUse: Finding what is sunk, floating or intersecting: use audit_placement, and fix_placement to fix it.
Reading one actor's exact location, rotation or bounds: use get_transform or get_bounding_box.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

kinds.description: Which relations and patterns to report: on (rests on the actor under it; read from short traces down from its bottom, so an actor without collision rests on nothing), mounted (held from the side, as a picture on a wall), inside (within another's bounds, the tightest such), nextTo (side by side, their sides within 2 cm, judged on boxes turned with the actors), faces (the line ahead of its front, its X axis, meets the nearest actor that is not a copy of it, or points within 20 degrees of the centre of that actor; a prop without a front, such as a crate or a table, faces whatever lies along its X axis), groups, rows (with grids), rings and roles. Omit for all of them but faces, which is listed only when kinds names it or actorNames or nameFilter narrow the report: across a whole level it would name a front for most props.

actorNames.description: Report only the relations these actors take part in, as subject or object, and the patterns they belong to; the rest of the level is still judged, so a lamp still rests on a table nobody named. Names not found come back under missing; when none is found the call fails with ACTOR_NOT_FOUND.

nameFilter.description: Report only the relations and patterns of actors whose label or object name contains this text; with actorNames, of the named actors that also match.

center.description: With radius: judge only the actors whose bounds come within radius cm of this point (named actors always count). Refused without radius.

radius.description: With center: the radius in cm of the area judged; above 0. Refused without center.

maxActors.description: At most this many actors are judged (1-400, default 300): named actors first, then the nearest to center, else the largest. A level cut short says so with truncated and actorsInScope.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

relations.description: One row per relation as [subject, relation, object] or [subject, relation, object, detail], grouped by subject, at most 200: ["Lamp", "on", "Table"], ["Chair_1", "faces", "Table", "25 cm away"], ["Shelf", "nextTo", "Wall", "touching its +Y side"]. An on row whose detail says an edge of it rests there stands only partly on that actor. What rests on the ground is listed only for the actors asked about by actorNames or nameFilter; roles.ground counts the rest.

groups.description: Actors standing together, each {members, center, size}: every member within about a footprint of another, as a table with its chairs and the lamp on it. A level that is one group lists none. members names at most 24; memberCount says how many there are when more.

rows.description: Copies of one prop (same class and size) in a line along X or Y, each {members, along (x or y), spacing in cm, even}: even is true when every step is within 5 percent of the spacing. members names at most 24; memberCount says how many there are when more.

grids.description: Copies of one prop in rows and columns, each {members, columns, rows, spacing [x, y] in cm, even}; their rows are not listed again under rows. members names at most 24; memberCount says how many there are when more.

rings.description: Copies of one prop standing evenly around a centre at one distance, each {members, center, radius in cm}. members names at most 24; memberCount says how many there are when more.

roles.description: The scene's roles: ground {name, supports (how many actors rest on it), top (its height)}, the ground-like actor most rest on; sun {name, elevation, azimuth}, the brightest directional light as the sun's angle above the horizon and its direction in degrees from +X toward +Y; sky (the sky atmosphere, sky light, fog, cloud and sky sphere actors); playerStarts and cameras [{name, location}], forPlayer on a camera a player views through from the start; playArea {center, size}, the navigation mesh bounds.

actorsExamined.description: Actors judged: visible actors with bounds in the area, lights, volumes and other bounds-only actors left out.

truncated.description: Present when maxActors cut the actors judged (actorsInScope says how many there were) or 200 relations cut the list (relationCount says how many there were).

actorsInScope.description: Present when maxActors cut the list: how many actors the area held.

relationCount.description: Present when the relations list was cut at 200: how many there were.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

componentName.description: Target component name on the actor.

properties.description: Component property key-value pairs. Each key is a name or dotted path, as propertyName takes it (BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled works). Collision goes through the component setters: CollisionProfileName (a preset), CollisionEnabled, CollisionResponses ({"Pawn": "Ignore"}), PhysMaterialOverride (a physical material path, None to clear).

meshPath.description: Static mesh asset (/Game path) to show on the new component; only a StaticMeshComponent takes one. A mesh that does not load fails the call, naming the component that was still added.

actorNames.description: Several actors whose component of componentName takes the same properties in one call and one undo step, in place of actorName (a row of point lights, each LightComponent0). The actors changed are counted in updatedActors and listed under affectedActors (which the receipt lists as changes), names that matched no actor come back in missing, and an actor whose component did not take everything is a results row {actorName, error} that fails the call PARTIAL_FAILURE.

propertyName.description: Component property to read or write: a name (Intensity), or a dotted path through structs at any depth (BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled, LightmassSettings.bShadowIndirectOnly). A bare name that is not on the component itself resolves to the one struct member carrying it (CollisionEnabled reads and writes BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled); a name several structs carry is refused with the full paths to choose from.

value.description: Property value (any type).

edit.description:
Which edit component variant to run.
add: Add a new component of a given type to an actor. If any requested property (or meshPath) does not apply, the call fails naming what did not, although the component was added.
remove: Remove a component that was added to this actor (edit=add, or by hand in the editor), by its exact name, in one undo step, leaving the level unsaved. A near miss is refused with COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND naming the closest component; a component of the actor class or its Blueprint, or the root, is refused with COMPONENT_NOT_REMOVABLE (a Blueprint one comes out with edit_scs).
set_property: Set one or more properties on a named actor component. For RelativeScale3D/RelativeLocation, note that a child inherits its parent's scale: Unreal multiplies parent and child scale COMPONENT-WISE in the child's own local axes, and rotation does NOT permute which axis each factor lands on. World size = ParentScale * ChildScale * MeshExtent per local axis, and world offset = ParentScale * RelativeLocation. Under a parent scaled non-uniformly, divide the offset you want by the parent scale on that axis.
set_properties: Alias of edit=set_property. The bridge dispatches both names to the same handler.

findBy=class: Preferred when callers use the explicit find_actors_by_class verb.
findBy=name: Preferred when callers use the explicit find_actors_by_name verb.
whenNotToUse: findBy=class: A tag-based lookup is more appropriate (use find_by_tag).
findBy=name: Actors should be located by tag (use find_by_tag).
findBy=mesh: The meshes and materials of one known actor are wanted (use get_components).
findBy=material: The materials of one known actor are wanted (use get_components).
findBy=material: The assets that reference a material are wanted, not the actors placed in the level (use asset.inspect_asset with lookup=dependencies and referencers=true).

limit.description: Most actors to return (1-1000, default 200); a longer match list is cut and reports truncated and totalCount.

name.description: Actor name or search query.

meshPath.description: Static mesh asset path, with or without the object name: /Game/Meshes/SM_Rock or /Engine/BasicShapes/Cube. An actor matches when a StaticMeshComponent of it (an instanced or hierarchical one too) draws exactly this mesh.

materialPath.description: Material or material instance asset path, with or without the object name: /Game/Materials/M_Rock. A component matches when a slot of it, an override or the mesh's own default, is exactly this asset or a dynamic instance made from it. Instances of a material are not followed: ask for each instance by its own path.

findBy.description:
Which find variant to run.
class: Find the actors in the level of a class or any subclass of it (a short native name such as PointLight, /Script/Engine.PointLight, or a Blueprint asset path), each with name and path: the first limit (default 200), with truncated and totalCount when more match. A class that resolves to nothing is refused with CLASS_NOT_FOUND, naming assets of that name.
name: Find the actors in the level whose label, object name or path contains a query (case-insensitive; a full object path is cut to its actor name), each with label, name, path and class: the first limit (default 200), with truncated and totalCount when more match. With no match, similar offers labels that match once case, separators and leading zeros are ignored.
mesh: Find the actors in the level that draw a static mesh (instanced and foliage components included), each with the components that do.
material: Find the actors in the level with a component that uses a material in any slot, as an override or as its mesh's default, each with the components and slots that do.

name.description: Actor name.

path.description: Actor path.

totalCount.description: Present only when limit cut the list: how many actors matched in all.

truncated.description: True when limit cut the list short; totalCount says how many matched.

similar.description: Only when nothing matched: up to 10 labels that contain the query once case, separators and leading zeros are ignored ("Bug1" finds Bug_01 and Bug_10).

worldSearched.description: The world searched: the Play-In-Editor world while a session runs, else the editor world.

whenNotToUse: A specific actor name is known (use find_by_name).

tag.description: Actor tag: one entry in the Tags list of an actor (not a Gameplay Tag) to add, remove, find or delete by.

limit.description: Most actors to return (1-1000, default 200); a longer match list is cut and reports truncated and totalCount.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

name.description: Actor name.

path.description: Actor path.

totalCount.description: Present only when limit cut the list: how many actors matched in all.

truncated.description: True when limit cut the list short; totalCount says how many matched.

discovery.summary: Fix z-fighting in one call: every actor with a face in the same plane as another surface moves a unit, so one surface is clearly in front, repeating until nothing is left to move. A piece lying wholly inside the other face (a door on a wall) comes forward; one only partly inside (a ramp sunk into the floor) goes back so the other shows. Two parts of one Blueprint actor are parted in the Blueprint itself, so every placed copy is fixed at once.
whenToUse: audit_placement reported coplanar faces, or surfaces flicker between two materials.
A level was built from boxes placed flush against each other and should be cleaned up before anyone looks at it.
whenNotToUse: Only some actors may move: limit the call with nameFilter. A tag of mcp.placement.ok does not exempt an actor, because no two faces flicker on purpose.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

nameFilter.description: Only fix pairs where the label or object name of either actor contains this text. Omit for the whole level.

distance.description: How far each face moves, in world units (0.1-20, default 1): far enough for the depth buffer, too little to see.

dryRun.description: List the moves without making them (default false).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

pairsFound.description: Coplanar face pairs found before fixing.

remainingPairs.description: Coplanar pairs still found afterwards; run audit_placement with kinds ["coplanar"] to see them.

passes.description: Passes made: a move can line an actor up with a neighbour that moved the same way, so the fix repeats (at most four passes; one under dryRun).

dryRun.description: Whether nothing was changed.

moved.description: One entry per actor: actorName, offset {x, y, z} it moved by, resized when both of its faces on one axis moved (for example "grew 2.0 units along X"), and pairs, each face with the other actor and whether it was brought forward or pulled back.

blueprintsFixed.description: Pairs inside one Blueprint actor, fixed in the Blueprint: which part moved off which, and where it now sits in every placed copy (the Blueprint is compiled and saved).

skipped.description: Pairs left alone, each with the reason and what to do instead.

discovery.summary: Fix what audit_placement reports, judged by its own rules: a sunk actor moves up and a floating one down onto the surface under it, and intersecting actors are pushed apart the shortest way out of each other, measured on their collision (the smaller moves further; floors, landscapes, locked and attached actors never move). kinds names which of sunk, floating and overlapping to fix, since each can be deliberate. Every move is one undo step; a run checks what it moved again, up to three rounds, and dryRun lists the moves without making them.
whenToUse: audit_placement, or the warnings of a spawn or a move, reported actors sunk into the floor, floating above it or intersecting each other.
A layout built by spawning at guessed heights must be settled onto its floor and pulled out of itself in one call.
whenNotToUse: Faces that flicker (z-fighting): use fix_coplanar.

An overlap or a height that is deliberate (a rock bedded in terrain, a floating platform, a kitbashed cliff): leave its kind out of kinds, limit the call with actorNames or nameFilter, or tag the actor mcp.placement.ok (control_actor.add_tag) so neither the audit nor this call judges it.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

kinds.description: What to fix, as audit_placement names it: sunk (moved up by its depth, onto the surface under it), floating (moved down by its clearance onto that surface; mounted actors, held from the side, are never floating), overlapping (pushed out of the actors it intersects). Required: every kind can be deliberate.

actorNames.description: Only these actors may move, by the names audit_placement reports. Names not found come back under missing; what they intersect stays put and they are pushed off it. A floor, a locked or an attached actor among them is listed under skipped with the reason.

nameFilter.description: Only actors whose label or object name contains this text may move. Omit it, with no actorNames, to fix every actor in the level.

dryRun.description: List the first round of moves without making them (default false).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examined.description: Actors that may move and were checked.

flagged.description: Of those, how many showed a kind asked for.

rounds.description: Rounds made: a move can land an actor in another, so what moved is checked again (at most three; one under dryRun).

remaining.description: Actors still showing a kind asked for afterwards: flagged ones it could not move, and moved ones a move left wrong (their rows carry remainingWarning). Under dryRun, every flagged one.

dryRun.description: Whether nothing was changed.

moved.description: One row per actor moved (or that would move): actorName, offset {x, y, z} in total, fixed (the kinds it was moved for) and remainingWarning, the audit's words for what is still wrong with it.

skipped.description: Actors left alone, each {actorName, reason}: one that never moves, a pair whose collision cannot be measured (instanced, skeletal or landscape bodies: separate those by hand) or whose collision does not touch (only their bounding boxes overlap).

affectedActors.description: The actors moved (not under dryRun); the receipt lists them as changes.

undo.description: What editor undo takes back: {undoable, transactionScope, steps}; every move of the call is one step. Absent under dryRun.

solverLimitReached.description: Present when the call stopped at its 4096 collision queries: run it again, or narrow it with nameFilter.

timeLimitReached.description: Present when no further round started because the call had run 15 seconds: run it again for the rest.

Every move is one undo step; a run checks what it moved again, up to three rounds, and dryRun lists the moves without making them.
