discovery.summary: Read one property's value and type from a named component on a live actor, or from a Blueprint's own component (blueprintPath, no instance needed); dotted paths reach into structs.
whenToUse: A component property value must be inspected.
A component template on a Blueprint with no instance in the level must be read.
whenNotToUse: The property should be changed (use set_component_property).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

blueprintPath.description: Canonical /Game Blueprint asset path. Reads the component template on the Blueprint CDO instead of a live actor, so a Blueprint with no instance in the level can still be inspected. Supply this or actorName.

componentName.description: Target component name on the actor.

propertyName.description: Component property to read or write: a name (Intensity), or a dotted path through structs at any depth (BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled, LightmassSettings.bShadowIndirectOnly). A bare name that is not on the component itself resolves to the one struct member carrying it (CollisionEnabled reads and writes BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled); a name several structs carry is refused with the full paths to choose from.

propertyPath.description: Same as propertyName (a name or a dotted path such as BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled); used when propertyName is absent.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

value.description: Property value (any type).

examples.title: Read one property's value and type from a named component on a live actor, or from a Blueprint's own component (blueprintPath, no instance needed); dotted paths reach into structs.

discovery.summary: List an actor's components (info components, the default): each with name, class, path, relative location, rotation and scale (and worldScale when a parent scales it), attach parent and visibility; componentNames keeps only those, naming the others in missingComponents. A Blueprint asset path lists its class default, which holds only the native components, not the ones the Blueprint adds (read those with edit_scs). Or read its bounds (bounds): origin and half-size extent of every component, colliding or not. The running game copy while Play runs.
whenToUse: info=components: The component composition of an actor must be inspected.
info=bounds: The spatial extent of an actor must be measured.
whenNotToUse: info=components: A single component property is needed (use get_component_property).
info=bounds: The actor has no renderable components (bounds are undefined).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

componentNames.description: Return only these components, by name (case-insensitive); a name that matches none is listed under missingComponents.

info.description:
Which get components variant to run; omit for 'components'.
components: List all components attached to an actor with their relative transforms.
bounds: Read the world-space bounding box of an actor; normalizes to get_bounding_box.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

name.description: Component name.

staticMesh.description: Static mesh asset path (static mesh components).

materials.description: Material drawn in each slot, overrides included (mesh components).

origin.description: World-space centre of the bounding box as [x, y, z].

extent.description: Half-size of the bounding box along each axis as [x, y, z].

examples.title: List an actor's components (info components, the default): each with name, class, path, relative location, rotation and scale (and worldScale when a parent scales it), attach parent and visibility; componentNames keeps only those, naming the others in missingComponents. A Blueprint asset path lists its class default, which holds only the native components, not the ones the Blueprint adds (read those with edit_scs). Or read its bounds (bounds): origin and half-size extent of every component, colliding or not. The running game copy while Play runs.

discovery.summary: Read where an actor is (the player's pawn too): its transform now, or watch it over game time in PIE (motion): location, velocity, rotation, chosen properties and points on it (bones, sockets, components, with their height over the ground) at every interval, to prove a jump, launch, patrol, fall, foot plant or a rocking hull in one call.
whenToUse: readMode=transform: The current transform of an actor must be inspected.
readMode=motion: A jump, spring launch, moving platform, enemy patrol or fall must be proven in PIE without a sleep-and-poll loop.
readMode=motion: The peak height, landing point or path of a moving actor is needed.

readMode=motion: An input must land at an exact moment (jump when a platform appears): inputs and startWhen run the whole timeline inside one call, so the caller's own delay between calls cannot shift it.
readMode=motion: Feet must be proven to plant without sliding, sinking or floating, or a hand or muzzle must be followed: points with groundTrace measure it per point.
readMode=motion: A pawn dies, or a trigger fires, and what touched it is unknown: overlaps names every actor that began touching it, sample by sample.

readMode=motion: An actor that does not exist yet must be watched from its first frame (a projectile, a thrown or dropped object, an enemy of a wave): spawnOf names its class, and the first one the game spawns after the call is watched.
whenNotToUse: readMode=transform: The transform should be changed (use set_transform).
readMode=motion: Nothing is playing: the editor world does not simulate (start PIE with control_editor.play).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level; while PIE runs, PlayerPawn names the player's pawn (PlayerController, GameMode, GameState, PlayerState and HUD work too).

spawnOf.description: In place of actorName, for an actor the game has not spawned yet: its class (a Blueprint as BP_Thing or its _C path, a native class by its short name; a subclass counts too). The call waits for the first one spawned after it and watches it from its first frame; actorName in the reply names it.

spawnWaitSeconds.description: With spawnOf: game seconds to wait for the spawn (default 10, at most 30); nothing spawned ends with endedBecause spawnTimeout and no samples. The wait comes out of maxRealSeconds, so the wait and the run still answer inside it.

durationSeconds.description: Game seconds to watch (default 2, at most 30). Game time, so a clock slowed with set_game_speed still covers the same span of play; a run that needs more wall-clock time than maxRealSeconds stops there (endedBecause realTimeCap).

intervalSeconds.description: Game seconds between samples (default 0.05; 0 samples every frame). At most 400 samples are kept.

propertyNames.description: Actor properties read at every sample, each as JSON (a number, true or false, the name of an enum value, the path of an object, or an array of them), e.g. ["bDead", "HP"], or a component's as "Component.Property" ("Visual.RelativeScale3D" catches a squash on landing), the component by its name or by the actor property that holds it ("CharacterMovement.MaxWalkSpeed"); a name that resolves to nothing is listed under missingProperties.

maxRealSeconds.description: Wall-clock cap (default 25, at most 50): the run stops here and reports how much game time it covered, so a long run or an editor throttled to 3 fps still answers before a client that gives up at 30 s. Raise it only for a client that waits longer.

key.description: Key name as simulate_input takes it: SpaceBar, D, A, Left, Enter.

atSeconds.description: Game seconds after the run starts to press it (default 0).

inputs.description: Keys pressed and released at exact game times during the run (at most 32), e.g. [{"key":"D","atSeconds":0,"holdSeconds":2},{"key":"SpaceBar","atSeconds":0.6,"holdSeconds":0.2}]. A key still held when the run ends is released.

points.description: Places on the actor sampled with it (at most 8): a component by its name (LegL), a bone or socket of any of its components (foot_l, hand_r), or a component's own socket as Component.Socket (Weapon.Muzzle). Each sample's points gives each one's world location [x, y, z]; a name the actor lacks is refused with the names it has. Fewer samples are kept with points: 400 x 2 / (2 + points).

groundTrace.description: With points: each sample's aboveGround gives each point's height over the first surface below it that blocks Visibility (the actor and what is attached to it ignored), negative when the point is inside that surface, and pointStats sums up its contact.

contactCm.description: With groundTrace: how far above its own lowest height a point still counts as planted (default 2 cm), so an ankle bone that never reaches the floor still counts as down when the foot is.

overlaps.description: Also watch which actors overlap the watched one, checked every frame: a sample names those that began (overlapsBegan) or stopped (overlapsEnded) touching it since the sample before, and overlapped lists every actor it touched. Finds what killed a pawn, what a pickup or trigger fired on, or an enemy wandering into a spawn point.

actorName.description: Actor whose property starts the run.

propertyName.description: That actor's property, as propertyNames reads it: bActorEnableCollision, or a component's as Component.Property (CharacterMovement.MovementMode starts the run on a landing when equals is MOVE_Walking).

equals.description: Value that starts the run, as samples show it (true, false, 3, "Walking").

waitForChange.description: Default true: start only when the value BECOMES equals (a platform appearing), not while it already is.

maxWaitSeconds.description: Game seconds to wait before giving up with endedBecause startWhenTimeout (default 10, at most 30).

startWhen.description: Hold the run (samples and inputs) until another actor's property takes a value, so the timeline starts on a game event instead of whenever the call arrived.

readMode.description:
Which get transform variant to run; omit for 'transform'.
transform: Read the world transform (location, rotation, scale) of an actor.
motion: Watch an actor over game time in Play-In-Editor and return its location, velocity, rotation and chosen properties at every interval, plus start/end and min/max extents, in one call; it can also follow points on the actor (bones, sockets, components) with their height over the ground, press keys at exact game times (inputs) and wait for another actor's property to change before it starts (startWhen). The warnings say what the game logged while it ran, and a Blueprint runtime error names the node, graph and Blueprint that raised it.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

location.description: World or relative location as [x, y, z].

rotation.description: Rotation as [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees.

actorName.description: The actor watched.

samples.description: One entry per sample: t (game seconds since the start), location [x, y, z], velocity [x, y, z] (cm/s: the movement or physics velocity, or for an actor moved by setting its location, the one its positions show since the sample before), rotation [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees (on the first sample and on each one where it changed, so a sample without it still has the last one written), properties, with points their world locations (points) and heights over the ground (aboveGround, with groundTrace; a point with nothing below it within 10 m is left out), and with overlaps the actors that began or stopped touching it since the sample before (overlapsBegan, overlapsEnded).

overlapped.description: With overlaps: every actor that touched the watched one during the run, first touch first; empty when nothing did.

passedThrough.description: Surfaces the actor went through between two frames while its collision was on, checked every frame, at most three: t, actorName and componentName of the surface, location and speed (cm/s). A fast physics body crosses a thin surface (a Plane has no thickness) between physics steps; a warning says so.

endedBecause.description: duration, realTimeCap, sampleCap, actorDestroyed (the actor was destroyed while its level kept running), levelChanged (the game loaded a level and PIE runs on in it: a death that reloads the level, or travel to the next one), worldEnded (PIE stopped), startWhenTimeout (startWhen never happened within maxWaitSeconds), spawnTimeout (spawnOf: nothing of the class spawned within spawnWaitSeconds) or gamePaused (game time stood still for 3 s: a title or pause menu holds the game; the warning says how to get past it).

inputsApplied.description: One entry per input: key, at, hold, and down/up, the game seconds since the start when it was pressed and released (up is when the run ended for a key still held).

waitedSeconds.description: Game seconds spent waiting for startWhen before the run began, or for a spawnOf spawn that never came.

min.description: Smallest x, y and z sampled (the lowest point is min[2]).

max.description: Largest x, y and z sampled (the peak height is max[2]).

missingProperties.description: propertyNames the actor's class does not have.

pointStats.description: Per point: min and max [x, y, z] over the run; with groundTrace also minAboveGround and maxAboveGround (a negative minimum means it sank into the surface, a large one that it never touched it), contactSeconds (time spent planted) and contactSlip (cm it moved across the ground while planted: a planted foot that slides shows here).

windowRestored.description: True when the editor window was minimized: a minimized editor runs PIE at about 3 fps, so it was put back on screen, without taking focus, before the run and is minimized again when the run ends. The background CPU throttle (Use Less CPU when in Background) is off for the run only, whatever the window did.

examples.title: Read where an actor is (the player's pawn too): its transform now, or watch it over game time in PIE (motion): location, velocity, rotation, chosen properties and points on it (bones, sockets, components, with their height over the ground) at every interval, to prove a jump, launch, patrol, fall, foot plant or a rocking hull in one call.

discovery.summary: List actors in the current level with their label, class, location, rotation and scale, plus any propertyNames values, narrowed by name filter, tag, class or outliner folder; page on with offset. near (a world point) with radius is how to find what is near a point, nearest first, each with its distance. summary counts the level by class, tag and folder instead.
whenToUse: The actors present in the level must be enumerated.
Every actor with one tag, of one class or in one outliner folder must be found, for example to see what a delete_by_tag would remove.
Something seen in a screenshot or at a coordinate must be identified: list the actors near that point, nearest first.
whenNotToUse: A specific known actor name is already available (use find_by_name).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

limit.description: Maximum number of actors to return in a list.

filter.description: Optional name substring filter for list.

offset.description: Skip this many matching actors; the next page starts at nextOffset from the previous reply.

tag.description: Only actors carrying this actor tag. With summary, shows what the tag covers before a delete_by_tag removes it.

className.description: Only actors of this class or a subclass, by name or path: TextRenderActor, Light (every light type), or a Blueprint such as BP_Sign, with or without _C.

folder.description: Only actors in this outliner folder or a folder under it (Level/Stage matches Level/Stage/Signs); "(none)" for the actors at the root.

propertyNames.description: Property or Blueprint variable names to read on every listed actor, returned per actor under properties, each as JSON (a number, true or false, the name of an enum value, the path of an object, or an array of them), e.g. Kind and Content, or a component's as "Component.Property" (StaticMeshComponent.LDMaxDrawDistance, Visual.RelativeScale3D; the component by its name, or by the actor property that holds it, as CharacterMovement.MaxWalkSpeed), keyed as asked. A name that an actor lacks, or whose component it lacks, is listed under missingProperties for that actor.

near.description: A world point as [x, y, z] (an {x, y, z} object works too): list what is close to it, nearest first, each row with its distance. With radius, only actors whose bounds come within radius of the point; without it, every matching actor sorted by distance. Combines with filter, tag, className and folder.

radius.description: World units from near: an actor is listed when its bounding box comes within this distance of the point (the distance is 0 for a box that contains the point, such as a floor slab under it). Needs near.

summary.description: Count the matching actors by class, actor tag and outliner folder (byClass, byTag, byFolder) instead of listing them; limit and offset do not apply. The cheap first look at an unfamiliar level.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

name.description: Actor name.

path.description: Actor path.

distance.description: With near: world units from the point to the actor's bounding box, 0 when the box contains it. Rows are sorted by it, nearest first; of equally near actors the smaller box comes first, so the level-wide foliage actor, which contains every point, trails.

actors.description: Matched actors; with near, nearest first, each with its distance.

totalCount.description: Listable actors matching the filter, before the limit is applied.

excludedCount.description: Actors present in the world but never listable here: templates, transient actors, the builder brush and WorldSettings. Explains why this total is below the actorCount get_editor_state reports for the same world.

isPieWorld.description: Whether the list was produced while a Play-In-Editor (PIE) session is active.

worldName.description: Name of the active world (or PIE world) the actors were listed from.

filter.description: Optional name substring filter for list.

hasMore.description: More matching actors exist past this page.

nextOffset.description: The offset of the next page; present only when hasMore.

name.description: Class, tag or folder.

byClass.description: summary: matching actors per class, as {name, count} rows sorted by name.

name.description: Class, tag or folder.

byTag.description: summary: matching actors per actor tag, as {name, count} rows sorted by name.

name.description: Class, tag or folder.

byFolder.description: summary: matching actors per outliner folder, as {name, count} rows sorted by name ("(none)" for the root).

examples.title: List actors in the current level with their label, class, location, rotation and scale, plus any propertyNames values, narrowed by name filter, tag, class or outliner folder; page on with offset. near (a world point) with radius is how to find what is near a point, nearest first, each with its distance. summary counts the level by class, tag and folder instead.

discovery.summary: Rename an actor: its label (the name the Outliner and every other call use), and with renameObject its object name too, which is the name a cooked level ships.
whenToUse: An actor should go by a different name.
A Blueprint class was renamed and its placed actors still carry the old class in their object names (BP_OldName_C_3): rename each with renameObject, then save the level.
whenNotToUse: A copy under a new name is wanted (use duplicate with newName).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

newName.description: The new label; letters, digits, spaces and underscores are safe.

renameObject.description: Also rename the object itself to newName, made valid and unique (default false: the label only). The label is editor-only; the object name ships in the cooked level. References from inside the same level follow the rename, a Level Sequence binding or a soft reference by the old path does not. An actor saved in its own package (World Partition) keeps its object name, with a note.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

actorName.description: The actor as later calls should name it.

actorPath.description: Full object path of the actor.

note.description: Why the object name was kept, when renameObject could not rename it.

examples.title: Rename an actor: its label (the name the Outliner and every other call use), and with renameObject its object name too, which is the name a cooked level ships.

discovery.summary: Turn collision on or off for an actor, give its components a collision preset (BlockAll, OverlapAllDynamic, NoCollision...), or set how they answer one channel (Pawn Ignore lets a character walk through, Pawn Block stops it); many actors at once with actorNames, as one undoable step.
whenToUse: Actor collision must be toggled.
Many actors must have collision toggled together (actorNames does them in one call).
A character must walk through an actor or be stopped by it (responses {"Pawn": "Ignore"} or {"Pawn": "Block"}), or the actor must only report overlaps, as a trigger does (profile OverlapAllDynamic).
whenNotToUse: A mode other than on and off (QueryOnly, PhysicsOnly): use edit_component (edit set_properties) with CollisionEnabled, which takes the ECollisionEnabled names.
Every placed copy of a class must change: use edit_scs set_property on its component with CollisionProfileName or CollisionResponses.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

actorNames.description: Several actors to change in one call and one undo step, in place of actorName; names not found are listed back under missing, and the actors changed under affectedActors (which the receipt lists as changes, with an actor handle each).

collisionEnabled.description: Turn collision on (true) or off (false). Omitted with profile or responses, the mode stays as the preset sets it.

profile.description: A collision preset of the project (BlockAll, BlockAllDynamic, OverlapAll, OverlapAllDynamic, NoCollision, Pawn, Trigger, PhysicsActor...); an unknown name is refused with the list. The reply reads the preset back.

responses.description: How the components answer each named channel, {"Pawn": "Ignore", "Visibility": "Block"}: an engine channel (WorldStatic, WorldDynamic, Pawn, Visibility, Camera, PhysicsBody, Vehicle, Destructible) or one the project added, by its name; each Block, Overlap or Ignore. Applied after profile, so the preset then reads Custom; the reply reads each channel back.

componentName.description: Only the primitive component of this name (the capsule of a character, not its mesh); every primitive component of the actor otherwise.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Turn collision on or off for an actor, give its components a collision preset (BlockAll, OverlapAllDynamic, NoCollision...), or set how they answer one channel (Pawn Ignore lets a character walk through, Pawn Block stops it); many actors at once with actorNames, as one undoable step.

discovery.summary: Set Blueprint variables on one placed actor (actorName, the playing copy during Play) from variables {name: value}, or on many actors with actors, each with its own; an actor reference takes an actor's name. Every name is checked first: one the class lacks refuses the call (PROPERTY_NOT_FOUND, listing its variables) and nothing is set. The construction script reruns, as a Details panel edit does, and the call is one undo step (a batch too). A value a variable will not take fails with VARIABLE_NOT_SET naming it (VARIABLE_BATCH_INCOMPLETE for actors); updated lists what was set.
whenToUse: Instance variables on a Blueprint actor must be configured.
Several actors each need their own variable values (actors).
whenNotToUse: The actor is not a Blueprint instance (variables are undefined).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

variables.description: Blueprint variable name to value map. A name the actor does not have refuses the whole call before anything is set; the error lists the variables it does have. An actor variable takes the other actor by label, name or path. A value that does not take (an object path that loads nothing) fails the call, naming it; the variables that did take are listed under updated.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

variables.description: Blueprint variable name to value map. An actor variable, or an array of them, takes each actor by its label or name as list shows it ("Door_1", ["Fire_1", "Fire_2"]) or by its object path.

discovery.summary: Move, rotate or scale placed actors (the playing copy during Play), chosen by transformMode; every member writes alike. location, rotation ([pitch, yaw, roll] degrees) and scale are world values, a part left out keeps its current value, and offset moves by [dx, dy, dz] instead of to a location (both together are refused). actors gives several actors their own values and actorNames gives many the same change in one call. A single move is one undo step and teleports, without sweeping. The reply reads the transform back off the actor; one that did not end up as asked (attached, simulating physics, constrained, or moved by game logic) fails with TRANSFORM_MISMATCH carrying where it is, and TRANSFORM_BATCH_INCOMPLETE names batch items that did not move. The placement is checked: groundZ, groundClearance, and placementWarning with suggestedLocation when it is sunk, floating or intersecting.

whenNotToUse: transformMode=transform: Only the transform needs to be read (use get_transform).

actorNames.description: Many actors given the same change: the location, offset, rotation or scale beside it (forty frost caps rescaled by one scale, a group raised by one offset). Reported as actors is.

report.description: With actors or actorNames: which items results lists, all (default) or only those that failed or look misplaced (placementWarning); movedActors counts every actor either way.

transformMode.description:
Which set transform variant to run; omit for 'transform'.
transform: Move, rotate or scale an actor by setting its world transform (location, rotation, scale) or moving it by an offset, or many actors in one call: actors gives each its own, actorNames gives all the same.
location: Alias of transformMode=transform (location-only intent); normalizes to transformMode=transform.
rotation: Alias of transformMode=transform (rotation-only intent); normalizes to transformMode=transform.
scale: Alias of transformMode=transform (scale-only intent); normalizes to transformMode=transform.
teleport: Alias of transformMode=transform. The bridge dispatches both names to the same handler.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

actorName.description: Label of the actor whose transform was written.

location.description: World location [x, y, z] read back off the actor after the write.

rotation.description: World rotation [pitch, yaw, roll] read back off the actor after the write.

scale.description: World scale [x, y, z] read back off the actor after the write.

results.description: actors or actorNames: one entry per actor (actorName, success, read-back location/rotation/scale, placementWarning, coplanarFaces, error), its placement checked once every actor in the call has moved; report failures keeps only the failed and misplaced ones.

movedActors.description: actors or actorNames: how many actors took their transform.

report.description: Echoes report when it narrowed results.

groundZ.description: Z of the solid surface under the actor; absent when nothing is below it.

groundClearance.description: How far the bottom of the actor's bounds sits above that surface; negative means it is sunk into it.

placementWarning.description: Present when the placement looks wrong: it intersects other actors, is sunk below the surface under it (the bottom of its bounds is under it, wherever its pivot is; suggestedLocation rests it), floats more than 50 units above it, has nothing below it (an actor held up from the side is mounted, never floating: see mountedOn; a floor or platform, four times wider than tall, is ground itself and never reported for it), or has a face in the same plane as another actor's, pointing the same way, which flickers where they overlap (z-fighting: see coplanarFaces). A water body is a surface, not a solid: an actor partly under water (a buoy, a hull, a wading pawn) is neither intersecting nor sunk, and groundZ is the water level. Tag the actor mcp.placement.ok when the placement is deliberate and it is never reported; the tag does not hide a shared plane, which always flickers. A player start, which collides with nothing, is judged by its capsule: the space a pawn spawns into.

mountedOn.description: The actor this one hangs on from the side (a window band flush on a hall, an awning on a facade): its bounds touch or overlap that actor's vertical face, so it is held up and is not reported floating or without a surface below. Present only then.

overlappingActors.description: The actors it intersects (up to 8): actorName, actorClass, penetrationDepth.

coplanarFaces.description: Its faces that lie in the same plane as a face of another actor and point the same way, so the overlap flickers between the two (z-fighting): direction (+X, -Z, ...), component, otherActor, otherComponent, overlapU and overlapV (the overlap's size in units), largest first. Move one about 2 units apart along direction, or stop a wall at a ceiling's underside; control_actor fix_coplanar nudges every pair. Present only when there is one.

suggestedLocation.description: The actor location (x, y, z) that rests the actor on the surface under it: its own location raised by the depth it is sunk, whatever its pivot. Present only when it is sunk.

affectedActors.description: actors or actorNames: the actors that took their transform, each by name and once; the receipt lists them as changes, with an actor handle each.

discovery.summary: Show or hide an actor in the editor and in play (visible, default true), or many actors at once with actorNames, as one undo step. Collision follows visibility: hiding turns its collision off, and showing turns it back on, even where set_actor_collision had turned it off. Showing also shows every primitive component, including one hidden on purpose. The single form replies visible as read back plus actorName; the many form replies updatedActors, affectedActors and the names not found under missing. A name that matches nothing is ACTOR_NOT_FOUND; an actor that does not read back as asked is VISIBILITY_MISMATCH.
whenToUse: An actor must be shown or hidden without being deleted.
Many actors must be shown or hidden together (actorNames does them in one call).
Preferred when callers use the explicit set_actor_visible verb.
whenNotToUse: The actor should be removed (use delete).

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

actorNames.description: Several actors to show or hide in one call and one undo step, in place of actorName; names not found are listed back under missing, and the actors changed under affectedActors (which the receipt lists as changes, with an actor handle each).

discovery.summary: Let actors fall under physics and keep where they come to rest, in one undo step: a pile of crates, rocks scattered on a slope, a toppled chair, a stack whose stability is in doubt. The editor's own Simulate runs for up to the seconds asked (of physics time), each named actor's root body simulating; it stops early once every body sleeps. The reply says, for each actor, where it ended up, how far it moved and turned, whether it came to rest or was still moving, whether it fell (more than fallCm below where it started, or out of the world), and its peak speed (a body launched by starting inside another reads high). With dryRun nothing is kept: a stability check. Answers after Simulate has ended, in about 2-10 s. A run that cannot finish keeps nothing: SIMULATE_STOPPED (Simulate stopped in the editor mid-run), SIMULATE_TIMEOUT, SETTLE_RUNNING (another settle is simulating), NO_LEVEL_VIEWPORT.
whenToUse: Props must rest naturally on what is under them (a heap of crates, rocks on uneven ground, books on a shelf), without computing each pose.
Checking whether a stack or a pile is stable before the game runs: dryRun, then read each actor's moved and turned (a piece that toppled moved and turned far, though it lies at rest) and unstable.
After spawning loose props above the ground, dropping them into place in one call.
whenNotToUse: Only lifting a sunk actor or lowering a floating one onto the surface under it, keeping its turn: use fix_placement, which needs no simulation.
Placing actors by relations (on, nextTo, facing): use arrange_by_relations.
While Play or Simulate runs or is starting: it refuses (PLAY_RUNNING), since it runs a Simulate session of its own.

In a level whose game pauses itself in Simulate (a title screen, a pause menu): nothing falls, so it answers GAME_PAUSED and keeps nothing; give the level a plain game mode first (manage_level set_world_settings gameMode).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorNames.description: The actors to settle, by exact name (1-64). Each needs a root that is a body with physics collision (a static mesh with simple collision: the engine cubes and most props); a floor or landscape, an actor with Lock Actor Movement, an attached actor, or one whose root is no body comes back under skipped with the reason and stays put. A name that matches no actor refuses with ACTOR_NOT_FOUND (missing lists them); when none of them can fall it refuses with NOTHING_TO_SETTLE. Everything else in the level takes part in the simulation as it is (static actors are what the bodies land on).

seconds.description: At most this much physics time (0.5-10, default 3): the run stops sooner once every body sleeps. A body still moving at the end comes back under unstable with its pose at that moment, which is kept.

fallCm.description: A body that ends more than this many cm below its START height fell (10-100000, default 500), measured from where it started, not from the floor: its old pose is kept rather than one under the floor, and it is listed under unstable. Dropping props from higher than 5 m onto the floor needs a larger fallCm.

dryRun.description: Simulate and report only: nothing is kept (default false). Use it to check whether a stack stands.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

actors.description: Each actor simulated as {actorName, to [x, y, z], rotation [pitch, yaw, roll], moved (cm), turned (degrees), resting (asleep at the end), fell, peakSpeed (cm/s)}.

unstable.description: Actors still moving when the run ended, or that fell: empty when everything came to rest.

skipped.description: Actors named that never fall, as {actorName, reason}; physics also refuses a mesh without simple collision once Simulate has started.

kept.description: How many resting poses were written to the level (0 under dryRun); control_editor undo takes them all back in one step.

endedBecause.description: rested (every body asleep), fell (every body asleep but those that fell, whose poses are not kept), seconds (the physics time asked for ran out) or deadline (the call had to answer before every body rested).

fps.description: Editor frames per second during the run; physics steps at most 1/30 s a frame, so a low rate makes the run take longer, never fall short.

dryRun.description: Present and true when nothing was kept because dryRun was set.

examples.title: Let actors fall under physics and keep where they come to rest, in one undo step: a pile of crates, rocks scattered on a slope, a toppled chair, a stack whose stability is in doubt. The editor's own Simulate runs for up to the seconds asked (of physics time), each named actor's root body simulating; it stops early once every body sleeps. The reply says, for each actor, where it ended up, how far it moved and turned, whether it came to rest or was still moving, whether it fell (more than fallCm below where it started, or out of the world), and its peak speed (a body launched by starting inside another reads high). With dryRun nothing is kept: a stability check. Answers after Simulate has ended, in about 2-10 s. A run that cannot finish keeps nothing: SIMULATE_STOPPED (Simulate stopped in the editor mid-run), SIMULATE_TIMEOUT, SETTLE_RUNNING (another settle is simulating), NO_LEVEL_VIEWPORT.

output.message: Simulated 3 actor(s) for 1.2 s of physics: 3 resting, 0 still moving or fell; 3 resting pose(s) kept as one undo step.

discovery.summary: Place actors in the level, or in the running game during Play (gone when Play stops), chosen by spawnKind; each call is one undo step. class spawns classPath (or actorClass), such as /Script/Engine.PointLight or a Blueprint class, or with meshPath alone a Movable static or skeletal mesh actor showing that mesh; blueprint spawns blueprintPath; batch places up to 500 items (1000 once repeat rows are unrolled) in one call, each a spawn payload that can also take materialPath, variables, properties, folder and tags, with shared defaults. location and rotation default to zero and scale to 1; folder files the actor in the outliner and tags tag it. The actor is labelled actorName, else after its mesh or class; when another actor has the same label, the reply's actorName is the actor's unique object name, which later calls must use. An unknown class or mesh is refused (CLASS_NOT_FOUND, MESH_NOT_FOUND), and an actor that destroys itself at once is SPAWNED_THEN_DESTROYED. The reply checks the placement: groundZ and groundClearance, and placementWarning with suggestedLocation for an actor sunk, floating or intersecting (tag mcp.placement.ok to mark one deliberate).
whenToUse: spawnKind=class: A new actor of a known Unreal class must be created in the scene.
spawnKind=class: A static or skeletal mesh must be placed as its own actor (meshPath alone; the actor class follows the mesh).
spawnKind=blueprint: A Blueprint instance must be placed in the scene.
spawnKind=batch: More than a couple of actors must be placed, such as laying out a level.
spawnKind=batch: A row or grid of the same actor must be placed (an item's repeat).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

classPath.description: Unreal class path (e.g. /Script/Engine.PointLight) for the actor to spawn.

actorClass.description: Alias of classPath accepted by the spawn handler (normalizeArgs alias).

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

meshPath.description: Canonical /Game mesh asset path to assign on spawn.

location.description: World or relative location as [x, y, z].

rotation.description: Rotation as [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees.

folder.description: Outliner folder path for the new actor (Level/Signs), made when missing.

tags.description: Actor tags for the new actor: delete_by_tag removes them again, and mcp.placement.ok marks a deliberate overlap before the placement is judged.

blueprintPath.description: Canonical /Game Blueprint asset path to spawn from.

actors.description: Actors to spawn, 1-500. Each is a spawn payload: classPath, blueprintPath or meshPath, plus actorName, location, rotation, scale ([x, y, z] arrays). Optional per item: materialPath (applied like set_material; componentName/materialSlot/allComponents narrow it), variables ({name: value} Blueprint variables set on the new instance, like set_blueprint_variables; in a running game they are set before its BeginPlay, so it starts with them), properties ({name: value} set on the root component, or on componentName's, as edit_component sets them: a light's Intensity, LightColor and AttenuationRadius), folder (outliner folder path), tags (actor tags; delete_by_tag removes the batch again), repeat ({count, offset [x, y, z], rows, rowOffset [x, y, z]}: count x rows copies of the item, each moved from its location by offset per copy and rowOffset per row, actorName numbered _1, _2, ...; a row of racks, a grid of lights; at most 1000 actors once unrolled). Items that fail are reported; the rest still spawn. Parts meant to hang in the air or sit inside another (ceiling ducts, lights, a flange on a pipe) take the tag mcp.placement.ok (defaults.tags covers the whole batch), so the reply keeps only what needs fixing.

defaults.description: Fields shared by every item (e.g. meshPath, materialPath, folder, tags); an item's own fields win.

report.description: Which items results lists: all, or failures only (items that failed to spawn or to take their material or variables, and items with a placementWarning); spawned and failed still count every item. Default all, or failures for a batch of more than 20 items once repeats are unrolled; the receipt still names every actor.

spawnKind.description:
Which spawn variant to run; omit for 'class'.
class: Spawn a new actor instance from a class path into the current level, or a mesh actor from a mesh path alone.
blueprint: Spawn an actor instance from a Blueprint asset path into the current level.
batch: Spawn many actors in one call; each item is a spawn payload, optionally with a material, Blueprint variables, outliner folder and tags.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

name.description: Target actor name in the current level.

undo.description: Whether editor undo takes the spawn back: {undoable: true, transactionScope: "Spawn Actors"} (control_editor undo removes every actor the call made), or {undoable: false, reasonCode, reason}.

groundZ.description: Z of the solid surface under the actor; absent when nothing is below it.

groundClearance.description: How far the bottom of the actor's bounds sits above that surface; negative means it is sunk into it.

placementWarning.description: Present when the placement looks wrong: it intersects other actors, is sunk below the surface under it (the bottom of its bounds is under it, wherever its pivot is; suggestedLocation rests it), floats more than 50 units above it, has nothing below it (an actor held up from the side is mounted, never floating: see mountedOn; a floor or platform, four times wider than tall, is ground itself and never reported for it), or has a face in the same plane as another actor's, pointing the same way, which flickers where they overlap (z-fighting: see coplanarFaces). A water body is a surface, not a solid: an actor partly under water (a buoy, a hull, a wading pawn) is neither intersecting nor sunk, and groundZ is the water level. Tag the actor mcp.placement.ok when the placement is deliberate and it is never reported; the tag does not hide a shared plane, which always flickers. A player start, which collides with nothing, is judged by its capsule: the space a pawn spawns into.

mountedOn.description: The actor this one hangs on from the side (a window band flush on a hall, an awning on a facade): its bounds touch or overlap that actor's vertical face, so it is held up and is not reported floating or without a surface below. Present only then.

overlappingActors.description: The actors it intersects (up to 8): actorName, actorClass, penetrationDepth.

coplanarFaces.description: Its faces that lie in the same plane as a face of another actor and point the same way, so the overlap flickers between the two (z-fighting): direction (+X, -Z, ...), component, otherActor, otherComponent, overlapU and overlapV (the overlap's size in units), largest first. Move one about 2 units apart along direction, or stop a wall at a ceiling's underside; control_actor fix_coplanar nudges every pair. Present only when there is one.

suggestedLocation.description: The actor location (x, y, z) that rests the actor on the surface under it: its own location raised by the depth it is sunk, whatever its pivot. Present only when it is sunk.

failed.description: Items that failed to spawn or to take their material, variables or properties.

placementWarnings.description: Items that spawned but look misplaced (sunk into the surface under them, floating, intersecting other actors, with nothing below, or with a face flickering against another actor's in the same plane); each carries its placementWarning in results. A warning is not a failure: it changes neither failed nor success.

results.description: Per item (only the failed ones and those with a placementWarning or ignoredKeys under report: failures, the default past 20 items): index (its place in the batch once repeats are unrolled), success, name, path, error, errorCode, variablesSet, variablesError, materialApplied, materialError, propertiesError, ignoredKeys (the item's keys no spawn reads, such as a "label" meant as actorName), and the placement facts set_transform reports (groundZ, groundClearance, placementWarning, overlappingActors, coplanarFaces, suggestedLocation), measured after the item took its tags, variables and material, so an item tagged mcp.placement.ok is never reported. name is the label the item asked for, or the unique actor name when it gave no actorName.

unnamedActors.description: The unique name of every item that gave no actorName, in batch order ("" where it failed), under either report mode. Their labels repeat (every cube is "Cube"), so these are the names later calls must use.

affectedActors.description: The actors that spawned, by the name each result carries, in batch order and under either report mode; the receipt lists them as changes, with an actor handle each (the first 20).

report.description: Echoes report when it narrowed results.

examples.title: Place actors in the level, or in the running game during Play (gone when Play stops), chosen by spawnKind; each call is one undo step. class spawns classPath (or actorClass), such as /Script/Engine.PointLight or a Blueprint class, or with meshPath alone a Movable static or skeletal mesh actor showing that mesh; blueprint spawns blueprintPath; batch places up to 500 items (1000 once repeat rows are unrolled) in one call, each a spawn payload that can also take materialPath, variables, properties, folder and tags, with shared defaults. location and rotation default to zero and scale to 1; folder files the actor in the outliner and tags tag it. The actor is labelled actorName, else after its mesh or class; when another actor has the same label, the reply's actorName is the actor's unique object name, which later calls must use. An unknown class or mesh is refused (CLASS_NOT_FOUND, MESH_NOT_FOUND), and an actor that destroys itself at once is SPAWNED_THEN_DESTROYED. The reply checks the placement: groundZ and groundClearance, and placementWarning with suggestedLocation for an actor sunk, floating or intersecting (tag mcp.placement.ok to mark one deliberate).

discovery.summary: Run one tool of Epic's editor toolsets (Unreal Engine 5.8 Toolset Registry) with a JSON input matching the inputSchema list_editor_toolsets returned, and answer with its output once it finishes. A tool whose name starts with a destructive verb (Delete, Remove, Destroy, Clear, Reset ...) is refused with DESTRUCTIVE_EDITOR_TOOL: run it with call_editor_tool_destructive. A tool that would run scripts or console code, and every ConfigSettingsToolset tool (it reaches this plugin's own settings; use system_control project settings), is never called (EDITOR_TOOL_BLOCKED).
whenToUse: list_editor_toolsets found an Epic tool for work no native capability covers.
whenNotToUse: A native capability covers the operation: prefer it.
The tool deletes or resets something: use call_editor_tool_destructive.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

toolName.description: Full tool name exactly as list_editor_toolsets lists it: the toolset, then the tool, e.g. EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset.GetSelectedActors.

input.description: The tool's arguments, shaped by the inputSchema list_editor_toolsets returned for toolName. Omit for a tool without arguments.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

effect.description: read or write, as judged from the tool's name.

output.description: The tool's own result: its JSON output parsed, or the raw text when it is not JSON.

examples.title: Run one tool of Epic's editor toolsets (Unreal Engine 5.8 Toolset Registry) with a JSON input matching the inputSchema list_editor_toolsets returned, and answer with its output once it finishes. A tool whose name starts with a destructive verb (Delete, Remove, Destroy, Clear, Reset ...) is refused with DESTRUCTIVE_EDITOR_TOOL: run it with call_editor_tool_destructive. discovery.summary: Explore the running level with a pawn the way a tester would, to find what a model cannot see by reading it: places the pawn falls out of the level (below its kill height) or leaves the playable area, traps it cannot get out of, parts of the nav mesh no path from the start reaches (islands: a sealed room), and Blueprint errors raised on the way. In a Play session started through this server (others are refused with PLAY_NOT_STARTED_BY_MCP). Go-Explore's first phase, without learning: an archive of cells (the grid cell, the height band and the truth of the track assertions), each kept with the moves that first reached it; every round walks the pawn back to a cell (along the nav mesh, else teleported) and explores from there with sticky random moves (the last one repeated 19 times in 20, jumps included), through the pawn's own movement: no OS input. op start begins a session for the player's pawn or actorName's and explores for seconds; continue explores more (cell picks where the next round starts, else cells chosen less often are preferred); read answers with what was found; stop ends the session. Each call answers after its seconds (at most 22); the window is held on screen without focus meanwhile.

discovery.summary: Call one reflected UFunction on a plugin's live object, marshalling arguments through the function's own property chain. No signature is hardcoded: whatever describe_reflected_api reports for the installed build is what this accepts, so an integration stays correct across plugin updates instead of silently passing a stale parameter list. Return and out parameters come back in `outputs`. Refuses when only the class default object exists, because invoking on the CDO mutates shared defaults and never reaches the running instance. This is arbitrary in-process invocation — it can reach any reflected function on any resolvable object — so it demands elevated consent.

control.description:
Which play variant to run; omit for 'play'.
play: Start Play-In-Editor (PIE) session; answers once the play world has begun play.
pause: Pause the running Play In Editor session, as the toolbar pause does; the reply says alreadyPaused when it was. No session is NO_ACTIVE_SESSION.
resume: Resume a paused Play In Editor session; wasPaused false says it was not paused and nothing changed. A pause the game holds itself (a pause menu) is GAME_PAUSED unless unpauseGame is true, and a widget that still holds keyboard focus is named in warnings. No session is NO_ACTIVE_SESSION.
stop: Stop the running PIE session.
eject: Eject the player from its pawn in PIE, as the editor's Eject button does: the session switches to Simulate in Editor and the view becomes a free camera that set_camera moves and screenshot photographs. Answers once the view has switched.

examples.title: Control Play In Editor with control: play (starts it, answering once play has begun), pause, resume, stop (answers once play has ended), eject (leave the pawn for a free camera) or possess (control another pawn by actorName, such as a character to test, or back to the player pawn).

discovery.summary: Walk a pawn of the running game to a goal along the nav mesh and judge the leg, in a Play session started through this server (control_editor play; a session started in the editor is refused with PLAY_NOT_STARTED_BY_MCP, since someone may be playing it). The player's pawn by default, or actorName's; goal is a point, or goalActor where that actor is. The verdict: pass only with evidence (the goal reached within acceptRadius, every check held, no script error), fail with what went wrong (stuck: no progress for stuckSeconds; fell: below its start by fallCm or out of the world; a script error during the leg; a check that did not hold), inconclusive (the nav mesh gives no full path, so the leg was not tried; still on the way at maxSeconds; or the game paused itself during the leg), error (the game left the level: Play stopped or the level changed). A paused game (a title screen, a pause menu) is refused with GAME_PAUSED: resume it with control_editor play, control resume, unpauseGame true. checks are assertions in execute's expect language, judged in the running game when the leg ends. The editor window is held on screen without focus for the leg, so the game runs at speed. The reply: verdict, ended (reached, stuck, fell, timeout, pawn_lost), checks, scriptErrors, timeline (where the pawn was, at most 50 samples), last, bestDistance, traveled, frames.
whenToUse: Whether the player can actually get from one place to another in the running game, with what went wrong if not.
whenNotToUse: Only whether a nav path exists, without playing: manage_ai get_ai_info info path.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

goal.description: Where the pawn should get to.

goalActor.description: An actor of the running game to walk to, in place of goal.

actorName.description: The pawn to drive (one with a controller); default the player's.

acceptRadius.description: How near the goal counts as reached, in cm (default 100).

stuckSeconds.description: Game seconds without getting nearer that count as stuck (default 2).

fallCm.description: How far below its start the pawn may drop before it counts as fallen (default 500).

maxSeconds.description: Game seconds the leg may take (default 15, at most 60; at most 25 real seconds).

checks.description: Assertions judged when the leg ends, in execute's expect language (Door_1 hidden, BP_Player.Health > 0), at most 16.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

ended.description: How the leg ended: reached, stuck, fell, timeout, paused, pawn_lost, world_ended, or the reason no leg was tried (no_path, partial, start_off_navmesh, goal_off_navmesh).

checks.description: Each check: text, verdict (ok, failed, unknown), actual.

scriptErrors.description: Blueprint runtime errors during the leg, each with the node that raised it.

timeline.description: Where the pawn was: { t, location }, at most 50 samples.

last.description: Where the pawn ended, [x, y, z].

bestDistance.description: The nearest it got to the goal, in cm (2D).

traveled.description: How far it moved, in cm.

discovery.summary: Restart the editor process, relaunching the same project, or close it (relaunch false). validateOnly lists the unsaved packages without doing either.
whenToUse: A plugin was enabled or disabled and the change needs a restart to take effect.
A pipeline needs to know whether a restart is safe right now; pass validateOnly.
A project setting that only applies at startup must be picked up.
The editor is no longer needed and should close (relaunch false).
Which packages have unsaved changes must be known (validateOnly).
whenNotToUse: Only a level needs reloading; use open_level.
A PIE session should end; use stop.
A Movie Render Queue render is running: refused with RENDER_IN_PROGRESS until it ends or manage_sequence cancel_render stops it.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

validateOnly.description: Report whether a restart would proceed, and what it would discard, without restarting.

discardUnsaved.description: Restart even though packages have unsaved changes, discarding them. Omitted, a restart with unsaved work is refused.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds to wait before restarting, so the response reaches the caller first. Clamped to 0.1-30.

relaunch.description: false closes the editor instead of relaunching it (default true). Unsaved packages are refused the same way.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

restarting.description: True once the restart has been scheduled; false under validateOnly or when closing.

closing.description: True once closing the editor (relaunch false) has been scheduled.

validateOnly.description: True when this call only reported what a restart would do.

wouldRestart.description: Under validateOnly, whether a real restart would proceed.

renderRunning.description: Under validateOnly, whether a Movie Render Queue render is running (a restart is refused until it ends).

unsavedPackages.description: Packages with unsaved changes a restart would discard.

unsavedCount.description: How many packages have unsaved changes.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds the editor waits before relaunching.

discardedPackageCount.description: Unsaved packages discarded by this restart.

examples.title: Restart the editor process, relaunching the same project, or close it (relaunch false). validateOnly lists the unsaved packages without doing either.

discovery.summary: Save every level and asset with unsaved changes, or only the packages named in assetPaths (the other dirty ones stay unsaved and are listed in leftDirtyPackages). Temporary packages are skipped; one that fails to save (read-only, not checked out) is listed in failedPackages and fails the call with SAVE_FAILED while the rest stay written. Refused during a Movie Render Queue render (RENDER_IN_PROGRESS). Not undoable.
whenToUse: All unsaved changes must be persisted.
Only the assets this task changed should be saved (assetPaths), leaving other unsaved work alone.
whenNotToUse: Nothing has changed since the last save.
A Movie Render Queue render is running: its sequence is in a temporary state until the job ends, so the save is refused with RENDER_IN_PROGRESS.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

assetPaths.description: Save only these assets or levels, e.g. ["/Game/UI/WBP_Menu"], and leave every other dirty package as it is; omit to save everything dirty. A named asset the editor has loaded is written even when it is not marked dirty (a material usage flag the editor set while loading).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

compensation.description: Compensating-cleanup receipt. Present on every outcome including the all-succeeded one, because each package lands independently and a completed save is already durable: non-atomic is a property of the operation, not of one result.

atomic.description: Always false. Packages land one at a time and the ones that landed stay landed.

rollback.description: Always "unavailable". No editor transaction can reach a finished save, so this call was not and cannot be undone.

rollbackReason.description: Why no rollback exists for this class of work.

state.description: Outcome across all steps: everything landed, some did, none did, or there was nothing to do.

items.description: One step of the non-atomic save, naming what landed or why it did not.

detail.description: What landed on disk, or the reason nothing did.

completed.description: Steps whose effect is now durable on disk.

items.description: One step of the non-atomic save, naming what landed or why it did not.

detail.description: What landed on disk, or the reason nothing did.

notCompleted.description: Steps that did not complete, each with its reason.

items.description: One step of the non-atomic save, naming what landed or why it did not.

detail.description: What landed on disk, or the reason nothing did.

skipped.description: Steps deliberately not attempted, such as transient packages.

items.description: Canonical capability id that reverses a durable effect.

compensatingCapabilities.description: Separate calls the caller may make to reverse a durable effect. Never a rollback of this call.

callerAction.description: Exact instruction for reaching a clean state; empty when nothing is outstanding.

leftDirtyPackages.description: With assetPaths: the other packages that still hold unsaved changes, left as they were.

examples.title: Save every level and asset with unsaved changes, or only the packages named in assetPaths (the other dirty ones stay unsaved and are listed in leftDirtyPackages). Temporary packages are skipped; one that fails to save (read-only, not checked out) is listed in failedPackages and fails the call with SAVE_FAILED while the rest stay written. Refused during a Movie Render Queue render (RENDER_IN_PROGRESS). Not undoable.

compensation.rollbackReason: Completed steps are already durable on disk. No editor transaction can reach a finished save, build or render, so nothing here was or can be undone.

discovery.summary: Capture a screenshot of the level viewport (optionally from a camera location and rotation given in the same call), of the running game view, or of the whole editor window with the game UI.
whenToUse: A visual snapshot of the editor or game viewport is needed.
whenNotToUse: A real-time capture stream is needed.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

path.description: Directory to save the PNG in, inside the project (relative to it, or absolute under it). Default Saved/Screenshots (game_viewport: Saved/Screenshots/WindowsEditor). A path outside the project is refused.

resolution.description: Maximum WxH for the returned PNG (e.g. "1280x720"). The capture is downscaled to fit inside this box with its aspect ratio preserved; a box at least as large as the viewport leaves the image untouched. Without it an image returned inline fits 1600x900, and a file-only capture (returnBase64 false) keeps the viewport size.

mode.description: Screenshot source: editor_viewport (default, the level viewport), game_viewport (the running game frame WITHOUT any UMG widgets) or full_editor_window (the editor window as displayed: the only mode that shows game UI and asset editors). While Play In Editor runs with the player ejected (control_editor play control=eject), the game is drawn by the editor viewport, so editor_viewport and game_viewport are then the same picture: the ejected view.

window.description: With mode full_editor_window, which window to capture: a list index (2, or "2") or a case-insensitive substring of its title ("WBP_HubUI"). Omit for the main editor frame, which is then always what is captured: a minimized main frame is restored without taking focus, and when that is not possible the call fails with EDITOR_WINDOW_MINIMIZED instead of capturing another window. A window restored for the capture is minimized again right after it. Every response lists the open windows under windows[], so read that to pick one.

location.description: editor_viewport (and game_viewport while the player is ejected): put the camera here first, in the same call ({x, y, z}); it stays there. Water and streamed texture detail follow the view over the next frames, which this call does not wait for: after a jump far from the last view (or right after a level opens) the picture can show black water or soft textures, so capture again from the same spot, or move with set_camera first. That is the level viewport camera, or, while Play In Editor runs with the player ejected, the ejected view. While Play In Editor runs and the player is not ejected there is no free camera to move and the call is refused with PIE_VIEW_NOT_EJECTED (eject first, or point the game camera with set_camera cameraOp=view_target), exactly as set_camera is.

rotation.description: editor_viewport (and game_viewport while the player is ejected): turn that camera to this first ({pitch, yaw, roll}), in the same call. Refused like location while Play In Editor runs and the player is not ejected.

returnBase64.description: Return the PNG inline as an image (default true); a capture also saves a file unless keepFile is false. With no resolution, an inline image is downscaled to fit 1600x900. false returns only the saved path and metadata, at the full viewport size.

keepFile.description: false: hand the image back without leaving a file in Saved/Screenshots (refused with returnBase64 false, which would leave no output at all). Default true. Files already written are listed by system_control list_output_files and removed by delete_output_file.

waitForShaders.description: true: when shaders are still compiling (after a scalability or material change), wait for the queue to drain before capturing, polling without blocking the game thread, for at most 25 seconds; shaderWait in the reply says how long it waited and how many jobs were left. Default false: capture now and report shadersCompiling.

includeMetadata.description: true: echo metadata back in the reply (default false).

metadata.description: An object of your own, such as a label or a step number, returned under metadata when includeMetadata is true; the capture itself never reads it.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

shadersCompiling.description: Shader compile jobs still outstanding when the picture was taken. Above 0, the surfaces they cover are drawn with the engine default material (black foliage, grey ground) and a warning says so; pass waitForShaders to capture after they finish.

shaderWait.description: With waitForShaders while shaders compiled: waitedSeconds, jobsLeft (still outstanding when the wait ended) and timedOut (true when jobs were left after the 25 second cap).

width.description: Width in pixels of the PNG actually returned.

height.description: Height in pixels of the PNG actually returned.

viewportWidth.description: Width in pixels of the viewport (or, for full_editor_window, the window) the picture was taken at. Present only when the image was downscaled (a resolution, or the 1600x900 inline default), so width/height differ from it.

viewportHeight.description: Height in pixels of the viewport or window the picture was taken at. Present only when the image was downscaled.

window.description: Title of the editor window that was actually captured.

mainWindow.description: full_editor_window: true when the captured window is the main editor frame.

windowRestored.description: full_editor_window: true when the window was minimized and was put back on screen, without taking focus, for the capture. It is minimized again right after the capture, so windows[] shows it minimized.

windows.description: Every visible editor window: index, title, x, y, width, height, isActive, isMinimized, isModal. Pass an index or a title substring back as the window parameter to capture a different one; x/y are screen coordinates for simulate_input.

cameraLocation.description: editor_viewport and an ejected game view: where the camera was for this picture.

cameraRotation.description: editor_viewport and an ejected game view: how the camera was turned for this picture.

view.description: Which view the picture is of: editor_viewport (the level viewport), pie_game (the running game as its possessed pawn sees it) or pie_ejected (the free camera of an ejected player). Absent for full_editor_window and for the game_viewport capture of a possessed game.

examples.title: Capture a screenshot of the level viewport (optionally from a camera location and rotation given in the same call), of the running game view, or of the whole editor window with the game UI.

discovery.summary: Set the viewport camera transform, its field of view, or the view target actor. While Play In Editor runs, the transform moves the free camera of an ejected player and is refused until the player is ejected.
whenToUse: cameraOp=transform: The viewport camera must be moved to a specific position and orientation.
cameraOp=transform: The view of a running game must be placed, for a screenshot of it: eject the player first, then set the camera.
cameraOp=fov: The camera FOV must be adjusted for the viewport.
cameraOp=view_target: The camera must follow or focus on a specific actor in PIE.
cameraOp=view_target: The camera view target must be set using the set_game_view_target alias.
whenNotToUse: cameraOp=transform: Play In Editor runs and the player is not ejected: the game draws its view target's camera (the pawn, or an actor set with view_target), which has no free camera to move, so the call is refused with PIE_VIEW_NOT_EJECTED (eject first, or use cameraOp view_target).
cameraOp=fov: The default FOV is acceptable.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

location.description: 3D location (x, y, z).

rotation.description: 3D rotation (pitch, yaw, roll).

fov.description: Camera field of view in degrees.

actorName.description: Name of the actor to target.

name.description: Name identifier.

blendTime.description: Blend time in seconds for set_view_target.

cameraOp.description:
Which set camera variant to run; omit for 'transform'.
transform: Set the viewport camera position and rotation: the level viewport, or, while Play In Editor runs with the player ejected (control_editor play control=eject), the free camera the game view is drawn from.
fov: Set the camera field of view of the view on screen: the level viewport, the free view of an ejected player, or while the player plays the running game's camera (method player_camera_manager; locked to the value until play stops).
view_target: Set the PIE view target to a specific actor by name.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

view.description: Which view moved: editor_viewport (the level viewport), or pie_ejected (the free camera of an ejected player while Play In Editor runs).

cameraLocation.description: Where the camera is after the call, {x, y, z}.

cameraRotation.description: How the camera is turned after the call, {pitch, yaw, roll}.

locationApplied.description: Whether the viewport took the requested location; false (with CAMERA_NOT_APPLIED) when it is locked to an actor, piloting or orthographic.

rotationApplied.description: Whether the viewport took the requested rotation.

examples.title: Set the viewport camera transform, its field of view, or the view target actor. While Play In Editor runs, the transform moves the free camera of an ejected player and is refused until the player is ejected.

discovery.summary: Control the clock of the running game during Play In Editor: game speed (slow motion), a fixed delta time, or step frames.
whenToUse: control=speed: Game speed must be changed for testing, e.g. slowed down to observe a short-lived actor.
control=fixed_delta_time: A fixed delta time is needed for deterministic stepping.
control=step_frame: The simulation must advance a fixed number of frames.
control=step_frame: The simulation must advance exactly one frame.
whenNotToUse: control=speed: PIE is not running (start it with control_editor play first).
control=fixed_delta_time: Variable delta time is preferred.
control=fixed_delta_time: PIE is not running.
control=step_frame: Real-time simulation is preferred.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

speed.description: Clock multiplier for the running game: 1 is normal, 0.05 runs it twenty times slower (above 0, up to 20).

deltaTime.description: Seconds every frame advances the running game, however long the frame really took (deterministic runs); 0 turns fixed stepping off. It also ends when PIE stops.

control.description:
Which set game speed variant to run; omit for 'speed'.
speed: Set the speed of the running game (Play In Editor time dilation, above 0 and up to 20; 1 is normal), for slow motion while testing. The reply gives speed, the dilation the world holds after the game clamps it, and timeDilation, the effective one. Refused when Play In Editor is not running (NO_ACTIVE_SESSION).
fixed_delta_time: Make every frame of the running game advance by a fixed delta time, or 0 to follow real time again.
step_frame: Advance the PIE simulation by one or more frames, each at the current game speed (slow motion makes each step shorter; timeDilation says so). The warnings say what the game logged during the steps, and a Blueprint runtime error names the node, graph and Blueprint that raised it.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

gameSeconds.description: Game seconds the steps advanced, when a fixed delta time is set (set_game_speed fixed_delta_time): steps x deltaTime x game speed.

timeDilation.description: The game speed the steps ran at, present when it is not 1: a step keeps the slow motion that was set, so at speed 0.1 each step advances a tenth of its frame of game time.

examples.title: Control the clock of the running game during Play In Editor: game speed (slow motion), a fixed delta time, or step frames.

whenToUse: The viewport resolution must be changed.
whenNotToUse: The default resolution is acceptable.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

output.description: What the command printed, at most 4096 characters.

examples.title: Set the game window resolution through the console (r.SetRes <width>x<height>, fractions dropped); it does not resize an editor viewport. The reply is the console command's: command and output.
