discovery.summary: Simulate a keyboard or mouse input event (key_down, key_up, key_tap, mouse_click, mouse_move), or list and press the live UMG widgets of a PIE session (widget_list, widget_click).
whenToUse: Synthetic input must be injected into the editor or PIE.
A game has to be played: key_tap taps a key, key_down with holdSeconds holds it for that many game seconds, and inputAction injects an Enhanced Input action directly when no key is mapped to it.

A game UI must be operated in PIE: widget_list names every live widget, and widget_click presses a Button, toggles a CheckBox or sets a Slider (value) by name without touching the OS cursor, so it works while the editor window is in the background.
whenNotToUse: Real hardware input is available.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

key.description: Key name: SpaceBar, D, Left, Enter, P. Escape is the editor stop-play key: in Play In Editor it ends the session instead of reaching the game, so test an action bound to Escape through another key mapped to it.

type.description: Input event type (key_down, key_up, key_tap = press then release, mouse_click, mouse_move), or widget_list / widget_click to operate the live UMG of a PIE session.

inputType.description: Alias for type used by simulate_input.

inputAction.description: Enhanced Input action to inject directly, as an asset path such as /Game/Input/IA_Move. A raw key already reaches Enhanced Input through the active mapping contexts (key_down D moves a pawn whose context maps D); use inputAction when no key is mapped to the action, or to inject an analog value.

value.description: Scalar value to inject for inputAction (default 1; use a negative value for the opposite direction), or the value to set a Slider to with widget_click. Ignored for a raw key.

holdSeconds.description: Keep injecting inputAction, or keep a raw key_down/key_tap key pressed, for this many seconds of GAME time so the pawn actually travels (default 0: an action lasts one frame, a key_down stays down until key_up, a key_tap lets go after 0.1s). Game time, not wall time: under set_game_speed 0.05 a 2s hold still delivers 2s of in-game input, which takes 40s of real time. A key_up for the same action or key stops the hold early. The reply comes back at once, while the key is still down: read the pawn after the hold, or press and watch in one call with control_actor sample_motion inputs.

x.description: Mouse X for simulate_input: while a game runs, mouse_move takes pixels of the game viewport and moves the game cursor there (where Get Mouse Position and Get Hit Result Under Cursor read it; a click at it is a key_tap of LeftMouseButton); otherwise desktop coordinates for the editor UI. Or the X value of an Axis2D or Axis3D inputAction.

y.description: Mouse Y for simulate_input, in the same space as x, or the Y value of an Axis2D or Axis3D inputAction.

z.description: Z value of an Axis3D inputAction (x and y give the other two).

widget.description: For type widget_click: the live UMG widget to drive, by name (PlayButton), or Owner.Name (WBP_MainMenu.PlayButton) when several share it. widget_list shows both.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

routedToPIE.description: The event was routed to the PIE viewport rather than the editor.

handledByPIE.description: PIE actually consumed the event. False here with routedToPIE true means the key reached the game and nothing bound it: no active input mapping context maps that key (inject the action with inputAction instead).

injectedAction.description: The Enhanced Input action that was injected, when inputAction resolved to one. Absent means the call went down the raw-key path, which reaches the game only through a mapping context that maps the key.

widgets.description: widget_list: each live user widget (userWidget, object, inViewport) with its Button/CheckBox/Slider children (name, type, enabled, visible, focused, and text, value or checked), texts (what its other visible text blocks read, at most 20) and, for one made at runtime and added to another widget's panel such as a list row, in (Owner.Panel).

widget.description: widget_click: the widget that was driven, as Owner.Name.

widgetType.description: widget_click: the driven widget's class (Button, CheckBox, Slider).

pawn.description: In PIE, the pawn the player controls, by the name actor calls take: read it (control_actor get_transform) once a hold is over to see what the input did.

examples.title: Simulate a keyboard or mouse input event (key_down, key_up, key_tap, mouse_click, mouse_move), or list and press the live UMG widgets of a PIE session (widget_list, widget_click).

discovery.summary: Record the running Play In Editor game as a replay (control start, the default: DemoRec, written by default under Saved/Demos; frameRate and durationSeconds), or stop it (stop; NOT_RECORDING when nothing records). Refused without a running game (NO_ACTIVE_SESSION). For playback, seeking or a killcam, use the sequence demo actions.
whenToUse: control=start: The running game must be recorded as a replay.
control=stop: An in-progress replay recording must be stopped.
whenNotToUse: control=start: A recording is already in progress.
control=start: The replay must be played back, sought or used as a killcam: the sequence demo actions (start_demo_recording, play_demo) handle the whole replay.
control=stop: No recording is in progress.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

name.description: Name identifier.

frameRate.description: Replay frames recorded per second, 1 to 120 (sets demo.RecordHz; the engine default is 8).

durationSeconds.description: Stop the recording by itself after this many seconds of game time.

control.description:
Which start recording variant to run; omit for 'start'.
start: Start a replay (demo) recording of the running Play In Editor game with DemoRec, named filename (or name; default Recording_<date and time>) and written by the replay streamer, by default under Saved/Demos. frameRate (1 to 120) sets demo.RecordHz, which stays set for later recordings; durationSeconds stops it after that much game time. NO_ACTIVE_SESSION without a running game, RECORDING_NOT_STARTED when no recorder starts.
stop: Stop the replay recording running in the Play In Editor game (DemoStop), which writes it out. NOT_RECORDING when no game runs or nothing records, which is also what a recording durationSeconds already ended leaves.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Record the running Play In Editor game as a replay (control start, the default: DemoRec, written by default under Saved/Demos; frameRate and durationSeconds), or stop it (stop; NOT_RECORDING when nothing records). Refused without a running game (NO_ACTIVE_SESSION). For playback, seeking or a killcam, use the sequence demo actions.

discovery.summary: Undo or redo the last editor transaction (the reply names it, or says there was none), or roll back to a restore point, undoing only what this server changed since.
whenToUse: history=undo: The most recent editor action must be reversed.
history=redo: A previously undone action must be re-applied.
history=restore_point: A multi-step change may need throwing away: begin first, rollback if the result is wrong.
history=restore_point: Before trying an approach that touches many actors or assets.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

op.description: begin opens the restore point, status lists what changed since it (the default), rollback undoes it, end closes it.

label.description: Name for the restore point (begin); default restore point.

history.description:
Which undo variant to run; omit for 'undo'.
undo: Undo the last editor transaction; the reply names it, and NOTHING_TO_UNDO means there was none.
redo: Redo the last undone editor transaction; the reply names it, and NOTHING_TO_REDO means there was none.
restore_point: Mark a restore point to roll the editor back to, undoing only what calls through this server changed, chosen by op. begin opens it (one at a time; label names it); status lists the editor's transactions since it, newest first, each with byMcp, and the assets created, removed or saved since (assetsCreated, assetsRemoved, packagesSaved); rollback undoes every step since it and refuses before undoing anything when a step was not made through this server (USER_STEP_SINCE_RESTORE_POINT names it) or the editor's history was cleared since (UNDO_HISTORY_CLEARED: a Blueprint compile or a level load clears it); end closes it. Undo deletes no created asset and restores no saved file: status and rollback list them, and cleanupCall is the manage_asset bulk_delete of the assets calls through this server created that are still there, ready to send (it asks for consent); an asset made by hand in the editor is listed but never in it. A rollback is refused while Play runs (PIE_RUNNING).

discovery.summary: Write a data table, chosen by edit. create makes a table (name and path, default /Game/DataTables, or dataTablePath) bound to the row struct at rowStructPath; create_row_struct makes a struct for its rows (name and path, default /Game/Structs, or rowStructPath) from members. add_row adds rowName with rowData, the columns it leaves out taking the struct defaults, and refuses a name already there (ROW_ALREADY_EXISTS); update_row changes only the columns rowData names in an existing row; import_rows loads rows of {rowName, rowData} in one call, each named row replaced whole (clearExisting drops every row first), and lists the rows that do not fit under invalidRows. set_row_struct (set_struct_as_row_struct is the same) binds another row struct and carries the rows over (migrateExistingRows, default true): a row whose values do not convert is dropped and listed under invalidRows, and a filled table is refused unless the rows are migrated or cleared. rowData keys are the struct property names, as inspect_data_table reads them back. Every edit saves the asset unless save is false (saved).
whenToUse: edit=create: A new DataTable is needed to hold rows of game data such as weapon stats or item lists; the row struct must already exist.
edit=create_row_struct: A new struct with named, typed columns is needed as the row type of a table.
edit=add_row: A new row must be added by name; columns left out of rowData take the row struct defaults.
edit=update_row: Some columns of an existing row must change while the columns not named keep their values.
edit=import_rows: Many rows must be loaded in one call; each named row is replaced whole and columns it omits reset to defaults.
edit=set_row_struct|set_struct_as_row_struct: A table must be bound to a different row struct; existing rows are migrated unless clearExisting drops them.
whenNotToUse: edit=create: A copy of an existing table is wanted, rows included (use asset.duplicate).
edit=create_row_struct: An existing struct only needs columns added, renamed or retyped (use struct.edit_struct).
edit=add_row: The row must be read or listed, not written (use datatable.inspect_data_table).
edit=update_row: A row must be removed instead of changed (use datatable.delete_data_table_row).
edit=import_rows: The table only needs emptying, with nothing loaded afterwards (use datatable.delete_data_table_row with deleteScope=all).

name.description: Name of the new data table (create) or row struct (create_row_struct).

path.description: Package path of the new asset: default /Game/DataTables for a table, /Game/Structs for a row struct.

dataTablePath.description: Asset path of the data table: the one to create (create, in place of name and path), or the one every other edit writes, e.g. /Game/DataTables/DT_Weapons.

rowStructPath.description: Asset path of a row struct: the one the table is bound to (create, set_row_struct), or the new struct (create_row_struct, in place of name and path).

save.description: Persist the asset to disk. Defaults to true; pass false to keep the change in memory only.

members.description: The columns of the new row struct, each { name, type } (or memberName, memberType) with optional defaultValue, tooltip and metadata. type takes Bool, Int, Float, String, Name, Text, Vector, Rotator, Transform, Object, SoftObject, Class, SoftClass, Enum:<Name> or Struct:<Path>, or a container: Array:..., Set:..., Map:<K>,<V>. Without members the struct keeps one placeholder member.

rows.description: Rows to import, each { rowName: <name>, rowData: { <field>: <value>, ... } }. The field names inside rowData are the row struct own property names, e.g. { rowName: ArcRifle, rowData: { DisplayName: Arc Rifle, Damage: 42 } }. A flat entry such as { rowName, Damage } is rejected as missing rowData.

clearExisting.description: Drop every existing row first (default false): before an import, or instead of migrating rows to a new row struct.

migrateExistingRows.description: Re-import the existing rows under the new struct (default true); rows that do not fit are reported in invalidRows.

set_row_struct: Bind a row UScriptStruct to an existing DataTable.
set_struct_as_row_struct: Set an existing UScriptStruct as the row struct for a DataTable (a user-defined struct is validated and compiled first).

discovery.summary: Judge the level viewport's picture as a reviewer would, in numbers: saliency (where the eye goes: how strongly each actor draws it, the focus point, and a named subject's rank), palette (five colours with their shares, the hue template of Cohen-Or et al. they fit best and how far the rest stray from it, and the colour cast of surfaces that should be grey), light (a lightness histogram, clipped and crushed shares, contrast, exposure, flat lighting and, on a subject lit by the sun, its key to fill ratio in stops) and cost (how much of the frame, and of each actor, the shader complexity view draws at a high cost). Read only: the camera moves only when location or rotation is given, and cost puts the viewport's view mode back after one frame in the shader complexity view.
whenToUse: Checking whether a shot draws the eye to its subject, without looking at it.
Judging a scene's palette and colour cast, or whether its lighting is flat, too dark or blown out.
Finding which actors cost the most to shade in a view.
whenNotToUse: Listing which actors are in view and their share of the frame (use describe_view).
A picture to look at is wanted (use control_editor screenshot).
Play In Editor runs: the level viewport does not show the running game (stop it, or use Simulate).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

aspects.description: What to judge (default saliency, palette and light; cost draws the viewport once in another view mode). Any other name refuses with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

subject.description: The actor the shot is about (label, name or path): its saliency share and rank, and its key to fill ratio against the sun. A name that matches no actor refuses with ACTOR_NOT_FOUND.

location.description: Camera location {x, y, z} in cm; omitted, the viewport's current one. The camera stays there afterwards, as describe_view leaves it.

rotation.description: Camera rotation {pitch, yaw, roll} in degrees; omitted, the viewport's current one.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

cellsAcross.description: Cells across the frame: each is the average of a square block of pixels, about 240 across whatever the viewport size.

saliency.description: With saliency (Boolean Map Saliency, Zhang and Sclaroff): top (up to 5 actors, ranked by density: its mean saliency per cell against the frame's mean, 1 for average, so above 1 draws the eye more than its size alone; share is its percent of the whole frame's saliency, which a large wall can hold without being what the eye goes to), background (the share where no actor is drawn), focus {x, y} (0 to 1 across and down, the most salient cell: blurred as fixations are, it can sit just beside the actor that draws it) and, with subject, subject {actorName, density, share, rank} (rank 1 draws the eye most; 0 draws no cell).

palette.description: With palette: colors [{hex, share}] (OKLab k-means, up to 5, largest first), harmony {chromatic (percent of cells with colour), template (i, V, L, I, T, Y or X), rotation (degrees), offBy (degrees the hues stray outside the template, weighted by chroma), verdict} and cast {tint (neutral, warm, cool, green or magenta), a, b (the mean OKLab shift of near-neutral surfaces)}. A score only: nothing is recoloured.

light.description: With light: histogram (8 lightness bins, percent of cells, dark to bright), clipped and crushed (percent near white or black), contrast (lightness from the darker 5 percent to the brighter 5 percent), medianLightness, flat (contrast under 0.25), exposure (dark, balanced or bright) and, with subject and a directional light, subject {lit, shadowed (percent of its cells facing toward or away from the sun), keyFill (stops brighter the lit side is drawn) or keyFillNote}; a subject whose materials are all unlit has only keyFillNote, since no light shades it.

cost.description: With cost: high (percent of the frame at red or beyond on the shader complexity ramp: a third of its maximum, its legend's Bad), mean (0 to 1) and actors [{actorName, frameShare, ofItself}] (up to 5 drawing at a high cost over at least 1% of the frame), or note when the view could not be read. The legend and crosshair the view mode draws over the frame are left out. While shaders still compile, what they cover draws with a stand-in material and a warning says so.

examples.title: Judge the level viewport's picture as a reviewer would, in numbers: saliency (where the eye goes: how strongly each actor draws it, the focus point, and a named subject's rank), palette (five colours with their shares, the hue template of Cohen-Or et al. they fit best and how far the rest stray from it, and the colour cast of surfaces that should be grey), light (a lightness histogram, clipped and crushed shares, contrast, exposure, flat lighting and, on a subject lit by the sun, its key to fill ratio in stops) and cost (how much of the frame, and of each actor, the shader complexity view draws at a high cost). Read only: the camera moves only when location or rotation is given, and cost puts the viewport's view mode back after one frame in the shader complexity view.

output.message: Analyzed the view (240 x 135 cells): saliency, light.

discovery.summary: Check the materials in the level viewport's view the way a technical artist would. pbr: the viewport is drawn in the Buffer Visualization view mode for base colour, metallic and roughness (the values the G-buffer holds, so tints and constants in the material count) and each lit, opaque actor in view is judged: too_dark (base colour under sRGB 30, darker than charcoal, on a quarter of it), too_bright (a non-metal over sRGB 240, whiter than snow; a metal's base colour is its reflectance, silver near 250), dark_metal (a metal's base colour under sRGB 155: metals reflect at least about a third of light), partial_metallic (metallic between 0.1 and 0.9 on a quarter: a surface is metal or not), mirror_roughness (roughness under 0.05 on half); an actor with an unlit or translucent material is listed under skipped with why. texel_density: each material slot of the static meshes in view at its sharpest 2D texture, as the texture streamer reckons it (texture size times the material's UV tiling for it over the mesh's UV density times the actor's scale), against the view's median: too_sharp (four times or more: memory spent on detail nobody sees) or too_blurry (a quarter or less). Only a slot whose material holds texture streaming data for the texture is judged, and the median is theirs when there are any; one without (a world-aligned material such as the engine's grid, or data never built) is listed with approximate and its ratio. instancing: static mesh actors of the level drawing one mesh with the same materials, groups of 8 or more, worth turning into one instanced mesh. Read only: the camera moves only when location or rotation is given, and the viewport's view mode and buffer are put back.
whenToUse: Reviewing a scene's materials for physically based values before lighting it: base colours too dark or too bright, half-metal surfaces, mirror-smooth roughness.
Finding a texture stretched or crammed compared to its neighbours, or a slot spending a 4K texture on a pebble.
Finding repeated meshes that could be drawn as one instanced mesh.
whenNotToUse: Judging the picture itself (where the eye goes, palette, light): use analyze_view.
Changing a material's values: use set_material_parameter or the material graph actions.
Play In Editor runs: the level viewport does not show the running game (stop it, or use Simulate).

checks.description: What to check (default all three). Any other name refuses with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

location.description: Camera location {x, y, z} in cm; omitted, the viewport's current one. The camera stays there afterwards, as describe_view leaves it.

rotation.description: Camera rotation {pitch, yaw, roll} in degrees; omitted, the viewport's current one.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

pbr.description: With pbr: judged and flagged (actors covering at least 20 cells of the view), actors [{actorName, share (of the view), baseColor [r, g, b] (median, sRGB 0-255), metallic and roughness (medians, 0-1), findings}] (flagged ones first, 30 at most) and skipped [{actorName, reason}] (unlit or translucent materials, which the G-buffer does not show), or note when the view could not be read.

texelDensity.description: With texel_density: medianTexelsPerMetre (of the judged slots in view, else of all), slots, judged (slots with streaming data), outliers and rows [{actorName, slot, material, texture, texelsPerMetre, ratio (to the median), finding (too_sharp or too_blurry), approximate (true when the material has no texture streaming data for the texture: UV channel 0 and no tiling assumed, so no finding)}] (furthest from the median first, 40 at most), or note.

discovery.summary: Capture the level viewport's view as machine-readable passes, aligned pixel for pixel: id (a PNG with one colour per actor, and the legend naming each colour's actor), depth (an EXR of the distance in cm) and normal (a PNG of the world normal, RGB = normal x 0.5 + 0.5), with a summary of each. location and rotation place the camera first, as describe_view and control_editor screenshot take them.
whenToUse: A frame must be analysed by a script, a probe or a model: which actor covers a region (id), how far each pixel is (depth), which way surfaces face (normal).
Regions of a screenshot must be attributed to actors, or distances in a shot measured.
whenNotToUse: A picture to look at is wanted (use control_editor screenshot).
Only which actors are in view and their share is needed (use describe_view, which writes no files).
Passes of a rendered sequence are needed (use manage_sequence add_render_pass).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

location.description: Camera location {x, y, z} in cm; omitted, the viewport's current one. The camera stays there.

rotation.description: Camera rotation {pitch, yaw, roll} in degrees; omitted, the viewport's current one.

width.description: Width of every pass in pixels (default 960, 64 to 4096); the height follows the viewport's shape so the passes line up with it.

outputPath.description: Folder inside the project, project-relative or absolute (default Saved/Captures).

name.description: File name prefix (default Passes_<date>_<time>): files are <name>_id.png, <name>_depth.exr and <name>_normal.png.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

fov.description: Horizontal field of view in degrees.

files.description: Absolute path of each pass written.

ids.description: id: each actor in the id image, largest first (up to 256): color (#rrggbb in the PNG), name (actor label), class and coverage (percent of the frame). Black is background (sky, void), dark grey (#404040) what only the editor draws.

depth.description: depth: nearest, median and farthest distance of the drawn pixels in cm, and the percent that is sky (nothing within 100 km).

normal.description: normal: percent of the drawn pixels facing up (normal z above 0.7), down (below -0.7) and sideways.

examples.title: Capture the level viewport's view as machine-readable passes, aligned pixel for pixel: id (a PNG with one colour per actor, and the legend naming each colour's actor), depth (an EXR of the distance in cm) and normal (a PNG of the world normal, RGB = normal x 0.5 + 0.5), with a summary of each. location and rotation place the camera first, as describe_view and control_editor screenshot take them.

discovery.summary: List what changed in the editor since a cursor: level actors added, deleted, moved or modified (with the properties edited and their values) and assets or levels created, removed, renamed, modified, saved or opened, each marked by who changed it: mcp (a call through this server), user (an edit made in the editor, and its undo and redo) or editor (anything else, such as saving, importing or opening a level by hand). The engine's own work on actors and objects (loading a level, compiling) is not kept. The reply hands back the cursor to send next time; without one it lists the most recent changes kept. Changes merge per object; 4096 objects are kept, and a cursor from before an editor restart or older than what is kept answers CHANGE_CURSOR_EXPIRED.
whenToUse: Work resumes after a pause, or another agent or the user may have changed the level: read what changed instead of listing everything again.
A reply warned that the user changed something in the editor since the last call.
whenNotToUse: The level's current contents are wanted, not what changed (use control_actor list).
Which editor transactions this server made since a restore point (use control_editor restore_point with op status).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

since.description: The cursor a previous changes_since reply returned. Omit it to get the most recent changes kept, and a cursor to start from.

limit.description: Most changes to list, oldest first (1-200, default 50). When more are left, truncated is true and the cursor returned continues from the last one listed.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

cursor.description: Send this as since next time to read only what changes after this reply.

truncated.description: More changes are left after these: call again with the cursor returned.

changes.description: One row per changed object, oldest change first: object (an actor's label, or an asset's package path), path, kind (actor, asset or level), events (added, modified, deleted, saved, renamed, removed, opened), by (mcp, user, editor), properties (the properties edited, at most 8), values (each edited property with from, its value before the first change kept, when the edit announced it beforehand as the Details panel does, and to, its value after the latest; a property changed back is left out), transform (for a live actor that stands elsewhere than when its first change was kept: location, rotation and scale that differ, each {from, to} as [x, y, z] or [pitch, yaw, roll]), actions (the calls through this server that changed it) and oldPath for a renamed asset.

examples.title: List what changed in the editor since a cursor: level actors added, deleted, moved or modified (with the properties edited and their values) and assets or levels created, removed, renamed, modified, saved or opened, each marked by who changed it: mcp (a call through this server), user (an edit made in the editor, and its undo and redo) or editor (anything else, such as saving, importing or opening a level by hand). The engine's own work on actors and objects (loading a level, compiling) is not kept. The reply hands back the cursor to send next time; without one it lists the most recent changes kept. Changes merge per object; 4096 objects are kept, and a cursor from before an editor restart or older than what is kept answers CHANGE_CURSOR_EXPIRED.

discovery.summary: Check whether a static mesh's geometry is sound, from its source triangles: closed (watertight) or open with how many holes, edges shared by three or more faces, faces turned inside out, faces with no area, seams where faces do not share their corners, and how many separate parts it is made of, with its size, surface area and (when closed) volume.
whenToUse: An imported, downloaded or generated mesh must be proven sound before it is placed, merged, used for collision or booleans, or shipped.
A mesh shows see-through gaps, black or inside-out faces, or splits into loose pieces.
whenNotToUse: Only the mesh's size, pivot, slots or triangle counts per material are needed (use inspect_object objectKind mesh).
The mesh must be cut into one asset per part (use manage_geometry split_mesh).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

meshPath.description: Static mesh asset path, e.g. /Game/Meshes/SM_Rock. Its source triangles (LOD 0 as imported or built) are checked, so a Nanite mesh answers at full detail. A placed actor's mesh is named by get_components.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

vertices.description: Distinct corner positions (to 0.01 cm): corners at one place count once, whether or not the source shares the vertex.

size.description: Extent [x, y, z] in cm, in the mesh's own space.

closed.description: True when every edge joins exactly two faces (seams count as joined): the surface is watertight (a solid, not a sheet or a shell with gaps).

volume.description: With closed: the volume it encloses, in cm³.

openEdges.description: Edges with a face on one side only and none on the other at that place: the outlines of holes and open rims.

holes.description: Separate outlines those open edges form (one per hole or open rim).

seamEdges.description: Places where two faces meet without sharing their corners (split for flat shading or UV seams): the surface renders whole, but booleans, remeshing and collision built from the mesh need it welded.

nonManifoldEdges.description: Edges shared by three or more faces (fins, faces stacked on one edge); they break booleans, remeshing and collision generation.

flippedEdges.description: Edges (seams included) whose two faces wind the same way along them, so one of the two faces points inward (a face turned inside out renders dark or vanishes).

degenerateTriangles.description: Faces with no area (slivers or a repeated corner).

parts.description: Separate pieces: groups of faces joined by corners at the same place.

largestParts.description: Up to 8 pieces, largest first: triangles, size [x, y, z] and center [x, y, z] in cm, in the mesh's own space.

examples.title: Check whether a static mesh's geometry is sound, from its source triangles: closed (watertight) or open with how many holes, edges shared by three or more faces, faces turned inside out, faces with no area, seams where faces do not share their corners, and how many separate parts it is made of, with its size, surface area and (when closed) volume.

discovery.summary: One image of an actor from several sides: front, back, left, right and top as true elevations (orthographic, in the actor's own turned frame, with a grid every round number of centimetres) and a three-quarter view, each tile labelled, the actor's size in the title. Shaded as clay from the geometry, the same whatever lights the level: the actor orange, everything else grey, and the parts of the actor hidden behind something (a foot sunk in the floor, a back against a wall) showing through it. Only the actor and the actors within reach of it are drawn, so a wall farther off never hides it while the floor it stands in stays. Returned as an image and written as a PNG under Saved/Captures; the level viewport is not moved.
whenToUse: Checking an actor from every side at once: sunk into the floor or floating, a missing back, a wrong size against the grid, a part poking through another.
Reviewing a prop or character after placing it, without moving the level viewport.
whenNotToUse: A picture of what the level viewport's camera sees is wanted (use control_editor screenshot).
Numbers about a shot are wanted rather than a picture (use describe_view or analyze_view).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: The actor to show (label, name or path). One that matches no actor refuses with ACTOR_NOT_FOUND; one that draws nothing the game shows (only editor icons) refuses with NOTHING_DRAWN.

views.description: The views, in this order (default all six). front looks at the side the actor faces (its X axis); left and right are its own; top looks straight down with its front at the bottom of the tile; three_quarter is a perspective view from its front right, above.

tileSize.description: Side of each square tile in pixels (default 320); the sheet is three tiles across.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

file.description: Absolute path of the PNG written.

size.description: The actor's drawn size in cm along its own X (front to back), Y (side to side) and Z.

views.description: Each tile in order: view and, for an elevation, grid (cm between lines; vertical lines pass the actor's pivot, horizontal ones in front, back, left and right sit at round heights above the world's zero).

shown.description: The other actors drawn: those whose boxes come within reach of the actor's (up to 63).

imageBase64.description: The sheet as a PNG, base64, returned as an image; left out past 3 MB (the file has it).

examples.title: One image of an actor from several sides: front, back, left, right and top as true elevations (orthographic, in the actor's own turned frame, with a grid every round number of centimetres) and a three-quarter view, each tile labelled, the actor's size in the title. Shaded as clay from the geometry, the same whatever lights the level: the actor orange, everything else grey, and the parts of the actor hidden behind something (a foot sunk in the floor, a back against a wall) showing through it. Only the actor and the actors within reach of it are drawn, so a wall farther off never hides it while the floor it stands in stays. Returned as an image and written as a PNG under Saved/Captures; the level viewport is not moved.

topics: what is at this point on screen
compare the view before and after
did the edit change the picture
discovery.summary: Describe what the level viewport's camera sees, as text: each actor in view with its share of the frame, its box on screen, how bright it is drawn and its distance, the share that is background (sky, void), and the frame's brightness; or only the actors named, with what hides each one that is not seen. points names what is under spots of the frame and where they are in the world; labels returns the frame with each listed actor boxed and numbered; saveAs keeps the frame under a name and compareWith says what changed in the picture since, region by region, with the actors drawn there before and after. location and rotation place the camera first, as control_editor screenshot takes them.
whenToUse: A shot must be checked without looking at a picture: is the subject in view, how much of the frame it fills, where it sits, whether it is lit or lost in the dark.
A camera placement must be compared or tuned by numbers (subject coverage, sky share, brightness).
A spot of the frame (from a screenshot, a click, a box) must be turned into an actor and a world location: points.
A picture where every actor is boxed and numbered to match the list is wanted, to point at one by number: labels.
Checking that an edit changed the picture where it should, and nowhere else: saveAs before it, compareWith after.
whenNotToUse: A picture is wanted (use control_editor screenshot).
Play In Editor runs: the level viewport does not show the running game (stop it, or use Simulate).
Whether collision blocks a line between two points (use raycast_world).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actors.description: Only these actors (label, name or path): their rows under actors (a row whose box nearer actors partly cover names them under coveredBy, as a sign half behind a row of blocks), and under notVisible each one that drew no pixel with its reason, outside the frame or hidden, with hiddenBy naming the actors drawn over its box (up to three, by share of the box). Names that match no actor are listed under notFound. limit does not apply.

location.description: Camera location {x, y, z} in cm; omitted, the viewport's current one. The camera stays there.

rotation.description: Camera rotation {pitch, yaw, roll} in degrees; omitted, the viewport's current one.

limit.description: Most actors to list, largest share first (default 20, at most 100); visibleActors counts them all.

points.description: Spots of the frame as {x, y} from 0 to 1 (x from the left, y from the top; 0.5, 0.5 is the middle): each answers under points at the same index with what is drawn there and what the line from the camera through it hits. A perspective viewport only.

labels.description: Also return the frame (at most 960 px wide) with each actor listed under actors boxed in its own colour and numbered from 1 in list order, as an image (imageBase64).

tolerance.description: With points: a spot where no actor is drawn (just beside a thin pole, past an edge) moves to the nearest pixel within this many where one is, and its row says where under snappedTo (default 0: no move).

saveAs.description: Keep this frame under a name for a later compareWith, with the camera it was taken from (until the editor closes; the same name replaces it, and a ninth name forgets the oldest). Drawn twice, to learn how much the renderer varies an unchanged frame by itself. With saveAs or compareWith the frame is read as the game draws it, so icons, gizmos and selection outlines are left out and other reads 0.

compareWith.description: Compare this frame with the one saved under that name, taken again from its camera: change lists what changed beyond the renderer's own noise. Refused with VIEW_BASELINE_NOT_FOUND for a name not saved, VIEW_SIZE_CHANGED when the viewport changed size, and CAMERA_MOVED when location or rotation (or the field of view) differs from the saved camera. With saveAs in the same call, the comparison comes first.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

visibleActors.description: Actors the game would draw with at least one pixel in the frame.

actors.description: Largest share first: name (actor label), class, coverage (percent of the frame), box [left, top, right, bottom] in percent of the frame's width and height, brightness (0-1, as drawn) and distance (cm from the camera to its bounds); with actors, coveredBy [{name, share}] lists the nearer actors drawn over at least 5% of its box. Editor icons and shapes hidden in game are left out.

background.description: Percent of the frame where no object was drawn (sky, void).

other.description: Percent drawn by what only the editor shows (icons, gizmos, shapes hidden in game) or no actor owns (BSP).

brightness.description: The frame as drawn: p10, median and p90 brightness (0-1), and the percent of the frame clipped (a channel at full) or dark (below 0.05).

notVisible.description: With actors: each named actor that drew no pixel, as {name, reason (outside the frame; at the edge of the frame, mostly outside it; hidden behind what is drawn over its box; or not drawn with nothing nearer over it), inFrame (percent of its projected box inside the frame), hiddenBy [{name, share (percent of its box)}], which leaves out actors centred farther than it and the ground under it}.

notFound.description: With actors: the names that match no actor.

points.description: With points, one per spot: x, y; drawn (actor, editor for what only the editor draws, or background); actorName, the actor drawn there; and hit, what the line from the camera through the spot hits first against Visibility collision: location, normal, distance (cm), actorName and componentName. A drawn actor with no collision is passed through, so hit can name what is behind it; no hit means nothing within 20 km. With tolerance, snappedTo {x, y} is the spot it moved to.

imageBase64.description: With labels: the frame as a PNG, base64, with each listed actor boxed and numbered; returned as an image.

change.description: With compareWith: comparedWith, changed (percent of the frame that changed: 8 x 8 pixel blocks compared by structure (SSIM) and colour beyond the renderer's own noise), regionCount, regions (up to 8, largest first: box [left, top, right, bottom] in percent of the frame, share of the frame, and before and after [{name, share}], the actors drawn there in each frame, up to three, by share of the region) and brightnessShift (mean brightness now minus then, -1 to 1). A moved actor shows as a region where it was and one where it is; no regions means nothing changed.

savedAs.description: With saveAs: the name the frame is kept under.

examples.title: Describe what the level viewport's camera sees, as text: each actor in view with its share of the frame, its box on screen, how bright it is drawn and its distance, the share that is background (sky, void), and the frame's brightness; or only the actors named, with what hides each one that is not seen. points names what is under spots of the frame and where they are in the world; labels returns the frame with each listed actor boxed and numbered; saveAs keeps the frame under a name and compareWith says what changed in the picture since, region by region, with the actors drawn there before and after. location and rotation place the camera first, as control_editor screenshot takes them.

discovery.summary: Explain why something does not happen, chosen by what: two actors that do not overlap or hit (collision), an actor that is not seen (visible), a key that does nothing (input), a widget not on screen (widget), a sound not heard (audible), a light that lights nothing (lit). Each walks an ordered fault tree over what the engine holds and answers the first cause with the call that fixes it, plus every check made.
whenToUse: what=collision: An overlap or hit event between two actors never fires.
what=collision: A trigger volume does nothing when something walks into it.
what=visible: A placed actor does not appear in the viewport or in Play.
what=input: A key or button press does nothing in Play.
what=input: An input action event never fires.
what=widget: A HUD, menu or other widget never appears.
what=audible: A placed sound or an actor's audio is silent.
what=lit: A light seems to have no effect on the scene or on one actor.
whenNotToUse: what=collision: The collision settings must be changed (use control_actor set_actor_collision, the nextCall the cause names).
what=visible: The actor should be found first; use inspect query_object or the outliner.
what=input: Legacy (Project Settings) input mappings: only Enhanced Input is explained.
what=widget: The widget appears but its layout is wrong (use manage_blueprint get_widget_info to read its tree).
what=audible: The sound must be changed or started (use manage_audio).
what=lit: The light must be created or tuned (use build_environment lighting actions).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: The first actor, by label, name or path.

otherActor.description: The second actor, by label, name or path.

event.description: The event that should happen: overlap (default) or hit.

actionPath.description: The Input Action asset the key should fire, e.g. /Game/Input/IA_Jump.

key.description: The key pressed, by engine key name (SpaceBar, E, Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom); omitted, any key mapped to the action counts.

widgetPath.description: The Widget Blueprint that should show, e.g. /Game/UI/WBP_HUD.

targetActor.description: The actor the light should reach; omitted, only the light itself is checked.

what.description:
Which explain variant to run.
collision: Explain why actorName and otherActor do not overlap (event overlap, the default) or hit each other (event hit), from what the engine uses to decide: collision turned off on an actor (ACTOR_COLLISION_DISABLED), no component taking part in collision queries (NO_COLLIDING_COMPONENT), a static mesh with no collision shape (NO_COLLISION_SHAPE), a channel response on either side that ignores the other's object type (RESPONSE_IGNORES; a hit needs Block both ways, RESPONSE_DOES_NOT_BLOCK), two blockers that raise hits rather than overlaps (BLOCKS_INSTEAD), Generate Overlap Events off on a side (OVERLAP_EVENTS_OFF), a simulating body without hit events (HIT_EVENTS_OFF), one told to ignore the other (IGNORED_WHEN_MOVING), and whether they touch now. Reads the running game during Play, the editor level otherwise. The reply gives verdict (failed, unknown when a check could not be made, or ok), cause (the first failed check: check, code, detail and, when one fixes it, nextCall), causes (every failed check) and checks (each check made, in order, passed, failed or unknown). Nothing is changed.
visible: Explain why actorName is not seen, from the player's camera during Play or the editor viewport otherwise: hidden in the game or in the editor (HIDDEN_IN_GAME, HIDDEN_IN_EDITOR), editor-only during Play (EDITOR_ONLY), its streaming level not visible (LEVEL_HIDDEN), no component that draws (NOTHING_TO_DRAW: each hidden, unregistered, or a static mesh component with no mesh), beyond a component's draw distance (CULLED_BY_DISTANCE), nearer than the near clip plane (INSIDE_NEAR_CLIP), outside the camera's field of view (OUT_OF_VIEW), drawn only for its owner or hidden from its owner (ONLY_OWNER_SEES, OWNER_NO_SEE), or buried in the surface under it (BURIED, with the location that rests it on top). The reply names the view it judged from (viewFrom). The reply gives verdict (failed, unknown when a check could not be made, or ok), cause (the first failed check: check, code, detail and, when one fixes it, nextCall), causes (every failed check) and checks (each check made, in order, passed, failed or unknown). Nothing is changed.
input: Explain why the Enhanced Input action at actionPath (pressed with key, when given) does nothing: no mapping context under /Game maps it (NOT_MAPPED), no Add Mapping Context node adds such a context in the game mode's player controller or pawn Blueprints, or during Play the player has none of them added (CONTEXT_NOT_ADDED: every key stays dead), and no event for the action in those Blueprints (NOT_HANDLED); during Play also no possessed pawn (NO_PAWN), a paused game (GAME_PAUSED) and a widget holding keyboard focus (WIDGET_HAS_FOCUS). A missing action is ACTION_NOT_FOUND. The reply gives verdict (failed, unknown when a check could not be made, or ok), cause (the first failed check: check, code, detail and, when one fixes it, nextCall), causes (every failed check) and checks (each check made, in order, passed, failed or unknown). Nothing is changed.
widget: Explain why the Widget Blueprint at widgetPath is not on screen. During Play: no instance exists (NOT_CREATED), one exists but was never added to the viewport or to another widget (NOT_IN_VIEWPORT), its visibility is Collapsed or Hidden (HIDDEN), its render opacity is 0 (TRANSPARENT), or its desired size is 0 by 0 (ZERO_SIZE). Outside Play: no Create Widget node for it in the game mode's player controller, pawn or HUD Blueprint or the level's own (NOT_CREATED_ANYWHERE), or the Blueprint that creates it never adds it to the viewport (NOT_ADDED); whether it is on screen is then unknown until Play. A missing Widget Blueprint is WIDGET_NOT_FOUND. The reply gives verdict (failed, unknown when a check could not be made, or ok), cause (the first failed check: check, code, detail and, when one fixes it, nextCall), causes (every failed check) and checks (each check made, in order, passed, failed or unknown). Nothing is changed.
audible: Explain why actorName's sound is not heard: no audio component (NO_AUDIO_COMPONENT), no sound on it (NO_SOUND), not playing during Play (NOT_PLAYING) or not starting by itself (NOT_AUTO_ACTIVATED), a volume multiplier of 0 (MUTED), or the listener beyond its attenuation range (OUT_OF_RANGE: inner radius plus falloff). The listener is the player's during Play (often the camera, far from the pawn in a side view) and the editor viewport otherwise (listener in the reply). The reply gives verdict (failed, unknown when a check could not be made, or ok), cause (the first failed check: check, code, detail and, when one fixes it, nextCall), causes (every failed check) and checks (each check made, in order, passed, failed or unknown). Nothing is changed.
lit: Explain why the light actorName lights nothing, or does not light targetActor: hidden or not affecting the world (LIGHT_OFF), an intensity of 0 (NO_INTENSITY), a Static light with lighting unbuilt (UNBUILT_LIGHTING), and against targetActor: beyond the attenuation radius (OUT_OF_RANGE, with the radius that reaches it), outside a spot light's outer cone (OUTSIDE_CONE), or no lighting channel in common (CHANNEL_MISMATCH). A light not found is LIGHT_NOT_FOUND. Auto exposure can also hide a lighting change: look with a fixed exposure before judging by eye. The reply gives verdict (failed, unknown when a check could not be made, or ok), cause (the first failed check: check, code, detail and, when one fixes it, nextCall), causes (every failed check) and checks (each check made, in order, passed, failed or unknown). Nothing is changed.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: World actor name to inspect.

name.description: Actor name identifier (alias of actorName).

propertyNames.description: Property values to add to the reply, by name (Intensity, bIsActive), as text under properties; a name the class lacks is listed under missingProperties. CollisionResponses reads every channel's response on a primitive component ({"Pawn": "Ignore", ...}). Without propertyNames or detailed no property values come back.

detailed.description: Every property the component's class declares, as text (up to 200): a Niagara or mesh component declares about 200, most of the reply. Prefer propertyNames.

On an actor the path may start with a component's name, including one added in the level (MyAudio.VolumeMultiplier). A bare name that is not on the object itself resolves to the one struct member carrying it. Give this or propertyPath.

propertyPath.description: Same as propertyName (a name or dotted path); used when propertyName is absent. Give this or propertyName.

info.description:
Which get component details variant to run; omit for 'details'.

property: Read a property on a world actor component (cross-parent to control_actor).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

componentName.description: Component name on the actor.

value.description: The value read; its type follows the property.

examples.title: Read one component of an actor or Blueprint: class, relative and world transform, mobility, visibility, attachment, bounds, collision, mesh and chosen property values; info=property returns a single property's value.

A mesh component adds its static mesh and the material drawn in each slot, overrides included; a Blueprint component adds its relative transform and visibility. componentNames narrows the list, naming the ones not found under missingComponents.
whenToUse: An actor's component list must be enumerated.
whenNotToUse: A single component's properties are needed; use get_component_property.
