kind.description:
Which create behavior tree variant to run; omit for 'behavior_tree'.
behavior_tree: Create a Behavior Tree asset named name in path (default /Game/AI/BehaviorTrees; savePath when path is absent), saved (saved); an asset already at the path is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS). It has no root yet: the first add_composite_node becomes the root.
graph_route: Create a Behavior Tree named name in savePath (default /Game; a path without a leading slash goes under /Game) with its editor graph, saved (saved). An asset already at the path is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS).
blackboard: Create a Blackboard asset named name in path (default /Game/AI/Blackboards), saved (saved). A Blackboard already there is kept as it is (alreadyExisted true); another kind of asset at the path is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

alreadyExisted.description: Whether a Blackboard was already at the path; it is kept as it was.

examples.title: Create an AI asset named name, chosen by kind, each saved (saved): behavior_tree a Behavior Tree in path (default /Game/AI/BehaviorTrees), graph_route the same in savePath (default /Game), blackboard a Blackboard in path (default /Game/AI/Blackboards), where a Blackboard already there is kept (alreadyExisted). Any other asset already at the path is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS).

discovery.summary: Create navigation helpers, chosen by kind: link_proxy places a NavLinkProxy whose point link joins startPoint and endPoint (relative to it) so agents cross a gap the navmesh does not connect; smart_link places one whose smart link alone does, switchable on and off; modifier places a NavModifierVolume marking the navmesh under it with areaClass (default NavArea_Obstacle) or, with blueprintPath, adds a NavModifier component to a Blueprint; modifier_component adds that component to a Blueprint or a placed actor. A label or component name already taken is refused.
whenToUse: kind=link_proxy: A level needs an authored navigation link between two points.
kind=smart_link: A level needs a navigation link that can toggle its area class.
kind=modifier: A region or an actor must mark the navmesh under it as a different area class.
kind=modifier_component: A Blueprint or a placed actor should carve or alter navigation around itself.
whenNotToUse: kind=modifier_component: Use set_nav_area_class to change the area of an existing component.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

location.description: World location for the spawned link actor.

rotation.description: Rotation as {pitch, yaw, roll} in degrees.

startPoint.description: Start of the link, relative to the link actor (its location and rotation).

endPoint.description: End of the link, relative to the link actor (its location and rotation).

direction.description: Which way agents may cross: BothWays (default), LeftToRight (start to end) or RightToLeft.

blueprintPath.description: Blueprint that receives a NavModifier component; omit to place a NavModifierVolume in the editor level instead.

componentName.description: Name of the component to add.

failsafeToDefaultNavmesh.description: Fall back to the default navmesh area when the modifier area class is unset.

extent.description: Half-size of the placed NavModifierVolume (volume form only; default 200, 200, 100).

failsafeExtent.description: Failsafe extent used when the actor has no collision.

save.description: Save the Blueprint asset after adding the component (Blueprint form only).

kind.description:
Which create nav actor variant to run.
link_proxy: Place a NavLinkProxy at location (and rotation) whose point link joins startPoint and endPoint, relative to the actor, in direction (BothWays by default, LeftToRight or RightToLeft), so agents path across a gap, drop or jump the navmesh does not connect; each end needs navmesh under it. Labelled actorName (an actor already under it is refused, NAME_TAKEN), else its own unique name; one undo step, the level left unsaved. The reply gives the link type, its endpoints and direction.
smart_link: Place a NavLinkProxy at location whose smart link alone (no point link beside it) joins startPoint and endPoint, relative to the actor, in direction (default BothWays): a link that can be switched on and off and change its navigation area (configure_smart_link_behavior); reacting when an agent reaches it needs a Blueprint child of NavLinkProxy (its Receive Smart Link Reached event). Labelled actorName (an actor already under it is refused, NAME_TAKEN); one undo step, the level left unsaved.
modifier: Stamp a navigation area: place a NavModifierVolume in the level, or with blueprintPath add a NavModifier component to a Blueprint.
modifier_component: Add a navigation modifier component to a Blueprint asset or to a placed actor.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

componentName.description: Name of the component to add.

examples.title: Create navigation helpers, chosen by kind: link_proxy places a NavLinkProxy whose point link joins startPoint and endPoint (relative to it) so agents cross a gap the navmesh does not connect; smart_link places one whose smart link alone does, switchable on and off; modifier places a NavModifierVolume marking the navmesh under it with areaClass (default NavArea_Obstacle) or, with blueprintPath, adds a NavModifier component to a Blueprint; modifier_component adds that component to a Blueprint or a placed actor. A label or component name already taken is refused.

discovery.summary: Edit a Behavior Tree graph: add composite, task, decorator, service or generic nodes and subnodes, connect or break connections, configure or remove nodes.
whenToUse: edit=add_composite: A Behavior Tree needs a Selector, Sequence or Simple Parallel branch.

edit=add_task: A Behavior Tree branch needs a leaf task. An enemy that chases the player is a Sequence with a MoveTo task whose Blackboard key (an Object key such as TargetActor) holds the player, run on its AI controller with run_behavior_tree.
edit=add_decorator: A Behavior Tree branch needs a conditional gate.
edit=add_service: A Behavior Tree branch needs recurring background work.
edit=add_node: A Behavior Tree graph needs a node placed at explicit coordinates.
edit=add_subnode: A graph node needs a decorator or service attached by class.
edit=connect: A parent graph node must be linked to a child.
edit=break_connections: A graph node must be detached from its links.
edit=configure_node: An existing Behavior Tree node needs property edits.
edit=set_node_properties: A graph node needs property or comment edits.
edit=remove_node: A graph node must be deleted.

compositeType.description: Composite node type: Selector, Sequence, or SimpleParallel (Parallel is the same).

nodeName.description: Name for the created composite node.

parentNodeId.description: ID of the parent node: 'root', a node GUID, or a node id as returned by add_composite/add_task (for example BTComposite_Selector_0).

nodeId.description: ID of the node.

subnodeType.description: Behavior Tree subnode kind for add_subnode.

comment.description: Comment text applied to the graph node.

edit.description:
Which edit behavior tree variant to run.
add_composite: Add a composite to a Behavior Tree and save it: compositeType Selector (runs its children until one succeeds), Sequence (until one fails) or SimpleParallel (Parallel is the same: its first child is the main task, the second runs beside it). It goes under parentNodeId (a composite by nodeId or nodeName), else under the root, and a tree with no root takes it as the root (isRoot). nodeName names it; nodeId and nodeName in the reply address it for edit=add_task, edit=add_decorator and edit=add_service. Another compositeType is refused (INVALID_ARGUMENT), as is a parent that is not found (PARENT_NOT_FOUND).
add_task: Add a task node to a Behavior Tree asset.
add_decorator: Add a decorator to a Behavior Tree node, or to the root when no node is named.
add_service: Add a service to a Behavior Tree asset.
add_node: Add a node through the Behavior Tree graph route.
add_subnode: Add a Behavior Tree decorator or service subnode.
connect: Connect Behavior Tree graph nodes.
break_connections: Break Behavior Tree graph connections.
configure_node: Configure a Behavior Tree node.
set_node_properties: Set Behavior Tree graph node properties.
remove_node: Remove a Behavior Tree graph node.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

nodeName.description: Resolved name of the created composite node.

isRoot.description: Whether this node became the tree root.

nodeId.description: ID of the node.

examples.title: Edit a Behavior Tree graph: add composite, task, decorator, service or generic nodes and subnodes, connect or break connections, configure or remove nodes.

discovery.summary: Edit a Blackboard asset (blackboardPath), chosen by edit, each saved: add_key adds keyName of keyType (an Object key a MoveTo target uses wants baseObjectClass /Script/Engine.Actor; an Enum key takes enumType), set_value sets the default a key starts with (UE 5.4+, Enum, Object and Class keys 5.5+), set_key_instance_synced shares one value across every AI. A taken name (NAME_TAKEN), a value of the wrong kind, a key of a parent Blackboard (KEY_IN_PARENT) and engine content are refused.
whenToUse: edit=add_key: A Blackboard needs a new typed entry, such as the actor an AI chases or the place it moves to.
edit=set_value: A Blackboard key needs a different authored default, such as a speed or a starting state.
edit=set_key_instance_synced: A Blackboard key must share its value across instances.

keyName.description: Blackboard key name, matched in any case.

baseObjectClass.description: Class an Object key holds or a Class key names, as a class path or name (e.g. /Script/Engine.Actor); Object and Class keys only. Without it the key is based on Object, which actor-only key filters such as the MoveTo target skip.

enumType.description: Enum an Enum key holds, by path (/Game/Enums/E_State, /Script/Engine.ECollisionChannel); Enum keys only. Without it the key has no enumerators to hold.

isInstanceSynced.description: Share the value of the key across every Blackboard component using this asset, so a value one AI sets reaches them all.

value.description: The default, in the kind the key holds: a boolean, a number, {x, y, z}, {pitch, yaw, roll}, text, an enumerator, or an asset or class path.

edit.description:
Which edit blackboard variant to run.
add_key: Add a key to a Blackboard asset (blackboardPath) and save it: keyName of keyType Bool, Int, Float, Vector, Rotator, Object, Class, Enum, Name or String. An Object or Class key is based on Object unless baseObjectClass names another class, and actor-only key filters (the target key of MoveTo) skip a key not based on Actor, so the actor an AI chases wants baseObjectClass /Script/Engine.Actor; an Enum key takes its enumerators from enumType. isInstanceSynced (default false) shares the value across every AI using the asset, and Blackboards deriving from this one get the key too. A name this Blackboard or a parent already has is refused (NAME_TAKEN), as are a class or enum that does not load and engine content (ENGINE_CONTENT).
set_value: Set the default of a Blackboard key, the value it holds when an AI starts with the asset, and save it: UE 5.4+ for Bool, Int, Float, Vector, Rotator, Name and String keys, 5.5+ for Enum, Object and Class keys. value takes the kind the key holds: true or false, a whole number, a number, {x, y, z}, {pitch, yaw, roll}, text, an enumerator by name or value, an asset path for an Object key (placed actors are not assets; None clears it) or a class path for a Class key. A value of the wrong kind or outside the base class of the key is refused, as is a key with no default on this engine (NOT_SUPPORTED) or one a parent Blackboard holds (KEY_IN_PARENT); value in the reply is what the key now holds.
set_key_instance_synced: Mark a Blackboard key instance-synced (isInstanceSynced, default true) or not, and save the asset. A synced key holds one value shared by every Blackboard component using the asset, so a value one AI sets reaches all of them. A key already set that way changes nothing (changed false), and a key a parent Blackboard holds is refused (KEY_IN_PARENT), naming the parent.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

baseClass.description: Class path an Object or Class key is based on.

saved.description: Whether the Blackboard reached disk.

value.description: The default the key now holds, as the engine writes it.

examples.title: Edit a Blackboard asset (blackboardPath), chosen by edit, each saved: add_key adds keyName of keyType (an Object key a MoveTo target uses wants baseObjectClass /Script/Engine.Actor; an Enum key takes enumType), set_value sets the default a key starts with (UE 5.4+, Enum, Object and Class keys 5.5+), set_key_instance_synced shares one value across every AI. A taken name (NAME_TAKEN), a value of the wrong kind, a key of a parent Blackboard (KEY_IN_PARENT) and engine content are refused.

discovery.summary: Create an Environment Query or edit it, chosen by edit, each saved: create makes the asset, add_generator gives an option its items (ActorsOfClass, CurrentLocation, Donut, OnCircle, PathingGrid, SimpleGrid, Composite), add_test adds a test (Distance, Dot, GameplayTags, Overlap, Pathfinding, PathfindingBatch, Project, Random, Trace), add_context points a generator or test at the querier, the items or a context class, configure_test_scoring sets the equation, clamps and filter of a test. A Behavior Tree runs it with a Run EQS Query task.
whenToUse: edit=create: An AI needs a spatial query asset.
edit=add_generator: An Environment Query needs its candidate item set.
edit=add_test: Generated Environment Query items need scoring or filtering.
edit=add_context: A generator should search around the querier or a test should measure to a context.
edit=configure_test_scoring: An existing Environment Query test needs scoring or filter tuning.

name.description: Name for the created asset or actor.

path.description: Canonical /Game output path for the created asset.

generatorSettings.description: Settings the generator reads, refused when it does not: ActorsOfClass searchRadius (also keeps items inside it) and actorClass; SimpleGrid and PathingGrid gridSize (half the grid side) and spacesBetween; OnCircle searchRadius or outerRadius (the circle radius) and spacesBetween; Donut innerRadius and outerRadius. Where a generator centers is set with add_eqs_context.

contextType.description: Querier (the AI running the query), Item (each item being tested), or Custom with contextClass.

contextClass.description: Context class for contextType Custom: a Blueprint based on EnvQueryContext_BlueprintBase, or a context class path.

contextProperty.description: Context property of the generator or test to set (SearchCenter, GenerateAround, DistanceTo, Context); default the first one it has.

testIndex.description: Test index counted across all options of the query, in the order the tests were added (the testIndex add_eqs_test returned).

optionIndex.description: Option whose generator takes the context when no testIndex is sent (default 0).

edit.description:
Which edit eqs query variant to run.
create: Create an Environment Query asset named name in path (default /Game/AI/EQS), saved (saved); an asset already at the path is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS). It has no items until edit=add_generator gives it a generator.
add_generator: Add an option to an Environment Query with a generator of generatorType and save it: ActorsOfClass, CurrentLocation, Donut, OnCircle, PathingGrid, SimpleGrid or Composite, with the generatorSettings that generator reads (a setting it does not read, or an actorClass that is no Actor, is refused). A generator centers on the querier unless edit=add_context points it elsewhere; optionIndex in the reply addresses the option.
add_test: Add a test to the first option of an Environment Query and save it: testType Distance, Dot, GameplayTags, Overlap, Pathfinding, PathfindingBatch, Project, Random or Trace, with engine defaults; a query with no option yet gets one. testIndex in the reply addresses it for edit=configure_test_scoring and edit=add_context.
add_context: Point a generator or test of an Environment Query at a context and save: contextType Querier (the AI running the query), Item (each item being tested) or Custom with contextClass (a Blueprint based on EnvQueryContext_BlueprintBase). It sets the context property of the test at testIndex (counted across options), else of the generator of option optionIndex (default 0); contextProperty picks one (SearchCenter of ActorsOfClass, GenerateAround of SimpleGrid, DistanceTo of Distance, Context of Trace), else the first is taken. A query with no generator yet, a target with no context property (the reply lists them) or a class that is not a context is refused.
configure_test_scoring: Set how a test of an Environment Query (testIndex, counted across options) filters and scores, and save: scoringEquation (Linear, Square, InverseLinear, SquareRoot or Constant), clampMin and clampMax, filterType (Minimum, Maximum, Range or Match) with floatMin and floatMax (a float range filters by Range unless filterType says otherwise), in testSettings or at the top level. The test becomes Filter and Score; unknown names and a call that sets nothing are refused.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Create an Environment Query or edit it, chosen by edit, each saved: create makes the asset, add_generator gives an option its items (ActorsOfClass, CurrentLocation, Donut, OnCircle, PathingGrid, SimpleGrid, Composite), add_test adds a test (Distance, Dot, GameplayTags, Overlap, Pathfinding, PathfindingBatch, Project, Random, Trace), add_context points a generator or test at the querier, the items or a context class, configure_test_scoring sets the equation, clamps and filter of a test. A Behavior Tree runs it with a Run EQS Query task.

discovery.summary: Build Mass entities, chosen by edit: create_config makes an empty Mass entity config asset and configure adds a trait to it or sets trait properties or a parent config, each saved; add_spawner places a Mass Spawner actor that spawns the config's entities at the items of an Environment Query when play begins. A configure call that sets nothing is refused.
whenToUse: edit=create_config: Crowd simulation needs an entity config asset.
edit=configure: A Mass entity config needs a trait, trait settings or a parent config.
edit=add_spawner: A level should spawn a crowd of Mass entities from a config.

name.description: Name for the created asset or actor.

path.description: Canonical /Game output path for the created asset.

configPath.description: Canonical /Game Mass Entity config asset path.

parentConfigPath.description: Parent Mass entity config asset to inherit from.

traitClass.description: Mass trait class (short name or path, a UMassEntityTraitBase subclass): edited when the config has it, added when it does not.

properties.description: Trait property values keyed by UPROPERTY name.

queryPath.description: Environment Query whose items are the spawn points; it runs around the spawner.

spawnCount.description: Number of entities the spawner creates.

actorName.description: Label for the placed spawner; a label already in the level is refused.

location.description: World location of the spawner (default the world origin).

edit.description:
Which edit mass entity variant to run.
create_config: Create a Mass entity config asset named name in path (default /Game/AI/Mass), saved, with no traits yet; an asset already at the path is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS).
configure: Change a Mass entity config and save: traitClass adds that trait when the config has none of it (a new config starts with no traits, and traits such as MassMovementTrait or a visualization trait are what give entities data and behaviour), properties go onto the trait traitIndex or traitClass names, else the first trait that takes them, and parentConfigPath makes it derive from another config (one that already derives from it is refused). A call with none of these, or a traitClass that is no Mass trait, is refused; traits lists the config's traits after the call, traitAdded says whether one was added, applied and failed name the fields.
add_spawner: Place a Mass Spawner actor in the current level: when play begins it spawns spawnCount entities (default 100) of the Mass entity config configPath at the items of the Environment Query queryPath, run with the spawner as querier (a SimpleGrid generator around the querier spreads them out). location places it (default the world origin) and actorName labels it; a taken label, a config or query that does not load (NOT_FOUND) or is another asset type (TYPE_MISMATCH) is refused. The entities exist only in play and are drawn only when the config has a visualization trait.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

configPath.description: Canonical /Game Mass Entity config asset path.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

examples.title: Build Mass entities, chosen by edit: create_config makes an empty Mass entity config asset and configure adds a trait to it or sets trait properties or a parent config, each saved; add_spawner places a Mass Spawner actor that spawns the config's entities at the items of an Environment Query when play begins. A configure call that sets nothing is refused.

discovery.summary: Build Smart Objects, chosen by edit, each saved: create_definition makes a definition asset, add_slot adds a slot at an offset, configure_slot enables a slot or adds registered activity tags, add_component puts a Smart Object component (with its definition) on an actor Blueprint. A taken path or component name, an unregistered tag and a definition that does not load are refused.
whenToUse: edit=create_definition: An interactable needs a Smart Object definition asset.
edit=add_slot: A Smart Object definition needs another interaction slot.
edit=configure_slot: An existing Smart Object slot needs enable/index edits.
edit=add_component: An actor Blueprint should expose a Smart Object definition.

name.description: Name for the created asset or actor.

path.description: Canonical /Game output path for the created asset.

definitionPath.description: Canonical /Game Smart Object definition asset path.

offset.description: Slot offset relative to the definition origin.

rotation.description: Rotation as {pitch, yaw, roll} in degrees.

slotIndex.description: Index of the slot to configure.

activityTags.description: Registered gameplay tags added to the slot activity tags; an unregistered tag fails the call.

componentName.description: Name of the component to add.

edit.description:
Which edit smart object variant to run.
create_definition: Create a Smart Object definition asset named name in path (default /Game/AI/SmartObjects), saved, with no slots yet (edit=add_slot); an asset already at the path is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS).
add_slot: Add a slot to a Smart Object definition at offset and rotation from its origin, enabled (default true), and save; slotIndex in the reply addresses it for edit=configure_slot.
configure_slot: Change slot slotIndex (default 0) of a Smart Object definition and save: enabled, and activityTags added to its activity tags (registered gameplay tags only: an unregistered one is refused and nothing changes). A call with neither is refused; behaviorCount reports its behavior definitions.
add_component: Add a Smart Object component named componentName (default SmartObjectComponent) to an actor Blueprint and save, using definitionPath when given (refused when it does not load). A component name the Blueprint already has is refused (ALREADY_EXISTS).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

definitionPath.description: Canonical /Game Smart Object definition asset path.

examples.title: Build Smart Objects, chosen by edit, each saved: create_definition makes a definition asset, add_slot adds a slot at an offset, configure_slot enables a slot or adds registered activity tags, add_component puts a Smart Object component (with its definition) on an actor Blueprint. A taken path or component name, an unregistered tag and a definition that does not load are refused.

discovery.summary: Create a State Tree or edit it, chosen by edit, each compiled and saved: create makes the asset with a Root state and a schema (component or ai, from the GameplayStateTree plugin), add_state adds a named state, add_transition links two states on a trigger, configure_task sets the properties of a task or the selection behavior of a state. compiled says whether the tree compiled (an uncompiled tree does not run), with compileMessages.
whenToUse: edit=create: An AI needs a StateTree instead of a Behavior Tree.
edit=add_state: A StateTree needs another state under a parent.
edit=add_transition: Two StateTree states need a trigger-driven link.
edit=configure_task: A StateTree state needs its task settings changed.
whenNotToUse: edit=create: Use create_behavior_tree for Behavior Tree logic.

name.description: Name for the created asset or actor.

path.description: Canonical /Game output path for the created asset.

schema.description: What runs the tree: component (default, a StateTreeComponent on any actor), ai (a StateTreeAIComponent on an AI controller, UE 5.4+), or the class path of another State Tree schema (a UStateTreeSchema subclass, such as /Script/MassAIBehavior.MassStateTreeSchema for Mass entities).

parentStateName.description: Parent state name for the added state.

stateType.description: State (default), Group, Linked, LinkedAsset (UE 5.4+) or Subtree.

triggerType.description: OnStateCompleted (default), OnStateSucceeded, OnStateFailed, OnTick, OnEvent (needs an event tag) or OnDelegate (newer engines).

taskName.description: Task to configure, matched by class or instance name (defaults to the first task).

taskIndex.description: Zero-based task index in the state (alternative to taskName).

selectionBehavior.description: State selection behavior (e.g. TryEnterState, TrySelectChildrenInOrder, TryFollowTransitions).

properties.description: Task property values keyed by UPROPERTY name, imported by reflection onto the task instance.

edit.description:
Which edit state tree variant to run.
create: Create a State Tree asset named name in path (default /Game/AI/StateTrees) with a Root state and a schema, compiled and saved: schema component (default; a StateTreeComponent on any actor runs it), ai (a StateTreeAIComponent on an AI controller, UE 5.4+) or the class path of another schema. component and ai come from the GameplayStateTree plugin and are refused while it is off (SCHEMA_NOT_AVAILABLE); an asset already at the path is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS). compiled says whether the tree compiled, with compileMessages.
add_state: Add a state named stateName under parentStateName (default Root) of a State Tree, compiled and saved: stateType State (default), Group, Linked, LinkedAsset (UE 5.4+) or Subtree. States are found by name, so a name the tree already has is refused (NAME_TAKEN), as is an unknown stateType. A state made here has no tasks yet. compiled false with compileMessages when the tree does not compile.
add_transition: Add a go-to-state transition from fromState to toState, compiled and saved: triggerType OnStateCompleted (default), OnStateSucceeded, OnStateFailed, OnTick, OnEvent (needs an event tag) or OnDelegate (newer engines). An unknown trigger or a state that is not found is refused; transitionId identifies it.
configure_task: Change a task of a State Tree state (taskName, else taskIndex, default the first) by its properties (UPROPERTY names on the task, its instance data or its Blueprint instance) and/or the state selectionBehavior (TryEnterState, TrySelectChildrenInOrder, TrySelectChildrenAtRandom, TryFollowTransitions), compiled and saved. A call with neither, a task that is not found, or properties no part of the task takes are refused; applied and failed name the fields.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Create a State Tree or edit it, chosen by edit, each compiled and saved: create makes the asset with a Root state and a schema (component or ai, from the GameplayStateTree plugin), add_state adds a named state, add_transition links two states on a trigger, configure_task sets the properties of a task or the selection behavior of a state. compiled says whether the tree compiled (an uncompiled tree does not run), with compileMessages.

discovery.summary: Read an AI asset: a pawn or AI controller Blueprint (each perception sense with its settings under the names the configure actions take, the engine teamId and the teamIdVariable set_perception_team stores, movement), a Behavior Tree summary, Blackboard keys, State Tree states or EQS query options; info=navigation returns NavMesh and agent settings; info=path says whether a pawn could walk between two points on the nav mesh, and why not.
whenToUse: info=ai: A caller needs the current state of an AI asset.
info=navigation: A caller needs current NavMesh and agent settings.
info=path: Before sending a pawn or AI somewhere: can it get there on foot, and if not, where does the way end?
whenNotToUse: info=path: Navigation settings or the nav mesh itself must be read (use info navigation).

fromActor.description: An actor whose location is the start, in place of from.

toActor.description: An actor whose location is the goal, in place of to.

projectExtent.description: How far from an end, per axis in cm, the nav mesh may be found (default 100, 100, 250).

info.description:
Which get ai info variant to run; omit for 'ai'.
ai: Read AI asset information.
navigation: Read navigation state and settings.
path: Say whether a pawn could walk from one point to another on the editor level's nav mesh, and why not: an end off the mesh within projectExtent (start_off_navmesh, goal_off_navmesh), both ends on it with nothing connecting them (no_path), or a partial path that stops gap cm short (partial). from and to are points, or fromActor and toActor stand for where those actors are. The reply gives reachable, reason, the path points (100 at most), pathLength in cm, and where each end lands on the mesh (fromOnMesh, toOnMesh). Refused with NAV_DATA_MISSING when the level has no nav mesh, and NAV_BUILD_IN_PROGRESS while it builds.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

rootDecoratorClasses.description: Class paths of decorators attached to the root node.

rootDecorators.description: Decorator objects attached to the root node.

rootGraphBlackboard.description: Blackboard assigned on the root graph node.

rootGraphBlackboardMatchesAssigned.description: Whether the root graph blackboard matches the assigned blackboard.

assignedBehaviorTree.description: Behavior Tree asset path assigned to the controller.

assignedBlackboard.description: Blackboard asset path assigned to the tree/controller.

hasRootNode.description: Whether the Behavior Tree has a root node.

testCount.description: Total number of tests across all options.

options.description: Query options: generator class, item type and their tests.

navMeshInfo.description: Navigation mesh and agent settings reported by the native Navigation domain (HandleGetNavigationInfo).

tileSizeUU.description: NavMesh tile size in Unreal units (default: 1000).

agentStepHeight.description: Maximum step height the agent can climb (default: 35).

isNavigationBuildInProgress.description: Whether a navigation build is running.

reachable.description: Whether a full path joins the two ends.

points.description: The path corners as [x, y, z], start to end (100 at most).

pathLength.description: Length of the path in cm.

gap.description: partial: how far the path stops short of the goal, in cm.

fromOnMesh.description: Where the start lands on the nav mesh, as [x, y, z].

toOnMesh.description: Where the goal lands on the nav mesh, as [x, y, z].

navData.description: The navigation data the path was found on.

examples.title: Read an AI asset: a pawn or AI controller Blueprint (each perception sense with its settings under the names the configure actions take, the engine teamId and the teamIdVariable set_perception_team stores, movement), a Behavior Tree summary, Blackboard keys, State Tree states or EQS query options; info=navigation returns NavMesh and agent settings; info=path says whether a pawn could walk between two points on the nav mesh, and why not.

discovery.summary: Make an AIController Blueprint run a Behavior Tree whenever it possesses a pawn (control run, the default: On Possess calls Run Behavior Tree with its BehaviorTree variable), take that out again (stop), only set the variable that holds the tree (assign_tree), or bind a Blackboard to a controller or tree (assign_blackboard). The run logic is engine nodes in the Blueprint, compiled and saved, so it works in a packaged game; a Blueprint that is not an AIController is refused (NOT_AI_CONTROLLER).
whenToUse: control=run: A controller should start a Behavior Tree whenever it possesses a pawn.
control=stop: A controller should no longer start a Behavior Tree when it possesses a pawn.
control=assign_tree: A controller should hold a Behavior Tree that its own logic runs.
control=assign_blackboard: A controller or Behavior Tree needs its Blackboard bound.
whenNotToUse: control=run: Use control_editor to start a PIE session; this edits the asset only.
control=stop: Use control_editor to stop a PIE session; this edits the asset only.
control=assign_blackboard: Use add_blackboard_key to author the Blackboard contents.

control.description:
Which run behavior tree variant to run; omit for 'run'.
run: Make an AIController Blueprint run a Behavior Tree whenever it possesses a pawn: its On Possess event calls Run Behavior Tree (which also starts the Blackboard) with its BehaviorTree variable, set to behaviorTreePath as control=assign_tree does. Engine nodes in the Blueprint, compiled and saved, so it works in a packaged game, for every pawn whose AI Controller Class is this one and whose Auto Possess AI covers how it enters the level. Re-running replaces it; control=stop takes it out. NOT_AI_CONTROLLER for another Blueprint, NOT_FOUND for a missing tree, and refused during Play.
stop: Take out the Run Behavior Tree logic control=run wrote into an AIController Blueprint, so possessing a pawn no longer starts a tree (its BehaviorTree variable and On Possess event stay), compiled and saved; removed false, and nothing changed, when there was none.
assign_tree: Put a Behavior Tree in an AIController Blueprint: its BehaviorTree variable (one it declares, else a new instance-editable DefaultBehaviorTree) holds behaviorTreePath by default, compiled and saved. Nothing runs the tree until control=run writes Run Behavior Tree on possess, or the controller calls it itself. NOT_AI_CONTROLLER for another Blueprint, NOT_FOUND for a missing tree.
assign_blackboard: Assign a Blackboard to an AIController or Behavior Tree asset.

discovery.summary: Set the movement limits on the CharacterMovement component of a Character Blueprint (an AI pawn) and save it: maxWalkSpeed, maxAcceleration, brakingDeceleration (walking), rotationRate (yaw, degrees per second), maxFlySpeed, jumpZVelocity and avoidanceWeight, plus useAccelerationForPaths (path following speeds up and slows down like a player instead of moving at full speed at once), orientRotationToMovement (turn to face where it goes) and useRVOAvoidance (steer around other agents). discovery.summary: Make an AIController Blueprint keep its focus on the player 0 pawn (focusPlayer) or the first actor carrying focusTag, finding it again each frame it has none (focusOp set, the default), or take that logic out (clear). Written into the Blueprint as engine nodes, compiled and saved, so it works in a packaged game.
whenToUse: focusOp=set: An AI should face and track the player, or an actor marked with a tag.
focusOp=clear: A controller should stop tracking its focus target.

focusPlayer.description: Focus the pawn of player 0, picked up again when it spawns late or respawns.

focusTag.description: Focus the first actor carrying this tag (mark the target with control_actor add_tag).

focusOp.description:
Which set focus variant to run; omit for 'set'.
set: Make an AIController Blueprint keep its focus on a target: the player 0 pawn (focusPlayer) or the first actor carrying focusTag. Each frame it has no focus actor, its Tick finds the target and calls Set Focus, so a target that spawns after the AI, or respawns, is picked up again; a pawn that uses its controller rotation turns to face it. Engine nodes in the Blueprint, compiled and saved; re-running replaces the target and focusOp=clear takes it out. Exactly one of focusPlayer and focusTag (INVALID_ARGUMENT); NOT_AI_CONTROLLER for another Blueprint.
clear: Take out the focus logic focusOp=set wrote into an AIController Blueprint, so it stops seeking a target each frame (a focus already set in a running game stays until something clears it), compiled and saved; removed false, and nothing changed, when there was none.

discovery.summary: Set up AI perception on an AI controller or pawn Blueprint, chosen by setting, each saved: setup adds the component and several senses at once, add_component only the component (kept when present), sight, hearing and damage tune one sense and keep what is not sent, team stores a team id variable (the engine team itself needs C++), controller is setup for an AIController path. An actor with no team is neutral, so a sense must detect neutrals to notice the player.
whenToUse: setting=setup: A Blueprint needs perception added and several senses tuned at once.
setting=add_component: A Blueprint needs an AIPerception component before senses are configured.
setting=sight: An AIPerception component needs sight-sense tuning.
setting=hearing: An AIPerception component needs hearing-sense tuning.
setting=damage: An AIPerception component needs damage-sense tuning.
setting=team: A team id should be stored on the AI for its own logic to read.
setting=controller: One call should add the perception component and set its senses together.
whenNotToUse: setting=setup: Use the individual configure_*_config actions for one sense.

loseSightRadius.description: Radius at which sight is lost.

teamId.description: Team id to store, 0 to 254 (255 means no team).

setting.description:
Which setup perception variant to run; omit for 'setup'.
setup: Add or update the AIPerception component of an AI controller or pawn Blueprint and save: enableSight, enableHearing and enableDamage set up or update each sense (sightRadius, loseSightRadius, peripheralVisionAngle, hearingRange), and dominantSense (Sight, Hearing, Damage, Touch or None) picks the sense whose stimulus location wins. A sense already set up keeps what this call does not send; a call that enables nothing and names no dominant sense is refused. createdNew says whether the component was added.
add_component: Add an AIPerception component to an AI controller or pawn Blueprint and save it; a Blueprint that already has one keeps it (alreadyExists true, nothing changed). Senses are added with setting=sight, setting=hearing and setting=damage, or several at once with setting=setup.
sight: Set the sight sense of an AIPerception component (added when missing) and save: sightRadius, loseSightRadius, peripheralVisionAngle (half-angle in degrees), and in sightConfig also pointOfViewBackwardOffset, nearClippingRadius, autoSuccessRange, maxAge (seconds a sighting is remembered, 0 forever) and detectionByAffiliation {enemies, neutrals, friendlies}; a sightConfig field wins over the top-level one. Only what is sent changes; a new sight sense starts at 3000, losing sight 500 further, 90 degrees, enemies and neutrals, 5 s. An actor with no team counts as neutral, so neutrals must stay detected for an AI to see the player.
hearing: Set the hearing sense of an AIPerception component (added when missing) and save: hearingRange, and in hearingConfig detectFriendly and maxAge (seconds, 0 forever); a hearingConfig field wins over the top-level one. Only what is sent changes; a new hearing sense hears 3000 units, enemies and neutrals, for 5 s, and the reply carries its settings under these names. Sounds reach it only through Report Noise Event or a Pawn Noise Emitter, not from audio.
damage: Set the damage sense of an AIPerception component (added when missing) and save: damageConfig.maxAge, the seconds a hit is remembered (a new sense starts at 10; 0 is forever). Hits reach it only through Report Damage Event, not from Apply Damage alone.
team: Store a team id (teamId 0 to 254, 255 meaning none) in a GenericTeamId integer variable on a Blueprint (added when missing) and save. It does not change the team the engine sees: an AI controller takes a team only in C++ (SetGenericTeamId is not exposed to Blueprints), so appliedToGenericTeamAgent is false, and an actor with no team counts as neutral to every AI. Read the variable from the project logic.
controller: Add or update the AIPerception component of an AI controller Blueprint (controllerPath) and save, as setting=setup does: enableSight, enableHearing and enableDamage set up or update each sense (sightRadius, loseSightRadius, peripheralVisionAngle, hearingRange) and dominantSense picks the leading one. A sense already set up keeps what is not sent; a call that enables nothing and names no dominant sense is refused.

discovery.summary: Hear how a space sounds where a listener stands: 256 rays cast evenly in every direction from location (or actorName's location; the rays pass through that actor) give the room as heard from there: its volume and surface, mean free path, length, width and height along its own walls (proportion: the largest over the smallest), the share of rays that meet nothing within maxDistance (default 5000 cm: open sky, a large doorway), the delay of the first reflection, and its reverberation time rt60, the seconds sound takes to fall 60 dB. rt60 comes from a traced decay (each ray reflected on, 30% of the reflections scattered, losing absorption of its energy at each, read off its Schroeder curve), so it holds in corridors, flat halls and rooms with openings; eyringRt60 gives Eyring's formula beside it only for a closed room no more than 3 times as long as its smallest side, where that formula holds. absorption (default 0.1) is the share of sound the surfaces soak up: bare concrete or tile about 0.02-0.05, plaster or wood about 0.1, a furnished room 0.2-0.3, a treated studio 0.5 and up. Rays trace the visibility channel against complex collision, as the engine's sound occlusion does. When half the rays escape or more, it is outdoors or very open and no reverb is suggested; otherwise nextCall makes a Reverb Effect with that decay (RE_Room in /Game/Audio/Effects) and zoneCall places it as a reverb zone over the room's box (roomCenter, roomSize; rename both together). Reads only. Refused with POINT_IN_SOLID (the listener is inside geometry), ACTOR_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_ARGUMENT (neither location nor actorName).
whenToUse: Choosing a reverb that fits a room, a hall, a corridor or a cave instead of guessing its decay time.
Checking whether a space is closed, long or open before placing audio volumes.
whenNotToUse: Making or placing a reverb with known settings: use create_audio_asset kind reverb_effect and create_audio_actor kind reverb_zone.
How loud a sound is: use measure_loudness.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

location.description: Where the listener stands, in cm: a point in the open air of the room.

actorName.description: An actor whose location is the listener, instead of location (a character, a sound source); the rays pass through it.

absorption.description: The share of sound energy the surfaces absorb at each reflection (default 0.1): 0.02-0.05 bare concrete or tile, 0.1 plaster or wood, 0.2-0.3 a furnished room, 0.5 and up heavy curtains or a treated studio.

maxDistance.description: How far a ray reaches, in cm (default 5000); a ray that meets nothing within it counts as open.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

listener.description: Where the rays were cast from.

openShare.description: The share of rays (0-1) that met nothing within maxDistance.

volumeM3.description: The volume seen from the listener, in cubic metres (a space around a corner is not counted).

surfaceM2.description: The surface seen from the listener, in square metres.

meanFreePathM.description: The mean distance sound travels between reflections (4 V / S), in metres.

firstReflectionMs.description: Out to the nearest surface and back, in milliseconds.

lengthM.description: The longer of the room's floor sides, along its own walls, in metres.

widthM.description: The shorter of its floor sides, in metres.

proportion.description: Its largest side over its smallest; past 3 it is long or flat and Eyring's formula does not hold.

roomCenter.description: The middle of the box around every first hit (world axes), in cm.

roomSize.description: The size of that box, in cm.

rt60.description: Seconds for sound to fall 60 dB, from the traced decay; absent when the decay fell less than 25 dB (most rays escaped).

eyringRt60.description: Eyring's formula, given only for a closed room with proportion under 3.

nextCall.description: The create_reverb_effect call making a Reverb Effect with decayTime rt60 (0.1-20 s, the engine's range).

zoneCall.description: The create_reverb_zone call placing that effect as an Audio Volume over roomCenter and roomSize.

output.message: A room of about 90 m3 (6.0 x 5.0 x 3.0 m) at absorption 0.10: sound takes 1.10 s to fall 60 dB (Eyring: 1.08 s). nextCall makes a Reverb Effect with that decay; zoneCall then places it as a reverb zone over the room.

discovery.summary: Configure sound attenuation: distance falloff and air absorption, spatialization, occlusion, reverb send, or a named attenuation preset.
whenToUse: setting=distance: Use it to configure distance attenuation: inner radius (or a box's size per axis), falloff distance and curve, and air absorption (a low-pass that muffles the sound with distance).

setting=spatialization: Use it to set how a Sound Attenuation asset places its sounds in space: spatialize on or off, and spatialization Default (panning) or Binaural (HRTF, for headphones). Only what is sent changes, a call with neither is refused, and another algorithm is INVALID_ARGUMENT. Saved unless save is false.

setting=occlusion: Use it to set occlusion on a Sound Attenuation asset (assetPath), each value only when sent: enable turns it on or off, occlusionFilterScale (0-1) times 20000 Hz is the low-pass cutoff when blocked, occlusionVolumeScale (0-1) the volume kept, occlusionInterpolationTime the seconds to blend. The reply reads the four values back; the asset is saved unless save is false.
setting=reverb_send: Use it to configure an audio reverb send.
setting=audio_occlusion: Use it to configure occlusion settings on a sound asset.

setting=preset: Use it to create a Sound Attenuation asset name in path (default /Game/Audio/Attenuation): innerRadius (default 400), falloffDistance (default 3600), attenuationShape Sphere (the default), Capsule, Box (sized per axis with extent) or Cone, and falloffMode Linear (the default), Logarithmic, Inverse or NaturalSound; another shape or mode is refused. An asset already at the path is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS (change one with configure_distance_attenuation). Saved unless save is false; the reply reads the values back.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

innerRadius.description: Inner radius of full volume, in centimetres: a Box shape takes it as its half-size on every axis, a Capsule as its radius (half height at least that), a Sphere or Cone as its radius.

falloffDistance.description: Distance over which attenuation falls off, in centimetres.

distanceAlgorithm.description: Distance falloff curve: Linear, Logarithmic, Inverse or NaturalSound. Left unchanged when omitted.

save.description: Persist the asset to disk (default true); false leaves the change in memory only.

extent.description: A Box shape's half-size on each axis in cm, {x, y, z}, each above 0: a zone the length of a hall without reaching as far sideways. It replaces the size innerRadius gives a box; another shape is refused.

attenuateWithLPF.description: Air absorption on or off: a low-pass whose cutoff drops with distance. Sending any lpf value turns it on unless this is false.

lpfRadiusMin.description: Distance in cm where the low-pass starts closing; nearer than this the cutoff is lpfFrequencyAtMin.

lpfRadiusMax.description: Distance in cm where the cutoff reaches lpfFrequencyAtMax.

lpfFrequencyAtMin.description: Low-pass cutoff in Hz at lpfRadiusMin and nearer (20000 leaves the sound unfiltered).

lpfFrequencyAtMax.description: Low-pass cutoff in Hz at lpfRadiusMax and beyond (900 sounds like a distant, muffled engine).

spatialize.description: Whether the sound is spatialized (default true).

spatialization.description: Spatialization algorithm: Default (the panner) or Binaural (HRTF). Left unchanged when omitted.

occlusionFilterScale.description: Low-pass filter scale applied while occluded (0-1).

enableReverbSend.description: Whether the sound sends to reverb.

reverbDistanceMin.description: Distance at which the reverb send starts.

reverbDistanceMax.description: Distance at which the reverb wet level reaches its maximum.

soundPath.description: Canonical /Game sound asset path (SoundWave, SoundCue or MetaSound).

name.description: Name of the asset, actor or mapping to create, or of the mapping to remove.

path.description: Canonical /Game folder for the created asset.

falloffMode.description: Attenuation falloff curve: Linear (the default), Logarithmic, Inverse or NaturalSound.

discovery.summary: Change a Sound Class or Sound Mix, chosen by setting, each saved: parent sets or clears a class's parent (a loop is refused), properties sets its volume, pitch, low-pass, LFE bleed and center-channel volume, mix_modifier adds or edits the adjuster a mix applies to a class (and the mix fades), mix_eq sets the mix's four EQ bands. A call that sets nothing is refused.
whenToUse: setting=parent: Use it to set the parent of a Sound Class, or clear it with an empty parentClass, keeping both classes' child lists in step (a mix modifier applying to children walks them). A parent that does not load (PARENT_NOT_FOUND), or that is the class itself or one of its children (CYCLIC_PARENT), is refused. Saved unless save is false.

setting=properties: Use it to set the properties of a Sound Class, each only when sent: volume and pitch (multipliers, 1 leaves them as authored), lowPassFilterFrequency (Hz; 20000 leaves the sound unfiltered), lfeBleed and voiceCenterChannelVolume (0-1). The reply lists all five; a call that sends none is refused. Saved unless save is false.

setting=mix_modifier: Use it to add a Sound Class modifier to a Sound Mix, or edit the one the mix already has for that class (replaced true), keeping what is not sent: volumeAdjuster and pitchAdjuster (multipliers; a new modifier starts at 1) and applyToChildren (default true). fadeInTime and fadeOutTime set the fades of the mix itself. Saved unless save is false.

setting=mix_eq: Use it to configure Sound Mix equalization: the four bands through eqSettings (frequencyCenterN, gainN, bandwidthN for N 0-3), or the low, mid, highMid and high fields on top of them. Sending a band switches the EQ on unless applyEQ is false; eqPriority ranks the mix against other active mixes. Values are clamped (gain 0-4, frequency 0-20000 Hz, bandwidth 0-2) and the reply lists every band after clamping; a call that sets nothing is refused.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

parentClass.description: Canonical /Game SoundClass asset path of the new parent; an empty string clears the parent.

save.description: Persist the asset to disk (default true); false leaves the change in memory only.

lowPassFilterFrequency.description: Low-pass filter cutoff frequency in Hz.

lfeBleed.description: Share of the sound sent to the LFE channel (0 to 1).

voiceCenterChannelVolume.description: Share of the sound sent to the centre speaker (0 to 1).

volumeAdjuster.description: Volume multiplier applied by the mix modifier.

pitchAdjuster.description: Pitch multiplier applied by the mix modifier.

applyToChildren.description: Whether the modifier also applies to the child sound classes (default true).

applyEQ.description: Whether the mix applies its EQ (default true).

eqPriority.description: EQ priority of the mix; the active mix with the highest priority supplies the EQ.

eqSettings.description: Four-band EQ as {frequencyCenter0..3, gain0..3, bandwidth0..3}; a missing key keeps its value.

lowFrequency.description: Centre frequency of EQ band 0 in Hz.

lowGain.description: Linear gain of EQ band 0 (0 to 4).

midFrequency.description: Centre frequency of EQ band 1 in Hz.

midGain.description: Linear gain of EQ band 1 (0 to 4).

highMidFrequency.description: Centre frequency of EQ band 2 in Hz.

highMidGain.description: Linear gain of EQ band 2 (0 to 4).

highFrequency.description: Centre frequency of EQ band 3 in Hz.

highGain.description: Linear gain of EQ band 3 (0 to 4).

setting.description:
Which configure sound class variant to run.
parent: Set the parent of a Sound Class, or clear it with an empty parentClass, keeping both classes' child lists in step (a mix modifier applying to children walks them). A parent that does not load (PARENT_NOT_FOUND), or that is the class itself or one of its children (CYCLIC_PARENT), is refused. Saved unless save is false.
properties: Set the properties of a Sound Class, each only when sent: volume and pitch (multipliers, 1 leaves them as authored), lowPassFilterFrequency (Hz; 20000 leaves the sound unfiltered), lfeBleed and voiceCenterChannelVolume (0-1). The reply lists all five; a call that sends none is refused. Saved unless save is false.
mix_modifier: Add a Sound Class modifier to a Sound Mix, or edit the one the mix already has for that class (replaced true), keeping what is not sent: volumeAdjuster and pitchAdjuster (multipliers; a new modifier starts at 1) and applyToChildren (default true). fadeInTime and fadeOutTime set the fades of the mix itself. Saved unless save is false.
mix_eq: Configure Sound Mix equalization: the four bands through eqSettings (frequencyCenterN, gainN, bandwidthN for N 0-3), or the low, mid, highMid and high fields on top of them. Sending a band switches the EQ on unless applyEQ is false; eqPriority ranks the mix against other active mixes. Values are clamped (gain 0-4, frequency 0-20000 Hz, bandwidth 0-2) and the reply lists every band after clamping; a call that sets nothing is refused.

discovery.summary: Measure how loud Sound Waves are the way broadcast and streaming measure it: EBU R128 integrated loudness in LUFS from each wave's own samples (K-weighted, so a deep rumble counts less than speech at the same level; gated, so silences and quiet tails do not pull it down), the loudness each plays at through its Volume, and its sample peak; spreadLu says how far apart they play. A peak meter says how high a sound reaches, not how loud it sounds: two waves with the same peak can play 10 LU apart. Mono counts one channel, as EBU R128 does, so a mono wave reads 3 LU under the same sound in stereo. Read only; normalize_loudness sets the Volumes.
whenToUse: Checking whether sound effects, dialogue or music play at consistent loudness before mixing.
Finding the sound that is far louder or quieter than its neighbours.
whenNotToUse: Making them play at one loudness: use normalize_loudness.
Hearing whether a sound plays at all in the level: use play_sound with measure.

lufs.description: Its integrated loudness in LUFS (EBU R128: K-weighted, gated at -70 LUFS and 10 LU under the mean), from its own samples.

volume.description: Its Volume (the wave's own gain, 1 as recorded).

peakAtVolumeDb.description: The sample peak through its Volume; above 0 it is louder than full scale before the mix.

note.description: Silent, or under 400 ms of sound: it has no loudness (its Volume is left alone).

saved.description: normalize_loudness: the wave was saved.

spreadLu.description: How many LU the loudest wave plays above the quietest (through their Volumes).

discovery.summary: Make Sound Waves play at one loudness: each wave's EBU R128 integrated loudness is measured from its own samples (as measure_loudness does) and its Volume set so it plays at targetLufs, all in one undo step, each wave saved unless save is false. The samples stay as they are; peakAtVolumeDb says when a raised wave now peaks above full scale before the mix. A silent wave, or one under 400 ms of sound, keeps its Volume (note). Mono counts one channel, as EBU R128 does, so a mono wave reads 3 LU under the same sound in stereo. Refused, changing nothing: ASSET_NOT_FOUND (a path that is not a Sound Wave), ENGINE_CONTENT (an engine wave: duplicate it into /Game first).
whenToUse: Sound effects, dialogue lines or music tracks must play at one loudness (a mixing pass, imported packs at different levels).
whenNotToUse: Only reading how loud they are: use measure_loudness.

discovery.summary: Play a sound: 2D, at a location (played or spawned), attached to an actor, or prime it for playback. A 2D sound (looping music too) plays until stop_sound. measure plays it 2D and reports how loud it played (peak and average dB, silent). The sounds already playing are listed by console_command au.DumpActiveSounds.
whenToUse: playback=2d: Use it to play a sound asset 2D, tied to no place, at volume and pitch (default 1) from startTime seconds, on the running game while one plays, else in the editor; it plays to its end, a looping one until stop_sound. A path that loads no sound is ASSET_NOT_FOUND, and an editor with sound off answers NOT_PLAYED.

playback=at_location: Use it to play a sound once at location (and rotation), at volume and pitch (default 1) from startTime seconds, with an optional attenuationPath and concurrencyPath (ASSET_NOT_FOUND when one does not load). It plays in the running game while one plays, heard from its listener, else in the editor. Fire and forget: only stop_sound with all true stops it.
playback=spawn_at_location: Use it to spawn a transient sound at a world location.

playback=attached: Use it to play a sound attached to an actor (actorName; in the running game while one plays, else in the level) on the component or socket attachPointName names, else on its root, at volume and pitch. The reply gives componentName, attachedTo and playing; an unknown actor is ACTOR_NOT_FOUND and an unknown attach point ATTACH_POINT_NOT_FOUND.
playback=prime: Use it to prime a sound asset for playback.

playback=measure: Use it to play a sound 2D and measure how loud it played, from the mixer's own meter: peak and average level in dB and a timeline, with silent: true when it played but produced no audio (an empty Sound Cue, a MetaSound whose audio output is unconnected). A Sound Wave also gets the peak, RMS and length of the recording itself (wavePeakDb, waveRmsDb, waveSeconds), which hold however slowly the editor draws. Answers when the sound ends or after maxSeconds.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

componentName.description: Name of the audio component that was created, spawned or faded.

peakDb.description: Loudest level the sound reached, in dB of full scale (0 is full scale, -120 means no signal). The mixer meters each sound after its own volume and before distance attenuation; the editor being in the background does not lower it.

averageDb.description: Mean level over every reading in dB, the release tail included.

silent.description: True when the peak stayed below -60 dB: the sound played but produced no audio; the warning says the likely cause.

envelopeUpdates.description: Meter readings that arrived, about one per editor frame; 0 means the engine never rendered the sound.

endedBecause.description: finished (the sound ended on its own), maxSeconds (cut there, as looping sounds and music always are) or stopped (stopped by another call, or its Play-In-Editor world ended).

timeline.description: Loudest reading in dB in each timelineStepSeconds step from the start, null for a step no reading landed in (a slow editor frame).

timelineStepSeconds.description: Seconds each timeline entry covers: 0.05 for sounds up to 5 s, longer so there are at most 100 entries.

wavePeakDb.description: A Sound Wave only: the loudest sample of the recording itself, in dB of full scale, read from its imported audio rather than the meter, so it holds however few frames the editor drew. Before volume. Compare sounds by this when matching levels.

waveRmsDb.description: A Sound Wave only: the average (RMS) level of the whole recording in dB, before volume.

waveSeconds.description: A Sound Wave only: the length of the recording in seconds.

discovery.summary: Configure a Character Blueprint's defaults by setting: movement_speeds (walk, crouch, swim, fly, acceleration, braking, friction), jump (launch speed, hold, double jump, air control, gravity), crouch, rotation (orient to movement or face the aim), capsule_component, mesh_component (skeletal mesh, Animation Blueprint, offset), camera_component (a third-person spring arm and camera, made when missing) or nav_movement (AI agent size, avoidance). Each compiles and saves the Blueprint, changes only the fields sent and reads the values back; a Blueprint that is not a Character is refused (NOT_A_CHARACTER).
whenToUse: setting=movement_speeds: A character must move, stop, crouch, swim or fly faster or slower, or several movement values change at once.
setting=jump: A character jumps too high, too low or too floaty, needs a double jump, or must steer in the air.
setting=crouch: A character must crouch, crouch-walk at another speed, or fit under lower gaps while crouched.
setting=rotation: A character must turn toward where it walks, or face where the camera aims.
setting=capsule_component: A character is taller, wider or smaller than its capsule, or gets stuck in doorways it should fit through.
setting=mesh_component: A character needs its body mesh or the Animation Blueprint that drives it, or its mesh floats, sinks or faces sideways.
setting=camera_component: A Character needs a camera that follows it from behind; without one the game views from the eyes of the pawn.
setting=nav_movement: An AI character paths through gaps too narrow for it, or AI characters walk into each other.
whenNotToUse: setting=movement_speeds: One value changes (set_movement_property).
setting=jump: Only the launch speed changes (set_movement_property).

walkSpeed.description: Top ground speed in cm/s (MaxWalkSpeed; engine default 600).

runSpeed.description: Run speed; ignored when walkSpeed is also supplied.

swimSpeed.description: Top swim speed in cm/s (MaxSwimSpeed; engine default 300).

flySpeed.description: Top fly speed in cm/s (MaxFlySpeed; engine default 600).

acceleration.description: How fast it reaches its top speed, in cm/s per second (MaxAcceleration; engine default 2048).

deceleration.description: How fast it stops on the ground with no input, in cm/s per second (BrakingDecelerationWalking; engine default 2048).

groundFriction.description: How sharply it turns and stops on the ground (GroundFriction; engine default 8; lower slides like ice).

jumpHeight.description: The jump launch speed in cm/s, not a height (JumpZVelocity; engine default 420): it rises about v*v/(1960*gravityScale) cm, so 420 is about 90 cm and 600 about 1.8 m.

jumpHoldTime.description: Maximum jump hold time in seconds.

maxJumpCount.description: Jumps before landing (JumpMaxCount; 1 by default, 2 for a double jump).

airControl.description: How much it can steer in the air, 0 to 1 (AirControl; engine default 0.05).

gravityScale.description: Multiplier on world gravity (GravityScale; 1 is normal, 2 falls twice as hard).

canCrouch.description: Whether the character is allowed to crouch.

orientToMovement.description: Whether the character orients rotation to movement.

rotationRate.description: Rotation rate in degrees per second.

useControllerRotationYaw.description: Whether controller yaw drives actor rotation.

useControllerRotationPitch.description: Whether controller pitch drives actor rotation.

useControllerRotationRoll.description: Whether controller roll drives actor rotation.

capsuleRadius.description: Capsule collision radius in world units.

capsuleHalfHeight.description: Capsule collision half-height in world units.

springArmLength.description: How far the camera sits behind the character, in cm (spring arm TargetArmLength; 300 on a new boom).

springArmLagEnabled.description: Whether spring-arm camera lag is enabled.

springArmLagSpeed.description: How fast a lagging camera catches up (CameraLagSpeed; 10 on a new boom, higher is tighter); it lags only with springArmLagEnabled.

cameraUsePawnControlRotation.description: Whether the spring arm follows the controller look rotation. The camera under it is always arm-relative.

navAgentRadius.description: The radius navigation plans paths for, in cm (NavAgentProps.AgentRadius).

navAgentHeight.description: The height navigation plans paths for, in cm (NavAgentProps.AgentHeight).

setting.description:
Which configure character variant to run.
movement_speeds: Set a Character Blueprint's Character Movement speeds in one call, then compile and save it: walkSpeed (MaxWalkSpeed, engine default 600), crouchSpeed (300), swimSpeed (300), flySpeed (600), acceleration (MaxAcceleration, 2048), deceleration (braking while walking, 2048) and groundFriction (8), plus the jump fields setting=jump takes. A value not sent keeps its own. A Character has one walk speed: runSpeed sets it only when walkSpeed is absent, otherwise the reply says runSpeedApplied false with a warning (a sprint is game logic that raises MaxWalkSpeed while a key is held). The reply reads back every speed and jump value.
jump: Set how a Character Blueprint jumps, then compile and save it: jumpHeight is the launch speed (JumpZVelocity, engine default 420; the apex is about v squared over 1960 cm at gravity scale 1, so 420 rises 0.9 m and 600 about 1.8 m), jumpHoldTime (seconds holding the button keeps lifting, default 0), maxJumpCount (2 for a double jump), airControl (0-1 steering while falling, default 0.05), gravityScale (default 1) and fallingLateralFriction (default 0). A value not sent keeps its own; the reply reads back all six, jumpHeight as jumpZVelocity.
crouch: Let a Character Blueprint crouch, then compile and save it: canCrouch (off on a new Character, so Crouch does nothing until it is on), crouchSpeed (MaxWalkSpeedCrouched, engine default 300) and crouchedHalfHeight (the capsule half-height while crouched, default 40); a field not sent keeps its value. The reply reads back all three. Crouching still needs input that calls Crouch and UnCrouch, and an Animation Blueprint that plays a crouch pose from the crouched state.
rotation: Choose what turns a Character Blueprint, then compile and save it: orientToMovement turns it toward where it moves at rotationRate degrees per second (yaw; engine default 360); useControllerRotationYaw, Pitch and Roll make it face the controller's aim. A new Character faces the controller's yaw (useControllerRotationYaw true, orientToMovement false). A third-person character usually sets orientToMovement true and useControllerRotationYaw false; a strafing shooter the opposite. Keep only one of those two on: both on fight every frame. A value not sent keeps its own; the reply reads back all five.
capsule_component: Resize a Character Blueprint's collision capsule (capsuleRadius and capsuleHalfHeight in world units; a new Character starts at 34 by 88, the third-person template uses 42 by 96), then compile and save it; a size not sent keeps its value. The reply reads both sizes back; a Blueprint that is not a Character is refused (NOT_A_CHARACTER). Move the mesh with it: its meshOffset z is usually minus the half-height, so the feet sit on the capsule bottom.
mesh_component: Set the inherited Mesh of a Character Blueprint, then compile and save it: skeletalMeshPath, animBlueprintPath (the Animation Blueprint that animates it), and meshOffset and meshRotation relative to the capsule; a field not sent keeps its value. Refused before anything changes: a path that does not load (ASSET_NOT_FOUND), and an Animation Blueprint made for a skeleton the mesh does not take (SKELETON_MISMATCH), which would leave the character in its rest pose. The reply names skeletalMeshAssigned and animBlueprintAssigned. A mannequin-style mesh usually needs meshOffset z at minus the capsule half-height and meshRotation yaw -90 to face forward (+X).
camera_component: Give a Character a third-person follow camera: a spring arm behind it with a camera on its end, made when missing; an existing arm changes only in the fields sent.
nav_movement: Set how AI navigation sees a Character Blueprint, then compile and save it: navAgentRadius and navAgentHeight (the agent size its movement reports to pathfinding) and avoidanceEnabled (RVO avoidance, so moving characters steer around each other). By default a spawned character copies its capsule size over the nav agent size; sending a size turns that copy off so the size stays (navAgentFollowsCapsule false). A value not sent keeps its own; the reply reads back all three and navAgentFollowsCapsule. The navmesh itself is built for the agent sizes in the project's Navigation System settings.

discovery.summary: Set one character movement property: walk speed, jump height (set as its launch speed, JumpZVelocity), gravity scale, ground friction, braking deceleration; compiled, saved and read back.
whenToUse: movementProperty=walk_speed: Walk speed must change.
movementProperty=jump_height: A character must jump higher or lower.
movementProperty=gravity_scale: Gravity must change.
movementProperty=ground_friction: Friction must change.

whenNotToUse: movementProperty=walk_speed: Use configure_movement_speeds.
movementProperty=jump_height: Use configure_jump.

walkSpeed.description: Top ground speed in cm/s (MaxWalkSpeed; engine default 600).

jumpHeight.description: The jump launch speed in cm/s, not a height (JumpZVelocity; engine default 420): it rises about v*v/(1960*gravityScale) cm, so 420 is about 90 cm and 600 about 1.8 m.

gravityScale.description: Multiplier on world gravity (GravityScale; 1 is normal, 2 falls twice as hard).

groundFriction.description: How sharply it turns and stops on the ground (GroundFriction; engine default 8; lower slides like ice).

movementProperty.description:
Which set movement property variant to run.
walk_speed: Set the top walking speed of a Character Blueprint (CharacterMovement MaxWalkSpeed, cm/s; engine default 600). Compiled and saved; the reply gives the value the compiled class holds. A negative speed is refused, and a Blueprint that is not a Character is NOT_A_CHARACTER.
jump_height: Set how fast a Character Blueprint leaves the ground when it jumps (CharacterMovement JumpZVelocity, cm/s; engine default 420): a launch speed, not a height. The apex is about speed squared / (1960 x gravityScale) cm, so 420 rises about 90 cm. Compiled and saved; the reply gives the value held. Negative is refused.
gravity_scale: Set the gravity multiplier of a Character Blueprint (CharacterMovement GravityScale: 1 is normal, 0 floats, negative falls upward). Compiled and saved; the reply gives the value held.
ground_friction: Set how quickly a walking Character Blueprint turns and stops (CharacterMovement GroundFriction; engine default 8, higher grips more). Compiled and saved; the reply gives the value held. Negative is refused.
braking_deceleration: Set how fast a walking Character Blueprint slows when no input is held (CharacterMovement BrakingDecelerationWalking, cm/s squared; engine default 2048). Compiled and saved; the reply gives the value held. Negative is refused.

discovery.summary: Hitboxes on a Blueprint, chosen by setting. hitbox adds or updates the HitboxCapsule, HitboxBox or HitboxSphere component (hitboxType, default Capsule) sized by hitboxSize (only the sizes sent change), on hitboxBoneName of its skeletal mesh when given (NO_SKELETAL_MESH without one), and sets the variables bIsHeadshotZone and HitboxDamageMultiplier. hit_detection makes sure a hitbox of hitboxType exists and sets HitboxDamageMultiplier, without sizing it. An unknown hitboxType is refused. These are a component and variables only: no damage happens until the Blueprint applies it on the hitbox overlap or hit event. Compiles and saves (SAVE_FAILED otherwise).
whenToUse: setting=hit_detection: A Blueprint needs a hitbox component of a given shape and a HitboxDamageMultiplier value, without sizing it.
setting=hitbox: A per-bone damage volume is needed.

damageMultiplier.description: Default of the Blueprint variable HitboxDamageMultiplier (added when missing; default 1). Nothing reads it until the Blueprint damage logic does.

hitboxBoneName.description: Bone of the Blueprint skeletal mesh (an SCS SkeletalMeshComponent or an inherited one such as a Character mesh) the hitbox attaches to; fails when the Blueprint has no skeletal mesh.

hitboxSize.description: Hitbox dimensions: extent for Box, radius/halfHeight for Sphere and Capsule.

isDamageZoneHead.description: Default of the Blueprint variable bIsHeadshotZone (added when missing; default false), for its damage logic to read.

discovery.summary: Configure projectiles: give a weapon a Fire function that shoots a projectile class, or set a projectile movement, collision or homing.
whenToUse: setting=projectile: The weapon shoots projectiles: Fire, called from input or AI, spawns one at the WeaponMesh Muzzle socket owned by the weapon and launches it at projectileSpeed, at most FireRate times a minute.
setting=movement: Projectile flight must change.
setting=collision: Impact or bounce behaviour must change.
setting=homing: The projectile should track a target.
whenNotToUse: setting=projectile: A hit must land at once (hitscan): trace in the weapon Blueprint graph instead (blueprint edit_graph).

projectileClass.description: The projectile the weapon shoots: its Blueprint path (/Game/Weapons/BP_Bullet) or class path.

projectileGravityScale.description: Gravity scale applied to the projectile.

bounceVelocityRatio.description: Fraction of velocity retained on bounce (0-1).

setting.description:
Which configure projectile variant to run; omit for 'projectile'.
projectile: Give a weapon a Fire function that spawns and launches a projectile class from its muzzle.
movement: Set the flight of a projectile Blueprint: projectileSpeed (cm/s, its initial and top speed), projectileGravityScale (0 flies straight, 1 drops like any object) and projectileLifespan (seconds before it is destroyed). Only the fields sent change; the Projectile Movement component is added when missing, and a Blueprint with no component tree is INVALID_BLUEPRINT. Compiled and saved; the reply gives the values it holds.
collision: Set the collision sphere radius of a projectile Blueprint (collisionRadius, cm) and its bounce (bounceEnabled; bounceVelocityRatio, the share of speed kept per bounce, 0 to 1). Only the fields sent change; CollisionComponent and Projectile Movement are added when missing. Compiled and saved; the reply gives the values held.
homing: Turn homing on (homingEnabled, default true) or off for a projectile Blueprint and set how hard it turns (homingAcceleration, cm/s squared, default 20000, changed only when sent). It steers only once something sets its Homing Target Component at runtime, such as the weapon after spawning it (blueprint edit_graph). Compiled and saved; the reply gives the values held.
