discovery.summary: Create a combat Blueprint named name in path (default /Game), chosen by kind; it is saved, and a path an asset already holds is refused. weapon_blueprint is an Actor with a WeaponMesh component (weaponMeshPath) and BaseDamage, FireRate, Range and Spread variables (defaults 25, 600, 10000, 2), and no firing logic of its own. projectile_blueprint flies (projectileSpeed, default 5000; projectileGravityScale, default 0), stops on what it meets with a collisionRadius sphere (default 5), applies damage (default 20) to it and is destroyed, never hits the actor that fired it, and is gone 5 s after firing when it meets nothing; projectileMeshPath is its mesh. A mesh path that does not load is refused before anything is made. damage_type (damage_type_setup) is a DamageType Blueprint for ApplyDamage to name.
whenToUse: kind=weapon_blueprint: A new weapon actor must be authored.

kind=projectile_blueprint: A projectile actor must be authored: it stops on what it meets, applies damage to it (ApplyDamage, so health logic on that actor takes it) and never hits the actor that fired it; one that meets nothing is gone 5 seconds after it is fired (configure_projectile setting movement, projectileLifespan, changes that).
kind=damage_type: A custom damage classification is needed.
kind=damage_type_setup: A damage class is needed by name and folder.
whenNotToUse: kind=damage_type|damage_type_setup: Damage multipliers are a Gameplay Effect execution (manage_gas configure_gameplay_effect add_execution_calculation).

name.description: Name for the created asset or actor.

path.description: Canonical /Game output path for the created asset.

fireRate.description: Rate of fire in rounds per minute.

range.description: Effective weapon range in world units.

weaponMeshPath.description: Static mesh assigned to the new WeaponMesh component; a path that does not load fails the call.

projectileGravityScale.description: Gravity scale applied to the projectile.

damage.description: Damage dealt to the actor it hits (default 20); kept in its Damage variable, which a placed copy can change.

kind.description:
Which create combat asset variant to run.
weapon_blueprint: Create an Actor Blueprint named name in path (default /Game) for a weapon: a WeaponMesh component showing weaponMeshPath, and BaseDamage, FireRate, Range and Spread variables set to baseDamage, fireRate, range and spread (defaults 25, 600, 10000, 2). It has no firing logic of its own. A mesh that does not load, or a path an asset already holds, is refused before anything is made; the Blueprint is compiled and saved.
projectile_blueprint: Create a projectile Blueprint named name in path (default /Game) that flies, damages what it hits and is destroyed on impact; projectileMeshPath is its mesh, and one that does not load, or a path an asset already holds, is refused before anything is made.
damage_type: Create a DamageType Blueprint named name in path (default /Game), a damage class ApplyDamage can name and a damaged actor can tell apart; compiled and saved, and a path an asset already holds is refused.
damage_type_setup: Create a DamageType Blueprint named name in path (default /Game) and answer its damageTypePath; compiled and saved, and a path an asset already holds is refused.

damage.description: Damage it deals on a hit.

discovery.summary: Add a data interface to a Niagara emitter: static mesh, skeletal mesh, spline, collision query, audio spectrum.
whenToUse: interfaceKind=static_mesh: Read static mesh data.
interfaceKind=skeletal_mesh: Read skeletal mesh data.
interfaceKind=spline: Sample spline data.
interfaceKind=collision_query: Query collisions in graph.
interfaceKind=audio_spectrum: Audio-reactive particles.
whenNotToUse: interfaceKind=collision_query: Use add_collision_module.

emitterName.description: Emitter within the system, by the name get_niagara_info lists. Module, renderer, data interface, event, parameter and simulation edits also read emitter, and with neither use the system's only emitter (a system with several refuses with EMITTER_NOT_FOUND, listing them); graph edits without one edit the system's own script.

save.description: Persist the asset to disk (default true); false leaves the change in memory only.

interfaceKind.description:
Which add niagara data interface variant to run.
static_mesh: Add a Static Mesh data interface as a user parameter of the system, User.<parameterName> (default MCP_StaticMeshDataInterface), for modules to sample a static mesh's surface; emitterName must name an emitter of the system. A parameterName the system already has is NAME_TAKEN, nothing changed. Saved unless save is false (saved).
skeletal_mesh: Add a Skeletal Mesh data interface as a user parameter of the system, User.<parameterName> (default MCP_SkeletalMeshDataInterface), for modules to sample a skeletal mesh's bones and surface; emitterName must name an emitter of the system. A parameterName the system already has is NAME_TAKEN, nothing changed. Saved unless save is false (saved).
spline: Add a Spline data interface as a user parameter of the system, User.<parameterName> (default MCP_SplineDataInterface), for modules to sample positions along a spline; emitterName must name an emitter of the system. A parameterName the system already has is NAME_TAKEN, nothing changed. Saved unless save is false (saved).
collision_query: Add a Collision Query data interface as a user parameter of the system, User.<parameterName> (default MCP_CollisionQueryDataInterface), for modules to trace against the world; emitterName must name an emitter of the system. A parameterName the system already has is NAME_TAKEN, nothing changed. Saved unless save is false (saved).
audio_spectrum: Add an Audio Spectrum data interface as a user parameter of the system, User.<parameterName> (default MCP_AudioSpectrumDataInterface), for modules to read the spectrum of playing audio (audio-reactive particles); emitterName must name an emitter of the system. A parameterName the system already has is NAME_TAKEN, nothing changed. Saved unless save is false (saved).

It goes where its dependencies hold (a force before Solve Forces and Velocity).
whenToUse: moduleKind=module: Emitter needs a module.
moduleKind=spawn_rate: Emitter spawns over time.
moduleKind=spawn_burst: Burst spawn needed.
moduleKind=spawn_per_unit: Spawn along a path/unit.
moduleKind=initialize_particle: Particle init needed.
moduleKind=velocity: Particles need velocity.
moduleKind=acceleration: Particles need acceleration.
moduleKind=force: Particles need force.
moduleKind=color: Particle color must change.
moduleKind=size: Particle size must change.
moduleKind=collision: Particles must collide.
moduleKind=kill_particles: Particles must die on condition.
moduleKind=camera_offset: Camera-relative particles.
moduleKind=particle_state: Particle lifecycle state needed.
moduleKind=sprite_renderer: Sprite rendering needed.
moduleKind=mesh_renderer: Mesh rendering needed.
moduleKind=ribbon_renderer: Ribbon/trail rendering.
moduleKind=light_renderer: Per-particle light needed.
moduleKind=simulation_stage: Custom sim stage needed.
moduleKind=event_generator: Emitter emits events.
moduleKind=event_receiver: Emitter consumes events.
whenNotToUse: moduleKind=module: Use connect_niagara_pins.
moduleKind=simulation_stage: Use enable_gpu_simulation.

emitterName.description: Emitter within the system, by the name get_niagara_info lists. Module, renderer, data interface, event, parameter and simulation edits also read emitter, and with neither use the system's only emitter (a system with several refuses with EMITTER_NOT_FOUND, listing them); graph edits without one edit the system's own script.

modulePath.description: Canonical /Niagara module script path to insert.

scriptType.description: Which script the graph edit works in: Spawn (default) or Update. With emitterName that is the particle spawn or particle update stack of that emitter; without it, the system spawn or update script.

save.description: Persist the asset to disk (default true); false leaves the change in memory only.

emitter.description: Emitter name; alias normalized to emitterName.

velocityMode.description: Velocity module: Linear (AddVelocity, the default), Cone (AddVelocityInCone) or FromPoint (AddVelocityFromPoint); any other name is refused.

forceType.description: Force module: Gravity (default), Drag, Wind, Curl (CurlNoise), Vortex or PointAttraction; any other name is refused.

materialPath.description: Canonical /Game material asset path for the renderer; its Niagara sprite or ribbon usage flag is set and the material saved, so the renderer never falls back to the default material.

meshPath.description: Canonical /Game static mesh for the mesh renderer; its materials get their Niagara mesh-particle usage flag set and saved, so the particles never fall back to the default material.

lightRadius.description: Multiplier on each particle's light radius (the renderer RadiusScale, engine default 1). Left unchanged when omitted.

stageIterationSource.description: What the stage runs over: Particles (the default, each particle), DataInterface (each element of a grid or other data interface) or DirectSet (a count you set; UE 5.2 and later). Any other name is refused.

eventName.description: Optional: the name expected; the generator module names its event, and a different one draws a warning.

eventType.description: Event generator module: Location (GenerateLocationEvent, the default), Death or Collision; any other name is refused.

spawnOnEvent.description: Whether the receiver spawns particles on each event.

eventSpawnCount.description: Particles spawned per received event (default 1); the engine uses it only with spawnOnEvent true.

moduleKind.description:
Which add niagara module variant to run; omit for 'module'.
module: Add a module to a Niagara emitter, where its dependencies hold: before the first module that must run after it (a force before Solve Forces and Velocity), else at the end of the stack.
spawn_rate: Insert the SpawnRate module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
spawn_burst: Insert the SpawnBurst_Instantaneous module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
spawn_per_unit: Insert the SpawnPerUnit module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
initialize_particle: Insert the InitializeParticle module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
velocity: Insert a velocity module into the emitter's particle spawn stack, chosen by velocityMode: Linear (AddVelocity, the default), Cone (AddVelocityInCone) or FromPoint (AddVelocityFromPoint); another mode is INVALID_ARGUMENT. Its inputs keep their defaults; set them with set_parameter_value. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false; the reply gives moduleName.
acceleration: Insert the AccelerationForce module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
force: Insert the force module forceType names (Gravity by default; Drag, Wind, Curl, Vortex, PointAttraction) into the emitter's particle update stack, before Solve Forces and Velocity, with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<moduleName>.<Input>"). Another forceType is INVALID_ARGUMENT. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false; the reply gives moduleName as the stack named it.
color: Insert the Color module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
size: Insert the ScaleSpriteSize module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
collision: Insert the Collision module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
kill_particles: Insert the KillParticles module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
camera_offset: Insert the CameraOffset module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
particle_state: Add a particle-state module.
sprite_renderer: Give the emitter a sprite renderer, or configure the one it has (rendererCreated false), drawing with materialPath (its Niagara sprite usage flag set and saved); without materialPath it keeps its material, the engine default on a new one. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false; the reply reads back materialPath and rendererPath.
mesh_renderer: Give the emitter a mesh renderer, or configure the one it has (rendererCreated false), drawing each particle as meshPath (required; it replaces the renderer's mesh list, and its materials get their Niagara mesh-particle flag). Without meshPath it is INVALID_ARGUMENT, since a mesh renderer with no mesh draws nothing. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false.
ribbon_renderer: Give the emitter a ribbon renderer (a strip joining its particles, for trails), or configure the one it has (rendererCreated false), drawing with materialPath (its Niagara ribbon usage flag set and saved); without it the material stays as it is. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false; the reply reads back materialPath.
light_renderer: Give the emitter a light renderer, a point light at each particle, or configure the one it has (rendererCreated false); lightRadius multiplies each particle's light radius (RadiusScale, engine default 1) and is read back. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false.
simulation_stage: Add an empty generic simulation stage named stageName to the emitter, running over stageIterationSource (Particles, the default, DataInterface or DirectSet on UE 5.2 and later; another name is INVALID_ARGUMENT). Stages run on GPU emitters. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false; the reply gives simulationStageCount.
event_generator: Insert the engine's event generator module for eventType (Location, the default, Death or Collision) into the emitter's particle update stack. The event it emits is named by that module, and the reply gives that name (eventName) for moduleKind=event_receiver on another emitter; an eventName given that differs is not applied and draws a warning. Another eventType is INVALID_ARGUMENT. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false.
event_receiver: Add an event handler to the emitter for the event eventName (the name moduleKind=event_generator reported): with spawnOnEvent true it spawns eventSpawnCount particles (default 1) per event, otherwise its script runs on every particle when the event arrives. Its handler script starts empty. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false.

steps.description: Steps to run (default 1): the system ages steps x deltaTime seconds.

reset.description: Restart the system from age 0 before stepping, so it ends at exactly steps x deltaTime seconds; also plays a finished system again. Without it the steps add to the age it has.

whenNotToUse: Actors named one by one, or carrying a tag: use control_actor delete, which matches whole names or tags.

A name already taken is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS, nothing changed.
niagara_ribbon: Create a Niagara ribbon effect: by default the engine LocationBasedRibbon template given its own SpawnRate of 60 a second, Ribbon Width Mode Direct Set and an infinite loop, so it trails whatever it is attached to, placed in the level only when location is given; tune SpawnRate.SpawnRate, InitializeParticle.Lifetime, Ribbon Width and Color with set_parameter_value.
particle_trail: Create a particle trail effect: by default a ribbon (the engine LocationBasedRibbon template given its own SpawnRate of 60 a second, Ribbon Width Mode Direct Set and an infinite loop) that trails whatever it is attached to, placed in the level only when location is given; tune SpawnRate.SpawnRate, InitializeParticle.Lifetime, Ribbon Width and Color with set_parameter_value.
impact: Create an impact effect system asset (the engine OmnidirectionalBurst template by default), placed in the level only when location is given.
environment: Create an environment effect (weather/atmosphere) system asset, placed in the level only when location is given.
volumetric_fog: Create a volumetric fog effect.
niagara: Place a Niagara system in the level as a Niagara actor, at a location or attached to an actor; autoActivate false places it switched off, for a sequence particle track or gameplay to start.
particle: Spawn a particle effect (Cascade or Niagara) from a preset name or a system asset.

discovery.summary: Edit a Niagara system: add an emitter (an asset, or a copy of another system's), user parameters or parameter bindings, set parameter values or dynamic inputs, emitter properties, GPU simulation, connect pins.
whenToUse: edit=add_emitter: System needs an emitter.
edit=add_emitter: An emitter built in one system is wanted in another.
edit=add_user_parameter: Expose a user param.

edit=bind_parameter: A Blueprint sets a value at run time (Set Niagara Variable on a user parameter): parameterName is the module input as get_niagara_info lists it (InitializeParticle.Color, ShapeLocation.Box Size), or an input of a dynamic input feeding one (RandomRangeFloat.Minimum), sourceBinding the user parameter (User.Tint).
edit=bind_parameter: A value must follow an engine, system or emitter parameter (sourceBinding Emitter.Age).
edit=set_parameter_value: A user parameter or a module input value must change.
edit=set_parameter_value: Several values of one system or emitter must change together (parameters): one call, one save.

edit=set_parameter_value: A module input changes nothing because a static switch gates it (a Ribbon Width written while InitializeParticle.Ribbon Width Mode is Unset): set the switch; get_niagara_info lists every staticSwitches value.
edit=set_parameter: A parameter value must change.
edit=set_parameter: One placed effect needs its own size, rate or colour while the other placements of its system keep theirs: actorName, with parameters for several values in one call.
edit=set_dynamic_input: Expression-driven value needed.
edit=set_emitter_properties: Emitter config must change.
edit=enable_gpu_simulation: GPU particles needed.
edit=connect_pins: Modules must wire together.
whenNotToUse: edit=add_emitter: Use create_niagara_emitter.
edit=enable_gpu_simulation: Use add_simulation_stage.
edit=connect_pins: Use add_niagara_module.

emitterName.description: Name for the new emitter handle (default the emitter asset's name, or the copied emitter's); a name the system already has gets a number.

sourceSystemPath.description: Niagara system to copy sourceEmitterName from, in place of emitterPath. The user parameters the emitter reads come along with their values when this system lacks them. An emitter that inherits from an emitter asset is refused (EMITTER_INHERITS): add that asset with emitterPath.

sourceEmitterName.description: The emitter of sourceSystemPath to copy, by the name get_niagara_info lists.

save.description: Persist the asset to disk (default true); false leaves the change in memory only.

parameterType.description: Niagara parameter type (Float, Vector, Color or LinearColor, ...).

sourceBinding.description: The parameter to read: a user parameter of the same type (User.Tint) or an engine, system or emitter one (Emitter.Age).

parameters.description: Several values written together and saved once, in place of parameterName and parameterValue: each {parameterName, parameterValue} names a user parameter, a module input or a module's static switch as get_niagara_info lists it (InitializeParticle.Lifetime, InitializeParticle.Ribbon Width Mode), and emitterName and save apply to every entry. With actorName (edit=set_parameter) each entry is a user parameter of that placed effect, in place of parameterName and value. The reply lists every entry (parameterName, applied, error); the call fails PARAMETER_BATCH_INCOMPLETE naming any that did not apply, and the others stay written.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

componentName.description: Actor form: which Niagara component of the actor takes the values, when it has several (a Blueprint with a fire and a smoke); default its first. A name it lacks is refused with the names it has.

value.description: Property value (any type).

targetNodeId.description: Niagara graph node the dynamic input is attached to.

moduleName.description: Module (function call) name that owns inputName; alternative to targetNodeId.

inputName.description: Module input name receiving the dynamic input.

replaceExisting.description: Whether an existing dynamic input is replaced.

emitterProperties.description: Emitter settings to change: enabled (boolean) turns the emitter on or off; moduleEnabled ({ModuleName: boolean}, names as get_niagara_info lists them) turns stack modules on or off, so a template module that works against the values set (a size curve, wind) can be switched off. Any other key is refused. Module inputs are set with set_parameter_value.

fixedBoundsEnabled.description: Whether fixed system bounds are enabled.

deterministicEnabled.description: Whether deterministic GPU simulation is enabled.

scriptType.description: Which script the graph edit works in: Spawn (default) or Update. With emitterName that is the particle spawn or particle update stack of that emitter; without it, the system spawn or update script.

fromNode.description: Source node: its GUID, name or title.

fromPin.description: Output pin name (or display name) on the source node.

toNode.description: Destination node: its GUID, name or title.

toPin.description: Input pin name (or display name) on the destination node.

edit.description:
Which edit niagara system variant to run.
add_emitter: Add an emitter to a Niagara system: an emitter asset (emitterPath), or a copy of another system's emitter with its modules, values, renderers and bindings (sourceSystemPath + sourceEmitterName), as the editor's copy and paste does.
add_user_parameter: Add a user parameter to a system.
bind_parameter: Drive a Niagara value from a parameter: a module input named as get_niagara_info lists it (InitializeParticle.Color) is linked to sourceBinding, as the stack's Link Inputs menu does; any other parameterName gets a Set Variables module in particle update that writes it from sourceBinding every frame.
set_parameter_value: Set Niagara parameter values: a user parameter, a module input named as get_niagara_info lists it (InitializeParticle.Lifetime), or a module's static switch (InitializeParticle.Ribbon Width Mode, an enum by its display name such as Direct Set); one with parameterName and parameterValue, or several with parameters, written together and saved once.
set_parameter: Set a Niagara user parameter: on a placed effect's component (actorName), so one placement of a shared system gets its own values, or its default on the system asset (assetPath).
set_dynamic_input: Configure a Niagara dynamic input expression.
set_emitter_properties: Enable or disable an emitter in a Niagara system (emitterProperties.enabled).
enable_gpu_simulation: Enable GPU simulation on a system.
connect_pins: Connect two Niagara graph pins (fromNode, fromPin, toNode, toPin), or with autoConnect wire the first compatible free pins.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

emitterName.description: Emitter within the system, by the name get_niagara_info lists. Module, renderer, data interface, event, parameter and simulation edits also read emitter, and with neither use the system's only emitter (a system with several refuses with EMITTER_NOT_FOUND, listing them); graph edits without one edit the system's own script.

userParametersAdded.description: User parameters a copy brought along (User.EmberRate), absent when none.

moduleInputCopiesWritten.description: Module input: how many copies of it (one per script that runs the module) took the value; static switch: how many module nodes took it.

saved.description: Whether the system was saved afterwards.

parameters.description: A parameters call: each entry {parameterName, applied, error (when it did not apply), moduleInputCopiesWritten}.

applied.description: A parameters call: how many entries were written.

componentName.description: Actor form: the Niagara component that took the values.

discovery.summary: Configure a gameplay ability: tags, cooldown, costs, activation and instancing policies; add it to an ability set.
whenToUse: setting=tags: An ability must carry, cancel, block or require gameplay tags.
setting=cooldown: The ability needs a wait between uses.
setting=costs: Activating the ability must spend an attribute such as mana or stamina.
setting=activation_policy: An ability must run on the server or be predicted by the client.
setting=instancing_policy: An ability must keep or drop state between activations.
setting=add_to_set: An ability must join a set that already exists.
whenNotToUse: setting=tags: The ability does not exist yet (use create_gameplay_ability).

abilityTags.description: Gameplay tags granted to this ability.

cancelAbilitiesWithTag.description: Tags of abilities cancelled when this activates.

blockAbilitiesWithTag.description: Tags of abilities blocked while this is active.

activationRequiredTags.description: Tags required to activate this ability.

activationBlockedTags.description: Tags that block activation of this ability.

cooldownEffectPath.description: Canonical /Game path to the cooldown Gameplay Effect.

costEffectPath.description: Canonical /Game path to the cost Gameplay Effect.

activationPolicy.description: Net execution policy: where the ability activates.

abilityClass.description: GameplayAbility class path; accepted wherever abilityPath is.

setting.description:
Which configure ability variant to run.
tags: Add gameplay tags to an ability Blueprint: abilityTags (its own asset tags), cancelAbilitiesWithTag and blockAbilitiesWithTag (abilities it cancels or blocks while active), activationRequiredTags and activationBlockedTags (tags its owner must have, or must not have, to activate). Tags are added, never replaced; each must be registered in the project (GAMEPLAY_TAG_NOT_REGISTERED before anything changes) and is read back from the compiled class before the ability is saved (ABILITY_TAGS_NOT_APPLIED otherwise).
cooldown: Set the Gameplay Effect an ability applies as its cooldown when it commits (cooldownEffectPath: a HasDuration GameplayEffect that grants a cooldown tag; the ability cannot activate again while its owner has that tag). Read back from the compiled class, then saved; the reply names the class it holds (cooldownEffectClass). An effect that does not load is ASSET_NOT_FOUND.

discovery.summary: Combine placed dynamic mesh actors, chosen by booleanOp, editing targetActor's mesh in place in world space: union adds toolActor, subtract cuts it out, intersection keeps only the overlap, trim cuts by trimActorName (keepInside keeps the inside), self_union resolves a mesh's own overlaps. keepTool (default true) keeps the tool actor; a result that would be empty or change nothing is refused (EMPTY_RESULT, NO_EFFECT) with the target as it was and the tool kept to move. Triangle counts before and after come back, and the edit is one undo step.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

booleanOp.description:
Which boolean mesh variant to run.
union: Union of two placed dynamic mesh actors: toolActor's volume joins targetActor's mesh, in place and in world space. keepTool (default true) keeps the tool actor, false deletes it once the union worked; a union that leaves nothing is EMPTY_RESULT with the target unchanged.
subtract: Cut toolActor's volume out of targetActor's dynamic mesh, in place and in world space (a hole, a doorway). A tool that does not cross the target's surface is NO_EFFECT and one that empties it EMPTY_RESULT, both leaving the target as it was and the tool in place to move; keepTool (default true) false deletes the tool once the cut worked.
intersection: Keep only where two placed dynamic mesh actors overlap: targetActor's mesh becomes the shared volume, in place and in world space. Meshes that do not overlap are EMPTY_RESULT with the target unchanged; keepTool (default true) false deletes toolActor once it worked.
trim: Trim a dynamic mesh actor by another one, trimActorName, kept in place: keepInside false (default) cuts away what lies inside it, true keeps only that part. Refused like a subtract or intersection when nothing would change or nothing would be left.
self_union: Resolve a dynamic mesh that overlaps itself (after an append or array): the overlapping shells are unioned into one surface, holes filled and flaps trimmed; trianglesBefore and trianglesAfter come back.

primitive=disc: A circular disc primitive must be created.
primitive=ring: A ring/annulus primitive must be created.
primitive=torus: A torus primitive must be created.
primitive=pipe: A pipe/tube primitive must be created.
primitive=arch: An arch primitive must be created.
primitive=ramp: A ramp primitive must be created.
primitive=stairs: A stair primitive must be created.
primitive=spiral_stairs: A spiral stair primitive must be created.
primitive=roof: A house, shed or hall needs a roof whose faces meet properly over its plan, however many corners it has.
primitive=sdf: A smooth organic or toy-like form must be modelled from several parts that flow into each other: a helmet, a hand, a shoe, a character body, a rounded prop.
primitive=sdf: A recess, socket or groove with a soft rim must be carved into a rounded form (subtract with blend), for example a visor.
whenNotToUse: primitive=roof: A flat roof: a box primitive.
primitive=roof: A gable roof with upright end walls: this makes hip roofs, every edge sloping.
primitive=sdf: One plain primitive is enough; use that primitive.
primitive=sdf: Hard mechanical parts with exact flat faces; use primitives with bevel and booleans.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

name.description: Name for the new asset or node.

location.description: World location {x, y, z}.

rotation.description: Rotation {pitch, yaw, roll}.

height.description: Box Y dimension: the box is X=width, Y=height, Z=depth (dimensions.{x,y,z}).

depth.description: Primitive depth: a box's size along Z; a plane's size along Y (a plane lies flat in XY, centred, facing +Z).

heightSegments.description: Tessellation segments along height (on a plane, along its depth, Y).

radius.description: Radius in cm (default 50). Torus and arch: from the centre to the middle of the tube (arch default 100). Pipe: the outer wall, as outerRadius. Spiral stairs: the inner radius when innerRadius is not given (default 150).

radialSegments.description: Radial tessellation segments for circular primitives.

numRings.description: Number of rings for sphere, capsule, torus, arch.

numSides.description: Number of sides for cylinder, cone, disc, ring, torus.

baseRadius.description: Cone base radius; defaults to radius.

topRadius.description: Cone top radius; non-zero makes a truncated cone. Defaults to 0.

length.description: Length along the primary axis: the capsule shaft, or the ramp run.

innerRadius.description: In cm, per variant. Disc and ring: the centred hole (disc default 0, solid; ring 25). Pipe: the inner wall (default 40). Torus and arch: the TUBE radius, its round cross-section, not a hole (default 20 torus, 25 arch); the opening under an arch is radius - innerRadius. Spiral stairs: the radius of the central well.

outerRadius.description: Outer radius for ring and pipe primitives.

angle.description: Sweep in degrees: torus default 360 (less leaves an open segment), arch default 180, a half ring. Both lie flat in the local XY plane, starting on local +X and turning toward +Y; give a rotation to stand an arch up.

steps.description: Number of steps (default 8; numSteps wins when both are sent).

numSteps.description: Number of steps for stair primitives.

floating.description: Build the stairs as free-floating steps with no solid underside.

numTurns.description: Number of turns for spiral stairs (converted to a curve angle).

footprint.description: The outline under the roof, its corners in order around it as {x, y} in cm in the actor's space (either winding; corners under 0.5 cm apart or in a straight line are dropped).

pitch.description: Slope of every face in degrees (default 30).

overhang.description: How far the eaves reach past the walls, in cm (default 0).

base.description: Close the roof underneath (default true), so the mesh is watertight.

shapes.description: Shapes combined in order onto shapes[0] (which must be a union) as one signed distance field, then meshed. Sizes are cm in the mesh's local space. Each joined shape takes a blend: the radius of the soft fillet where it meets what came before. An entry with mirror or repeat stands for all its copies (at most 1024 shapes in all), applied in its place in the order.

type.description: sphere (radius), ellipsoid (radii), box (extent = half size, rounding), capsule (radius, length of the straight part, along local Z), cylinder (radius, length, rounding, along local Z), torus (radius to the tube centre, thickness = tube radius, in local XY), cone (radius at the bottom, topRadius, length, along local Z, rounded ends). radius also sets an ellipsoid's radii and a box's extent when those are left out; any other size a type does not read is refused.

operation.description: union adds the shape (default), subtract carves it out of what came before (a recess, socket or groove), intersect keeps only the overlap.

center.description: Shape centre in the mesh's local space, cm (default 0,0,0); with relativeTo, in that shape's frame.

relativeTo.description: Index of an earlier shapes[] entry to place this one on: center, rotation, repeat and mirror are then measured from that shape's centre along its own turned axes (not scaled by its size), so the eyes, mouth or buttons of a leaning or turned part stay on it without working out the rotation. mirror then reflects across that shape's own planes.

rotation.description: Shape rotation {pitch, yaw, roll} in degrees; turns the shape's local Z axis for capsule, cylinder, cone and torus.

radius.description: Radius in cm (sphere, capsule, cylinder, cone base; torus: distance to the tube centre). Default 50.

radii.description: Ellipsoid radii along local X, Y, Z in cm.

extent.description: Box half size along local X, Y, Z in cm.

rounding.description: Box or cylinder edge rounding radius in cm (0 = sharp).

length.description: Capsule straight length, cylinder or cone height, in cm (default 100).

topRadius.description: Cone radius at the top in cm (0 = point; larger than radius widens upward).

blend.description: Smooth-join radius in cm with the shapes before it: 0 is a hard edge; a few cm reads as a soft fillet on a union and as a rounded rim on a subtract.

materialId.description: Material slot of the surface this shape forms (default 0). A subtract shape owns the surface it carves, so a carved visor can take its own slot.

mirror.description: Also add this shape reflected across the mesh's own plane through the origin normal to each listed axis ("y" mirrors y to -y): both eyes, both ears or a pair of legs from one entry. Each axis doubles the copies so far, so ["x","y"] gives four; repeat copies are mirrored too.

repeat.description: Copies of this shape with the same size, blend, operation and materialId: a row with offset, or a ring with axis. A row of stitches, rivets round a rim or curls round a head is one entry. The reply's parts[] still lists one entry per shapes[] item, with copies.

count.description: How many, the shape itself included.

offset.description: Row: each copy moves this much further from the previous one, cm.

axis.description: Ring: turn the copies about this mesh axis through pivot (each copy turns with it).

angle.description: Ring: total sweep in degrees (default 360, evenly spaced all round; a smaller arc puts the last copy at its end).

pivot.description: Ring: a point on the turning axis, cm (default 0,0,0).

resolution.description: Grid cells along the longest side of the shapes' bounds (default 128, 16-256): higher is finer and slower; 160-200 suits a hero part.

primitive.description:
Which create primitive variant to run.
box: Create a box dynamic mesh actor.
sphere: Create a sphere dynamic mesh actor.
cylinder: Create a cylinder dynamic mesh actor.
cone: Create a cone dynamic mesh actor.
capsule: Create a capsule dynamic mesh actor.
plane: Create a plane dynamic mesh actor: flat in XY, centred on its origin, facing +Z.
disc: Create a disc dynamic mesh actor.
ring: Create a ring dynamic mesh actor.
torus: Create a torus dynamic mesh actor.
pipe: Create a pipe dynamic mesh actor.
arch: Create an arch dynamic mesh actor.
ramp: Create a ramp dynamic mesh actor.
stairs: Create a stairs dynamic mesh actor.
spiral_stairs: Create a spiral stairs dynamic mesh actor.
roof: Create a hip roof mesh actor over a footprint: every face rises from its outline edge at pitch (default 30 degrees) and meets the others along ridges, hips and valleys where the outline's straight skeleton puts them, for any simple outline of 3 to 64 corners in either winding: rectangles, L, T and U plans, bays and angled walls (no holes). footprint is in the actor's space at the top of the walls (z 0); overhang (cm, default 0) carries the roof planes out past the walls, the eaves dropping by overhang x tan(pitch); base (default true) closes it underneath at the eaves' height, so the mesh is watertight (with an overhang that underside lies below the wall top: set the roof that much higher, or base false to leave it open). Each face is its own polygroup, its UVs in metres along its eave and up its slope, so a tiling roof material lies in rows along every eave. The reply gives faces (one per outline edge), ridgeHeight above the walls, eaveHeight, triangles and watertight; one undo step. Refused, making nothing: INVALID_ARGUMENT (fewer than 3 corners apart, an outline that crosses itself, an overhang that folds it over itself), ROOF_FAILED (faces that do not make a clean mesh).
sdf: Create one smooth organic mesh actor from blended shapes (a signed distance field): spheres, ellipsoids, rounded boxes, capsules, cylinders, tori and cones joined with soft fillets, carved with rounded recesses, or intersected, each shape with its own material slot.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

faces.description: Roof faces: one per outline edge.

ridgeHeight.description: Height of the highest ridge or peak above the walls.

eaveHeight.description: Height of the eaves: 0 without an overhang, below the walls with one.

watertight.description: Every edge of the mesh is shared by two triangles.

undo.description: What editor undo takes back: {undoable, transactionScope}.

parts.description: One entry per shape, saying which surface it formed.

groupId.description: Polygroup of the surface this shape formed (index+1).

triangles.description: Triangles of that surface; 0 when another shape covered it entirely.

copies.description: How many shapes this entry became with its repeat and mirror (the shape itself included); absent for a single shape.

warning.description: Present when a union shape is under two grid cells across: its surface can come out ragged, or as almost nothing when it formed under 24 triangles; raise resolution or thicken it.

resolution.description: Grid cells along the longest side, as used.

examples.title: Create a primitive mesh actor: box, sphere, cylinder, cone, capsule, plane, disc, ring, torus, pipe, arch, ramp, stairs, spiral stairs, a hip roof over any footprint, or one smooth organic mesh from blended shapes (sdf) with soft fillets where they meet. Each is a DynamicMeshActor with no collision: traces and players pass through it, and what stands on it reads "nothing below it", until configure_mesh_collision gives it some.

discovery.summary: Deform a mesh: bend, twist, taper, stretch, spherify, cylindrify, smooth, relax, noise, lattice, displace by texture. Each edits the placed dynamic mesh in one undo step and leaves the level unsaved.
whenToUse: deform=bend: A mesh must be bent.
deform=twist: A mesh must be twisted.
deform=taper: A mesh must be tapered.
deform=stretch: A mesh must be stretched.
deform=spherify: A mesh must be pushed toward spherical.
deform=cylindrify: A mesh must be pushed toward cylindrical.
deform=smooth: A mesh must be smoothed.
deform=relax: A mesh must be relaxed without shrinking.
deform=noise_deform: A mesh must be displaced by noise.
deform=lattice_deform: A complex deformation must be applied via a lattice.
deform=displace_by_texture: A mesh must be displaced by a texture.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: Actor name in the level.

targetActor.description: The dynamic mesh actor to edit, by label or name (actorName is the same and wins when both are sent).

axis.description: Axis to deform along: X, Y or Z (default Z).

strength.description: Deformation strength: bend/twist angle in degrees, taper flare percent, noise displacement in units, stretch factor, spherify/cylindrify blend 0-1.

frequency.description: Noise frequency in cycles per unit; defaults to three bumps across the mesh's largest dimension.

position.description: Position {x, y, z} for the operation.

latticeResolution.description: Control lattice resolution for lattice deformation.

deform.description:
Which deform mesh variant to run.
bend: Bend a dynamic mesh along axis (X, Y or Z, default Z) by strength degrees (default 45), the bend spread over its length along that axis and centred on its local origin, the pivot. The reply gives the angle.
twist: Twist a dynamic mesh about axis (X, Y or Z, default Z) by strength degrees (default 45) across its length along that axis, centred on its local origin. The reply gives the angle.
taper: Flare a dynamic mesh around axis (X, Y or Z, default Z): its cross-section grows by strength percent (default 50) at the middle of its length and not at all at the ends, so a positive strength bulges it and a negative one pinches it (a sine profile, not a straight taper).
stretch: Scale a dynamic mesh along one axis (X, Y or Z, default Z) by strength (default 1.5: 2 doubles it, 0.5 halves it) about its local origin, the other axes unchanged.
spherify: Pull every vertex of a dynamic mesh toward a sphere around its bounds centre, as large as its largest half-extent: strength 0 to 1 (default 1, clamped) is how far, 1 making it that sphere.
cylindrify: Pull every vertex of a dynamic mesh toward a cylinder around axis (X, Y or Z, default Z) through its bounds centre, its radius the average distance of the vertices from that axis: strength 0 to 1 (default 1, clamped) is how far. The reply gives avgRadius and verticesModified.
smooth: Smooth a dynamic mesh: iterations (default 10) of Laplacian smoothing, each moving every vertex strength (default 0.2) of the way toward its neighbours; the mesh shrinks a little. Fewer than 1 iteration or a strength of 0 is refused.
relax: Relax a dynamic mesh: the same smoothing as smooth with other defaults (3 iterations, strength 0.5), to even out vertex spacing. Fewer than 1 iteration or a strength of 0 is refused.
noise_deform: Displace a dynamic mesh along its normals by Perlin noise: strength is the height in cm (default 5) and frequency the noise cycles per cm (default three bumps across its largest dimension). The reply gives both.
lattice_deform: Ripple a dynamic mesh with a sine wave: every vertex moves along axis (X, Y or Z, default Z) by a wave latticeResolution cycles across its bounds (2 to 16, default 3), at most weight (-2 to 2, default 0.25) times a quarter of its largest size, fading to nothing three quarters of that size from position (default the bounds centre). A procedural ripple, not a cage of control points.
displace_by_texture: Raise a dynamic mesh by a heightmap texture projected straight down over its X/Y bounds: each vertex moves along axis (X, Y or Z, default Z) by (luminance - midpoint) x heightScale (midpoint 0 to 1, default 0.5; heightScale cm, default 10). A texture that does not load is TEXTURE_NOT_FOUND, one whose source format cannot be read TEXTURE_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

topics: author a mesh from vertices and faces
discovery.summary: Edit a procedural/dynamic mesh: create one, append vertices, triangles, a whole polygon cage (append_polygons), parts laid out in rows and grids (append_cuboids), a loft through cross sections (append_loft) or copies of a detailed static mesh (append_mesh) in one call, delete the triangles of a region (delete_triangles), give triangles material ids by region (set_material_id), bake AO, edge, cavity and height masks for materials to read (bake_vertex_colors), set vertex positions, colors or UVs, split normals, translate, or subtract another mesh.
whenToUse: edit=create: A mesh must be built vertex by vertex rather than from a primitive.
edit=create: An existing static mesh asset must be cut, trimmed or edited: create with meshPath, edit, then bake it with convert_to_static_mesh.
edit=append_vertex: A mesh is being authored point by point.
edit=append_triangle: A face must be added to an authored mesh in one call.

edit=append_polygons: A smooth, rounded model starts as a coarse cage: append its vertices and faces here (one polygroup per face), then optimize_mesh subdivide with scheme catmull_clark and iterations 2 or 3.
edit=append_polygons: Faces must be built from an explicit vertex list, quads and larger polygons included, with polygroups or material ids set up front.
edit=append_cuboids: A model is built from rectangular parts: posts and rails, beams, pillars, crates and containers, panels, windows, steps or furniture.

edit=append_cuboids: The same part repeats in a row, a grid or a block (repeat count with offset, rows with rowOffset, layers with layerOffset), each copy taking the next id of materialIds for colour variety.
edit=append_loft: A shape changes its cross section along its length: a ship hull or a car body (sections narrowing to the bow or nose), a fuselage, a bottle, a horn, a tapered column.
edit=append_loft: A pointed end is wanted: give endPoint (or startPoint) and the last section closes as a fan to it.
edit=append_loft: Parts of the skin need their own materials: edgeMaterials gives each edge of the section loop an id, so the strip it sweeps (a waterline band, a stripe, a window row) keeps it.

edit=append_mesh: A model needs detail an existing mesh already has: containers on a ship, window frames on a facade, seats in rows, bolts on a plate, crates in a stack. Copy the detailed part here instead of approximating it with boxes, then bake with convert_to_static_mesh.
edit=append_mesh: The copies need different colours: give materialIds a list for the painted slot and each copy takes the next id.
edit=delete_triangles: A part of an authored mesh must go: faces nobody sees, a piece built in the wrong place, every triangle of one material id before it is rebuilt.
edit=set_vertex_position: An authored vertex must be nudged without rebuilding the mesh.
edit=set_vertex_color: Authored geometry must carry colour the material reads.
edit=bake_vertex_colors: A material needs masks (dirt in crevices, wear on edges, a height gradient) without textures: bake once the shape is final, then convert_to_static_mesh or convert_to_nanite.

edit=bake_vertex_colors: Channels: R is ambient occlusion (1 open, 0 occluded); G is 1 minus the convex edge (1 on flat or concave surface, lower along an outward fold such as a rim); B is 1 minus the concave cavity (1 on flat or convex surface, lower in a crease); A is height (0 at the bottom of the bounds, 1 at the top, along local Z).
edit=bake_vertex_colors: White means no effect for every channel except height, so a mesh that was never baked, which reads (1, 1, 1, 1), behaves like one whose masks are all quiet.

edit=bake_vertex_colors: The values reach the static mesh unchanged: the conversion cancels the sRGB encoding the static-mesh build applies (UE 5.1 and later), so a material's VertexColor node reads the baked value and a stored byte is the value times 255.

edit=set_material_id: One mesh needs several materials: give each part an id (0 is the default), then bake with convert_to_static_mesh or convert_to_nanite and list one material per id in materials; entry i is the material of id i.
edit=set_material_id: Triangles must be picked by where they are: region.box, region.normal (the top faces are {x:0,y:0,z:1}), region.groupIds or region.materialIds.
edit=set_uvs: An authored vertex needs an exact UV rather than a generated one.
edit=split_normals: Authored geometry shades too soft across its creases.
edit=translate: Authored geometry must shift inside its own local space.
edit=difference: A caller reaches for the CSG name for a subtraction.
whenNotToUse: edit=create|append_polygons: A parametric shape is enough; use a create_* primitive.
edit=append_cuboids: Separate actors are wanted rather than one mesh: use control_actor.spawn.
edit=append_loft: The shape is round about one axis: use model_mesh with modeling=revolve.
edit=append_loft: The shape follows a curved path with one profile: use model_mesh with modeling=sweep or extrude_along_spline.
edit=append_mesh: Each copy must stay a separate actor (moved, hidden or destroyed on its own): use control_actor.spawn.
edit=delete_triangles: A solid must be cut by another shape: use boolean_subtract.
edit=set_vertex_color: A material parameter is the right place for the colour.
edit=bake_vertex_colors: The mesh will be rebuilt afterwards by morphology or remesh_voxel, which drop vertex colours; bake after them.
edit=set_uvs: The whole mesh needs unwrapping; use auto_uv or unwrap_uv.
edit=split_normals: Normals only need recomputing; use recalculate_normals.
edit=translate: The actor itself should move; set its transform instead.
edit=difference: The canonical spelling is available; use boolean_subtract.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

name.description: Name for the new asset or node.

actorName.description: Actor name in the level.

enableCollision.description: Enable simple collision on the created DynamicMesh actor.

meshPath.description: Static mesh asset to start from: its geometry is copied in, each section as the material id of its slot, in the mesh's own local space. Omitted, the mesh starts empty.

position.description: Position {x, y, z} for the operation.

v0.description: First corner {x, y, z} of the appended triangle. The triangle faces the side (v1 - v0) x (v2 - v0) points to, as append_polygons faces do; the other side is culled.

v1.description: Second corner {x, y, z} of the appended triangle.

v2.description: Third corner {x, y, z} of the appended triangle.

groupID.description: Polygroup id assigned to the appended triangle.

vertices.description: New points {x, y, z} in the mesh's local space, at most 20000. The faces of this call index into this list, so its first point is index 0. Points are never merged with the mesh's existing ones, and a point no face uses is left out.

faces.description: Faces, each a list of three or more vertex indices into vertices (at most 20000 faces). List a face's corners so that (v1 - v0) x (v2 - v0) points outward, and let two faces that share an edge run along it in opposite directions; the call refuses a face wound the other way, or an edge shared by more than two faces, and names the face. A face with more than three corners is triangulated (it may be concave) and all its triangles keep the face's polygroup. The new faces get smooth normals, shared where they meet; split_normals creases the hard edges.

faceGroups.description: Polygroup id of each face, one entry per face, 0 to 1000000 (default: a new unique group per face). Subdivision with catmull_clark treats every polygroup as one face of the cage, so leave this out for a cage of separate faces; give several faces one id to make one flat region.

faceMaterials.description: Material id of each face, one entry per face, 0 to 255 (default 0). A material id becomes a static-mesh material slot when the mesh is baked with convert_to_static_mesh or convert_to_nanite.

min.description: Corner with the smallest x, y and z, in the mesh's local space.

max.description: Corner with the largest x, y and z; larger than min on every axis.

materialId.description: Material id of every face of the box and its copies (default 0); a baked asset gets one slot per id.

materialIds.description: Material ids the copies take in turn (copy k takes entry k modulo the list length), counted along count, then rows, then layers: colour variety across a stack or a row. Replaces materialId.

open.description: Faces to leave out, by the direction they face: a face nobody sees (the bottom of a post on a floor, the faces two touching boxes share) costs triangles and can flicker.

count.description: Copies along offset, the box itself included (default 1).

offset.description: Step from one copy to the next, e.g. {x: 200} for one every 2 m.

rowOffset.description: Step from one row to the next.

layers.description: Layers of those rows (default 1), e.g. the tiers of a stack.

layerOffset.description: Step from one layer to the next.

repeat.description: Lay the box out count x rows x layers times, each copy moved by offset per step, rowOffset per row and layerOffset per layer. A step larger than the box leaves a gap between copies.

boxes.description: Boxes to append, at most 2500 once repeats are unrolled: each an axis-aligned box from min to max, its six faces wound outward and each face its own polygroup.

sections.description: Cross sections in order along the shape, 2 to 256, each a list of {x, y, z} points in the mesh's local space, the same count in every section (3 or more for a closed loop). Point k of one section joins point k of the next, so list every section in the same turning order from the same starting place. A section need not be flat (a raked bow); a section a few cm across gives a blunt end, endPoint a sharp one.

closed.description: Each section is a closed loop and the loft a closed tube (default true). false joins open polylines into a sheet (an awning, a curved panel), its faces turned by the order of the points; flip reverses them.

caps.description: Close a closed tube's first and last sections with a flat face each (default true), unless startPoint or endPoint closes that end.

startPoint.description: Close the first section as a fan of triangles to this point instead of a flat cap: a bow, a nose cone, a spire. Needs closed true.

endPoint.description: Close the last section as a fan of triangles to this point instead of a flat cap: a bow, a nose cone, a spire. Needs closed true.

edgeMaterials.description: Material id of each edge of the section loop, one per edge (point k to point k+1; a closed loop has as many edges as points, an open one one fewer): the strip each edge sweeps keeps it, for a painted band, a stripe or a row of windows. Default 0.

capMaterialId.description: Material id of the end caps and tip fans (default 0).

flip.description: Reverse every face. A closed tube is turned outward from the first section's turning order and the way the sections run, so flip is for an open sheet or an inside surface (a tunnel seen from within).

location.description: Where the copy's pivot goes, in the target mesh's local space (default 0, 0, 0).

rotation.description: Turn of the copy in degrees (default none).

scale.description: Scale of the copy on each axis (default 1, 1, 1); a negative axis mirrors it, faces still turned outward.

materialIds.description: The target material id of each material slot of the copied mesh, one entry per slot in slot order (the reply's sourceSlots, or inspect_object objectKind=mesh, says how many): an id, or a list of ids the copies take in turn (copy k takes entry k modulo the list length) for colour variety across a stack or a row. Omitted, each slot keeps its own index as its id.

count.description: Copies along offset, the copy itself included (default 1).

offset.description: Step from one copy to the next, e.g. {x: 200} for one every 2 m.

rowOffset.description: Step from one row to the next.

layers.description: Layers of those rows (default 1), e.g. the tiers of a stack.

layerOffset.description: Step from one layer to the next.

repeat.description: Lay the copy out count x rows x layers times, each copy moved by offset per step, rowOffset per row and layerOffset per layer. A step larger than the copy leaves a gap between copies.

placements.description: Where the copies go, at most 2500 once repeats are unrolled: each placement a transform in the target mesh's local space, an optional repeat on up to three axes (its steps add to location and are not turned by rotation), and how the copy's material slots map to the target's material ids.

lod.description: Which geometry is copied: source (default) is the full-detail source mesh; render is the mesh as it draws, for a Nanite mesh its fallback, often a twentieth of the source triangles: use it to lay out many copies of a Nanite part within the mesh's 500000-triangle budget.

triangleIndices.description: Triangle ids the operation is limited to; omit to apply it to the whole mesh. Give this or region, not both.

region.description: Pick the triangles to work on by where they are or what they carry, instead of by id; give this or triangleIndices, not both. Every filter given must hold, so they AND together. Boxes and directions are in the mesh's local space, not world space. A region that matches nothing is refused (REGION_EMPTY) with the mesh's local bounds in the message, and the reply's trianglesSelected says how many triangles were picked.

box.description: Triangles whose centroid lies inside this box (inclusive), in the mesh's local space.

min.description: Corner with the smallest x, y and z.

max.description: Corner with the largest x, y and z.

normal.description: Direction {x, y, z} in the mesh's local space; picks the triangles that face it, within normalAngle. {x: 0, y: 0, z: 1} is the top faces.

normalAngle.description: Degrees either side of normal that still count as facing it (default 30).

groupIds.description: Triangles that belong to one of these polygroup ids; a mesh without polygroups is all group 0.

materialIds.description: Triangles that carry one of these material ids (a mesh without material ids is all 0).

vertexIndex.description: Index of the vertex the operation targets.

setAll.description: Apply the colour to every vertex instead of one.

aoRays.description: Hemisphere rays per vertex for occlusion (default 32, clamped to 8-256); the bake cuts them on a very dense mesh to keep the call short, and the reply says how many it used.

aoDistance.description: How far an occluder can be, in cm (default 15% of the bounds diagonal); nearer geometry darkens R, farther geometry is ignored.

curvatureScale.description: Strength of the G and B masks (default 1): a fold of a quarter turn (90 degrees) is a full edge or cavity at 1; use 2 to make a 45 degree fold full, 0 to switch both masks off.

blurIterations.description: Neighbour-averaging passes over R, G and B (default 1, 0 to 16); 0 keeps the masks per vertex and noisy.

materialId.description: Material id to set, 0 to 255. The baked asset gets the highest id used + 1 slots.

splitAngle.description: Angle threshold in degrees above which normals are split.

translation.description: Translation {x, y, z} applied to every mesh vertex.

targetActor.description: The dynamic mesh actor to edit, by label or name (actorName is the same and wins when both are sent).

edit.description:
Which edit dynamic mesh variant to run.
create: Spawn a DynamicMesh actor to author geometry into: empty, or a copy of a static mesh asset.
append_vertex: Append one vertex to a DynamicMesh actor and return its index.
append_triangle: Append a triangle to a DynamicMesh actor from three corner positions.
append_polygons: Author a polygon cage on a DynamicMesh actor in one call: new vertices and faces of three or more corners, each with its own polygroup and material id.
append_cuboids: Append axis-aligned boxes to a DynamicMesh actor in one call, each with a material id, faces left open and a repeat along up to three axes (a railing, a stack of crates, a grid of windows, shelves, pillars), wound outward for you.
append_loft: Append a surface lofted through cross sections to a DynamicMesh actor: each section a loop of points (the same count in every one), joined in order with every face turned outward, the ends capped flat or closed to a tip point.
append_mesh: Copy a static mesh asset into a DynamicMesh actor at placements, each repeated along up to three axes, with its material slots mapped to the target's material ids (a list cycles copy by copy for colour variety): a model assembled from detailed parts in one call, its copies keeping the asset's normals and UVs.
delete_triangles: Delete the triangles of a DynamicMesh actor that triangleIndices or a region picks (by box, facing direction, polygroup or material id), with the points only they used.
set_vertex_position: Move one vertex of a DynamicMesh actor to a new position.
set_vertex_color: Set the vertex colour on one vertex, or on every vertex, of a DynamicMesh actor.
bake_vertex_colors: Bake ambient occlusion, convex-edge, concave-cavity and height masks into the vertex colours of a DynamicMesh actor, for a material to read through its VertexColor node.
set_material_id: Set the material id (the static-mesh material slot) of triangles of a DynamicMesh actor: every triangle, the triangleIndices you list, or a region.
set_uvs: Set the UV coordinate of one vertex on a UV channel of a DynamicMesh actor.
split_normals: Split the normals of a DynamicMesh actor above an angle threshold to harden edges.
translate: Translate every vertex of a DynamicMesh actor, leaving the actor transform alone.
difference: Subtract a tool mesh from a target mesh under the difference spelling of boolean_subtract.

examples.title: Edit a procedural/dynamic mesh: create one, append vertices, triangles, a whole polygon cage (append_polygons), parts laid out in rows and grids (append_cuboids), a loft through cross sections (append_loft) or copies of a detailed static mesh (append_mesh) in one call, delete the triangles of a region (delete_triangles), give triangles material ids by region (set_material_id), bake AO, edge, cavity and height masks for materials to read (bake_vertex_colors), set vertex positions, colors or UVs, split normals, translate, or subtract another mesh.

discovery.summary: Give a placed dynamic mesh actor UVs, chosen by uvOp, in uvChannel (default 0, made when missing); each edit is one undo step. auto and unwrap cut seams with XAtlas and pack the islands into 0-1 (a bounds-sized box projection when XAtlas writes nothing); project box-projects, with tileSize the world size one texture repeat covers (else the texture spans each side once); pack_islands repacks the islands already there; transform shifts (uvOffset), scales (uvScale, about the middle of 0-1) and turns (rotation, degrees) the UVs already there.
whenToUse: uvOp=auto: A mesh needs UVs that follow its surface, such as before a texture, a lightmap or a bake.
uvOp=unwrap: A mesh needs UVs that follow its surface.
uvOp=project: A box-like mesh needs simple UVs fast, or a tiling material must repeat at a real-world size (tileSize).
uvOp=pack_islands: Islands overlap or stray outside 0-1 after edits, such as before a lightmap bake.
uvOp=transform: A texture on a mesh must repeat more or less often, shift or turn, keeping its UV layout.

actorName.description: Actor name in the level.

targetActor.description: The dynamic mesh actor to edit, by label or name (actorName is the same and wins when both are sent).

uvOp.description:
Which edit uvs variant to run.
auto: Unwrap a dynamic mesh actor with XAtlas into uvChannel (default 0, made when missing): seams are cut and the islands packed into the 0-1 square, compacting the mesh first (compacted). When XAtlas writes nothing it falls back to a bounds-sized box projection (method box_projection_fallback, with xatlasError saying why). The reply gives uvElementCount; none at all is UV_GENERATION_FAILED.
unwrap: Same as uvOp=auto: unwrap a dynamic mesh actor with XAtlas into uvChannel, falling back to a bounds-sized box projection, and report uvElementCount.
project: Box-project UVs onto a dynamic mesh actor into uvChannel (default 0, made when missing): each triangle takes the face of the box it points at. tileSize is the world size one texture repeat covers, for tiling materials such as brick or concrete; without it the box is the mesh bounds and the texture spans each side once. The reply gives projectionSize.
pack_islands: Repack the UV islands already in uvChannel (default 0) of a dynamic mesh actor into the 0-1 square without overlap, keeping each island's shape.
transform: Move, scale and turn the UVs already in uvChannel (default 0) of a dynamic mesh actor, in that order: uvOffset {u, v} shifts them, uvScale {u, v} scales them about the middle of the 0-1 square (2 repeats a texture twice), rotation turns them by degrees about the same point. The reply echoes what was applied.

discovery.summary: Polygon modeling on a mesh: extrude, inset, outset, offset faces, bevel, chamfer, bridge, loft, sweep, revolve, shell, loop cut, edge split, poke faces, group triangles into quads, or extrude/duplicate along a spline. Extrude, inset, outset, offset, bevel, chamfer and poke work on every triangle, on triangleIndices, or on a region picked by box, facing direction, polygroup or material id. Dynamic meshes are always triangles.
whenToUse: modeling=extrude: Faces must be extruded along a direction; pick them with triangleIndices or a region (the top faces are region.normal {x:0,y:0,z:1}).
modeling=inset: Faces must be inset; pick them with triangleIndices or a region.
modeling=outset: Faces must be outset; pick them with triangleIndices or a region.
modeling=offset_faces: Faces must be offset; pick them with triangleIndices or a region.
modeling=bevel: Edges must be beveled; pick the faces whose edges bevel with triangleIndices or a region.
modeling=chamfer: Edges must be chamfered; pick the faces whose edges chamfer with triangleIndices or a region.
modeling=bridge: Two edge loops must be bridged.
modeling=loft: A lofted surface between profiles must be created.
modeling=sweep: A swept solid must be created.
modeling=revolve: A lathe/revolve solid must be created.
modeling=shell: A hollow shell must be generated.
modeling=loop_cut: An edge loop must be inserted.
modeling=edge_split: Specific edges must be subdivided.
modeling=poke: Faces must be split from their centre, or pushed out into pyramids or spikes; pick them with triangleIndices or a region.
modeling=quadrangulate: A triangulated mesh must be edited as quads.
modeling=extrude_along_spline: A mesh must be swept along a spline path.
modeling=duplicate_along_spline: Copies of a mesh must be distributed along a spline.
whenNotToUse: modeling=poke: The whole mesh should be refined evenly; use subdivide.
modeling=quadrangulate: Real quad topology is needed in an exported asset; meshes in Unreal are always triangles.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: Actor name in the level.

targetActor.description: The dynamic mesh actor to edit, by label or name (actorName is the same and wins when both are sent).

offset.description: Offset vector.

triangleIndices.description: Triangle ids the operation is limited to; omit to apply it to the whole mesh. Give this or region, not both.

region.description: Pick the triangles to work on by where they are or what they carry, instead of by id; give this or triangleIndices, not both. Every filter given must hold, so they AND together. Boxes and directions are in the mesh's local space, not world space. A region that matches nothing is refused (REGION_EMPTY) with the mesh's local bounds in the message, and the reply's trianglesSelected says how many triangles were picked.

box.description: Triangles whose centroid lies inside this box (inclusive), in the mesh's local space.

min.description: Corner with the smallest x, y and z.

max.description: Corner with the largest x, y and z.

normal.description: Direction {x, y, z} in the mesh's local space; picks the triangles that face it, within normalAngle. {x: 0, y: 0, z: 1} is the top faces.

normalAngle.description: Degrees either side of normal that still count as facing it (default 30).

groupIds.description: Triangles that belong to one of these polygroup ids; a mesh without polygroups is all group 0.

materialIds.description: Triangles that carry one of these material ids (a mesh without material ids is all 0).

segments.description: Subdivisions for a rounded bevel (UE 5.4 or later); omit or 0 for a flat bevel.

splineActorName.description: Spline actor name for extrude/sweep along spline.

cap.description: Close open ends: the tube ends of a loft, sweep or extrude along a spline, or for a revolve flat discs from the first and last profile points to the axis (revolve default true).

steps.description: Path steps along a sweep (default 16; the profile uses half as many sides), or segments around the axis for a revolve (default 16, 3 to 512; 48 or more reads as round).

name.description: Name for the new asset or node.

location.description: World location {x, y, z}.

rotation.description: Rotation {pitch, yaw, roll}.

radius.description: Distance from the axis in cm, 0 or more.

height.description: Height above the base in cm.

profile.description: Points from bottom to top, at least 2. For a hollow shape with walls, go up the outside and back down the inside. A closed loop (end on the first point) with cap false turns a solid ring section, such as a moulding or a tyre. Omit for a small built-in vase.

angle.description: Degrees to turn the profile about local Z, 1 to 360 (default 360), starting on local +X and turning toward +Y; less leaves an open wedge whose two cut faces are not closed.

axis.description: Axis: X, Y or Z, any case; another name is refused.

edges.description: Edge ids to split at their midpoints.

respectUVSeams.description: Never pair two triangles across a UV seam (default true).

respectHardNormals.description: Never pair two triangles across a hard edge (default false).

modeling.description:
Which model mesh variant to run.
extrude: Extrude selected faces of a dynamic mesh.
inset: Inset selected faces of a dynamic mesh.
outset: Outset selected faces of a dynamic mesh.
offset_faces: Offset selected faces of a dynamic mesh.
bevel: Bevel selected edges of a dynamic mesh.
chamfer: Chamfer selected edges of a dynamic mesh.
bridge: Bridge two edge loops of a dynamic mesh.
loft: Loft between two or more profile curves.
sweep: Sweep a profile along a path of a dynamic mesh.
revolve: Turn a profile of {radius, height} points around the vertical axis into a new dynamic mesh actor: a vase, column, bottle, tower or dome.
shell: Create a shell (inner offset) of a dynamic mesh.
loop_cut: Insert evenly spaced edge loops across a dynamic mesh, perpendicular to an axis.
edge_split: Split edges of a dynamic mesh at their midpoints.
poke: Poke faces of a dynamic mesh: add a centre vertex to each triangle (optionally pushed out along its normal) and fan it into three triangles.
quadrangulate: Group pairs of adjacent triangles of a dynamic mesh into quad PolyGroups, so PolyGroup edits (extrude, inset, bevel by group) act on quads. The mesh itself stays triangles.
extrude_along_spline: Extrude a profile along a spline actor.
duplicate_along_spline: Duplicate a mesh along a spline actor.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

trianglesSelected.description: Triangles the operation worked on: the triangleIndices or region selection, else every triangle of the mesh.

trianglesAfter.description: Triangle count after (before + 2 per poked triangle).

skipped.description: Degenerate or missing triangles that were left alone.

singleTriangleGroups.description: Triangles left in a group of their own.

largerGroups.description: Groups of more than two triangles.
