discovery.summary: Optimize, smooth or repair a mesh: simplify, remesh (uniform or voxel), subdivide (pn tessellation, or Catmull-Clark, Loop and bilinear surfaces from a polygroup cage), morphology (voxel offset: dilate, contract, close to fillet where unioned parts meet, open), merge or weld vertices, remove degenerates, fill holes, flip or recalculate normals, recompute tangents.
whenToUse: optimization=simplify_mesh: A mesh must be simplified.
optimization=remesh_uniform: A uniform remesh is needed.

optimization=remesh_voxel: A watertight voxel remesh is needed, for example to fuse unioned or overlapping parts into one skin. The grid cell is targetEdgeLength, or the longest side divided by voxelCount (default 128). The surface is rebuilt, so UVs, material ids, polygroups and vertex colours are dropped: run auto_uv, set_material_id and bake_vertex_colors afterwards.

optimization=subdivide: A mesh must be refined. For a smooth, rounded model, author a coarse polygon cage (edit_dynamic_mesh append_polygons, one polygroup per face, or create_box) and subdivide it with scheme catmull_clark, iterations 2 or 3.
optimization=subdivide: The cage carries material ids and polygroups through the subdivision, so assign them with set_material_id first.
optimization=morphology: Joined parts need a smooth blend: boolean_union them, then morphology close with a distance about the fillet radius, then auto_uv, set_material_id and bake_vertex_colors.
optimization=morphology: A mesh must grow or shrink evenly (dilate, contract), or small bumps must go (open).
optimization=merge_vertices: Duplicate vertices must be welded/merged.
optimization=weld_vertices: Vertices must be welded by threshold.
optimization=remove_degenerates: Degenerate triangles must be removed.
optimization=fill_holes: Mesh holes must be capped.
optimization=flip_normals: Normals must be flipped (inside-out).
optimization=recalculate_normals: Normals must be recalculated.
optimization=recompute_tangents: Tangents must be recomputed for correct shading.
whenNotToUse: optimization=subdivide: Edges must stay sharp; subdivision rounds every edge of the cage.
optimization=morphology: Edges must stay crisp; the grid rounds every feature narrower than about twice distance.
optimization=morphology: UVs, material ids, polygroups or vertex colours must survive; the surface is rebuilt from the grid, so set them afterwards.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: Actor name in the level.

targetActor.description: The dynamic mesh actor to edit, by label or name (actorName is the same and wins when both are sent).

voxelCount.description: Grid cells along the mesh's longest side for the voxel operations (default 128, clamped to 16-256): more cells keep thinner detail and cost more time and triangles. The reply's voxelSize is the resulting cell width in cm.

iterations.description: Subdivision level, 1 to 6 (default 1). Each level quadruples the face count, so 2 or 3 is enough for a smooth result; the call is refused past 500000 triangles.

scheme.description: Subdivision scheme (default pn). pn: PN tessellation, which adds triangles and keeps the shape. catmull_clark: a smooth subdivision surface over a polygon cage, where every polygroup is one face (build the cage with edit_dynamic_mesh append_polygons, or start from create_box, which has one polygroup per face); the surface rounds toward the cage, and polygroups and material ids carry through. loop: smooths the triangles as they are and needs no cage. bilinear: cuts the cage into quads without smoothing. iterations is the level.

operation.description: dilate grows the surface outward by distance, contract shrinks it inward; close (the default) fills creases and rounds the seams where parts meet, a fillet up to about twice distance wide; open shaves off bumps and thin parts smaller than distance.

distance.description: Offset distance in cm (default 2% of the mesh's longest side). Keep it above one voxel (the longest side divided by voxelCount) or the effect barely registers.

optimization.description:
Which optimize mesh variant to run.
simplify_mesh: Simplify a dynamic mesh to a target triangle count.
remesh_uniform: Uniformly remesh a dynamic mesh to a target edge length.
remesh_voxel: Voxel-wrap a dynamic mesh into one watertight, smooth-shaded surface (the engine's solidify): the mesh is sampled into a grid and rebuilt, closing holes and merging overlapping parts.
subdivide: Subdivide a dynamic mesh: pn tessellation (default), or a Catmull-Clark, Loop or bilinear subdivision surface.
morphology: Offset a dynamic mesh's surface through a voxel grid: dilate, contract, close (fillet the seams where unioned parts meet) or open.
merge_vertices: Merge coincident vertices of a dynamic mesh.
weld_vertices: Weld vertices of a dynamic mesh within a distance.
remove_degenerates: Remove degenerate triangles from a dynamic mesh.
fill_holes: Fill boundary holes of a dynamic mesh.
flip_normals: Flip normals of a dynamic mesh.
recalculate_normals: Recalculate normals of a dynamic mesh.
recompute_tangents: Recompute tangents of a dynamic mesh.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

cageFaces.description: Cage faces: polygroups for catmull_clark and bilinear, triangles for loop; absent for pn.

voxelCount.description: Grid cells along the longest side after clamping.

voxelSize.description: Width of one grid cell in cm.

note.description: What the rebuild dropped, and a hint when distance is under one voxel.

examples.title: Optimize, smooth or repair a mesh: simplify, remesh (uniform or voxel), subdivide (pn tessellation, or Catmull-Clark, Loop and bilinear surfaces from a polygroup cage), morphology (voxel offset: dilate, contract, close to fillet where unioned parts meet, open), merge or weld vertices, remove degenerates, fill holes, flip or recalculate normals, recompute tangents.

discovery.summary: Split a static mesh asset into one static mesh per connected part (or per material slot), each with its own pivot, the materials it uses and a collision choice.
whenToUse: A library pack or kit came in as one static mesh and its props must be placed one by one: split it, then place each new mesh (offset says where its pivot stood in the source, so the original layout can be rebuilt).
A mesh must be separated by material slot (by material).
whenNotToUse: A dynamic mesh actor being modelled must become an asset (use convert_to_static_mesh).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

meshPath.description: The static mesh asset to split; it is not changed.

by.description: parts (default): one mesh per separate object, where connected pieces whose bounds touch or come within gap cm are one object (a crate's planks stay one crate); material: one per material slot.

gap.description: With by parts: pieces whose bounds come within this many cm of each other are one object (default 2).

outputPath.description: Folder for the new meshes (default: the folder of the source mesh).

namePrefix.description: Names are <namePrefix>01, <namePrefix>02 ..., largest part first (default <source name>_Part); a name already taken refuses the split before anything is made.

pivot.description: Each new mesh's pivot: bottom (default), the bottom centre of its bounds, so it stands on what it is placed on; center; or source, the source's own origin.

minTriangles.description: Objects with fewer triangles are left out (default 12): loose bits, decal cards.

maxParts.description: More parts than this (default 64) refuses the split with nothing made.

dropRepeats.description: Leave out an object that only repeats a larger one where it stands, such as an LOD copy an importer merged into the mesh (default true).

dryRun.description: Answer the meshes the split would make (size, triangles, offset, and exists when the name is taken) and create nothing, to tune gap and minTriangles first. A large pack can take longer than one call waits.

collision.description: Collision for the baked asset: box (default) is one box the size of the bounds, which pawns can stand on (on a converted-over asset too); complex uses the render triangles as simple collision too, exact but costly; none gives the asset no collision at all.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

meshes.description: One entry per new mesh, largest first: assetPath, triangles, size [x, y, z], offset [x, y, z] (its pivot in the source's space), slots; saved: false when it could not be written to disk.

skippedSmall.description: Objects left out for having fewer than minTriangles triangles.

droppedRepeats.description: Objects left out as repeats of a larger one.

discovery.summary: Configure an interactable: door, chest or switch properties, a door that follows a switch, or its interaction trace.
whenToUse: setting=door: An existing door needs a new open angle, open time or locked state; fields left out keep their value.
setting=door: A door must open and shut with a switch or lever (switchPath); each placed door then gets its placed switch as LinkedSwitch (control_actor.set_blueprint_variables).
setting=chest: An existing chest needs its locked state, lid open angle, open time or loot table path changed; fields left out keep their value.

setting=switch: An existing switch needs a different type (a pressure_plate is on while stood on, a button or lever flips per press), a toggle-back rule or a reset delay; fields left out keep their value.
setting=trace: The trigger of an interactable Blueprint must be resized: every sphere gets radius traceDistance, every box gets extent traceDistance by traceRadius.
setting=trace: Give traceDistance, traceRadius and traceType together, since an omitted one resets to 200, 50 or sphere; traceType only stores a name.
whenNotToUse: setting=door|chest|switch: The Blueprint does not exist yet or lacks the components its create step adds (use manage_interaction.create_interactable).
setting=door|chest|switch: One placed actor needs its own values, not the Blueprint default (use control_actor.set_blueprint_variables).
setting=trace: The Blueprint has no sphere or box component to resize (add one with manage_interaction.create_interactable, kind=component).
setting=trace: Only one of several sphere or box components should change, since every one is resized (use blueprint.edit_scs).

doorPath.description: Canonical /Game door actor Blueprint asset path.

openAngle.description: Open angle in degrees (a new door gets 90, a new chest lid 100).

openTime.description: Seconds the door or lid takes to swing fully open or shut (a new door gets 0.5, a new chest 0.6).

switchPath.description: The switch, lever or trigger Blueprint (from create_interactable) the door follows: on when switched on, shut when off. The door is then locked against opening when a pawn walks up, unless locked is given.

chestPath.description: Canonical /Game chest actor Blueprint asset path.

switchType.description: button (the default) or lever flip on each press; pressure_plate is on only while stood on.

canToggle.description: Whether the switch can toggle back off.

traceType.description: Free-text name stored in the TraceType Name variable of the Blueprint (default sphere). It does not choose or change a trace shape: the shape comes from the sphere and box components, which traceDistance and traceRadius resize.

traceDistance.description: Interaction trace distance in world units.

traceRadius.description: Cross-section of each box component in world units (default 50): a box gets extent traceDistance by traceRadius. Sphere components ignore it.

setting.description:
Which configure interactable variant to run.
door: Configure persistent door properties, or make the door follow a switch.
chest: Configure persistent chest properties.
switch: Change a switch Blueprint made by create_interactable: switchType (button or lever flip per press, pressure_plate holds while stood on; a new type rewrites the switch logic), canToggle and resetTime (Blueprint variables). Only the fields sent change, and the Blueprint is saved; one without the SwitchMesh component is refused.
trace: Configure persistent interaction trace data.

discovery.summary: Create an interactable: a door or chest that opens when a pawn comes near, a switch or lever a pawn presses (it fires OnSwitchChanged), a trigger actor, an interactable interface, or an interaction component.
whenToUse: kind=door: A door Blueprint is needed with a pivot, a door mesh and a trigger box, plus open-angle, timing, lock and key variables; the door swings open (yaw, over openTime) while a pawn overlaps the trigger and it is unlocked, and autoClose shuts it autoCloseDelay seconds after the last pawn leaves. Calling it again on an existing door adds that opening logic.

kind=chest: A chest Blueprint is needed with a base mesh, a lid mesh on a pivot, a trigger sphere and an optional locked state; its lid swings open (pitch, over openTime) while a pawn overlaps the trigger and the chest is unlocked.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

lightType.description: Light kind: point, spot, directional, rect or sky (any case), or the class name PointLight, SpotLight, DirectionalLight, RectLight or SkyLight. A light class of your own goes in lightClass.

lightClass.description: Light class name or path, for a class lightType does not name, including a Blueprint light (/Game/Lights/BP_Lamp.BP_Lamp_C); build_environment list_light_types lists the loaded ones. Wins over lightType.

name.description: Light actor name.

intensity.description: Brightness: the light component's Intensity, set as given, in the component's own units (a directional light is in lux). Left out, the engine default stays. properties.intensity wins over it.

color.description: Light color [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a]. Linear 0-1 channels, stored by the engine as the 8-bit sRGB color: {r: 1, g: 0.7, b: 0.42} reads back as (255, 218, 173). A missing channel reads 0 (alpha 1). properties.color wins over it.

location.description: World location {x, y, z}; 0, 0, 300 when omitted.

rotation.description: Actor rotation {pitch, yaw, roll} or {x, y, z, w}. A spot or directional light shines along its forward axis, so pitch -90 points it straight down.

properties.description: Light component settings, applied to the lights they fit; the reply lists what went in as details.applied, what did not as details.refused ("name: why") and any value replaced for being out of range as details.adjusted. Keys: intensity (0 or more; a negative reads 0), color (as above), castShadows (true or false), useAsAtmosphereSunLight (true or false; a directional light given properties is the atmosphere sun unless this says false), attenuationRadius (above 0, point and spot lights; an invalid value reads 1000), innerConeAngle and outerConeAngle (0 to 180 degrees, spot lights; clamped), sourceWidth and sourceHeight (above 0, rect lights; an invalid value reads 100). A sky light takes only the top-level intensity and color. Any other key, or one that does not fit the light, is refused by name.

streamingMethod.description: Level streaming method: Blueprint (loaded on demand) or AlwaysLoaded.

streamingDistance.description: How far the volume reaches from its centre on each axis, in world units, over 0 (default 10000).

streamingUsage.description: What the volume controls (default LoadingAndVisibility: load and show the level while a viewer is inside).

bUseExternalActors.description: Also move the level actors into one-file-per-actor packages (default false).

priority.description: World Partition grid priority (higher wins when grids overlap).

setting.description:
Which configure level streaming variant to run; omit for 'streaming'.
streaming: Change how the open level streams a sublevel (levelName: its package path or short name): streamingMethod Blueprint or AlwaysLoaded (switched as the Levels panel does), bShouldBeVisible, bShouldBlockOnLoad and bDisableDistanceStreaming; only the fields sent change. A level on disk that the open level does not stream yet is added to it first; one that does not exist is LEVEL_NOT_FOUND. The open level stays unsaved unless save is true.
streaming_distance: Stream a sublevel by where the player is: place a Level Streaming Volume, a box reaching streamingDistance (default 10000) from volumeLocation (default the origin) on each axis, bound to the sublevel (levelName) so it loads while a viewer is inside it. streamingUsage picks what it controls (LoadingAndVisibility, the default, Loading, VisibilityBlockingOnLoad, BlockingOnLoad, LoadingNotVisible); an unknown one or a distance of 0 or less is refused before anything is placed. createVolume false only lists the volumes bound to the level. A level on disk the open level does not stream yet is added first. The open level stays unsaved unless save is true.
world_partition: Turn World Partition on for the open level in place: it creates the World Partition object on the level's World Settings (save and reload the level before streaming works); bUseExternalActors also moves every actor into its own package (one file per actor), which data layers need. Turning it off on a partitioned level is refused (NOT_SUPPORTED), as is a level that cannot take it. The level stays unsaved unless save is true.
grid_size: Set a World Partition streaming grid of the open level (gridName; omitted, the first grid, or MainPartition on a Runtime Hash Set level): gridCellSize, loadingRange (how far from the player its cells load), bBlockOnSlowStreaming and priority; only the fields sent change, and a grid missing by name is added with createIfMissing (default true), the others at their defaults (cell 12800, range 25600). On a Runtime Hash Set level the grid is a runtime partition row, which must have a Main Layer to hold the values (PARTITION_HAS_NO_LAYER otherwise). The reply gives the edited grid values as they now stand (on a Runtime Hash Set level, the values it set) and lists every grid; a grid found with nothing sent to change is refused. The level stays unsaved unless save is true.
hlod_layer: Create an HLOD layer asset (hlodLayerName, in hlodLayerPath, default /Game/HLOD): layerType Instancing, MeshMerge (default), MeshSimplify or MeshApproximate, spatially loaded (default true) with its cellSize (default 25600) and loadingDistance (default 51200). An unknown layerType is refused before anything is created; each value reports whether it took (layerTypeApplied and the others). Saved unless save is false.
data_layer_assignment: Add a placed actor (actorName: label or name, or actorPath) to a data layer of the open level (dataLayerName: its short or full name), so it loads and shows with that layer. One already in the layer is reported (alreadyAssigned); a layer that is not there is refused with the ones that are. Needs World Partition with external actors; the level stays unsaved unless save is true.

kind.description:
Which create level structure variant to run.
level: Create an empty level asset, levelName in levelPath (default /Game/Maps), saved unless save is false. bCreateWorldPartition makes it a World Partition level (external actors then default on; bUseExternalActors false keeps them in the level). A level already at that path is reported (alreadyExisted), never replaced. loadAfterCreate opens it, refused with DIRTY_PACKAGES (naming them) when open levels have unsaved changes the load would drop.
sublevel: Create an empty level asset (sublevelName, in sublevelPath, else beside the open level, or /Game/Maps when the open level was never saved) and stream it into the open level by streamingMethod (Blueprint, the default, or AlwaysLoaded). parentLevel, when given, must be the open level (PARENT_LEVEL_NOT_LOADED otherwise, nothing created). A level already at that path is reported (alreadyExisted, streamingAdded), not replaced; manage_level add_sublevel streams it. save (default true) saves the new level and the open level.
level_instance: Place a Level Instance actor that loads an existing level asset at a location, so one saved level (a room, a building) can be reused inside another.
packed_level_actor: Bake the static meshes of a level into a Packed Level Blueprint (instanced static mesh components) and optionally place it (UE 5.3 or later).
data_layer: Create a World Partition data layer: a DataLayerAsset named dataLayerName in dataLayerAssetPath (default /Game/DataLayers), saved, and its instance in the open level, Runtime (streams in the game, the default) or Editor (organises the editor only), visible and loaded in the editor by default. Needs World Partition with external actors (WORLD_PARTITION_NOT_ENABLED, EXTERNAL_ACTORS_NOT_ENABLED); an unknown dataLayerType is refused before anything is created. Add actors with assign_actor_to_data_layer.
minimap_volume: Place a World Partition minimap volume, the area the minimap builder captures: a box brush of extent (half size, default 10000 on each axis) at location, labelled volumeName (default MinimapVolume). A level without World Partition is refused (WORLD_PARTITION_NOT_ENABLED); UE 5.1 or later. The level stays unsaved unless save is true.

discovery.summary: Edit the level Blueprint of the open level (levelPath names another loaded level; by default the persistent level), chosen by edit. open opens its editor; add_node adds a node by class or alias (an event bound to a placed actor with actorName and eventName, a reference to one, a component getter with memberClass and memberName) and lists its pins; connect_nodes links two pins through the graph schema, which refuses incompatible ones (CONNECTION_REFUSED, with its reason) and adds the conversion node a cast needs; remove_node removes a node by id, name or title; set_pin_default_value sets an input pin. The level stays unsaved unless save is true (saved), and a transient /Temp level is refused.
whenToUse: edit=open: The level blueprint graph must be edited.
edit=add_node: A new node must be added to level scripting.
edit=add_node: Level logic must react to a placed actor (K2Node_ActorBoundEvent with actorName and eventName) or use one (K2Node_Literal with actorName).
edit=add_node: A function of a class outside the common Blueprint libraries must be called (K2Node_CallFunction with functionName and memberClass).

edit=add_node: A placed actor's component must be used, such as the light component whose SetLightColor changes a light (K2Node_VariableGet with memberClass and memberName, its self pin fed from the actor's K2Node_Literal).
edit=connect_nodes: Two level blueprint nodes must be wired together.
edit=remove_node: A level blueprint node must be deleted, or an unbound K2Node_CallFunction ("Could not find a function named None") must be repaired.
edit=set_pin_default_value: A level blueprint node's input pin needs a literal value instead of a wire (a light color, a print string, a number).
whenNotToUse: edit=open: A sub-level blueprint is needed; use the asset path directly.

edit=add_node: The level Blueprint's nodes must be read, or edited beyond these edits; blueprint.inspect_graph and blueprint.edit_graph take the open level's path (/Game/Maps/L_Main) as blueprintPath.
edit=connect_nodes: The nodes are in a Blueprint asset, not the level Blueprint; use blueprint.edit_graph (edit=connect_pins).
edit=set_pin_default_value: The node is in a Blueprint asset, not the level Blueprint; use blueprint.edit_graph (edit=set_pin_default_value).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

save.description: Save the level after the edit (default false, because saving also writes every other unsaved change in that level); the reply says saved: false while it is only in memory.

functionName.description: Function to bind when nodeClass is K2Node_CallFunction (e.g. PrintString); short function names may also be passed as nodeClass.

memberClass.description: Class that declares functionName when it is not in the common Blueprint libraries, or memberName: a native class name or a Blueprint asset path. The node's Target (self pin) takes an object of that class, so an actor's function or component getter is fed from its K2Node_Literal, while a component's function (a light's SetLightColor is LightComponent's) takes the component that getter returns, not the actor. One that names no class is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

memberName.description: Variable a K2Node_VariableGet or K2Node_VariableSet reads or writes, required by both and refused for other nodes: a level Blueprint variable (its own or inherited, such as Tags), or with memberClass a property of that class, such as a placed actor's component (PointLightComponent on PointLight, StaticMeshComponent on StaticMeshActor); with memberClass the node always has the self pin the actor's K2Node_Literal feeds, even for Actor. A wrong name is refused with that class's components listed (VARIABLE_NOT_FOUND), and one Blueprints cannot read, or for a VariableSet write (not Blueprint-visible, read-only), with VARIABLE_NOT_ACCESSIBLE.

actorName.description: Placed actor (label, name or object path) in the edited level that a K2Node_ActorBoundEvent fires for or a K2Node_Literal references; required by both, refused for other nodes. A label two actors share is refused with their names, and an actor of another loaded level with that level (ACTOR_IN_OTHER_LEVEL).

eventName.description: Event dispatcher of actorName that a K2Node_ActorBoundEvent binds, e.g. OnActorBeginOverlap or OnActorEndOverlap; a wrong name is refused with the actor's events listed. Refused for any other node: BeginPlay or Tick go in nodeClass (EventBeginPlay, EventTick).

sourceNodeName.description: Source node: the nodeName or nodeId add_level_blueprint_node returned, or its title. An exact match wins; otherwise the last node whose name or title contains it.

targetNodeName.description: Target node: the nodeName or nodeId add_level_blueprint_node returned, or its title. An exact match wins; otherwise the last node whose name or title contains it.

nodeId.description: The node: the nodeId or nodeName add_level_blueprint_node returned, or its title, matched exactly (a node that only contains it is not taken). A name or title several nodes share is refused with their names (AMBIGUOUS_NODE).

unboundOnly.description: Remove every call-function node that has no bound function instead of a named node.

pinName.description: Input pin name or display name, as add_level_blueprint_node lists them (NewLightColor on SetLightColor).

propertyValue.description: The pin's new default: a number, true or false, text, an enum value name, an asset path, a vector as X,Y,Z or {x,y,z}, a rotator as P,Y,R or {pitch,yaw,roll}, a color as {r,g,b,a}.

edit.description:
Which edit level blueprint variant to run.
open: Open the Level Blueprint editor of the open level (levelPath picks a loaded sublevel; default the persistent level), creating the Level Blueprint when the level has none yet. A level never saved (/Temp) has none to open, and an editor that does not open is EDITOR_NOT_OPENED; a headless editor only checks the Blueprint is there (headlessSafeMode). Nothing is changed or saved.
add_node: Add a node to the level blueprint graph, including an event bound to a placed actor (OnActorBeginOverlap of a trigger), a reference to one, or a getter of its component; the reply lists the node's pins.
connect_nodes: Link sourceNodeName.sourcePinName to targetNodeName.targetPinName in the level Blueprint through the graph schema: incompatible types or directions are refused with the schema's reason (CONNECTION_REFUSED), a cast gets its conversion node, and a pin that takes one link drops its old one. A pin a node lacks is PIN_NOT_FOUND, naming the pins on both nodes. The level stays unsaved unless save is true (saved).
remove_node: Remove a level blueprint node by id, name or title (one several nodes share is refused), or purge unbound call nodes.
set_pin_default_value: Set the default value of an input pin on a level blueprint node (in its event graph or one of its functions), such as the color SetLightColor sets; a read-only (const reference) pin gets it through a MakeLiteral node wired into it.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

nodeName.description: The node whose pin was set.

appliedValue.description: Literal actually stored on the pin (or the resolved object path for an object or class pin).

literalNodeId.description: Guid of the MakeLiteral node carrying the value when the pin itself takes no literal.

saved.description: Whether the level was saved.

The level stays unsaved unless save is true (saved), and a transient /Temp level is refused.

discovery.summary: Configure client-side prediction: client, movement, server correction, or add prediction data (a variable replicated only to the owning client).
whenToUse: setting=client: Use it to set whether a Character Blueprint always sends clients the server time stamp of its last movement update (CharacterMovement bNetworkAlwaysReplicateTransformUpdateTimestamp), which the linear smoothing of simulated proxies uses; it changes nothing unless the character replicates its movement. Other Blueprints are refused; saved (SAVE_FAILED when it cannot be written).

setting=movement: Use it to set a Character Blueprint's movement network smoothing mode and smoothing distances; only the fields sent are written, other Blueprints are refused; saved (SAVE_FAILED when it cannot be written).

setting=server_correction: Use it to set how long, in seconds, a Character Blueprint smooths the moves other machines see (smoothingRate: CharacterMovement NetworkSimulatedSmoothLocationTime and RotationTime and the listen-server pair, all four together). Other Blueprints are refused; saved (SAVE_FAILED when it cannot be written).

setting=add_data: Use it to add a Blueprint variable, or convert an existing one of the same type, that replicates only to the owning client (COND_AutonomousOnly) for client-side prediction state. Pawn, Character, Controller and ActorComponent Blueprints only (no other actor is an autonomous proxy); the reply says whether the Blueprint itself replicates.

networkNoSmoothUpdateDistance.description: CharacterMovement NetworkNoSmoothUpdateDistance in cm: corrections farther than this snap without smoothing.

smoothingRate.description: Seconds simulated proxies take to smooth a server correction (location and rotation, dedicated and listen server).

dataType.description: Variable type in the add_variable grammar: Vector, Rotator, Transform, Float, Int, Bool, Name, Struct:/Game/Path/S_Name.S_Name, Array:Vector and so on.

variableName.description: Variable to add or convert; default PredictionData_<dataType> (required when dataType is not a plain type name).

Other Blueprints are refused; saved (SAVE_FAILED when it cannot be written).
movement: Set a Character Blueprint's movement network smoothing mode and smoothing distances; only the fields sent are written, other Blueprints are refused; saved (SAVE_FAILED when it cannot be written).
server_correction: Set how long, in seconds, a Character Blueprint smooths the moves other machines see (smoothingRate: CharacterMovement NetworkSimulatedSmoothLocationTime and RotationTime and the listen-server pair, all four together). Other Blueprints are refused; saved (SAVE_FAILED when it cannot be written).

discovery.summary: Configure replication on a Blueprint: property replication and conditions, RepNotify, net role, dormancy, relevancy, priority, update frequency, cull distance, push model, replicated movement, replication graph, net driver.
whenToUse: setting=property: Use it to turn replication of a Blueprint variable on or off, optionally with its replication condition.
setting=condition: Use it to set a Blueprint property replication condition.
setting=rep_notify: Use it to make a Blueprint variable RepNotify: it replicates, and clients call repNotifyFunc when its new value arrives.
setting=net_role: Use it to choose how clients see an Actor Blueprint's actors: ROLE_None turns replication off, ROLE_SimulatedProxy or ROLE_AutonomousProxy turn it on.
setting=dormancy: Use it to set an Actor Blueprint's default network dormancy.
setting=always_relevant: Use it to set always-relevant replication behavior.
setting=only_relevant_to_owner: Use it to set owner-only relevancy behavior.
setting=autonomous_proxy: Use it to make every replicated variable of a Blueprint replicate to the autonomous proxy only (COND_AutonomousOnly), or undo that; fails when it has no replicated variable.
setting=priority: Use it to configure actor network bandwidth priority.
setting=update_frequency: Use it to configure actor network update frequency.
setting=cull_distance: Use it to configure network relevancy cull distance.
setting=push_model: Use it to turn push-model replication on or off for every replicated variable of a Blueprint; fails when it has none.
setting=replicated_movement: Use it to configure replicated movement.
setting=replication_graph: Use it to set an Actor Blueprint's spatially loaded (World Partition) and net load on client defaults; only the fields sent are written.
setting=net_driver: Use it to write the game net driver's rate limits to its class defaults and DefaultEngine.ini, and to the running net driver when there is one; only the fields sent are written.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

propertyName.description: Property name.

condition.description: Replication condition, a ELifetimeCondition name such as COND_OwnerOnly, COND_SkipOwner, COND_InitialOnly or COND_AutonomousOnly; an unknown name is refused.

repNotifyFunc.description: Function clients call when the variable's new value arrives; the variable also becomes replicated. It must take no parameters and return nothing: the Blueprint's own or an inherited one is used, a missing one is created empty (functionCreated), one with parameters or a return value is refused (the compiler drops it), and a name another member holds is NAME_TAKEN.

role.description: How clients see the actor: ROLE_None (not replicated), ROLE_SimulatedProxy or ROLE_AutonomousProxy (replicated). ROLE_Authority is refused: the server always has it.

dormancy.description: Net dormancy, a ENetDormancy name: DORM_Never, DORM_Awake, DORM_DormantAll, DORM_DormantPartial or DORM_Initial; an unknown name is refused.

isAutonomousProxy.description: true: every replicated variable replicates to the autonomous proxy only (COND_AutonomousOnly). false: variables using COND_AutonomousOnly go back to COND_None; other conditions stay.

spatiallyLoaded.description: World Partition: stream the actor in by distance (AActor bIsSpatiallyLoaded).

netLoadOnClient.description: Load the placed actor on clients with the map (AActor bNetLoadOnClient).

maxClientRate.description: Game net driver MaxClientRate (bytes per second per LAN client).

maxInternetClientRate.description: Game net driver MaxInternetClientRate (bytes per second per internet client).

netServerMaxTickRate.description: Game net driver NetServerMaxTickRate (server ticks per second).

dormancy: Set an Actor Blueprint's default network dormancy.

only_relevant_to_owner: Set owner-only relevancy behavior.
autonomous_proxy: Make every replicated variable of a Blueprint replicate to the autonomous proxy only (COND_AutonomousOnly), or undo that; fails when it has no replicated variable.

cull_distance: Configure network relevancy cull distance.

discovery.summary: Blueprint RPCs, chosen by setting. create makes a function graph named functionName (a free name: NAME_TAKEN otherwise) in an Actor or ActorComponent Blueprint (INVALID_TARGET otherwise) whose calls run where rpcType says: Server, Client or NetMulticast. inputs are its parameters ({name, type}); reliable defaults to true. The function body is the graph of that name, built with manage_blueprint edit_graph, and it is called like any function. The Blueprint compiles and saves, and actorReplicates says whether it replicates, without which no RPC leaves the machine. reliability makes an existing RPC (that function, or a custom event set to replicate) reliable or not; a non-replicating one is NOT_AN_RPC. validation true is refused (NOT_SUPPORTED): only C++ RPCs validate, so check the parameters at the start of the body. changed false means the flag already had that value and nothing was compiled or saved.
whenToUse: setting=create: Use it to create a Blueprint RPC: a function graph named functionName whose calls run where rpcType says, with inputs as its parameters. Actor and ActorComponent Blueprints only.
setting=validation: Use it to clear an RPC's validation flag (withValidation false); true is refused, since a Blueprint RPC has no validation step.
setting=reliability: Use it to make an RPC reliable or unreliable.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

functionName.description: The RPC. For setting=create, a new name that no function, variable, event or other member of the Blueprint or its parent class holds (NAME_TAKEN). For validation and reliability, an existing RPC: a function create made, or a custom event set to replicate in the editor (NOT_FOUND, or NOT_AN_RPC for one that does not replicate).

rpcType.description: Where the call runs: Server (called on a client, on an actor its player owns, and run on the server), Client (called on the server, run on the owning player client) or NetMulticast (called on the server, run there and on every client). Multicast is accepted too, in any case; anything else is refused.

reliable.description: Reliable: resent until it arrives, in order. Unreliable calls can be dropped under load, which suits frequent cosmetic updates. Creating defaults to true.

inputs.description: RPC parameters, each {name, type}, with the types add_function inputs take (Float, Vector, Actor, Array<Int> ...), sent with every call. A nameless entry or a type no pin takes is refused (TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED) before anything changes. Default none.

withValidation.description: true is refused (NOT_SUPPORTED): only C++ RPCs have a validation step, so check the parameters at the start of the RPC body instead. false clears a validation flag an earlier call stored (changed says whether one was there).

setting.description:
Which configure rpc variant to run.
create: Create a Blueprint RPC: a function graph named functionName whose calls run where rpcType says, with inputs as its parameters. Actor and ActorComponent Blueprints only.
validation: Clear an RPC's validation flag (withValidation false); true is refused, since a Blueprint RPC has no validation step.
reliability: Make an RPC reliable or unreliable.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

functionName.description: The RPC the call created or changed: its function graph, or the replicated custom event.

rpcType.description: Server, Client or NetMulticast: where the call runs (the server, the owning player client, or the server and every client).

reliable.description: Whether the RPC is reliable: resent until it arrives, in order. An unreliable call can be dropped under load.

compiled.description: Whether the Blueprint compiled cleanly after the change.

saved.description: Whether the asset was saved to disk.

actorReplicates.description: Whether the Blueprint itself replicates (Replicates in its class defaults). Its replicated variables and RPCs reach no other machine until it does; nothing here turns it on.

withValidation.description: The validation flag asked for; only false gets this far, since a Blueprint RPC has no validation step.

changed.description: Whether the call changed anything. false: the flag already had the value asked for, so nothing was compiled or saved.

discovery.summary: Build a PCG graph, chosen by edit. create makes a graph asset and create_subgraph one to run inside another (with parentGraphPath it adds the Subgraph node there too); a graph already at the path is refused unless overwrite is true, which hands back that graph unchanged (created false). connect_pins wires an output pin of one node to an input pin of another (labels default to Out and In; PIN_NOT_FOUND lists the labels). set_node_settings changes an existing node (found by nodeId or nodeName) and refuses an edit that changes nothing. set_partition_grid_size sets the world or one component's generation grid and saves the level unless save is false. Graph edits save the graph unless save is false (saved).
whenToUse: edit=create: Procedural content (scattered rocks, trees, props along splines) needs a graph to build it.
edit=create_subgraph: Steps several PCG graphs share (scatter rules, cleanup) should live in one graph run from each.
edit=connect_pins: Points must flow from one PCG node into the next, such as a sampler into a spawner.
edit=set_node_settings: A PCG node must scatter, filter or spawn differently, such as a denser sampler or another mesh.
edit=set_partition_grid_size: Partitioned PCG makes too many small cells, or cells too large to stream well.
whenNotToUse: edit=connect_pins|set_partition_grid_size: A node is added (add_pcg_node).

edit.description:
Which edit pcg graph variant to run.
create: Create a PCG graph asset at graphPath (or assetPath, or name in path, default /Game/PCG), saved unless save is false. A PCG graph already at the path is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS) unless overwrite is true, which returns that graph unchanged (created false); another kind of asset there is refused. The reply gives graphPath, name, created and saved. Needs the PCG plugin.
create_subgraph: Create a PCG graph at subgraphPath to run inside other graphs (the same rules as edit=create: one already there is refused unless overwrite is true, which reuses it), and with parentGraphPath add a Subgraph node running it to that graph, titled nodeName and placed at x, y. The reply gives subgraphPath, created and saved, and with a parent also parentGraphPath, nodeId (the new node, for edit=connect_pins) and parentSaved. A parent that does not load is ASSET_NOT_FOUND. Saved unless save is false.
connect_pins: Wire sourcePin (or outputName) of sourceNodeId to targetPin (or inputName) of targetNodeId in a PCG graph (graphPath or assetPath). A node is found by its nodeId (object name), its title, its index in the graph, or input and output for the graph's own ends (NODE_NOT_FOUND). A pin left out is the node's Out or In pin, else its first; a label it lacks is PIN_NOT_FOUND listing the labels. An edge already there is kept, not doubled. The reply gives both node ids, both pin labels and saved; saved unless save is false.
set_node_settings: Change a node of a PCG graph, found by nodeId or nodeName (an object name, title, index, or input and output; NODE_NOT_FOUND): settings sets properties by name (INVALID_SETTINGS for one it lacks), texturePath, meshPath and actorClass set the texture, mesh or spawned class of nodes that take them (each checked to load), title renames it and x, y move it. An edit that changes nothing, or sends only a meshPath or class the node has no slot for, is refused. The reply gives nodeId, title, nodeType, settingsApplied and saved; saved unless save is false.
set_partition_grid_size: Set the size of the cells partitioned PCG generates in (gridSize, a whole number of world units above 0): scope world (the default) sets the PCG world actor's partition grid, scope component one PCG component's generation grid (actorName, componentName or componentPath; COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND). The reply gives previousGridSize and gridSize. Saved with the level unless save is false, which saves every unsaved change in that level too.

saved.description: Whether the graph reached disk.

examples.title: Add a pin to a material function (assetPath), chosen by io: input adds a Function Input named inputName of inputType (default Vector3; an unknown type is refused) that callers wire into; output adds a Function Output named inputName that carries out whatever is wired into it, of that type. A name the function already has is NAME_TAKEN. The node lands at x, y (default 0, 0), the function recompiles and is left unsaved; the reply gives its nodeId for connect_nodes.

discovery.summary: Add a node to a material graph: any expression class by name, or a typed node (parameters, texture sample/coordinate, math, noise, panner, rotator, fresnel, switches, custom HLSL, function call, landscape layer), or build a whole graph (nodes, wires, material properties) in one batch.
whenToUse: nodeKind=node: An expression is needed by class name with no dedicated adder, such as Constant, Constant3Vector (with defaultValue), ComponentMask or Saturate.
nodeKind=node: A texture object must feed a Custom node or a material function input (nodeType TextureObjectParameter with name and texturePath).
nodeKind=node: A material must read a value of a Material Parameter Collection (nodeType CollectionParameter with collectionPath and name).
nodeKind=custom_expression: A calculation the standard nodes cannot express is needed as HLSL, with named inputs and optional extra outputs.
nodeKind=fresnel: A rim light, edge glow or view-angle fade is needed.
nodeKind=if: A value must switch by comparing two numbers: A greater than, equal to or less than B.
nodeKind=math: Values must be combined or reshaped: Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, Lerp, Clamp, Power, Frac, OneMinus or Append.
nodeKind=noise: A surface needs procedural variation such as dirt, clouds or breakup, with a scale and a number of octaves (levels).
nodeKind=panner: UVs must scroll over time, as with flowing water or a conveyor belt.
nodeKind=pixel_depth: Distance from the camera per pixel is needed, for depth fades or distance-based blending.
nodeKind=reflection_vector: A reflection direction is needed, for example to sample a cubemap for fake reflections.
nodeKind=rotator: UVs must rotate over time, as with spinning dials or radial effects.
nodeKind=scalar_parameter: A float value must be tweakable per material instance, such as roughness, opacity or a speed.
nodeKind=static_switch_parameter: A compile-time on/off toggle must pick between two graph branches for each instance.
nodeKind=switch: A compile-time two-way branch is needed with no named parameter, chosen by a bool input or the node default.
nodeKind=texture_coordinate: A texture must repeat more or less often across a surface, or read a UV channel other than 0.
nodeKind=texture_sample: A texture must be sampled in the graph; pass parameterName to make it a texture parameter that instances can override.
nodeKind=vector_parameter: A color or vector value must be tweakable per instance, such as a tint or an emissive color.
nodeKind=vertex_normal: The world-space vertex normal is needed, for example for slope-based blending.
nodeKind=voronoi: A cell, crack or cobble-like pattern is needed from a Voronoi noise function; scale is its only setting.
nodeKind=world_position: The world position of each pixel is needed, for world-aligned textures or height-based blending.
nodeKind=material_function: A reusable material function must be called from a material or another function as a single node.
nodeKind=landscape_layer: A landscape weight layer needs its layer info asset, with hardness, physical material and weight-blend option, so it can be painted.
nodeKind=batch: Many nodes, wires and material properties must be built at once, with the material compiled and saved only at the end.
nodeKind=batch: New nodes must be wired to each other in the same call by id ($id) without waiting for node ids.
whenNotToUse: nodeKind=node: The node already exists and only needs wiring or moving (use material.connect_nodes or material.set_node_position).
nodeKind=custom_expression: The code or inputs of an existing Custom node must change (use material.update_custom_expression).
nodeKind=fresnel: The Fresnel node already exists and only needs wiring (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=if: A per-instance toggle is wanted (add a static switch parameter, then use material.set_material_parameter with parameterKind=static_switch).
nodeKind=math: A math node already exists and only needs new wires (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=noise: A noise texture asset is wanted instead of a per-pixel node (use texture.create_texture with kind=noise).
nodeKind=panner: The panner exists and only its wiring or position changes (use material.connect_nodes or material.set_node_position).
nodeKind=pixel_depth: A pixel depth node exists and only needs wiring (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=reflection_vector: The reflection vector node exists and only needs wiring (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=rotator: The rotator exists and only needs wiring (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=scalar_parameter: An existing scalar parameter value must change (use material.set_material_parameter with parameterKind=scalar).
nodeKind=static_switch_parameter: The value of an existing switch must change on an instance (use material.set_material_parameter with parameterKind=static_switch).
nodeKind=switch: The choice must change per instance (use a static switch parameter, set with material.set_material_parameter and parameterKind=static_switch).
nodeKind=texture_coordinate: The UV node exists and only needs wiring (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=texture_sample: An instance only needs a different texture (use material.set_material_parameter with parameterKind=texture).
nodeKind=texture_sample: The texture asset itself must be made, adjusted or configured (use texture.create_texture, texture.adjust_texture or texture.configure_texture).
nodeKind=vector_parameter: An existing vector parameter value must change (use material.set_material_parameter with parameterKind=vector).
nodeKind=vertex_normal: A normal map should shade the surface: wire a texture sample into Normal (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=voronoi: The Voronoi node exists and only needs wiring (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=world_position: The world position node exists and only needs wiring (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=material_function: The function does not exist yet (use material.create_material with kind=function).
nodeKind=material_function: The function needs another input or output pin (use material.add_function_io).
nodeKind=landscape_layer: The material needs a layer blend node that lists the layers (use material.configure_layer_blend).
nodeKind=landscape_layer: The landscape must be painted with the layer (use build_environment.edit_landscape with edit=paint_landscape_layer).
nodeKind=batch: Only one wire is needed (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=batch: Nodes must be deleted or unwired; batches do not run those (use material.delete_node or material.disconnect_nodes).

nodeType.description: Material expression to add: its class name without the MaterialExpression prefix (Constant, Lerp, TextureSample, ScalarParameter, Multiply...) or the full class name; Float, Color, TexCoord and StaticSwitch are accepted as short names. An unknown type adds nothing (UNKNOWN_TYPE).

name.description: Parameter name, when the node type is a parameter of any kind (scalar, vector, static switch, TextureObjectParameter, TextureSampleParameter2D), or the parameter of collectionPath a CollectionParameter node reads.

collectionPath.description: Material Parameter Collection a CollectionParameter node reads (name picks its parameter); a collection that does not load, or lacks the parameter, adds nothing and fails, listing its parameters.

texturePath.description: Texture for a texture node (TextureObjectParameter, TextureSample...): its default, with the sampler type set to match (a normal map samples as Normal). A path that does not load adds nothing and fails.

defaultValue.description: Initial value for a Constant (number) or Constant3Vector (rgb array or {r,g,b}) node.

x.description: Node X position (preferred spelling; posX is the fallback).

y.description: Node Y position (preferred spelling; posY is the fallback).

outputType.description: Output type: Float1 (default), Float2, Float3, Float4 or MaterialAttributes.

description.description: Node title shown in the material editor (the Custom node Description).

inputs.description: Input definitions, each {name}; wire one with connect_nodes targetPin set to that name.

additionalOutputs.description: Extra output pins after the return value, each {name, type}: type Float1 (default), Float2, Float3, Float4 or MaterialAttributes. Assign each by name in the HLSL (Emis = ...;) and wire it as "$node.Name".

constA.description: Value used while input A is unwired (Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, Lerp).

constB.description: Value used while input B is unwired (Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, Lerp).

path.description: Folder for the layer info asset, e.g. /Game/Landscape/Layers (overrides the material folder).

physicalMaterialPath.description: Physical material the layer applies, e.g. /Game/Physics/PM_Grass.

noWeightBlend.description: Exclude the layer from weight blending (default false).

save.description: Save the asset afterwards. Defaults to true; pass false to keep the change in memory only.

operations.description: Steps run in order, 1-200. Each is {edit, ...the params of that edit}: edit is a node adder (add_material_node, add_scalar_parameter, add_vector_parameter, add_texture_sample, add_texture_coordinate, add_math_node, add_noise, add_custom_expression, ...; or add_material_node with nodeKind, as in the single call: {"edit": "add_material_node", "nodeKind": "world_position"}), use_material_function, connect_nodes, set_node_position, update_custom_expression, set_blend_mode, set_shading_model, set_material_domain or set_two_sided. Optional per step: id (names the created node; later steps use "$id" in sourceNodeId/targetNodeId/nodeId), from/to ("$id.Pin" shorthand for connect_nodes, where a source pin may be channel letters like "$uv.G"; "Main.EmissiveColor" is the material output). A created node without x/y is laid out automatically. Deleting and disconnecting are not batched. Every edit and "$id" is checked before any step runs, so a misspelled one refuses the batch with nothing applied (problems lists each); a step that fails when it runs stops the batch with the steps before it applied (their node ids are in nodeIds). When every step ran, the material is compiled and saved once.

dryRun.description: Check the batch without running a step (default false): every edit and "$id", with every problem in one reply. Node names, pins and values are checked only when it runs. Nothing is changed, compiled or saved.

nodeKind.description:
Which add material node variant to run; omit for 'node'.
node: Add a generic material node by type.
custom_expression: Add a custom HLSL expression node to a material graph.
fresnel: Add a fresnel node to a material graph.
if: Add a conditional If node to a material graph.
math: Add a math operation node to a material graph.
noise: Add a noise node to a material graph.
panner: Add a panner node to a material graph.
pixel_depth: Add a pixel depth node to a material graph.
reflection_vector: Add a reflection vector node to a material graph.
rotator: Add a rotator node to a material graph.
scalar_parameter: Add a scalar parameter node to a material graph.
static_switch_parameter: Add a static switch parameter node to a material graph.
switch: Add a switch node to a material graph.
texture_coordinate: Add a texture coordinate node to a material graph.
texture_sample: Add a texture sample node to a material graph.
vector_parameter: Add a vector parameter node to a material graph.
vertex_normal: Add a vertex normal node to a material graph.
voronoi: Add a voronoi noise node to a material graph.
world_position: Add a world position node to a material graph.
material_function: Insert a material function reference into a material graph.
landscape_layer: Create the landscape layer info asset (the weight layer a landscape material paints) for a layer name, beside the material or in path.

details.description: Operation details.

nodeId.description: Created node ID.

posX.description: X coordinate the node was placed at.

posY.description: Y coordinate the node was placed at.

estimatedWidth.description: Approximate node width; an estimate from the node name, not a measurement.

estimatedHeight.description: Approximate node height, from connector count plus an allowance for a parameter node's inline default-value widget. Offset the next node by at least this much to avoid overlap.

overlappingNodes.description: Names of existing expressions whose estimated bounds intersect this one. Absent when placement is clear.

placementWarning.description: Human-readable overlap warning, present only when overlappingNodes is non-empty.

assetPath.description: The material the batch edited, compiled and saved.

results.description: Per-step outcome: index, edit, id, success, nodeId, placementWarning, error. A step that ran and has nothing more to say (a plain connect_nodes) is counted in succeeded, not listed; a failed batch lists every step.

nodeIds.description: Step id -> node id for every node the batch created.

failedIndex.description: Index of the step that stopped the batch (failures only).

compiled.description: False when the material does not compile after the batch; compileErrors says why.

compileErrors.description: Compile errors after the batch, empty when the material compiles.

saved.description: Whether the material was saved after the batch.

dryRun.description: True when nothing ran (dryRun).

wouldCreate.description: dryRun: the nodes the batch would create.

problems.description: Every step the check refused, each with index, edit, errorCode and error; nothing was applied.

examples.title: Add a node to a material graph: any expression class by name, or a typed node (parameters, texture sample/coordinate, math, noise, panner, rotator, fresnel, switches, custom HLSL, function call, landscape layer), or build a whole graph (nodes, wires, material properties) in one batch.

discovery.summary: Recompile a material or material function from its graph (compileOp compile, the default; rebuild runs the same recompile) and wait for every shader. A material that does not compile answers compiled false with compileErrors, since it renders as the default material until fixed; saved says whether it was written (save, default true). A material function is updated without the shader check.
whenToUse: compileOp=compile: The compile errors of an edited graph must be read; a material that fails to compile renders as the default material.
compileOp=compile: Graph edits left the asset unsaved, so it must be compiled and saved.
compileOp=rebuild: The shader must be regenerated after graph edits; the compile, error check and save are identical to a plain compile.
whenNotToUse: A property or parameter was just set (material.set_material_property and material.set_material_parameter already recompile).
compileOp=compile: Domain, blend mode or node counts are wanted rather than compile errors (use material.get_material_info).

materialPath.description: Material asset path (accepted in place of assetPath).

save.description: Save the asset afterwards. Defaults to true; pass false to keep the change in memory only.

compileOp.description:
Which compile material variant to run; omit for 'compile'.
compile: Compile a material and report its compile errors.
rebuild: Rebuild and compile a material (alias of compileOp=compile).

compiled.description: False when the material does not compile; compileErrors says why.

compileErrors.description: Compile errors from the material translator and, once it has finished, the shader compile (where a Custom node's HLSL fails); empty when it compiles.

saved.description: Whether the asset was saved.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Recompile a material or material function from its graph (compileOp compile, the default; rebuild runs the same recompile) and wait for every shader. A material that does not compile answers compiled false with compileErrors, since it renders as the default material until fixed; saved says whether it was written (save, default true). A material function is updated without the shader check.

discovery.summary: Add a Landscape Layer Blend node to a landscape material, listing the paint layers in order (layers; the first previews at full weight), each with its blend: weight, height or alpha. Every call adds a new node, at x, y (default 0, 0); wire its output with connect_nodes (blendNodeId). An unknown blend type is refused. The material recompiles and is saved unless save is false (saved).
whenToUse: A landscape material needs a Landscape Layer Blend node listing its paint layers, each with a weight, height or alpha blend.
All named layers must be added to one blend node in one call (layers takes [{name, blendType}] or plain names).
whenNotToUse: Layer info assets for the layers must be created (use material.add_material_node with nodeKind=landscape_layer).
A finished material must be assigned to a landscape (use build_environment.sculpt with sculptOp=material).

layers.description: The paint layers, in order, each { name } or { name, blendType } to give that layer its own blend.

blendType.description: Blend for the layers that do not name one: LB_WeightBlend (default), LB_HeightBlend or LB_AlphaBlend (Weight, Height or Alpha work too).

x.description: Node X position of the layer blend node.

y.description: Node Y position of the layer blend node.

save.description: Save the asset afterwards. Defaults to true; pass false to keep the change in memory only.

details.description: Operation details.

discovery.summary: Wire an output of sourceNodeId (sourcePin: a name, an index or channel letters such as G or RG; default its first output) into targetPin of targetNodeId, replacing whatever fed that input. targetNodeId Main is the material output (BaseColor, Roughness, Normal, EmissiveColor...), or in a material function its output named targetPin (the first when left out). The material recompiles and is left unsaved (save_all keeps it). NODE_NOT_FOUND names Main when the target id is missing; INVALID_PIN or PIN_NOT_FOUND lists the inputs the node has.
whenToUse: The output of one material node must feed an input of another node in the same material or function.
A node result must drive a material output such as BaseColor or Roughness (targetNodeId Main).
whenNotToUse: A whole graph of nodes and wires is being built (use material.add_material_node with nodeKind=batch).
A wire must be removed (use material.disconnect_nodes).

assetPath.description: Material asset path (accepted in place of materialPath).

sourcePin.description: Source output: its name, its index, or channel letters of the default output ("G", "RG"; X/Y/Z/W work too). Omit for the default output.

targetPin.description: Target pin name. On the material output (targetNodeId Main): BaseColor, Metallic, Specular, Roughness, Anisotropy, EmissiveColor, Opacity, OpacityMask, Normal, Tangent, WorldPositionOffset, SubsurfaceColor, ClearCoat, ClearCoatRoughness, AmbientOcclusion, Refraction, PixelDepthOffset (and SurfaceThickness, Displacement on newer engines); a Cloth material's Cloth and FuzzColor, and CustomData0/CustomData1, name the clear-coat and subsurface pins they share.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Wire an output of sourceNodeId (sourcePin: a name, an index or channel letters such as G or RG; default its first output) into targetPin of targetNodeId, replacing whatever fed that input. targetNodeId Main is the material output (BaseColor, Roughness, Normal, EmissiveColor...), or in a material function its output named targetPin (the first when left out). The material recompiles and is left unsaved (save_all keeps it). NODE_NOT_FOUND names Main when the target id is missing; INVALID_PIN or PIN_NOT_FOUND lists the inputs the node has.

discovery.summary: Create a material asset: a standard material, a decal, landscape or post-process material, a material function, or a Material Parameter Collection (values every material reading it shares).
whenToUse: kind=material: A mesh, surface or effect needs a shader of its own and no material asset exists for it yet.
kind=material: A translucent, unlit or two-sided material is wanted from the start (materialDomain, blendMode, shadingModel, twoSided).
kind=decal: A material is needed to project onto surfaces as a deferred decal, such as scorch marks or stains.
kind=landscape: A material is being made for a landscape; it starts empty (Surface domain, Opaque) and its layers are added afterwards.
kind=post_process: A full-screen effect such as a vignette or color grade needs a post-process domain material.
kind=function: A chunk of graph logic must be reused by several materials as one node, listed in the function library unless exposeToLibrary is false.

kind=parameter_collection: One value must drive many materials at once, set once at runtime (a level-wide wetness, wind strength, time of day or flash): a material reads it with a CollectionParameter node (material.add_material_node nodeType CollectionParameter with collectionPath and name), and a Blueprint sets it with SetScalarParameterValue or SetVectorParameterValue of the Kismet Material Library, the collection on its Collection pin.
kind=parameter_collection: An existing collection needs another parameter or new defaults: send it again; parameters are never removed, since materials read them by id.
whenNotToUse: kind=material: A variation of an existing material with different parameter values is wanted (use material.create_material_instance).
kind=material: An existing material must be copied as it is (use asset.duplicate).
kind=decal: A decal material already exists and only its blend mode must change (use material.set_material_property).
kind=landscape: The material exists and only needs assigning to a landscape (use build_environment.sculpt with sculptOp=material).
kind=post_process: A built-in post-process setting such as bloom or exposure is enough (use build_environment.configure_post_process).
kind=function: The logic is used by one material only (build it in that material with material.add_material_node).
kind=parameter_collection: The value differs per object (use a material instance and material.set_material_parameter, or a dynamic material instance per actor).

name.description: Asset name.

path.description: Package path.

materialDomain.description: Material domain: Surface, DeferredDecal, LightFunction, Volume, PostProcess or UI (a widget, brush or font material). The Details panel label (User Interface) and the MD_ name work too.

blendMode.description: Blend mode, such as Opaque, Masked, Translucent, Additive, Modulate or AlphaComposite. The Details panel label and the BLEND_ name work too.

shadingModel.description: Shading model, such as DefaultLit, Unlit, Subsurface, ClearCoat or TwoSidedFoliage. The Details panel label and the MSM_ name work too.

save.description: Save the asset afterwards. Defaults to true; pass false to keep it in memory only.

exposeToLibrary.description: Expose in the material function library.

scalars.description: Scalar parameters, each {name, default}: a name the collection lacks is added, one it has takes the new default (0 when a new one gives none).

vectors.description: Vector parameters, each {name, default}: default as [r, g, b, a] or {r, g, b, a} (alpha 1 when omitted); a name the collection lacks is added, one it has takes the new default.

kind.description:
Which create material variant to run; omit for 'material'.
material: Create a new material asset.
decal: Create a decal material asset (DeferredDecal domain, Translucent by default).
landscape: Create a landscape material asset (Surface domain, Opaque by default).
post_process: Create a post-process material asset (PostProcess domain by default).
function: Create a new material function asset.
parameter_collection: Create a Material Parameter Collection, values every material that reads it shares, or add parameters to one and set their defaults.

details.description: Operation details.

created.description: kind=parameter_collection: true when the call made the collection, false when it updated one.

added.description: kind=parameter_collection: the parameters this call added.

scalars.description: kind=parameter_collection: every scalar parameter of the collection after the call, {name, default}.

vectors.description: kind=parameter_collection: every vector parameter after the call, {name, default [r, g, b, a]}.

saved.description: kind=parameter_collection: whether the collection reached disk.

discovery.summary: Create a material instance from a parent material or another instance (a child instance), optionally with its parameter values already set, or several instances (a palette) under one consent.
whenToUse: A variation of a base material is needed with new parameter values and no second node graph.
An instance should start with scalar, vector or texture overrides already applied (pass parameters).
A palette of instances of one parent must be made at once (instances), under one consent instead of one per instance.
whenNotToUse: The material needs its own node graph (use material.create_material).
An existing instance needs new values (use material.set_material_parameter); the parent must be a base material, not another instance.

name.description: Instance name.

parentMaterial.description: The parent, as a /Game path: a Material, or another Material Instance for a child instance.

parameters.description: Several parameter values at once, each {parameterName, parameterType (scalar | vector | texture), value, or texturePath for a texture}; applied counts those that took, and an entry that did not is listed under parameters with why and fails the call.

save.description: Save the asset afterwards. Defaults to true; pass false to keep it in memory only.

instances.description: Several instances in one call, in place of name: each {name, and any of parentMaterial, savePath, parameters, save}; the call's own parentMaterial, savePath and save are every entry's defaults. Every entry is reported under instances; the call fails naming any that were not created.

details.description: Operation details.

instances.description: With instances: one entry per instance in order: name, success, error and errorCode when it failed, and what a single create reports (assetPath, parameters).

created.description: With instances: how many were created.
