Make a palette of instances under one consent

discovery.summary: Delete nodes from a material or material function graph: nodeId, or nodeIds for several. Every wire to a deleted node is cut, the material outputs it fed included, so what it fed falls back to its default; the material is then recompiled and saved unless save is false. Ids that match nothing come back in notFound, and NOT_FOUND answers only when none matched (read the ids with get_material_info or find_node).
whenToUse: An unused or wrong node must leave a material or function graph, taking its wires with it.
Several stray nodes must go in one call (nodeIds).
whenNotToUse: Only the wire to a node must be cleared while the node stays (use material.disconnect_nodes).
Unused nodes must be found first (use material.get_material_info with info=subgraph and orphansOnly=true).

materialPath.description: The material or material function /Game path.

nodeId.description: Node ID to delete.

nodeIds.description: Node IDs to delete in one batch, in place of nodeId.

save.description: Save the asset afterwards. Defaults to true; pass false to keep the change in memory only.

notFound.description: Ids that matched no node; the call still succeeds while one matched.

saved.description: Whether the material was saved.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Delete nodes from a material or material function graph: nodeId, or nodeIds for several. Every wire to a deleted node is cut, the material outputs it fed included, so what it fed falls back to its default; the material is then recompiled and saved unless save is false. Ids that match nothing come back in notFound, and NOT_FOUND answers only when none matched (read the ids with get_material_info or find_node).

discovery.summary: Unplug the wire into pinName of nodeId (or with nodeId Main a material output such as BaseColor), keeping both nodes; the input falls back to its default. A pin name that matches none fails listing the inputs; a material function output node with no pinName unplugs every output. The material recompiles and is left unsaved (save_all keeps it).
whenToUse: The wire into one input pin of a node must be cleared while both nodes stay.
A material output such as BaseColor must be unplugged (nodeId Main with pinName BaseColor).
whenNotToUse: A node is no longer needed (use material.delete_node, which also clears every wire that used it).
A pin must take a different source (use material.connect_nodes, which replaces the current wire).

assetPath.description: Material asset path (accepted in place of materialPath).

nodeId.description: Node ID.

pinName.description: Input to unplug: a pin of nodeId by name or label (a custom node input such as OB), or for nodeId Main a material output input (BaseColor, Normal...). A name that matches none fails listing the inputs; only a material function's output node takes none, unplugging every output.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Unplug the wire into pinName of nodeId (or with nodeId Main a material output such as BaseColor), keeping both nodes; the input falls back to its default. A pin name that matches none fails listing the inputs; a material function output node with no pinName unplugs every output. The material recompiles and is left unsaved (save_all keeps it).

discovery.summary: Inspect a material or material function: summary with its parameters and overrides, node lookup, node details/properties/connections, node chains and connected subgraphs.
whenToUse: info=material: An existing material must be understood before editing: node ids, parameter names, wiring, domain and blend mode, or the parent and overrides of an instance.
info=function: A material function must be understood before calling or editing it: its inputs, outputs, description and library exposure.
info=find_node: A node id is unknown and the node must be found by expression class, parameter name, function pin name or Custom node title.
info=node_details|node_properties: The settings of one node must be read back, such as a scalar or vector parameter default or a function input or output pin.
info=node_connections|node_chain: The wiring of a node must be traced across the graph, for example to see where its result ends up at the material output.
info=subgraph: Nodes not wired to any output (orphans) must be found, or the connected island around one node listed.
whenNotToUse: info=material: Shading model, sampler counts or the instances of a parent are wanted (use asset.query_asset lookup=material_stats or asset.list kind=material_instances).
info=function: The materials that call the function must be found (use asset.inspect_asset with lookup=dependencies and referencers=true).
info=find_node: The material asset itself must be located by name or class (use asset.query_asset).
info=node_details|node_properties: A parameter value or Custom node code must change, not be read (use material.set_material_parameter or material.update_custom_expression).

info=node_details|node_properties: Any other property of a node must change, such as the Texture or SamplerType of a texture parameter (use inspect.set_property with objectPath "<material path>.<material name>:<nodeId>").
info=node_connections|node_chain: A wire must be added, cut or rerouted, not traced (use material.connect_nodes or material.disconnect_nodes).
info=subgraph: Orphaned nodes are to be removed (use material.delete_node once their ids are known).

materialPath.description: Material asset path (accepted in place of assetPath).

filter.description: Which sections to return: parameters, expressions, connections, or all (default).

nodeId.description: A node, by the id the graph lists: material and function report only the connections touching it; node_details, node_properties and node_connections describe it; node_chain and subgraph start from it (node_chain also takes it as startNodeId; subgraph needs it unless orphansOnly is true).

nodeIds.description: Only report connections touching these nodes.

nodeName.description: Name to find: a node id, parameter name, function input or output name, or custom node title (substring match).

expressionIndex.description: Zero-based position in the expression list; picks the node when nodeId is omitted.

direction.description: Connection direction to report (inputs or outputs).

depth.description: Traversal depth; -1 walks the whole graph.

upstream.description: Walk every upstream producer, overriding direction and depth.

downstream.description: Report downstream connections instead of upstream.

startNodeId.description: Starting node ID accepted by the handler in place of nodeId.

endPin.description: Terminal pin name to stop the chain walk at.

orphansOnly.description: Report only the nodes whose result reaches no output of the material or function: nothing wired to them, or a branch that ends in a node nothing reads (left behind when the node it fed was rewired). Accepted in place of nodeId.

info.description:
Which get material info variant to run; omit for 'material'.
material: Read a material or material function (domain, blend mode, parameters, node count), or a material instance (its parent and parameter overrides).
function: Retrieve information about a material function.
find_node: Find a node in a material graph by type or name.
node_details: Retrieve details of a material node.
node_properties: Retrieve properties of a node in a material graph.
node_connections: Retrieve connections for a node in a material graph.
node_chain: Retrieve the chain of nodes connected to a starting node.
subgraph: Retrieve the connected subgraph from a starting node.

assetType.description: Asset type: Material, MaterialFunction or MaterialInstance.

parent.description: MaterialInstance: the material or instance it overrides.

baseMaterial.description: MaterialInstance: the material at the root of its parent chain, which owns the node graph.

parameterOverrides.description: MaterialInstance: each overridden parameter (name, type scalar/vector/texture, value).

nodeCount.description: Number of expression nodes in the graph.

domain.description: Material domain, e.g. Surface, PostProcess, UI.

blendMode.description: Blend mode, e.g. Opaque, Masked, Translucent.

exposeToLibrary.description: Whether a material function is exposed to the library.

parameters.description: Material parameters of every kind (name, type, nodeId). A texture parameter also carries texture (its default texture path, empty while none is set) and samplerType (Color, Normal, Masks, ...); a runtime virtual texture parameter carries its virtual texture under texture.

details.description: Operation details.

nodeId.description: Resolved node ID.

vectorDefault.description: DefaultValue as rgba, for vector parameter expressions.

inputName.description: Pin name, for a function input.

inputType.description: Pin type, for a function input.

outputName.description: Pin name, for a function output.

sortPriority.description: Pin sort priority, for function input/output expressions.

usePreviewValueAsDefault.description: Whether a function input previews its default.

type.description: Expression class name of the start node.

connections.description: Edges found, each with sourceNodeId, sourceOutputIndex, targetNodeId, targetInput, hop and direction. A targetNodeId of "Main" is the material output node.

examples.title: Inspect a material or material function: summary with its parameters and overrides, node lookup, node details/properties/connections, node chains and connected subgraphs.

discovery.summary: Set material parameter values, chosen by parameterKind. On a material instance it overrides a parameter its parent publishes (a name it does not publish is PARAMETER_NOT_FOUND, listing the published ones); on a base material it sets the parameter node's default, refused while the material is open in its editor (ASSET_EDITOR_OPEN; the editor would write its own copy back on close). scalar takes a number value, vector value {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a], texture texturePath, static_switch value true or false, and a missing value is refused; parameter takes parameterType (scalar, the default, vector or texture) with value, several at once with parameters, or several instances under one consent with assets. The asset is saved unless save is false (saved).
whenToUse: parameterKind=parameter: Several parameter values on a base material or an instance must change in one call (parameters list).
parameterKind=parameter: Several material instances must be retuned at once, a palette recoloured (assets), under one consent instead of one per instance.
parameterKind=parameter: The default of a parameter node on a base material must change; on an instance the value is stored as an override.
parameterKind=scalar: A float parameter such as roughness, opacity or a speed must change on an instance or as a base material default.
parameterKind=vector: A color or vector parameter such as a tint must change; value takes an rgba object or an array of at least three numbers.
parameterKind=texture: A texture parameter must point at a different texture asset (texturePath).
parameterKind=static_switch: A static switch parameter must be turned on or off; on an instance this rebuilds the shader permutation.
whenNotToUse: The parameter is not on the base material yet (add it there with asset.edit_material_instance edit=add_parameter or material.add_material_node).
parameterKind=parameter: Every override on an instance must be cleared back to its parent (use asset.edit_material_instance edit=reset_parameters).
parameterKind=texture: The texture asset itself needs other compression or LOD settings (use texture.configure_texture).

parameterType.description: Parameter kind: scalar (default), vector, or texture. Selects which parameter expression the value is written to.

value.description: Parameter value.

parameters.description: Several parameter values at once, each {parameterName, parameterType (scalar | vector | texture), value, or texturePath for a texture}; applied counts those that took, and an entry that did not is listed under parameters with why and fails the call.

assets.description: Several materials or material instances at once, in place of assetPath: each {assetPath, and parameters or parameterName with value}; the call's own save applies to every entry. Every entry is reported under assets, and the call fails naming any that did not apply.

save.description: Save the asset afterwards. Defaults to true; pass false to keep the change in memory only.

parameterKind.description:
Which set material parameter variant to run; omit for 'parameter'.
parameter: Set a material parameter value by parameterType: scalar (the default) takes a number value, vector {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a], texture a texturePath (or the path in value); a missing value is refused. parameters sets several on one asset, assets several material instances under one consent, each entry checked on its own (the reply lists the ones that failed). On a material instance an override of its parent (a name the parent does not publish is PARAMETER_NOT_FOUND, listing those it does), on a base material the parameter node's default (refused while the material is open in its editor). Saved unless save is false (saved).
scalar: Set a scalar parameter to value (a number): on a material instance an override of its parent (a name the parent does not publish is PARAMETER_NOT_FOUND, listing those it does), on a base material the parameter node's default (refused while the material is open in its editor). Saved unless save is false (saved).
vector: Set a vector (colour) parameter to value, {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a]: on a material instance an override of its parent (a name the parent does not publish is PARAMETER_NOT_FOUND, listing those it does), on a base material the parameter node's default (refused while the material is open in its editor). Saved unless save is false (saved).
texture: Set a texture parameter to the texture at texturePath: on a material instance an override of its parent (a name the parent does not publish is PARAMETER_NOT_FOUND, listing those it does), on a base material the parameter node's default (refused while the material is open in its editor). Saved unless save is false (saved).
static_switch: Turn a static switch parameter on or off (value true or false; an instance rebuilds its shader permutation): on a material instance an override of its parent (a name the parent does not publish is PARAMETER_NOT_FOUND, listing those it does), on a base material the parameter node's default (refused while the material is open in its editor). Saved unless save is false (saved).

details.description: Operation details.

The asset is saved unless save is false (saved).

discovery.summary: Set a property of a material, or override it on a material instance, by materialProperty: blend_mode, domain, shading_model or two_sided. The material recompiles and is saved unless save is false (saved), and the reply gives the value written; on an instance the value becomes an override of its parent, as its Material Property Overrides do (instanceOverride), and the domain cannot be overridden (MATERIAL_INSTANCE). An unknown value is INVALID_ENUM, listing the valid ones, and leaves the asset as it was; a material function is UNSUPPORTED_ASSET_TYPE; engine content is refused (ENGINE_CONTENT), so duplicate it into /Game first.
whenToUse: materialProperty=blend_mode: A material must become translucent, cut out (Masked) or additive instead of Opaque.
materialProperty=domain: A material must change domain, for example between Surface, DeferredDecal, PostProcess and UI.
materialProperty=shading_model: A surface needs a different shading model, such as DefaultLit, Unlit, Subsurface, ClearCoat or Hair.
materialProperty=two_sided: Both faces of a mesh must render, as with leaves, cloth or thin sheets.
whenNotToUse: materialProperty=blend_mode|shading_model|two_sided: Only a parameter of a material instance must change (use material.set_material_parameter).
materialProperty=blend_mode: A new material is being created with the blend mode already known (use material.create_material with blendMode).
materialProperty=domain: The target is a material instance: the domain belongs to its parent material (find it with material.get_material_info).
materialProperty=domain: A new material is being created with the domain already known (use material.create_material with materialDomain).
materialProperty=shading_model: A new material is being created with the shading model already known (use material.create_material with shadingModel).

assetPath.description: Material or material instance /Game asset path; an instance takes the value as an override of its parent (every property but the domain).

blendMode.description: Blend mode, such as Opaque, Masked, Translucent, Additive, Modulate or AlphaComposite. The Details panel label and the BLEND_ name work too.

save.description: Save the asset afterwards. Defaults to true; pass false to keep the change in memory only.

materialDomain.description: Material domain: Surface, DeferredDecal, LightFunction, Volume, PostProcess or UI (a widget, brush or font material). The Details panel label (User Interface) and the MD_ name work too.

shadingModel.description: Shading model, such as DefaultLit, Unlit, Subsurface, ClearCoat or TwoSidedFoliage. The Details panel label and the MSM_ name work too.

value.description: Two-sided value: true renders both faces, false only the front.

materialProperty.description:
Which set material property variant to run.
blend_mode: Set the blend mode of a material.
domain: Set the material domain of a material.
shading_model: Set the shading model of a material.
two_sided: Set the two-sided flag on a material.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Set a property of a material, or override it on a material instance, by materialProperty: blend_mode, domain, shading_model or two_sided. The material recompiles and is saved unless save is false (saved), and the reply gives the value written; on an instance the value becomes an override of its parent, as its Material Property Overrides do (instanceOverride), and the domain cannot be overridden (MATERIAL_INSTANCE). An unknown value is INVALID_ENUM, listing the valid ones, and leaves the asset as it was; a material function is UNSUPPORTED_ASSET_TYPE; engine content is refused (ENGINE_CONTENT), so duplicate it into /Game first.

discovery.summary: Move a node of a material or material function graph (materialPath or assetPath; nodeId as add_material_node and get_material_info give it) to x and y, keeping every wire. The move is one undo step (the reply's undo block says so); the material recompiles and is left unsaved; the reply gives where the node now sits and warns when it overlaps another.
whenToUse: Overlapping nodes reported by a node add (overlappingNodes) must be spread out without losing wires.
A cluttered graph must be tidied by moving an existing node to new x and y.
whenNotToUse: A new node needs a position (pass x and y when adding it with material.add_material_node).
Wires must change (use material.connect_nodes or material.disconnect_nodes).

assetPath.description: Material asset path (accepted in place of materialPath).

nodeId.description: Node ID to move.

x.description: New X coordinate (posX is the fallback spelling).

y.description: New Y coordinate (posY is the fallback spelling).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

nodeId.description: Moved node ID.

posX.description: X coordinate the node now sits at.

posY.description: Y coordinate the node now sits at.

estimatedWidth.description: Approximate node width; an estimate, not a measurement.

estimatedHeight.description: Approximate node height from connector count plus the inline default-value widget allowance.

overlappingNodes.description: Names of expressions still overlapping after the move. Absent when the placement is clear.

placementWarning.description: Human-readable overlap warning, present only when overlappingNodes is non-empty.

examples.title: Space a stacked parameter node out

discovery.summary: Update a custom expression node: its HLSL code, inputs, output type, additional outputs or title. An input that keeps its name keeps its wire. The material is then compiled and saved, and compiled, compileErrors and saved in the reply say how that went (a step of build_material_graph leaves both to the batch).
whenToUse: The HLSL code of an existing Custom node must be rewritten without rebuilding its wiring.
Inputs, output type, extra outputs or the title of a Custom node must change; inputs that keep their name keep their wire.
whenNotToUse: A new Custom node is needed (use material.add_material_node with nodeKind=custom_expression).
The node is a parameter or any other non-Custom expression; only Custom nodes are accepted (parameter values use material.set_material_parameter).

nodeId.description: Node ID.

inputs.description: Replacement input list, each {name}; inputs whose names stay keep their connections.

outputType.description: Output type: Float1, Float2, Float3, Float4 or MaterialAttributes.

description.description: Node title shown in the material editor.

additionalOutputs.description: Extra output pins after the return value, each {name, type}: type Float1 (default), Float2, Float3, Float4 or MaterialAttributes. Assign each by name in the HLSL (Emis = ...;) and wire it as "$node.Name".

compiled.description: False when the material does not compile after the edit (the default material renders in its place); compileErrors says why. A material function has no translation of its own to read, so this is true for one.

compileErrors.description: Compile errors after the edit, from the material translator and, once it has finished, the shader compile (where a Custom node's HLSL fails); empty when it compiles.

saved.description: Whether the material or function was saved after the edit.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Rewrite a custom node's HLSL

discovery.summary: Add a cinematic track: camera cut, camera shake, transform, property, skeletal animation, material parameter, particle, event, fade, level visibility, shot, or subsequence.
whenToUse: trackKind=camera_cut: A camera cut track must be added for shot transitions.
trackKind=camera_shake: Camera shake must be animated along the sequence.
trackKind=transform: Add a transform track to animate actor transforms during cinematic.
trackKind=property: Add a property track to animate a specific property on a bound actor.

trackKind=skeletal_animation: Add a skeletal animation track to play animations on a skeletal mesh. A clip whose skeleton the mesh cannot play is refused with SKELETON_MISMATCH instead of silently showing the rest pose. Overlap the clips before and after it and give easeInFrames/easeOutFrames to crossfade between them instead of cutting in one frame.
trackKind=material_parameter: Add a material parameter collection track to animate material parameters.
trackKind=particle: Add a particle track to trigger particle systems during cinematic: trigger fires a one-shot burst (a hit, a spark) once, activate keeps a system running for the section.
trackKind=event: Add an event track to trigger events at specific frames.
trackKind=fade: Add a fade track for cinematic fade-in/fade-out transitions.
trackKind=level_visibility: Add a level visibility track to control level streaming during cinematic.
trackKind=shot: A shot track must be added to organize camera cuts.
trackKind=subsequence: A sub-sequence must be nested inside the master sequence.
whenNotToUse: trackKind=camera_cut: The sequence already has a camera cut track.
trackKind=camera_shake: No camera shake is needed.

trackKind=camera_shake: The shake is gameplay feedback during play (a hit, a landing): create a Blueprint with parentClass /Script/EngineCameras.LegacyCameraShake (blueprint.create) and call PlayerCameraManager StartCameraShake from a graph (blueprint.edit_graph).
trackKind=transform|property|skeletal_animation|material_parameter|particle|event|fade|level_visibility: The track is not needed for this sequence.
trackKind=fade: The fade happens during play (level start, death, level change): call PlayerCameraManager StartCameraFade from a graph (blueprint.edit_graph).
trackKind=shot: The master sequence already has a shot track.
trackKind=subsequence: The sequence should remain flat.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

path.description: Canonical /Game sequence asset path.

actorName.description: Actor name in the current level.

cameraName.description: Actor name in the current level.

endFrame.description: Section end in display-rate frames; used when durationFrames is absent.

rowIndex.description: Sequencer row index for the created section.

save.description: Whether to save the sequence asset after the mutation.

property.description: Property to animate, by name (Transform, Intensity...); required, or send it as propertyName (refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT when neither is sent).

propertyName.description: Property name to animate (alias of property).

propertyType.description: Property value type hint (alias of type).

animationPath.description: Animation sequence asset path (alias of animationSequencePath).

componentName.description: Component of the actor the track works on. skeletal_animation: the skeletal mesh that plays the clip (default the actor's root when that is a skeletal mesh; it gets its own binding under the actor, because Sequencer otherwise plays the clip on the first skeletal mesh it finds, which on a character built from several meshes copies another's pose and shows nothing). material_parameter: the component owning the material.

easeInFrames.description: Frames at the start of the section over which the clip blends in from the clip it overlaps (0 or omitted: it takes over at once).

easeOutFrames.description: Frames at the end of the section over which the clip blends out into the clip that overlaps it.

materialPath.description: Material asset path for a material render pass.

materialIndex.description: Material slot index on the component.

value.description: Key value at startFrame: a number for a scalar parameter, or an {r, g, b, a} object for a color parameter.

activate.description: Whether the key activates (true) or deactivates (false).

particleKey.description: The key at startFrame: trigger fires the system once, the key for a one-shot burst; activate keeps it running, so a one-shot that finishes starts again until the section ends; deactivate stops it. Default from activate.

levelNames.description: Level names toggled by the visibility track.

visibility.description: Level visibility state: Visible or Hidden.

trackKind.description:
Which add cinematic track variant to run.
camera_cut: Add a camera cut track to a cinematic sequence.
camera_shake: Add a camera shake track to a cinematic sequence.
transform: Add a transform track to animate actor transforms during cinematic.
property: Add a property track to animate a specific property on a bound actor.
skeletal_animation: Add a skeletal animation track to play animations on a skeletal mesh. A clip whose skeleton the mesh cannot play is refused with SKELETON_MISMATCH instead of silently showing the rest pose. Overlap the clips before and after it and give easeInFrames/easeOutFrames to crossfade between them instead of cutting in one frame.
material_parameter: Add a material parameter collection track to animate material parameters.
particle: Add a particle track to trigger particle systems during cinematic: trigger fires a one-shot burst (a hit, a spark) once, activate keeps a system running for the section.
event: Add an event track to trigger events at specific frames.
fade: Add a fade track for cinematic fade-in/fade-out transitions.
level_visibility: Add a level visibility track to control level streaming during cinematic.
shot: Add a cinematic shot track to a master sequence.
subsequence: Add a sub-sequence to a master sequence shot track.

bindingGuid.description: Binding GUID of the targeted camera or created cut.

sectionName.description: Name of the created section, assigned by Sequencer.

discovery.summary: Cinematic cameras and shots, chosen by setting. camera sets a CineCameraActor's focal length, aperture, sensor size and focus distance and reads back what the camera kept after clamping to its lens (values); rig_rail sets a rail rig's positionOnRail (0 to 1) and rig_crane a crane rig's pitch, yaw and arm length, each placing the rig at the world origin when actorName names none (spawned); shot sets a shot's display name, range or row. camera and the rigs are one undo step, and a call with nothing to set is refused.
whenToUse: setting=camera: Camera lens, focal length, aperture, or focus must be set.
setting=rig_crane: A camera must boom or swing on a crane arm.
setting=rig_rail: A camera must move along a rail for dolly shots.
setting=shot: Shot display name or frame range must be set.
whenNotToUse: setting=camera: Default camera settings are acceptable.
setting=rig_crane: No crane-based camera movement is needed.
setting=rig_rail: No rail-based camera movement is needed.
setting=shot: The shot does not exist on the shot track.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

cameraName.description: Actor name in the current level.

actorName.description: Actor name in the current level.

currentFocalLength.description: Focal length in millimetres (read before focalLength).

currentAperture.description: Aperture as an f-stop (read before aperture).

manualFocusDistance.description: Manual focus distance in centimetres (read before focusDistance).

focusDistance.description: Manual focus distance alias in centimetres.

label.description: Actor label alias for the camera or rig actor (alias of actorName).

path.description: Canonical /Game path of the master sequence that owns the shot track.

shotSequencePath.description: Picks the shot whose section plays this shot sequence (alternative to sectionIndex or sectionName).

sectionName.description: Shot section display name to configure (alternative to sectionIndex).

shotName.description: Name for the new sequence or asset.

sectionIndex.description: Index of the shot section to configure.

endFrame.description: Section end in display-rate frames; used when durationFrames is absent.

rowIndex.description: Sequencer row index for the created section.

save.description: Whether to save the sequence asset after the mutation.

setting.description:
Which configure cinematic variant to run.
camera: Set the lens of a CineCameraActor (actorName): currentFocalLength or focalLength (mm), currentAperture or aperture (f-stop), sensorWidth and sensorHeight (mm), manualFocusDistance or focusDistance (cm), each also accepted inside a lens, filmback or focus object. The camera clamps them to its lens limits and the reply reads back what it kept (values). One undo step; a call with nothing to set, or an actor with no CineCameraComponent, is refused.
rig_crane: Set cranePitch and craneYaw (degrees) and craneArmLength (cm) on a CameraRig_Crane named actorName, placing one at the world origin when actorName names none (spawned true). One undo step; a call with no setting is refused, and an actor of another class is RIG_CLASS_MISMATCH.
rig_rail: Set positionOnRail (0 to 1, where the camera mount sits along the rail spline) on a CameraRig_Rail named actorName, placing one at the world origin when actorName names none (spawned true). One undo step; a call with no setting is refused, and an actor of another class is RIG_CLASS_MISMATCH.
shot: Configure shot settings (display name, range) for a cinematic shot.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Cinematic cameras and shots, chosen by setting. camera sets a CineCameraActor's focal length, aperture, sensor size and focus distance and reads back what the camera kept after clamping to its lens (values); rig_rail sets a rail rig's positionOnRail (0 to 1) and rig_crane a crane rig's pitch, yaw and arm length, each placing the rig at the world origin when actorName names none (spawned); shot sets a shot's display name, range or row. camera and the rigs are one undo step, and a call with nothing to set is refused.

discovery.summary: Create a cinematic piece, chosen by kind. master_sequence makes a level sequence (name in path, default /Game/Cinematics, or sequencePath) at frameRate (default 24 fps) playing from startFrame (default 0) for durationFrames (default 240) or to endFrame, and saves it; it starts with no tracks, so add shots with add_shot_track and sub-sequences with add_subsequence. A level sequence already there is kept (alreadyExists); another asset there is ASSET_TYPE_MISMATCH. cine_camera_actor places a Cine Camera Actor named actorName (or label) at location and rotation with the lens, filmback and focus settings given (appliedProperties) and, with path or sequencePath, binds it to that sequence (bindingGuid); during Play it goes into the running game.
whenToUse: kind=cine_camera_actor: A cinematic camera actor must be created for a shot.
kind=master_sequence: A new cinematic with shots must be scaffolded.
whenNotToUse: kind=cine_camera_actor: An existing camera should be used.
kind=master_sequence: A flat sequence without shots is sufficient.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

currentFocalLength.description: Focal length in millimetres (read before focalLength).

currentAperture.description: Aperture as an f-stop (read before aperture).

manualFocusDistance.description: Manual focus distance in centimetres (read before focusDistance).

focusDistance.description: Manual focus distance alias in centimetres.

path.description: Level Sequence to bind the new camera to (sequencePath is read in its place); left out, the camera is placed unbound.

actorName.description: Actor name in the current level.

label.description: Actor label alias for the camera or rig actor (alias of actorName).

location.description: Camera location.

rotation.description: Camera rotation as {pitch, yaw, roll} (x/y/z are accepted as aliases).

name.description: Name of the new sequence; alone, it is created in path (default /Game/Cinematics).

frameRate.description: Frame rate as fps or a rate string such as 24fps or 24000/1001.

startFrame.description: Custom playback range start frame (paired with endFrame).

endFrame.description: Playback range end frame (exclusive); used when durationFrames is absent.

kind.description:
Which create cinematic asset variant to run.
cine_camera_actor: Create a CineCameraActor in the level and bind it to the sequence.
master_sequence: Create the master level sequence of a cinematic: an empty sequence at frameRate (default 24 fps) with its playback range, saved; shots and sub-sequences are added to it afterwards.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

actorName.description: Label of the created camera actor.

actorPath.description: Path to the created camera actor.

bindingGuid.description: Sequencer binding GUID (present when a sequence path was supplied).

appliedProperties.description: Camera properties applied to the created actor.

examples.title: Create a cinematic piece, chosen by kind. master_sequence makes a level sequence (name in path, default /Game/Cinematics, or sequencePath) at frameRate (default 24 fps) playing from startFrame (default 0) for durationFrames (default 240) or to endFrame, and saves it; it starts with no tracks, so add shots with add_shot_track and sub-sequences with add_subsequence. A level sequence already there is kept (alreadyExists); another asset there is ASSET_TYPE_MISMATCH. cine_camera_actor places a Cine Camera Actor named actorName (or label) at location and rotation with the lens, filmback and focus settings given (appliedProperties) and, with path or sequencePath, binds it to that sequence (bindingGuid); during Play it goes into the running game.

discovery.summary: Create a level sequence (sequenceOp create, the default): name in the folder path (default /Game), or path naming the asset itself; it is saved (saved), and a level sequence already there is kept and answered with alreadyExists, while another asset there is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS. duplicate copies the sequence at path into the folder destinationPath as newName and saves the copy; rename gives the sequence at path the name newName in its folder (a path starting with / moves it), references following it; the engine saves it and leaves a redirector at the old path when other assets reference it. Only /Game paths are written (SEQUENCE_PATH_NOT_WRITABLE); a source that is not a level sequence is INVALID_SEQUENCE, and a taken destination ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS.
whenToUse: sequenceOp=create: A new cinematic or animation sequence asset is needed.
sequenceOp=duplicate: A sequence must be copied to a different folder or name.
sequenceOp=rename: A sequence asset needs a new name.
whenNotToUse: sequenceOp=create: An existing sequence should be opened instead.
sequenceOp=duplicate: The sequence should be renamed in place.
sequenceOp=rename: The sequence should be duplicated to preserve the original.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

name.description: Name of the new sequence, made in the folder path names (default /Game). Leave it out when path names the sequence itself.

path.description: Sequence asset path, such as /Game/Cinematics/SEQ_Shot; with name, create reads it as the folder instead.

newName.description: New name for the sequence asset.

sequenceOp.description:
Which create variant to run; omit for 'create'.
create: Create a Level Sequence asset and save it: name in the folder path names (default /Game), or path alone naming the sequence itself (/Game/Cinematics/SEQ_Shot). A Level Sequence already there is kept and answered with alreadyExists true; another asset there is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS, and a path outside the writable content roots SEQUENCE_PATH_NOT_WRITABLE. The new sequence is empty, with no bindings or camera, at the project's default display rate (30 fps out of the box) and 24000 ticks per second.
duplicate: Copy a Level Sequence to destinationPath (a folder; one not starting with / is under the source folder) as newName, and save the copy. A destination already taken is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS, a source that is not a Level Sequence INVALID_SEQUENCE, a destination outside the writable content roots SEQUENCE_PATH_NOT_WRITABLE. The reply gives duplicatedPath and saved; the copy keeps the original's bindings, which still point at the same level actors.
rename: Rename a Level Sequence: newName keeps its folder, a path starting with / moves it there. The engine saves the renamed sequence and leaves a redirector at the old path when other assets reference it. A name already taken is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS, a source that is not a Level Sequence INVALID_SEQUENCE, a path outside the writable content roots SEQUENCE_PATH_NOT_WRITABLE. The reply gives oldPath and sequencePath.

Which edit sequence bindings variant to run.

whenToUse: edit=add_track: A new track (transform, float, event, etc.) must be added.
edit=add_section: A section must be added to animate a sub-range of a track.
edit=add_section: Music or a sound must play in a cutscene: add an Audio track, then a section with soundPath.
edit=add_keyframe: A property value must be animated at a specific frame.
edit=set_locked: A track must be protected from accidental edits.
edit=set_muted: A track must be temporarily silenced.
edit=set_solo: A single track must be isolated for preview.
edit=set_section: Two animation clips should crossfade: overlap their sections, ease the later one in and the earlier one out.
edit=set_section: A section must start or end on another frame.
edit=set_section: An animation clip should play faster or slower (playRate).
whenNotToUse: edit=add_track: The track type is not supported by the sequence.

edit=add_section: A sound must play in the running game, not inside a sequence.
edit=add_keyframe: The actor is not bound to the sequence.

edit=set_muted: The track should be permanently removed.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

path.description: Canonical /Game sequence asset path.

trackType.description: Track type: "Audio" (music or sound, then add_section with soundPath), "Transform", or a MovieScene track class name such as MovieSceneEventTrack.

trackName.description: Display name for the new track; track actions find it by this name. A track type that takes no name keeps its own, which the reply reads back.

actorName.description: Actor name in the current level.

bindingId.description: Camera binding GUID for a camera cut section (required on a camera cut track).

soundPath.description: Audio track only: /Game path of the SoundWave, SoundCue or MetaSound the section plays. Without end the section is as long as the sound (one second for a looping one).

end.description: Section end in display-rate frames, after start (default 100; with soundPath, the length of the sound).

property.description: Property to key: Transform, Location, Rotation or Scale; Visibility, which shows (true) or hides (false) the bound actor in the editor and in renders; or a float or bool property by name.

value.description: Keyframe value. For property "Transform" pass a composed object with any subset of {location:{x,y,z}, rotation:{pitch,yaw,roll}, scale:{x,y,z}}; each component supplied must carry all of its finite axes; a new Transform track starts from the current transform of the actor, so the parts a key leaves out keep their values. Add lookAt:{x,y,z} beside location to aim the key at that point (a camera at its subject): pitch and yaw are worked out, roll comes from rotation.roll or 0, and the yaw turns the short way from the key before, so an orbit of aimed keys never spins round. For "Location"/"Rotation"/"Scale" pass that component object alone. Visibility takes true or false; other properties take their own scalar value, so no type is declared here.

interpolation.description: How the curve leaves this key: auto (default) a smooth curve through the keys, linear a steady rate to the next key (a bullet, a constant pan), constant a hold that jumps at the next key.

value.description: Key value, in the form value takes.

interpolation.description: How the curve leaves this key; default the interpolation of the call.

keys.description: Several keys on this property in one call, in place of frame and value: a whole curve, or a flash shown on one frame and hidden on the next. Each entry is {frame, value, interpolation}; they are written in order, so lookAt keys turn the short way from the entry before. Every frame is checked before any key is written.

sectionIndex.description: Which section of the track, in the order info=keys lists them (default 0).

startFrame.description: New start of the section in display-rate frames.

endFrame.description: New end of the section in display-rate frames, after its start.

easeInFrames.description: Frames the section fades in over; 0 removes its ease in.

easeOutFrames.description: Frames the section fades out over; 0 removes its ease out.

playRate.description: The speed of an animation section (2 is twice as fast). Without endFrame the section keeps playing the same frames, so it gets shorter or longer by the same factor, as in Sequencer.

edit.description:
Which edit sequence tracks variant to run.
add_track: Add an empty track of trackType to a Level Sequence: on the binding of actorName (an actor the sequence already binds), or as a sequence-wide track without it (Audio for music, Fade, Event). trackName gives it a display name later track actions can address it by. One undo step; the sequence is left unsaved. The reply gives trackId (its object name), trackClass and trackName read back. An unknown type is TRACK_CREATION_FAILED (list_track_types gives the names), a class that is no track INVALID_CLASS_TYPE, an actor the sequence does not bind BINDING_NOT_FOUND.
add_section: Add a section to an existing track in a Level Sequence; on an Audio track, soundPath puts music or a sound in it.
add_keyframe: Add a keyframe for a property at a specific frame on a bound actor.
set_locked: Lock (locked, default true) or unlock every section of a Level Sequence track, so the Sequencer will not move or edit them; the track still plays. One undo step; the sequence is left unsaved.
set_muted: Mute (muted, default true) or unmute a track of a Level Sequence by trackName: a muted track stays in the sequence but is not evaluated, so it plays and renders nothing. One undo step; the sequence is left unsaved. A trackName the sequence lacks is TRACK_NOT_FOUND.
set_solo: Solo a track of a Level Sequence (solo, default true) by muting every other track, or with solo false unmute every track, those muted before included. The reply counts the tracks it changed (affectedTrackCount, disabledOtherTrackCount). One undo step; the sequence is left unsaved.
set_section: Move, trim, ease or speed up a section already on a track: its start and end frames, the frames it eases in and out over, and the play rate of an animation section.

playRate.description: An animation section: its play rate now (1 when it warps time another way).

control.description:
Which create render job variant to run; omit for 'create'.
create: Create a Movie Render Queue job for sequencePath on mapPath (default: the open level), named renderJobName, with a PNG image sequence output and a deferred render pass, plus any output settings sent (outputDirectory, fileNameFormat, resolution, frameRate, a frame range, settings.handleFrameCount and zeroPadFrameNumbers), all checked before the job is made. The job lives in this editor session queue, not on disk; render it with control start.
queue: Enable a render job in the MRQ queue without starting execution. Enqueue does NOT mean render completion.
start: Start MRQ render execution. Blocks until completion, fatal error, or timeout. Supports advisory cancellation. renderTimeoutMs (how long the render may run before it is cancelled) defaults to 300000 (5 minutes) and may be as long as the plugin's MaxMovieRenderTimeoutMs (one hour by default); the native transport waits that long plus the cancellation wait for the reply.
cancel: Stop the Movie Render Queue render that is running, as the queue window's Stop does: every job is cancelled, frames already written stay on disk, and the sequence gets back the state the render held it in.
remove: Remove a render job from the Movie Render Queue, or every job (allJobs). Rendered files stay on disk. The queue holds a limited number of jobs, and a finished job stays queued (an unrestricted start renders it again), so remove finished ones before creating more.

compensation.guidance: Rendered frames are written to the configured MRQ output directory and are not removed by any capability; delete them from disk. The render itself only supports advisory cancellation while running.

discovery.summary: Cut a Level Sequence between its cameras the way an editor would, as its camera cut track: the playback range is split into segments (segmentSeconds, default 0.5), and at each segment's middle every camera is scored by how it shows the subjects as the sequence plays them (each subject hidden behind something or out of frame, the first, the main one, counting double; the main one too small or too large), and every cut by its jump (two cameras within 30 degrees of each other round the main subject) and its crossing of the line between the first two subjects. The cheapest edit whose shots all last minShotSeconds to maxShotSeconds (default 1.5 to 8) is found by dynamic programming over segment, camera and time held, and replaces the camera cut track's sections, cameras bound to the sequence when they are not, in one undo step. dryRun answers the shots without writing. Refused, changing nothing, with NO_CUT (some moment no camera sees the main subject: unseenSeconds lists when), ACTOR_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_SEQUENCE, INVALID_ARGUMENT (fewer than 2 cameras, a range shorter than the shortest shot).
whenToUse: A scene has several cameras and needs cutting between them: which camera is on when, without cutting across the line or jumping between near-identical angles.
Re-cutting after the action or the cameras changed: run it again, it replaces the cuts.
whenNotToUse: Placing one camera on a shot: use frame_shot.
Moving a camera along a path: use fly_through.
Adding one cut by hand: use add_cinematic_track kind=camera_cut.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

sequencePath.description: The Level Sequence to cut; its playback range is the range edited.

cameras.description: The camera actors to cut between (2-12), by name; where the sequence moves one, it is judged where the sequence has it.

subjects.description: The actors the cut serves (1-4), most important first: the first must be seen at every moment (NO_CUT otherwise), and the line between the first two is the one cuts should not cross.

segmentSeconds.description: How finely the range is judged, in seconds (default 0.5): cuts fall on these steps.

minShotSeconds.description: Shortest shot, in seconds (default 1.5; at least segmentSeconds).

maxShotSeconds.description: Longest shot, in seconds (default 8; at least minShotSeconds).

dryRun.description: Find the edit and answer without writing it (default false).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

camerasUsed.description: The cameras the edit cuts to, in order of first use.

crossings.description: Cuts that cross the line between the first two subjects (0 unless no other edit fits).

undo.description: What editor undo takes back: {undoable, transactionScope, steps}; every cut is one step. Absent under dryRun.

topics: fly the camera through the level
discovery.summary: Fly a camera through points of the level and key the flight into a Level Sequence, never nearer to geometry than a clearance: between two points the camera goes straight when nothing is in the way, else round or over what is (a search through free space, cut short wherever a straight line is clear), and the corners are smoothed into one minimum-snap curve (unbroken in speed, acceleration and jerk) at rest at both ends, timed by distance over seconds (default the path length at 3 m/s). It faces lookAt (an actor) the whole way, else the way ahead. Keys every tenth of a second go on a transform track of its own (an earlier one of that camera is replaced: replacedTrack says so), with a camera cut to it over the flight and the playback range grown to hold it, all in one undo step, from the sequence's playback start; the camera is the actor named camera (default FlyCamera), or a CineCameraActor spawned under that label. dryRun answers the corners and the length without writing. Refused, changing nothing, with POINT_IN_SOLID (a point nearer to geometry than clearanceCm; point gives its index), NO_PATH (no way through free space joins two points, or the smoothed curve cannot be kept clear), ACTOR_NOT_FOUND (lookAt), INVALID_SEQUENCE, INVALID_ARGUMENT.
whenToUse: A camera must move smoothly through a level (a fly-through, a drone shot, a reveal) without working out keys or clipping through walls.
A cinematic needs a camera move between given places, looking at one actor all the way.
whenNotToUse: A still camera framing actors: use frame_shot.
Keying one transform by hand: use add_keyframe.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

sequencePath.description: The Level Sequence to key the flight into (/Game/...); the keys start at its playback start.

through.description: The points the camera passes, in order, in cm (2-16). Each must stand at least clearanceCm from geometry (a point beside a wall or near the floor is POINT_IN_SOLID).

lookAt.description: An actor the camera faces the whole way (the middle of what it draws); left out, the camera faces the way it is going.

seconds.description: How long the flight takes (0.5-600; default its length at 300 cm a second, at least 1).

clearanceCm.description: How far from geometry the camera stays, in cm (default 50): the straight lines between corners keep all of it, the smoothed curve at least 80% of it. A gap narrower than twice this cannot be flown through.

camera.description: The camera actor to fly, by name; when no actor has this name a CineCameraActor is spawned with it as its label (default FlyCamera).

dryRun.description: Plan the flight and answer without writing anything (default false).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

spawned.description: The camera was spawned by this call (with dryRun: would be).

corners.description: The corners the curve passes, as [x, y, z], the given points among them (64 at most).

bindingGuid.description: The camera's binding in the sequence.

startFrame.description: First frame of the flight, at the sequence's display rate.

playbackGrown.description: The playback range was lengthened to hold the flight.

cameraCut.description: A camera cut to the camera covers the flight.

replacedTrack.description: The camera already had a transform track in this sequence, and the flight replaced it (its keys are gone; undo brings them back).

undo.description: What editor undo takes back: {undoable, transactionScope, steps}; the camera, its keys and the cut are one step. Absent under dryRun.

topics: aim a camera at two actors
discovery.summary: Place a camera so one or two actors sit where they should on screen: by default one subject on the left third line, two on the left and right third lines (framing gives each its own screen point). It searches the places around the subjects for the best view: every subject clear of what stands between (each sight line to it traced), the camera out of walls and floors, seen a little from above, a lone subject three-quarter on from its front and turned into the frame; the camera never rolls. One subject is sized by shotSize (close: its box spans 90% of the frame; medium: 55%; wide: 25%); two are sized by how far apart their screen points are, and kept about as far from the camera as each other (a two-shot, not one subject looming over the other). Moves the camera actor named camera (default ShotCamera), or spawns a CineCameraActor under that label when no actor has it, and sets its focal length (focalLength; else 85, 50 or 24 mm by shot size, 35 mm for two subjects) and its manual focus on the first subject, all in one undo step. dryRun answers the same without moving or spawning anything. Each subject comes back with its target, where it landed (screen) and how hidden it is. Refused, changing nothing, with ACTOR_NOT_FOUND (a subject is not in the level; missing lists it), NO_CLEAR_SHOT (no place found sees every subject at least half clear with the camera out of solid geometry: the best one tried is in the details), INVALID_ARGUMENT (a subject that draws nothing, framing points that do not fit the subjects, focalLength on a plain camera, a camera actor with no camera component).
whenToUse: A camera must show one or two actors well composed (on the thirds, a two-shot of a conversation) without working out where it stands and where it points.
Setting up the camera of a cinematic shot or a screenshot; a Level Sequence can then cut to it (add_camera_cut_track).
Checking whether an actor can be seen clearly at all from around it: dryRun answers NO_CLEAR_SHOT when nothing can.
whenNotToUse: Moving the editor viewport rather than a camera actor: use control_editor set_camera or focus_actor.
Animating a camera over time: key its transform in a Level Sequence (add_keyframe).
Changing only a camera's lens, focus or filmback: use configure_cinematic setting=camera.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

subjects.description: The one or two actors to frame, by exact name. Each is framed by the box of what it draws: its centre goes to its framing point, and its size sets the distance.

x.description: Left edge -1, centre 0, right edge 1; the third lines are at -0.333 and 0.333.

framing.description: Where each subject's centre should sit on screen, one {x, y} per subject in the order of subjects (default: one subject at {x: -0.333, y: 0}, two at {x: -0.333, y: 0} and {x: 0.333, y: 0}). Two subjects need points apart from each other.

shotSize.description: One subject: how much of the frame its box spans, the larger of its height share and its width share (close 90%, medium 55%, the default, wide 25%); it also picks the default focal length. Two subjects are sized by their framing points, so it only picks the lens.

focalLength.description: Focal length in mm for a cine camera (default by shotSize: close 85, medium 50, wide 24; two subjects 35), kept within what its lens allows. A plain camera actor has no lens: its own field of view is used and focalLength is refused.

camera.description: The camera actor to move (a CineCameraActor or a CameraActor), by name; when no actor has this name a CineCameraActor is spawned with it as its label (default ShotCamera, so repeated calls move the same camera).

dryRun.description: Find the shot and answer without moving or spawning anything (default false).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

spawned.description: The camera was spawned by this call (with dryRun: would be).

location.description: Where the camera stands, as [x, y, z].

rotation.description: Its rotation as [pitch, yaw, roll]; roll is always 0.

fieldOfView.description: Horizontal field of view in degrees.

focalLength.description: Cine camera: the focal length set, in mm.

focusDistance.description: Cine camera: the manual focus distance set, in cm (to the first subject's centre).

target.description: A screen point as [x, y]: x -1 (left edge) to 1 (right edge), y -1 (bottom) to 1 (top).

screen.description: Where its centre landed, as [x, y].

error.description: How far that is from its target, in the same units (0.02 is about 1% of the frame's width).

hidden.description: Share of the sight lines from the camera to it that something else blocks (0-1).

fill.description: One subject: the share of the frame its box spans.

undo.description: What editor undo takes back: {undoable, transactionScope, steps}; the move or spawn and the lens are one step. Absent under dryRun.

discovery.summary: Play, pause or stop a level sequence in the editor; pause with startTime moves the playhead to that time and holds the frame there, so the level shows that moment.
whenToUse: control=play: A sequence must be previewed in the editor viewport.
control=play: A screenshot must show the scene moving through a shot: play, then pause with startTime to hold one moment.
control=pause: Sequence playback must be paused.
control=pause: A pose, camera or effect must be checked at one moment of the sequence: pause with startTime, then take a screenshot.
control=stop: Sequence playback must be stopped and the playhead reset to the start.
whenNotToUse: control=stop: The sequence should only be paused.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

path.description: Canonical /Game sequence asset path.

startTime.description: Sequence time in seconds. play starts there; pause jumps the playhead there and holds that frame, so the viewport and screenshots show the scene at that moment. A time past the end of the playback range is refused: frame N at 24 fps is N / 24 seconds.

loopMode.description: Sequencer loop mode for the preview: once or loop.

control.description:
Which play variant to run; omit for 'play'.
play: Open a Level Sequence (path) in Sequencer and play it as an editor preview in the level viewport. startTime jumps there first; without it play carries on from the playhead (from the start when it sits at the end). loopMode once or loop sets the Sequencer's own loop setting, which stays for later previews. The reply reads back startTime (seconds), currentFrame and playbackStart/playbackEnd in display frames. Nothing in the asset or level changes. A time past the playback range or another loopMode is INVALID_ARGUMENT; a path that is not a Level Sequence is SEQUENCE_NOT_FOUND.
pause: Pause the Sequencer preview of a Level Sequence, or hold it at one moment to inspect it: startTime (seconds) moves the playhead there and poses the animated meshes at once, so a screenshot taken next shows that moment even with the editor in the background; a sequence not open is opened first. The reply reads back currentFrame in display frames. Without startTime a sequence not open in Sequencer is EDITOR_NOT_OPEN; a time past the playback range is INVALID_ARGUMENT. Nothing in the asset changes.
stop: Stop the Sequencer preview of a Level Sequence and put the playhead back on the start of its playback range (where Jump to Start goes, not frame 0), posing the animated meshes there. The reply reads back currentFrame in display frames. A sequence not open in Sequencer is EDITOR_NOT_OPEN; nothing in the asset changes.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Play, pause or stop a level sequence in the editor; pause with startTime moves the playhead to that time and holds the frame there, so the level shows that moment.

discovery.summary: Set how this editor session records and plays demo replays, chosen by setting. demo stores the default replayName and friendlyName, extra additionalOptions, maxRecordTimeSeconds (up to 86400), checkpointSaveMaxMSPerFrame (up to 1000 ms; also written to the engine config and the demo driver defaults), playbackSpeed, prioritizeActors and loadDefaultMapOnStop; a recording or playback running now takes them at once (appliedToRuntime), and the reply lists everything stored. killcam_duration sets how many seconds start_killcam replays (up to 600). All but the checkpoint budget last until the editor closes.
whenToUse: setting=demo: Replay recording settings must be configured before recording.
setting=killcam_duration: Killcam duration must be set for replay-based kill cameras.
whenNotToUse: setting=demo: Default replay settings are acceptable.
setting=killcam_duration: No killcam is needed.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

replayName.description: Default replay name for recordings that do not name one.

checkpointSaveMaxMSPerFrame.description: Max checkpoint save MS per frame (<=1000).

prioritizeActors.description: Whether to prioritize actor replication during recording.

loadDefaultMapOnStop.description: Whether to load the default map on stop.

setting.description:
Which configure demo settings variant to run; omit for 'demo'.
demo: Configure replay settings (max record time, checkpoint interval, speed, actor priority).
killcam_duration: Configure killcam replay duration (max 600 seconds).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Set how this editor session records and plays demo replays, chosen by setting. demo stores the default replayName and friendlyName, extra additionalOptions, maxRecordTimeSeconds (up to 86400), checkpointSaveMaxMSPerFrame (up to 1000 ms; also written to the engine config and the demo driver defaults), playbackSpeed, prioritizeActors and loadDefaultMapOnStop; a recording or playback running now takes them at once (appliedToRuntime), and the reply lists everything stored. killcam_duration sets how many seconds start_killcam replays (up to 600). All but the checkpoint budget last until the editor closes.

discovery.summary: Record and play back gameplay replays in the running game, chosen by control; outside Play every control is NOT_IN_PIE. start_recording records replayName (else the configured default, else McpReplay_<time>) until stop_recording, which answers the name, and is refused while a replay plays or records (ALREADY_PLAYING, ALREADY_RECORDING). play plays replayName back (refused while recording); pause pauses or resumes it (paused; without it, toggles); seek jumps to timeSeconds, clamped to the replay's length, and answers once playback gets there (REPLAY_SEEK_TIMEOUT after 10 s); set_playback_speed sets speed (at most 16); start_killcam plays the last durationSeconds of the playing replay, or of replayName. pause, seek and set_playback_speed need a replay playing (NOT_PLAYING). Replies give the replay state (activeReplayName, recording, playing, currentTimeSeconds, totalTimeSeconds, paused, playbackSpeed).
whenToUse: control=play: A recorded demo replay must be played back.
control=pause: Demo playback must be paused.
control=seek: Demo playback must be seeked to a specific time.
control=set_playback_speed: Demo playback speed must be changed.
control=start_recording: A demo replay must be recorded.
control=stop_recording: An in-progress demo recording must be stopped.
control=start_killcam: A killcam replay must be triggered.
whenNotToUse: control=play: A recording is in progress (ALREADY_PLAYING).
control=pause|seek|set_playback_speed: Demo is not playing.
control=start_recording: A recording is already in progress (ALREADY_RECORDING).
control=stop_recording: No recording is in progress (NOT_RECORDING).
control=start_killcam: No killcam is needed.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

seconds.description: Seek time in seconds (alias of timeSeconds).

control.description:
Which play demo variant to run; omit for 'play'.
play: Play the replay replayName (or demoName) back in the running game at the configured playback speed. Refused while recording (ALREADY_RECORDING) and outside Play (NOT_IN_PIE); PLAYBACK_FAILED when the replay does not start. Replies give the replay state (activeReplayName, recording, playing, currentTimeSeconds, totalTimeSeconds, paused, playbackSpeed).
pause: Pause the playing replay (paused true) or resume it (paused false); without paused it toggles. NOT_PLAYING when no replay plays. Replies give the replay state (activeReplayName, recording, playing, currentTimeSeconds, totalTimeSeconds, paused, playbackSpeed).
seek: Jump the playing replay to timeSeconds, clamped to its length, and answer once playback is within 0.25 s of it (actualTimeSeconds); REPLAY_SEEK_TIMEOUT after 10 s, NOT_PLAYING when no replay plays.
set_playback_speed: Set the playing replay's speed (speed or playbackSpeed, 1 is real time, at most 16); later playback keeps it. NOT_PLAYING when no replay plays.
start_recording: Start recording the running game as a replay named replayName (or demoName; else the configure_demo_settings default, else McpReplay_<unix time>), labelled friendlyName, until control=stop_recording. Refused while a replay plays (ALREADY_PLAYING) or records (ALREADY_RECORDING), and outside Play (NOT_IN_PIE). Replies give the replay state (activeReplayName, recording, playing, currentTimeSeconds, totalTimeSeconds, paused, playbackSpeed).
stop_recording: Stop the recording control=start_recording began and answer its replayName; NOT_RECORDING when none runs, NOT_IN_PIE outside Play.
start_killcam: Play back the last durationSeconds (default the configure_killcam_duration value) of the playing replay, starting replayName first when none plays, and answer once playback reaches that point; NOT_AVAILABLE without a replay to play.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Record and play back gameplay replays in the running game, chosen by control; outside Play every control is NOT_IN_PIE. start_recording records replayName (else the configured default, else McpReplay_<time>) until stop_recording, which answers the name, and is refused while a replay plays or records (ALREADY_PLAYING, ALREADY_RECORDING). play plays replayName back (refused while recording); pause pauses or resumes it (paused; without it, toggles); seek jumps to timeSeconds, clamped to the replay's length, and answers once playback gets there (REPLAY_SEEK_TIMEOUT after 10 s); set_playback_speed sets speed (at most 16); start_killcam plays the last durationSeconds of the playing replay, or of replayName. pause, seek and set_playback_speed need a replay playing (NOT_PLAYING). Replies give the replay state (activeReplayName, recording, playing, currentTimeSeconds, totalTimeSeconds, paused, playbackSpeed).

whenToUse: Sequence asset metadata must be written.
whenNotToUse: The target is not a /Game asset path.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

path.description: Canonical /Game sequence asset path.

key.description: Single metadata key to write (paired with value).

value.description: Value written under key.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.
