discovery.summary: Set sequence properties: playback range and frame rate, display rate, tick resolution, playback speed, view range, work range.
whenToUse: sequenceProperty=properties: Sequence timing properties must be configured.
sequenceProperty=display_rate: The sequence display rate must be changed.
sequenceProperty=tick_resolution: The sequence tick resolution must be changed.
sequenceProperty=playback_speed: A sequence must play faster or slower in game, or in the preview.
sequenceProperty=view_range: The visible region in the Sequencer must be bounded.
sequenceProperty=work_range: The editable region must be bounded.
whenNotToUse: sequenceProperty=properties: Properties are being read rather than set.
sequenceProperty=display_rate: The tick resolution needs changing instead.
sequenceProperty=tick_resolution: The display rate needs changing instead.
sequenceProperty=playback_speed: The speed value is not a positive number.
sequenceProperty=view_range: The work range needs changing instead.
sequenceProperty=work_range: The view range needs changing instead.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

path.description: Canonical /Game sequence asset path.

frameRate.description: Frame rate as fps or a rate string such as 24fps or 24000/1001.

lengthInFrames.description: Playback length in display-rate frames, counted from playbackStart (or the current start); playbackEnd wins when both are sent.

resolution.description: Tick resolution in whole ticks per second (24000, 60000), at least the display rate.

sequenceProperty.description:
Which set properties variant to run; omit for 'properties'.
properties: Set the display frame rate of a Level Sequence (frameRate, such as 24 or 29.97) and its playback range in display-rate frames: playbackStart, and playbackEnd or lengthInFrames (end = start + length; playbackEnd wins). Send at least one; one undo step, and the sequence is left unsaved. The reply reads the values back; a negative frame or an unreadable rate is INVALID_ARGUMENT, another asset type INVALID_SEQUENCE.
display_rate: Set the display frame rate of a Level Sequence (frameRate: 24, 29.97, "30fps", "30000/1001"), the rate its timeline counts frames in; keys stay at the same times. An unreadable rate is INVALID_ARGUMENT; the reply reads the rate back. One undo step; the sequence is left unsaved.
tick_resolution: Set the tick resolution of a Level Sequence, the time grid keys and sections are stored on (resolution: whole ticks per second such as 24000, the default, or 60000; a ratio N/D is N ticks every D seconds), moving every key, section and range onto the new grid as the Sequencer does so nothing shifts in time. Anything else, zero included, is INVALID_ARGUMENT, and so is a resolution coarser than the display rate, which could not hold every frame. The reply gives tickResolution and previousTickResolution, and warns when the display rate does not fall on whole ticks. One undo step; the sequence is left unsaved.
playback_speed: Set the play rate of a Level Sequence (speed, above 0; 1 is normal, 0.5 half speed) on every level sequence actor in the editor level that plays it, which is the rate it runs at in game and Play In Editor, and on the Sequencer preview when the sequence is open there (a preview setting that is not saved). The actors change in one undo step and the level is left unsaved. The reply lists the actors (levelSequenceActors) and sequencerUpdated. With neither an actor nor an open Sequencer it is PLAYBACK_TARGET_NOT_FOUND; speed 0 or below is INVALID_ARGUMENT.
view_range: Set the view range of a Level Sequence, the part of the timeline the Sequencer window shows: start and end in seconds, end after start (INVALID_ARGUMENT otherwise). Display only: playback and keys are untouched.
work_range: Set the work range of a Level Sequence, the stretch of timeline the Sequencer shows and edits within: start and end in seconds, end after start (INVALID_ARGUMENT otherwise). An end past the playback range extends playback to it (playbackExtended), so keys out there play; the reply gives the range in seconds and in display-rate frames.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Set sequence properties: playback range and frame rate, display rate, tick resolution, playback speed, view range, work range.

discovery.summary: Record a take with the Take Recorder (Takes plugin), chosen by setting: sources picks the actors and allowlisted source classes to record and the sequence or preset to record from; recorded_tracks turns recorded properties of actor sources on or off; panel opens the panel and reads its mode, sequence, frame rate and source count; start_recording begins a take once its countdown ends, for duration seconds or until stop_recording; stop_recording finalizes the take and says whether it recorded anything (RECORDING_OUTPUT_EMPTY when not). Setup changes are refused while a take records (RECORDING_ACTIVE), and a refused call leaves the panel and sources as they were.
whenToUse: setting=sources: Actors (characters, cameras, props) must be chosen for recording before a take starts.
setting=recorded_tracks: A take should record only some properties of an actor, such as its transform but not its lights.
setting=panel: The Take Recorder state (mode, sequence, frame rate, sources) must be read before setting up a take.
setting=start_recording: A take recording must be started.
setting=stop_recording: An in-progress take recording must be stopped and finalized.
whenNotToUse: setting=start_recording: A take is already recording (RECORDING_ACTIVE).
setting=stop_recording: No recording is in progress (NOT_RECORDING).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: Actor name in the current level.

sourceClasses.description: Take Recorder source classes to add besides actors, each listed in the plugin setting TakeRecorderSourceClassAllowlist (by default /Script/TakeRecorderSources.TakeRecorderCameraCutSource and TakeRecorderLevelVisibilitySource); another class is INVALID_SOURCE_CLASS.

clearSources.description: Remove every existing source before adding the ones sent (default false); alone it empties the take.

takePresetPath.description: Take Preset whose template sequence seeds a new take; cannot be combined with a sequence path or recordInto (INVALID_ARGUMENT), and one that does not load is TAKE_PRESET_NOT_FOUND.

recordType.description: How an actor source records the actor: possessable (onto the actor in the level), spawnable (the take spawns its own copy) or projectDefault (the Take Recorder project setting). Anything else is INVALID_ARGUMENT.

actors.description: Actor names to record (alias of actorNames).

recordParentHierarchy.description: Also record the actors the source actor is attached under, so its motion keeps its parents.

recordingSequencePath.description: Level Sequence the take is set up from: recorded as a new take based on it, or into it with recordInto true; the same as sequencePath. One that is not a Level Sequence is INVALID_SEQUENCE.

takeSequencePath.description: Level Sequence the take is set up from, the same as sequencePath.

frameRate.description: Frame rate as fps or a rate string such as 24fps or 24000/1001.

recordInto.description: Record into the sequence named by sequencePath instead of a new take based on it (default false).

tracks.description: Recorded properties to turn on or off, by the names the actor source lists (such as Transform), matched without case.

enabled.description: Turn the matched recorded properties on (default true) or off.

disableOthers.description: Turn off every recorded property not named (default false), so the take records only those.

duration.description: Seconds (above 0) to record after the countdown before the take stops by itself.

setting.description:
Which configure take recorder variant to run.
sources: Set what the next take records: actors by name (actorName, actorNames, actors or sourceActors; in the editor world or the running game) are added as enabled actor sources, and sourceClasses adds allowlisted source classes; clearSources true removes every source first. Before the sources it applies the take setup the call names: a Level Sequence (sequencePath, recorded as a new take based on it, or into it with recordInto true) or a takePresetPath, and frameRate. recordType, recordParentHierarchy and reduceKeys set the options of the actor sources. The reply gives addedSources, requestedSources and sourceCount. Refused: no actors, classes or clearSources (INVALID_ARGUMENT), an actor not found (ACTOR_NOT_FOUND), a class not allowlisted (INVALID_SOURCE_CLASS), any change while recording (RECORDING_ACTIVE); a refused call leaves the sources and the panel as they were.
recorded_tracks: Choose what actor sources record: the recorded properties named in tracks, properties or trackNames (as the source lists them, such as Transform; matched without case) turn on, or off with enabled false, and disableOthers turns every other one off. It acts on the sources of the actors named (an actor not yet a source is added first) or on every actor source; recordType, recordParentHierarchy and reduceKeys set their options. The reply gives actorSourceCount, matchedProperties, changedProperties and appliedSourceOptions. Refused: nothing to change (INVALID_ARGUMENT), no actor sources (NO_ACTOR_SOURCES), no named property found (RECORDED_PROPERTY_NOT_FOUND), any change while recording (RECORDING_ACTIVE); a refused call removes the sources it added.
panel: Open the Take Recorder panel (or bring it forward) and read its state: panelOpen, mode (NewRecording, RecordingInto, EditingPreset or ReviewingRecording), the sequencePath it is set up with, frameRate (with frameRateNumerator and frameRateDenominator), frameRateFromTimecode and sourceCount. Needs the Takes plugin (NOT_AVAILABLE). Every other Take Recorder action except setting=stop_recording opens the panel itself.
start_recording: Start a Take Recorder take, set up as setting=sources sets it when any source or sequence field is sent. The panel needs a Level Sequence and at least one enabled, valid source; otherwise CANNOT_START_RECORDING with hasSequence, sourceCount and validSourceCount. The reply comes once recording has begun after the countdown: sequencePath, sequencePackagePath, subsceneFolderPath, state, recording and countdownSeconds. A recorder that stops first is RECORDING_START_FAILED and one not started within the countdown plus 10 s RECORDING_START_TIMEOUT; both put the setup back (rolledBack). duration (seconds after the countdown) stops the take by itself, otherwise setting=stop_recording ends it. Refused while a take records (RECORDING_ACTIVE). Sequencer is not opened.
stop_recording: Stop the take that is recording and finalize its Level Sequence: sequencePath, sequencePackagePath, subsceneFolderPath (where the per-source sequences go), state, recording false, isRecorded, bindingCount, trackCount and hasRecordedData. A take that recorded nothing answers RECORDING_OUTPUT_EMPTY instead of success; nothing recording is NOT_RECORDING with the recorder state.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

hasRecordedData.description: Whether the take is marked recorded and has bindings or tracks.

isRecorded.description: Whether the sequence is marked as a recorded take.

bindingCount.description: Object bindings in the recorded sequence.

trackCount.description: Tracks in the recorded sequence, master and bound.

examples.title: Record a take with the Take Recorder (Takes plugin), chosen by setting: sources picks the actors and allowlisted source classes to record and the sequence or preset to record from; recorded_tracks turns recorded properties of actor sources on or off; panel opens the panel and reads its mode, sequence, frame rate and source count; start_recording begins a take once its countdown ends, for duration seconds or until stop_recording; stop_recording finalizes the take and says whether it recorded anything (RECORDING_OUTPUT_EMPTY when not). Setup changes are refused while a take records (RECORDING_ACTIVE), and a refused call leaves the panel and sources as they were.

discovery.summary: Delete a Blueprint Struct asset (deleteScope struct, the default: refused with STRUCT_IN_USE, naming referencers, while other assets use it, unless force deletes it anyway and recompiles the loaded Blueprints that used it; NOT_FOUND when there is none) or remove one member (member: by memberName or varGuid; the assets using the struct are refreshed, and it is saved unless save is false).
whenToUse: deleteScope=struct: An unused struct asset must be deleted; a struct still referenced is refused, with its referencers listed, unless force is set.
deleteScope=member: One field must be removed from a struct; referencing Blueprints and DataTables are refreshed afterwards.
whenNotToUse: deleteScope=struct: The struct should be renamed or moved instead of removed (use struct.edit_struct).
deleteScope=struct: The assets that use the struct must be found first (use struct.get_struct with info=usage).
deleteScope=member: A field only needs a new name or type (use struct.edit_struct).

structPath.description: Asset path of the Blueprint Struct (e.g. /Game/Structs/S_MyStruct).

force.description: Delete even when other assets use the struct, breaking them: the loaded Blueprints among them recompile, and the engine removes their variables of it (the reply's warnings name them). Default false: refused with STRUCT_IN_USE, listing the referencers.

varGuid.description: Stable member GUID, as get_struct lists it; pass this or memberName.

save.description: Persist the struct to disk. Defaults to true; pass false to keep the change in memory only.

deleteScope.description:
Which delete struct variant to run; omit for 'struct'.
struct: Delete a Blueprint Struct asset.
member: Remove a member from a Blueprint Struct.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Delete a Blueprint Struct asset (deleteScope struct, the default: refused with STRUCT_IN_USE, naming referencers, while other assets use it, unless force deletes it anyway and recompiles the loaded Blueprints that used it; NOT_FOUND when there is none) or remove one member (member: by memberName or varGuid; the assets using the struct are refreshed, and it is saved unless save is false).

discovery.summary: Create a user-defined struct or edit it: members, defaults, metadata, types, order, rename, duplicate, import, recompile, refresh dependencies, instanced struct properties.
whenToUse: edit=create_struct: A new Blueprint struct is needed; give its members up front, otherwise it keeps one placeholder member.
edit=add_struct_member: One or several fields, each with a type, optional default and tooltip, must be added to an existing struct.
edit=rename_struct_member: A field must be renamed while keeping its type and default; it is found by memberName or varGuid.
edit=reorder_struct_members: One field, named by memberName or varGuid, must move to first, last, or before or after another field.
edit=set_struct_member_default: A field needs a new default value; a value that cannot convert to the field type is rejected.
edit=set_struct_member_metadata: A field needs a tooltip or metadata key and value pairs.
edit=set_struct_member_type: A field needs a different type, for example Int to Float or a container; self-referencing and cyclic types are refused.
edit=rename_struct: The struct asset needs a new name or folder; a redirector is left at the old path when it is referenced, and dependent Blueprints recompile.
edit=duplicate_struct: A struct must be forked into a new asset with the same members, for example to try a second revision.
edit=import_struct: A struct must be rebuilt from a member list or a JSON file; members are replaced and a failed apply is rolled back.
edit=recompile_struct: Dependent Blueprints must be recompiled after a struct change and their compile errors listed; the changed assets are saved unless save is false.
edit=refresh_struct_dependencies: A struct was edited outside these tools and its Blueprints and DataTables must be rebuilt against the new layout; the affected assets are listed.
edit=set_instanced_struct_property: An FInstancedStruct property on an asset must be set to a chosen struct type with given field values.
whenNotToUse: edit=create_struct: A DataTable is wanted as well as its row struct (use datatable.edit_data_table to create the table and bind the struct).
edit=add_struct_member: A variable is needed on a Blueprint, not a field on a struct (use blueprint.edit_variable).
edit=rename_struct_member: A field must be removed instead of renamed (use struct.delete_struct with deleteScope=member).
edit=reorder_struct_members: The current member order must be read before moving anything (use struct.get_struct).
edit=set_struct_member_default: Values stored in a DataTable row must change, not the struct default (use datatable.edit_data_table).
edit=set_struct_member_metadata: Metadata for an enum entry is wanted (use enum.edit_enum).
edit=set_struct_member_type: The assets that use the struct must be found before a type change (use struct.get_struct with info=usage).
edit=rename_struct: A non-struct asset must be renamed or moved (use asset.rename or asset.move).
edit=duplicate_struct: An asset that is not a struct must be copied (use asset.duplicate).
edit=import_struct: The definition must be exported as JSON, not imported (use struct.get_struct with info=export).
edit=recompile_struct: One Blueprint must be compiled rather than a struct (use blueprint.compile).
edit=refresh_struct_dependencies: Only the struct status and validity must be read (use struct.get_struct).
edit=set_instanced_struct_property: A plain property on an actor or asset must be written (use inspect.set_property).

name.description: Struct name.

path.description: Package path (default /Game/Structs).

structPath.description: Full asset path of the new struct, e.g. /Game/Structs/S_WeaponRow; alternative to name and path.

members.description: Member definitions, each { name, type } (or memberName, memberType) with optional defaultValue, tooltip and metadata.

save.description: Persist the struct to disk. Defaults to true; pass false to keep the change in memory only.

memberType.description: Unreal property type: Bool, Int, Float, String, Name, Text, Vector, Rotator, Transform, Object, SoftObject, Class, SoftClass, Enum:<Name>, Struct:<Path>, or with container prefix Array:..., Set:..., Map:<K>,<V>:

varGuid.description: Stable member GUID, as get_struct lists it; pass this or memberName.

position.description: Where the moved member goes: first or last of the struct, or before or after the member named in relativeTo.

relativeTo.description: Name or GUID of the member to place the moved member next to. Required for before and after; ignored for first and last.

newName.description: New struct name; the struct stays in its folder unless destinationFolder is given.

destinationFolder.description: Folder to move the renamed struct into, e.g. /Game/Data.

newStructPath.description: Full new object path, e.g. /Game/Data/S_WeaponStats.S_WeaponStats; alternative to newName.

destinationPath.description: Folder for the copy, e.g. /Game/Structs, when destinationName is given, the path ends in "/" or the folder exists; the copy is destinationPath/destinationName, or keeps the source name without one. Otherwise the full new asset path, e.g. /Game/Structs/S_WeaponRow_V2. A copy onto an existing struct is refused with ALREADY_EXISTS.

destinationName.description: Name of the new asset. With destinationPath it is placed in that folder; on its own the copy stays beside the source.

sourcePath.description: Project-relative JSON file holding the members: a bare array, or an object with a members array as export_struct returns. Used when members is omitted.

propertyName.description: Property name.

edit.description:
Which edit struct variant to run.
create_struct: Create a new Blueprint Struct asset.
add_struct_member: Add a new member to a Blueprint Struct.
rename_struct_member: Rename a member in a Blueprint Struct.
reorder_struct_members: Reorder members in a Blueprint Struct.
set_struct_member_default: Set the default value of a member in a Blueprint Struct.
set_struct_member_metadata: Set metadata (tooltip, etc.) on a member in a Blueprint Struct.
set_struct_member_type: Change the type of a member in a Blueprint Struct.
rename_struct: Rename a Blueprint Struct asset.
duplicate_struct: Duplicate a Blueprint Struct asset.
import_struct: Replace the members of an existing Blueprint Struct, or create a new one, from member definitions or a JSON file.
recompile_struct: Recompile a Blueprint Struct to update generated headers.
refresh_struct_dependencies: Refresh dependencies of a Blueprint Struct after external changes.
set_instanced_struct_property: Set a property on an FInstancedStruct on an asset.

details.description: Operation details.

discovery.summary: Read structs, chosen by info. struct (read, members and export give the same reply) reads a Blueprint or native struct: name, status, validity and every member { guid, name, type, default, tooltip, containerType, metaData }, the members array import_struct takes back; list lists the Blueprint struct assets under path (default /Game/Structs, recursive); usage lists the assets that reference a Blueprint struct (assetPath, className, referencerType Blueprint, Struct, DataAsset or Other), narrowed by a searchScope path prefix; compare diffs two Blueprint structs member by member, paired by member guid so a rename reads as renamedFrom and renamedTo, each diff added, removed or changed with its type and default in each, plus tooltip and metadata mismatches (metadata from UE 5.5); instanced_property reads an FInstancedStruct property of an asset. Nothing is written.
whenToUse: info=struct|read|members: A struct's member names, types, defaults and tooltips must be known before rows or edits are written; native /Script structs such as Vector can be read too.
info=list: The Blueprint structs under a folder must be found; the search is recursive and defaults to /Game/Structs.
info=usage: Every asset that references a struct, such as Blueprints, other structs and DataTables, must be found before changing or deleting it.
info=compare: Two structs must be diffed for added, removed, renamed or retyped members and changed defaults, tooltips or order.
info=export: A struct definition must be returned as JSON members that import_struct accepts, to reuse or restore it.
info=instanced_property: The struct type and field values held in an FInstancedStruct property of an asset must be read.
whenNotToUse: info=struct|read|members: A struct must be changed rather than read (use struct.edit_struct).
info=list: Assets of another type must be found (use asset.query_asset).
info=usage: References to an asset that is not a struct are needed (use asset.inspect_asset).
info=compare: A struct must be brought in line with another; the comparison only reports differences (use struct.edit_struct).
info=export: A struct must be copied as a new asset (use struct.edit_struct with edit=duplicate_struct).
info=instanced_property: A plain property on an actor or asset must be read (use inspect.get_property).

structPath.description: Asset path of the Blueprint Struct (e.g. /Game/Structs/S_MyStruct).

path.description: Package path to search (default /Game/Structs), recursive.

propertyName.description: Property name.

info.description:
Which get struct variant to run; omit for 'struct'.
struct: Read a Blueprint or native struct: name, status, validity and every member as { guid, name, type, default, tooltip, containerType, metaData }.
read: Read a struct definition: the same reply as info=struct, with the name, status, validity and every member. It returns no row or instance values.
members: List a struct's members with guid, type, default, tooltip and metadata. The reply is the same as info=struct, so it also carries the struct name, status and validity.
list: List the Blueprint struct assets under path (default /Game/Structs), searching its subfolders.
usage: List the assets that reference a Blueprint struct, each with assetPath, className and referencerType (Blueprint, Struct, DataAsset or Other), and usageCount; searchScope keeps only those whose path starts with it.
compare: Diff two Blueprint structs member by member: members are paired by their guid (then by name), so a rename reads as renamedFrom and renamedTo; each diff is added, removed or changed with the type and default in each struct (inA, inB), plus tooltip and metadata mismatches (metadata from UE 5.5). Identical structs give an empty diff.
export: Return a struct definition as JSON: the same reply as info=struct, whose members array (name, type, default, tooltip, metaData) import_struct accepts as members or as a sourcePath file. Nothing is written to disk.
instanced_property: Get a property from an FInstancedStruct on an asset.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Read structs, chosen by info. struct (read, members and export give the same reply) reads a Blueprint or native struct: name, status, validity and every member { guid, name, type, default, tooltip, containerType, metaData }, the members array import_struct takes back; list lists the Blueprint struct assets under path (default /Game/Structs, recursive); usage lists the assets that reference a Blueprint struct (assetPath, className, referencerType Blueprint, Struct, DataAsset or Other), narrowed by a searchScope path prefix; compare diffs two Blueprint structs member by member, paired by member guid so a rename reads as renamedFrom and renamedTo, each diff added, removed or changed with its type and default in each, plus tooltip and metadata mismatches (metadata from UE 5.5); instanced_property reads an FInstancedStruct property of an asset. Nothing is written.

discovery.summary: Configure display and rendering variables: resolution, fullscreen, quality, a console variable, FPS counter, profiling overlay.
whenToUse: setting=resolution: The editor window resolution must be changed.
setting=fullscreen: The editor must switch between windowed and fullscreen modes.
setting=quality: A scalability quality group must be changed at runtime.
setting=cvar: A single CVar must be set to a value.
setting=fps: The frames-per-second counter should be shown or hidden.
setting=profile: A specific engine profiling stat overlay must be enabled.
whenNotToUse: setting=resolution: Only the render resolution scale is needed (use set_resolution_scale).
setting=quality: Full scalability state must be set atomically (use set_scalability).
setting=fps: Detailed per-category stats are needed (use show_stats).
setting=profile: A structured profiling capture is needed (use start_profiling).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

category.description: Scalability category (shadow, texture, effect, postprocess, foliage, shading, viewdistance, ...).

name.description: CVar name (alternatively cvar, key, or command).

command.description: Alternate CVar name field (parsed as name + value).

value.description: Value to assign to the CVar.

setting.description:
Which configure display variant to run.
resolution: Set the screen resolution via the r.SetRes console command.
fullscreen: Toggle fullscreen mode via r.SetRes or r.FullScreenMode console command.
quality: Set an engine scalability quality CVar (sg.*Quality) for a category and level.
cvar: Set a console variable value, derived from name/cvar/key/command plus value.
fps: Toggle the FPS HUD overlay via the stat fps console command.
profile: Toggle a profiling stat display (CPU, GPU, memory, render/game thread) via console command.

discovery.summary: Configure performance settings, chosen by setting: scalability levels or a baseline profile (saved, kept across restarts); session-only console settings (frame rate cap, resolution scale, vsync, LOD and mip bias, Nanite, occlusion culling, texture streaming, draw-call batching, GPU timing), each set as the console does and read back, with appliedCVars and notSet in the reply and CVAR_UNAVAILABLE when none took; World Partition streaming and grid; a shader recompile.
whenToUse: setting=scalability: A scalability group level must be changed atomically.
setting=frame_rate_limit: A maximum FPS cap must be applied.
setting=resolution_scale: The primary render resolution scale must be changed.
setting=vsync: VSync must be toggled at runtime.
setting=lod: A forced LOD level or LOD bias must be applied.
setting=nanite: Nanite rendering must be switched on or off, for example to compare against the fallback meshes.
setting=occlusion_culling: Occlusion culling must be switched on or off.
setting=texture_streaming: Texture streaming must be switched or its pool resized.
setting=world_partition: World Partition streaming must be switched, or its grid cell size or loading range changed.
setting=gpu_timing: Per-frame GPU timing instrumentation must be enabled or disabled.
setting=draw_calls: Draw-call count must be reduced through instancing or batching.
setting=shaders: Shaders must be recompiled after shader source files changed.
setting=baseline: A predefined performance baseline profile must be applied.
whenNotToUse: setting=scalability: A single CVar outside scalability groups is needed (use set_cvar).
setting=frame_rate_limit: VSync should be used instead for display-synced limiting.
setting=resolution_scale: The window resolution must change (use set_resolution).
setting=lod: Per-actor LOD is the goal (use control_actor).
setting=nanite: One mesh must gain or lose Nanite (a setting of that static mesh asset).
setting=occlusion_culling: The scene is too small to benefit from occlusion culling.
setting=texture_streaming: A one-off texture import is the goal (use manage_asset).
setting=world_partition: Level streaming is managed per-sublevel (use manage_level).
setting=gpu_timing: A full profiling capture is needed (use start_profiling).
setting=draw_calls: Actors should be merged into a single mesh (use merge_actors).
setting=shaders: A full material recompile is needed (use manage_asset compile_material).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

category.description: Scalability group: ViewDistance, AntiAliasing, Shadow, GlobalIllumination, Reflection, PostProcess, Texture, Effects, Foliage or Shading. Omit (or Overall) to set every group.

maxFPS.description: Maximum frames per second; 0 for no cap.

scale.description: Percent of the window resolution per axis (100 is full resolution); 0 for the engine default.

enabled.description: VSync on (true, the default) or off (false).

forceLOD.description: LOD index every static mesh draws (0 is the most detailed); -1 returns to distance-based LOD.

lodBias.description: Texture mip bias, -15 to 15 (r.MipMapLODBias); positive is blurrier, 0 the default.

poolSize.description: Streaming pool size in megabytes, at least 1, or -1 for the engine default.

cellSize.description: Cell size of the first runtime grid, in cm.

streamingDistance.description: Loading range of the first runtime grid, in cm: cells this close to a streaming source load.

enableBatching.description: Same as enabled; enabled wins when both are given.

enableInstancing.description: Dynamic instancing of compatible draws (r.MeshDrawCommands.DynamicInstancing), default true.

mode.description: changed (the default): shaders whose source changed; global: the global shaders.

forceRecompile.description: Recompile every shader, overriding mode (default false); slow on a large project.

profile.description: performance (Low), balanced (High, the default) or quality (Epic).

setting.description:
Which configure performance variant to run.
scalability: Set one scalability group (category), or every group, to a level from 0 (Low) to 4 (Cinematic), clamped, and save it where the editor loads its scalability at startup, as the Scalability menu does, so it stays across restarts. An unknown category is refused.
frame_rate_limit: Cap the frame rate of this editor session, Play In Editor included, at maxFPS (t.MaxFPS); 0 removes the cap. Set as the console does and read back; gone on restart. A minimized or unfocused editor still drops to about 3 fps (Editor Preferences > Use Less CPU when in Background). A negative maxFPS is refused. Reply appliedCVars and notSet.
resolution_scale: Set the 3D render resolution of game views to scale percent of the window per axis (r.ScreenPercentage: 100 full, 50 a quarter of the pixels, upscaled to the window). Play In Editor renders at it; the level viewport keeps its own screen percentage (Editor Preferences > Performance), and dynamic resolution, when on, overrides it. Set as the console does and read back, for this session only; 0 returns to the engine default, a negative scale is refused. Reply appliedCVars and notSet.
vsync: Turn vertical sync on or off for this editor session: r.VSyncEditor, which the editor windows and Play In Editor present by, and r.VSync, which a game process reads. Set as the console does and read back; gone on restart (a packaged game takes vsync from its own settings). Reply appliedCVars and notSet.
lod: Set a texture mip bias (lodBias, r.MipMapLODBias, -15 to 15: positive draws lower-resolution mips, so textures blur and use less memory) and/or force static meshes to one LOD (forceLOD, r.ForceLOD: a LOD index, -1 back to distance-based LOD). Send at least one; only what is sent changes. Set as the console does and read back, for this session only. Reply appliedCVars and notSet.
nanite: Turn Nanite rendering on or off for this session (r.Nanite, default on): off draws every Nanite mesh with its fallback mesh, as a platform without Nanite would. It changes nothing on a project or graphics API without Nanite (Windows needs DirectX 12 with Shader Model 6). Set as the console does and read back. Reply appliedCVars and notSet.
occlusion_culling: Turn hardware occlusion culling on or off (r.AllowOcclusionQueries, default on): with it, meshes hidden behind others are skipped before drawing. Set as the console does and read back, for this session only; the project setting is Project Settings > Rendering > Occlusion Culling. The occlusion slop and minimum screen radius are renderer constants with no setting. Reply appliedCVars and notSet.
texture_streaming: Turn texture streaming on or off (r.TextureStreaming; off keeps every texture at full resolution, which can run out of video memory on a large project) and/or size its pool (poolSize megabytes, r.Streaming.PoolSize; -1 returns to the engine default). Only what is sent changes; a call with neither, or a poolSize of 0, is refused. Set as the console does and read back, for this session only. Reply appliedCVars and notSet.
world_partition: World Partition streaming of the open level: enabled switches Enable Streaming in its World Settings (off loads every actor of the world into the editor, slow on a large world; one undo step); cellSize and streamingDistance set the cell size and loading range in cm of its first runtime grid (MainPartition on a Runtime Hash Set level) through manage_level_structure configure_grid_size, which then answers with every grid. Send at least one; the level is left unsaved. A level without World Partition is refused (WORLD_PARTITION_NOT_ENABLED); UE 5.0 confirms a streaming change in a dialog an automated call answers No, so there it can be refused (STREAMING_NOT_CHANGED).
gpu_timing: Turn GPU timing on or off and show or hide the stat GPU overlay to match: in the Play In Editor view while it runs, else in the level viewport used last, which draws stats only while realtime. Up to UE 5.7 it also sets r.GPUStatsEnabled, which gates GPU timing (UE 5.8 always times the GPU). Reply overlayShown says whether the overlay is on screen now. Session only; needs the editor.
draw_calls: Set the two draw-call batching switches of the renderer: enableInstancing merges compatible visible meshes into instanced draws (r.MeshDrawCommands.DynamicInstancing) and enabled renders from cached mesh draw commands (r.MeshDrawCommands.UseCachedCommands). Both default to on, as in the engine, so a call with no params restores the defaults. Set as the console does and read back, for this session only. Reply appliedCVars and notSet; to merge actors into one mesh use merge_actors.
shaders: Run a shader recompile: mode changed (the default) recompiles shaders whose source files changed, global the global shaders; forceRecompile true recompiles every shader, which can hold the editor for minutes on a large project (the call can outlast the client timeout while the editor keeps working). Any other mode is refused; one material recompiles with manage_asset compile_material. Reply command is the console command run.
baseline: Set every scalability group to one engine level by profile: performance = Low (0), balanced = High (2, the default), quality = Epic (3), saved where the editor loads its scalability so it stays across restarts. Any other profile is refused. VSync and the frame cap are left as they are (setting=vsync, setting=frame_rate_limit).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Configure performance settings, chosen by setting: scalability levels or a baseline profile (saved, kept across restarts); session-only console settings (frame rate cap, resolution scale, vsync, LOD and mip bias, Nanite, occlusion culling, texture streaming, draw-call batching, GPU timing), each set as the console does and read back, with appliedCVars and notSet in the reply and CVAR_UNAVAILABLE when none took; World Partition streaming and grid; a shader recompile.

discovery.summary: Set or read the project's rendering methods by plain name: global illumination and reflections (lumen, screen_space, none), shadows (virtual, maps), anti-aliasing (tsr, taa, fxaa, msaa, none), hardware ray tracing, mesh distance fields, MegaLights, and the default bloom, auto exposure and motion blur. Each change is saved to DefaultEngine.ini and applied live where its console variable allows; the reply reads every setting back and lists the ones that wait for an editor restart.
whenToUse: A project must switch to or away from Lumen, virtual shadow maps or TSR, or turn hardware ray tracing or distance fields on.
A stylized game must drop the default auto exposure, bloom or motion blur.
The current rendering methods must be read (send no setting).
whenNotToUse: One post-process volume or camera must look different (use build_environment configure_post_process).
Any other project setting (use set_project_setting).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

shadows.description: Shadow map method: virtual shadow maps or classic shadow maps.

hardwareRayTracing.description: Support hardware ray tracing (applies after an editor restart).

meshDistanceFields.description: Generate mesh distance fields, which software Lumen traces (applies after an editor restart).

megaLights.description: Use MegaLights by default (UE 5.5 and later; listed under unavailable on older engines).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

settings.description: Every setting above as it reads after the call, by the same names and values.

restartRequired.description: Changed settings that take effect only after the editor restarts (control_editor restart_editor).

unavailable.description: Settings this engine version does not have; nothing was written for them.

note.description: A setting that cannot work as set, such as Lumen without distance fields or hardware ray tracing.

examples.title: Set or read the project's rendering methods by plain name: global illumination and reflections (lumen, screen_space, none), shadows (virtual, maps), anti-aliasing (tsr, taa, fxaa, msaa, none), hardware ray tracing, mesh distance fields, MegaLights, and the default bloom, auto exposure and motion blur. Each change is saved to DefaultEngine.ini and applied live where its console variable allows; the reply reads every setting back and lists the ones that wait for an editor restart.

discovery.summary: Run one console command against the editor world, or through the first player while Play In Editor runs, and return what it printed (output, at most 4096 characters). A command the engine does not recognise fails (EXEC_FAILED); one holding ;, |, &&, a backtick or several lines, or a blocked name (quit, exit, py, crash and the like), is refused (COMMAND_BLOCKED). Success means the engine ran it, not that it had the effect wanted.
whenToUse: A console command must be run with explicit empty-input rejection.
The sounds playing right now must be listed (is the music still on, did a loop stop): au.DumpActiveSounds puts each one with its asset, owner and volume in output.

C++ must be recompiled while the editor runs: LiveCoding.Compile (read_log shows the result; a Live Coding patch is lost when the editor restarts, so a lasting change needs a full build with the editor closed).
An arbitrary console command must be run and its result returned.
whenNotToUse: The command is empty or whitespace-only.
A dedicated system_control action exists for the operation.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

command.description: The non-empty console command to execute.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

output.description: Bounded console output captured from the command.

examples.title: Run one console command against the editor world, or through the first player while Play In Editor runs, and return what it printed (output, at most 4096 characters). A command the engine does not recognise fails (EXEC_FAILED); one holding ;, |, &&, a backtick or several lines, or a blocked name (quit, exit, py, crash and the like), is refused (COMMAND_BLOCKED). Success means the engine ran it, not that it had the effect wanted.

discovery.summary: Create a new C++ class in a project module, as the editor's New C++ Class does: a header and a .cpp from a parent class (Actor, Character, ActorComponent, Object ..., or None for a plain class), then the editor's own compile.
whenToUse: Gameplay logic or a base class belongs in C++: a new class file pair must be added to the project source.
whenNotToUse: A Blueprint class is enough (use manage_blueprint create).
Existing C++ only needs compiling (use run_ubt, or console_command LiveCoding.Compile).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

className.description: The class name without its prefix: MyActor makes AMyActor (an Actor parent), MyThing makes UMyThing (an Object parent). Letters, digits and _.

parentClass.description: The C++ class to derive from, by name or path (Actor, Character, Pawn, ActorComponent, SceneComponent, Object, BlueprintFunctionLibrary, /Script/Engine.GameModeBase), or None for a plain C++ class. A Blueprint class is refused: derive from its C++ parent.

moduleName.description: The project module that gets the files; default the module named after the project, else its first runtime module. A wrong name lists the modules.

subfolder.description: Folder under the module's Public (or Private) folder, such as Gameplay/Pickups; default none. A module without Public and Private folders refuses one: its own folder is no include path, so the class would not compile there.

classLocation.description: public (default): header in Public, .cpp in Private; private: both in Private. A module without those folders takes both files in its own folder.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

className.description: The C++ class name with its prefix (AMyActor).

headerPath.description: Absolute path of the new header.

moduleName.description: The module the class went into.

classPath.description: The class's path once compiled (/Script/<Module>.<Name>), for a class with a UObject parent.

compiled.description: Whether the editor compiled the module after adding the files (Live Coding or hot reload, as its settings say); a Live Coding compile has only started when this answers, and read_log category LogLiveCoding says whether it succeeded.

note.description: What the class needs before it can be used: a build, a restart, or nothing.

examples.title: Create a new C++ class in a project module, as the editor's New C++ Class does: a header and a .cpp from a parent class (Actor, Character, ActorComponent, Object ..., or None for a plain class), then the editor's own compile.

discovery.summary: Make a Widget Blueprint and fill it, or raise an editor notification, chosen by widgetOp. create makes a Widget Blueprint asset (name and savePath, default /Game/UI/Widgets, or widgetPath) from UserWidget or a subclass (widgetType). add_child adds a widget of childClass (TextBlock, Button, Image and so on) under parentName (default the root panel; PARENT_NOT_FOUND for a name that is no panel), named name, with text for one that shows text. show only raises an editor toast with message for duration seconds (default 4): it puts nothing on screen in the game. To show a Widget Blueprint in the game, give a Blueprint Create Widget and Add to Viewport nodes (blueprint.edit_graph), or use blueprint.add_behaviour for a HUD piece.
whenToUse: widgetOp=create: A new UMG widget asset must be created.
widgetOp=add_child: A child component must be added to an existing widget.
widgetOp=show: A short message must be shown to the person at the editor.
whenNotToUse: widgetOp=show: A widget Blueprint must be displayed in game (add it to the viewport from Blueprint logic).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

name.description: Widget name (derived from widgetPath if absent).

widgetPath.description: Full widget asset path such as /Game/UI/WBP_Menu; supplies name and savePath when they are omitted.

widgetType.description: Parent class: UserWidget (default) or another UserWidget subclass by name or path; anything else is refused.

parentName.description: Panel to add the child under (get_widget_info lists the panels); omitted, the root panel. A name that is not a panel fails with PARENT_NOT_FOUND.

widgetId.description: Only "notification" (the default); any other value is refused.

duration.description: Seconds the notification stays up (default 4, 0.5 to 60).

widgetOp.description:
Which create widget variant to run; omit for 'create'.
create: Create a widget asset via the manage_widget_authoring bridge action.
add_child: Add a child widget component to a parent widget via the manage_widget_authoring bridge action.
show: Show an editor toast notification with a message; it cannot put a widget Blueprint on screen.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

componentName.description: Name the new widget got.

examples.title: Make a Widget Blueprint and fill it, or raise an editor notification, chosen by widgetOp. create makes a Widget Blueprint asset (name and savePath, default /Game/UI/Widgets, or widgetPath) from UserWidget or a subclass (widgetType). add_child adds a widget of childClass (TextBlock, Button, Image and so on) under parentName (default the root panel; PARENT_NOT_FOUND for a name that is no panel), named name, with text for one that shows text. show only raises an editor toast with message for duration seconds (default 4): it puts nothing on screen in the game. To show a Widget Blueprint in the game, give a Blueprint Create Widget and Add to Viewport nodes (blueprint.edit_graph), or use blueprint.add_behaviour for a HUD piece.

discovery.summary: Delete files the MCP wrote (screenshots or environment snapshots), one path or a list of paths; nothing outside Saved/Screenshots, Saved/unreal-mcp, tmp/unreal-mcp or temp/unreal-mcp can be reached.
whenToUse: A screenshot or snapshot the task created is no longer needed.
whenNotToUse: A project asset must go (use manage_asset delete).
The screenshot is not taken yet (pass keepFile: false to screenshot instead).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

path.description: Project-relative file path exactly as list_output_files shows it, e.g. Saved/Screenshots/check.png.

paths.description: Several project-relative file paths to delete in one call; each gets its own entry in results. Takes precedence over path.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

path.description: With path: the file that was deleted.

deleted.description: With path: true when the file is gone.

existsAfter.description: With path: whether the file still exists after the call.

results.description: With paths: one entry per path (path, deleted, and errorCode plus error when it was not deleted). The call fails with PARTIAL_DELETE when any path was not deleted.

deletedCount.description: With paths: how many files were deleted.

failedCount.description: With paths: how many paths were not deleted.

examples.title: Delete files the MCP wrote (screenshots or environment snapshots), one path or a list of paths; nothing outside Saved/Screenshots, Saved/unreal-mcp, tmp/unreal-mcp or temp/unreal-mcp can be reached.

discovery.summary: Change a SaveGame slot on disk: set saved properties and write it again (a missing slot is created from saveGameClass), or delete the slot.
whenToUse: Test runs left values in a save (a best score, unlocks) that must be put back.
A save must be seeded or removed to test a load, continue or first-run flow.
whenNotToUse: The slot only needs reading (use list_save_games).
A running game must change now: it keeps what it loaded, so set the GameInstance value too (inspect.set_property).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

slotName.description: Slot to change, as list_save_games lists it: its file name without .sav.

userIndex.description: User index the game saves under (default 0).

properties.description: Saved properties to set, by name, each value as list_save_games shows it ({"BestScore": 0}). All are checked before the slot is written. A slot being created may leave them out: it is written with its class defaults.

saveGameClass.description: SaveGame subclass to create the slot from when it does not exist yet, such as /Game/Core/BP_Save.BP_Save_C (SaveGame itself is abstract); an existing slot keeps its own class.

deleteSlot.description: true deletes the slot instead; properties are then ignored.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

slotName.description: The slot changed.

saveGameClass.description: Class path of the slot's SaveGame object.

properties.description: Every saved property as read back from the written slot.

created.description: True when the slot did not exist and was created from saveGameClass.

saved.description: True when the slot was written.

deleted.description: With deleteSlot: true when the slot is gone.

existsAfter.description: With deleteSlot: whether the slot still exists after the call.

examples.title: Change a SaveGame slot on disk: set saved properties and write it again (a missing slot is created from saveGameClass), or delete the slot.

discovery.summary: Enable or disable a plugin, or limit it to some build targets: targets ["Editor"] keeps an editor-only plugin out of the packaged game.
whenToUse: pluginState=enable: Migrated content depends on a plugin that is installed but disabled (for example ChaosVehicles for the advanced vehicle template).

pluginState=enable: A plugin used only in the editor should stay out of the packaged game (targets ["Editor"]), or one the game uses must stay on when the plugin that brought it in is limited to the editor.
pluginState=disable: A plugin enabled for a since-removed experiment should no longer load.
whenNotToUse: pluginState=enable: The plugin is not installed at all — list_plugins returns NOT_FOUND and this cannot download it.
pluginState=enable: The effect is needed within the current session; this takes effect only after a restart.
pluginState=disable: Project content still references the plugin's classes or assets.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

pluginName.description: Plugin name exactly as reported by list_plugins (the .uplugin name, not the friendly name).

targets.description: Build targets the plugin is enabled for, every other build leaving it out: ["Editor"] keeps it in the editor and out of a packaged game. An empty list lifts the limit.

pluginState.description:
Which enable plugin variant to run; omit for 'enable'.
enable: Enable a plugin for this project by writing it into the .uproject, or limit it to some build targets (targets ["Editor"] keeps an editor-only plugin out of a packaged game). A plugin on only because another plugin needs it is written into the project file. A plugin the editor has not loaded yet needs a restart, so the response reports restartRequired.
disable: Disable a plugin for this project by removing it from the .uproject. Assets that depend on it fail to load after the restart, so confirm dependents first.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

enabled.description: Enabled state now recorded in the .uproject.

targets.description: The build targets the plugin is now limited to; absent when it is enabled for every target.

changed.description: False when the plugin was already in the requested state and nothing was written.

restartRequired.description: True when this editor loads or drops the plugin only at its next start; a packaged game takes the project file as it is when it builds.

examples.title: Enable or disable a plugin, or limit it to some build targets: targets ["Editor"] keeps an editor-only plugin out of the packaged game.

discovery.summary: Run Python in the editor: inline code (1 MB at most) or a .py file inside the project (a path outside it, or reached through a symlink, is SECURITY_VIOLATION). Needs the Python Editor Script Plugin (PYTHON_NOT_AVAILABLE otherwise) and an explicit consent grant; dialogs answer their default. The reply gives what the script printed (output) and, when it raised, the traceback (error).
whenToUse: Editor-side Python automation must run inline or from a script file.
whenNotToUse: Untrusted code without review; runs arbitrary editor-side code.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

code.description: Python code to execute inline (1 MB max).

file.description: Path to a .py file to execute.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

error.description: Captured stderr and the interpreter traceback when the script raises.

executionId.description: Correlates the run with the temp wrapper under Saved/Temp/MCP_Python.

codeSha256.description: SHA-256 of the executed code, as logged.

examples.title: Run Python in the editor: inline code (1 MB at most) or a .py file inside the project (a path outside it, or reached through a symlink, is SECURITY_VIOLATION). Needs the Python Editor Script Plugin (PYTHON_NOT_AVAILABLE otherwise) and an explicit consent grant; dialogs answer their default. The reply gives what the script printed (output) and, when it raised, the traceback (error).

whenNotToUse: A single setting must be written (use set_project_setting).

key.description: Requested key, when one was asked for.

value.description: Value of the requested key.

hint.description: How to get a full section dump.

examples.title: Read project settings: with no section, the engine version, project name and directory, default maps and general settings; with a section or category (rendering, input, physics, audio, packaging...), every config property of it, or one key's value.

statusQuerySupported.description: Whether this engine version supports status queries.

discovery.summary: List every plugin discovered by this editor with its enabled state, category, version and mounted content path; enabledOnly and filter (name or category) narrow the list.

discovery.summary: Run a script of capability calls in one request, on every UE 5.x, in the S-expression grammar of read_graph_as_code: (let name (capability.id :param value ...)) calls a capability and keeps what it returns (what a direct execute returns: its declared output fields, the rest under details), name.field.0.field reads into it; (for item list ...) goes over a list, (range n) counts 0 to n-1; (if cond ... (else ...)); (expect "assertion") checks the editor in execute's expect language (Crate1.location.z in 0..100, Lamp on Table; the text can be made as it runs: (expect (+ c.label " on Floor"))); (return value) ends the script with its result. Expressions: (not a), (and a b), (or a b), (== a b), (!= a b), (< a b), (<= a b), (> a b), (>= a b), (+ a b) (it also joins text: (+ "Crate_" i)), (- a b), (* a b), (/ a b), (list a b), (obj :x 1 :y 2), literals, null and names; a name is bound once in its block. The whole script is checked before anything runs: every call names a capability, with only parameters its contract declares and each one it requires, and every name is bound before use. Each call is then held to everything a direct execute is (its contract, the caller's scope and path limits, the console policy) and runs on its handler inside this one request. run_script always asks for elevated consent, and each capability the script calls that asks for consent must be named in destructive, which that one consent then covers. A failed call or expectation stops the script and rolls back what it changed, as far as editor undo reaches: a Blueprint compile or a level load clears the undo history (rollback then says what could not be undone), saved files stay saved, and assets it created are listed in cleanupCall. A script cannot call run_script, run_recipe, undo, redo or restore_point, and does not start while a restore point is open (RESTORE_POINT_OPEN). The reply: returned, and steps (one line per call: its line, capability, and ok or its error code and message).
whenToUse: The same call must run for many actors or assets, or later calls depend on what earlier ones returned: one script instead of a round trip per call.
Several changes must all happen or none: a failed call or expectation rolls back the ones before it.
whenNotToUse: One call does the job, or the capability takes many targets itself (spawn with actors, set_transform with actors, build_graph with steps).
Logic the game runs is wanted: write_graph_from_code writes it into a Blueprint.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

script.description: The script, statements one after another (; starts a comment to the end of the line). Refused before anything runs: SCRIPT_PARSE_ERROR, SCRIPT_INVALID, UNKNOWN_CAPABILITY (a name search does not find), UNDECLARED_PARAMETER and MISSING_REQUIRED_PARAMETER (checked against the capability's contract), SCRIPT_UNBOUND_NAME, CONSENT_NOT_LISTED, SCRIPT_STEP_REFUSED. Stopped and rolled back while running: the failed call's own error code, SCRIPT_TYPE (an operator or for over the wrong kind of value), SCRIPT_VALUE (a path into a result that holds no such field: the fields it has are named), EXPECTATION_FAILED, ENGINE_ERROR (the engine logged an error during a call), STEP_DEFERRED (a call that answers later cannot run in a script), SCRIPT_BUDGET, SCRIPT_DEADLINE.

destructive.description: The capabilities the script calls that ask for consent, by id or alias (control_actor.delete, asset.delete); this run's one elevated consent covers exactly these.

maxSteps.description: Calls the script may make; default 200. Past it the script stops (SCRIPT_BUDGET) and rolls back.

deadlineMs.description: Milliseconds after which no further call starts; default 20000, at most 25000 (a client gives up on a call at 30 s). Past it the script stops (SCRIPT_DEADLINE) and rolls back.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

steps.description: One line per call made: "line N capability ok" (a loop's run of the same call as one line, "ok x25"), or "line N capability CODE: message" for the call that stopped the script.

returned.description: The value of (return ...), when the script returned one.

rolledBack.description: On a failure: whether everything the script changed was undone.

rollback.description: On a failure: what undoing the script did, or why it could not undo everything.

cleanupCall.description: On a failure: the manage_asset bulk_delete call that removes the assets the script created, which undo does not remove.
