whenNotToUse: The camera must move first, or shaders finish compiling, in the same call (use control_editor.screenshot, which takes the same shots plus location, rotation and waitForShaders).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

filename.description: File name of the PNG (.png is added; a folder part is dropped). Default Screenshot_<unix time>.

mode.description: What to capture: editor_viewport (default, the level viewport), game_viewport (the running game frame without its UMG widgets) or full_editor_window (the editor window as displayed, game UI and asset editors included).

window.description: With mode full_editor_window, which window to capture: a list index (2, or "2") or a case-insensitive substring of its title ("WBP_HubUI"). Omit for the main editor frame; responses list the open windows under windows[].

resolution.description: Maximum WxH for the PNG (e.g. "1280x720"), aspect ratio kept, never upscaled. Without it an image returned inline fits 1600x900.

keepFile.description: false: hand the image back without leaving a file in Saved/Screenshots (refused with returnBase64 false, which would leave no output at all). Default true. Files already written are listed by list_output_files and removed by delete_output_file.

path.description: game_viewport mode only: project-relative folder to write the PNG into (default Saved/Screenshots/WindowsEditor).

returnBase64.description: Return the PNG inline as an image (default true); a capture also saves a file unless keepFile is false. With no resolution, an inline image is downscaled to fit 1600x900. false returns only the saved path and metadata, at the full viewport size.

includeMetadata.description: true: echo metadata back in the reply (default false).

metadata.description: An object of your own, such as a label or a step number, returned under metadata when includeMetadata is true; the capture itself never reads it.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Capture a screenshot as a PNG, returned inline (downscaled to fit 1600x900 unless resolution sets the box) and saved under Saved/Screenshots unless keepFile is false. mode editor_viewport, the default, shoots the level viewport; game_viewport the running game frame without its UMG widgets (path picks the folder; NO_VIEWPORT when no game runs); full_editor_window the editor window as displayed, game UI and asset editors included (window picks another open window by index or title). returnBase64 false returns only the saved path, at full size.

discovery.summary: Set one setting (section and key): applied to the live settings object and saved where the editor itself saves that class, the project Default<Config>.ini for a project setting, the user Saved config for a per-user one (EditorPerProjectUserSettings). configFile names the file written.
whenToUse: A single project setting value must be written.

The level the game or the editor opens first must change: section GameMapsSettings, key GameDefaultMap (the game and a packaged build) or EditorStartupMap (the editor), value the level as /Game/Maps/L_Main.L_Main.
whenNotToUse: The full settings document must be read (use get_project_settings).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

section.description: Settings section: a settings class path such as /Script/EngineSettings.GameMapsSettings, its class name (GameMapsSettings), or a raw ini section in brackets ([SystemSettings]); a name that is none of these is refused.

value.description: Setting value.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Set one setting (section and key): applied to the live settings object and saved where the editor itself saves that class, the project Default<Config>.ini for a project setting, the user Saved config for a per-user one (EditorPerProjectUserSettings). configFile names the file written.

discovery.summary: Unreal Insights: start, stop, pause or resume a trace session, capture a trace, send or write a snapshot, launch the Insights viewer.
whenToUse: control=start: A new trace session must be started.
control=stop: The trace session must be terminated.
control=pause: Trace capture must be temporarily suspended.
control=resume: A paused trace session must continue capturing.
control=capture_trace: A trace must be captured for later analysis.
control=send_snapshot: A snapshot must be forwarded to an active trace session.
control=write_snapshot: A point-in-time trace snapshot must be written to disk.
control=launch_viewer: The Insights GUI must be launched for trace analysis.
whenNotToUse: control=start: A session is already running (use pause/resume/stop).
control=resume: No session is paused.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

channels.description: Trace channels (validated: letters, digits, underscore, comma, space, hyphen).

connectionType.description: Trace connection type; network is restricted to loopback.

traceFile.description: File mode: .utrace file name, resolved inside Saved/Profiling (default a generated McpInsights_<time>.utrace).

overwrite.description: Replace an existing trace file of that name (default false: an existing file is refused).

launchViewer.description: Open the Unreal Insights application on the trace: default true for control=launch_viewer (start_unreal_insights), false for the other variants.

snapshotPath.description: Snapshot .utrace file name, resolved inside Saved/Profiling (default a generated name).

control.description:
Which start session variant to run; omit for 'start'.
start: Start an Unreal Insights trace session.
stop: Stop the active trace session.
pause: Pause the active trace session.
resume: Resume a paused trace session.
capture_trace: Capture an Unreal Insights trace to a .utrace file under Saved/Profiling (use control=start for a network trace).
send_snapshot: Send a trace snapshot to a trace server (Unreal Insights) on this machine.
write_snapshot: Write a trace snapshot to a snapshot path.
launch_viewer: Open the Unreal Insights application on a trace: starts a trace session when none is running (the same inputs as control=start) and launches the viewer; pass launchViewer: false to only start the trace.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Unreal Insights: start, stop, pause or resume a trace session, capture a trace, send or write a snapshot, launch the Insights viewer.

discovery.summary: Stream the editor log to this connection (subscribe, unsubscribe), or turn a Gameplay Debugger category on or off.
whenToUse: control=subscribe: New editor log lines must be streamed as they arrive.
control=unsubscribe: A log subscription made with subscribe must end.
control=spawn_category: A Gameplay Debugger category (AI, BehaviorTree, EQS, Perception, ...) must show or hide in the in-game debugger.
whenNotToUse: control=subscribe: A one-shot historical log read is needed.
control=unsubscribe: No subscription is active.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

categoryName.description: A registered category name, case ignored (letters, digits, underscore, hyphen only).

category.description: Same as categoryName; categoryName wins when both are given.

enabled.description: Show (true, default) or hide (false) the category in game.

control.description:
Which subscribe variant to run; omit for 'subscribe'.
subscribe: Subscribe this connection to the live editor log stream (every category; filter on the client, or use read_log for a filtered one-shot read).
unsubscribe: Stop streaming the live editor log to this connection.
spawn_category: Turn a registered Gameplay Debugger category (AI, BehaviorTree, EQS, Navigation, Perception and the like) on or off: its ActiveInGame and ActiveInSimulate settings for this editor session (not saved to the project's config), and at once in a running game's debugger (replicatorUpdated). A name that is not registered is refused (CATEGORY_NOT_FOUND) with the ones that are.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Stream the editor log to this connection (subscribe, unsubscribe), or turn a Gameplay Debugger category on or off.

discovery.summary: Check that assets load without error, with dataValidation that they pass the project's and the engine's Data Validation (the editor's Validate Assets), and with materialUsage that their meshes' materials carry the usage flags a cooked game needs: each asset path, or every asset under a folder (recursive by default); returns isValid, per-path results and the checked and invalid counts.
whenToUse: Asset references must be validated before use.
Assets must pass Data Validation (the editor's Validate Assets) before they are relied on or shipped.
Before packaging: materialUsage finds the meshes a cooked game would draw with the default material.
whenNotToUse: A single asset must be imported or created (use manage_asset).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

path.description: Another single asset or folder path; validated alongside assetPath when both are given.

recursive.description: For a folder path, include its subfolders (default true).

dataValidation.description: Also run Data Validation on every asset that loads (default false): an asset row gains dataValidation (valid, invalid or notValidated, the last when no validator checks that kind of asset) with its errors and warnings, a folder row the count of each verdict and issues (up to 20 assets with errors or warnings). An invalid asset makes its row invalid.

materialUsage.description: Also list the material usage flags the assets' meshes need and their materials lack (default false): a Nanite static mesh's slots, a skeletal mesh's, and a Blueprint's mesh components (Nanite, instanced, spline or skeletal), as materialUsage [{material, usage, property, unsaved, component, asset}] (a folder: at most 40, with materialUsageCount). The editor sets such a flag only while it draws the mesh outside play, so a mesh that only appears in play draws the default material there and in a cooked game; set property true on the material (inspect set_property) to fix one. unsaved true: the editor set the flag (drawing a preview or loading a mesh sets it) but it is not on disk yet; save that material (control_editor save_all with assetPaths). On UE 5.8 a material instance holds its own flags, so material can name the instance. A missing flag makes its row invalid.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

isValid.description: True when every path loaded (and, with dataValidation, none was invalid; with materialUsage, no flag was missing).

results.description: One row per path: path, isValid, kind (asset, directory, missing or invalid), message, assetCount for a folder, with dataValidation its verdict, errors, warnings or issues, and with materialUsage the missing flags (materialUsage, and materialUsageCount for a folder).

examples.title: Check that assets load without error, with dataValidation that they pass the project's and the engine's Data Validation (the editor's Validate Assets), and with materialUsage that their meshes' materials carry the usage flags a cooked game needs: each asset path, or every asset under a folder (recursive by default); returns isValid, per-path results and the checked and invalid counts.

output.message: Asset validation completed; all assets valid

discovery.summary: Edit the pixels of an 8-bit texture in place (assetPath; a 16-bit or HDR source is refused, and a grayscale one becomes BGRA8), chosen by adjust: curves maps the channel through curvePoints ({x, y} pairs from 0 to 1, at least two); levels remaps inBlack to inWhite (0 to 1) with gamma; blur averages over radius (default 2, 1 to 10); sharpen at strength (default 1, up to 5); desaturate by amount (default 1, fully gray); invert flips the colors. channel picks R, G, B or A for curves, levels and invert (otherwise the three color channels). The texture is saved unless save is false (saved), with no undo, so duplicate it first to keep the original; engine content is refused (ENGINE_CONTENT).
whenToUse: adjust=curves: A tonal curve such as an S-curve for contrast must be applied to one colour channel or to all of them.
adjust=levels: Brightness or contrast must change through black point, white point or gamma, on one channel or on all colour channels.
adjust=blur: A texture must be softened; radius is a whole number from 1 to 10.
adjust=sharpen: A soft or downsampled texture needs crisper edges; strength runs from 0 to 5.
adjust=desaturate: A texture must lose colour, fully or by an amount from 0 to 1.
adjust=invert: Colour channels must be flipped, for example the green channel of a normal map to change its handedness.
whenNotToUse: The original pixels must be kept, since these edits are made in place (duplicate the texture first with asset.duplicate).
adjust=curves: Two textures must be blended, not one edited (use texture.create_texture with kind=combined).
adjust=blur: A smaller copy is wanted rather than softer pixels (use texture.create_texture with kind=resized).
adjust=sharpen: The texture only looks soft at a distance (use texture.configure_texture for mip bias and streaming).
adjust=desaturate: A grayscale copy of one channel is wanted as a new texture (use texture.create_texture with kind=channel_extract).
adjust=invert: A normal map only needs its compression fixed (use texture.configure_texture).

assetPath.description: Texture /Game path. Its source must be 8-bit BGRA8 or single-channel G8 (a channel_extract result); a G8 texture is rewritten as BGRA8 with its gray in R, G and B and alpha 255. Other source formats (G16, RGBA16, float, HDR) fail with an error naming the format found.

curvePoints.description: Curve control points as {x, y} pairs in 0-1; at least two.

save.description: Save after adjustment.

adjust.description:
Which adjust texture variant to run.
curves: Apply curve-based adjustments to a texture.
levels: Adjust levels (black/white points, gamma) on a texture.
blur: Apply a blur filter to a texture.
sharpen: Apply a sharpen filter to a texture.
desaturate: Desaturate a texture by an amount.
invert: Invert color channels of a texture.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Edit the pixels of an 8-bit texture in place (assetPath; a 16-bit or HDR source is refused, and a grayscale one becomes BGRA8), chosen by adjust: curves maps the channel through curvePoints ({x, y} pairs from 0 to 1, at least two); levels remaps inBlack to inWhite (0 to 1) with gamma; blur averages over radius (default 2, 1 to 10); sharpen at strength (default 1, up to 5); desaturate by amount (default 1, fully gray); invert flips the colors. channel picks R, G, B or A for curves, levels and invert (otherwise the three color channels). The texture is saved unless save is false (saved), with no undo, so duplicate it first to keep the original; engine content is refused (ENGINE_CONTENT).

discovery.summary: Change one setting of a 2D texture asset (assetPath), chosen by setting; the texture is saved unless save is false (saved). compression sets compressionSettings by engine name, with or without the TC_ prefix (Normalmap, Masks, Grayscale, HDR, EditorIcon for UI, BC7 ...); texture_group sets textureGroup, with or without TEXTUREGROUP_ (World, Character, UI, Effects ...), so the texture follows that group's LOD and streaming rules; an unknown name in either is refused with the valid names. lod_bias drops lodBias top mips at runtime (1 halves each side, 0 restores full size). virtual_texture sets virtualTextureStreaming (required); materials sampling the texture then need the matching sampler type (Virtual Color and so on, or back) or they stop compiling. streaming_priority sets neverStream (required): true keeps every mip resident; there is no per-texture streaming priority.
whenToUse: setting=compression: A texture needs the compression its use calls for: Normalmap for a normal map, Masks for packed masks read without sRGB, Grayscale for one channel, HDR for HDR images, EditorIcon for UI art.
setting=lod_bias: A background or distant texture uses too much memory and can lose its largest mip levels; a lodBias of 1 drops one level.
setting=streaming_priority: A texture must stay sharp because every mip is kept resident instead of streaming in late; there is no per-texture streaming priority to set.
setting=texture_group: A texture must move to another group, such as UI, Character or Effects, so it follows that group's LOD rules.

setting=virtual_texture: A very large texture must stream as a virtual texture, or stop; afterwards set the SamplerType of each material node that samples it (inspect.set_property with objectPath "<material path>.<material name>:<nodeId>", SAMPLERTYPE_VirtualColor and so on).
whenNotToUse: The pixels or size of the texture must change, not its asset settings (use texture.adjust_texture or texture.create_texture).
setting=lod_bias: A smaller copy of the source image is wanted, not a runtime mip drop (use texture.create_texture with kind=resized).
setting=streaming_priority: The global texture streaming budget must change, not one texture (use system_control.configure_performance with setting=texture_streaming).

compressionSettings.description: Engine compression name, with or without TC_: Default, Normalmap, Masks, Grayscale, Displacementmap, VectorDisplacementmap, HDR, EditorIcon (UserInterface2D), Alpha, DistanceFieldFont, HDR_Compressed, BC7, HalfFloat, and from UE 5.1 SingleFloat and HDR_F32.

save.description: Save the texture after the change (default true); saved says whether it reached disk.

lodBias.description: Whole mips to drop (a fraction is cut off): 1 halves each side, 0 restores full size.

neverStream.description: true keeps every mip resident, false lets the texture stream; leaving it out is refused.

textureGroup.description: Engine texture group, with or without TEXTUREGROUP_: World, WorldNormalMap, WorldSpecular, Character, CharacterNormalMap, Weapon, Vehicle, Cinematic, Effects, Skybox, UI, Lightmap, Shadowmap, ColorLookupTable, Bokeh, Pixels2D and the rest.

virtualTextureStreaming.description: true streams the texture as a virtual texture (the project must have virtual texturing enabled), false stops; leaving it out is refused.

setting.description:
Which configure texture variant to run.
compression: Set a 2D texture's compression setting by its engine name, with or without the TC_ prefix (Normalmap or TC_Normalmap). The reply names the setting applied (compressionSettings) and whether the texture reached disk (saved). An unknown name is refused with the valid names and nothing changes.
lod_bias: Set a 2D texture's LOD bias: the number of top mips dropped at runtime (1 halves each side, 0 restores full size). The reply carries lodBias and saved.
streaming_priority: Set never-stream on a 2D texture (neverStream, required): true keeps every mip resident instead of streaming them in, false lets it stream again. UTexture has no per-texture streaming priority to set. The reply carries neverStream and saved.
texture_group: Set a 2D texture's texture group (its LOD group) by engine name, with or without the TEXTUREGROUP_ prefix (UI or TEXTUREGROUP_UI), so it follows that group's LOD and streaming rules. The reply names the group applied (textureGroup) and saved; an unknown name is refused with the valid names and nothing changes.
virtual_texture: Switch virtual texture streaming on or off for a 2D texture (virtualTextureStreaming, required). Materials that sample the texture must then use the matching sampler type (Virtual Color, Virtual Normal and so on, or the plain type when it is switched off), or they stop compiling. The reply carries virtualTextureStreaming and saved.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Change one setting of a 2D texture asset (assetPath), chosen by setting; the texture is saved unless save is false (saved). compression sets compressionSettings by engine name, with or without the TC_ prefix (Normalmap, Masks, Grayscale, HDR, EditorIcon for UI, BC7 ...); texture_group sets textureGroup, with or without TEXTUREGROUP_ (World, Character, UI, Effects ...), so the texture follows that group's LOD and streaming rules; an unknown name in either is refused with the valid names. lod_bias drops lodBias top mips at runtime (1 halves each side, 0 restores full size). virtual_texture sets virtualTextureStreaming (required); materials sampling the texture then need the matching sampler type (Virtual Color and so on, or back) or they stop compiling. streaming_priority sets neverStream (required): true keeps every mip resident; there is no per-texture streaming priority.

discovery.summary: Create a texture: gradient, noise, pattern, text, normal from height, ambient occlusion baked from a mesh, resized copy, channel pack/extract, or a combination of two textures.
whenToUse: kind=gradient: A linear, radial or angular gradient ramp texture is needed, for example a mask or falloff.
kind=noise: A procedural Perlin, ridged or billow noise texture is needed as a mask, cloud or roughness variation; it can tile.
kind=pattern: A checker, grid, brick, stripe or dot pattern texture is needed, for example a debug or placeholder surface.
kind=text: Words must appear on a surface: a shirt print, sign, label, logo or number, sampled by a material or a decal.
kind=ao_from_mesh: A static mesh needs a ray-traced ambient occlusion map in its UV space; a convex mesh comes out flat white.
kind=normal_from_height: A normal map must be derived from a heightmap texture; strength scales the bump depth.
kind=resized: A texture must be copied at a smaller or larger size such as 512px; the source texture is left as it is.
kind=channel_pack: Separate AO, roughness and metallic maps must be packed into the channels of one linear texture.

kind=channel_pack: Sources are 8-bit BGRA8 or single-channel G8 textures such as channel_extract results; a BGRA8 source gives its same channel (alpha from its alpha), a G8 source gives its gray to whichever channel it is assigned, and any other source format (G16, RGBA16, float, HDR) fails naming the format found.
kind=channel_extract: One channel of a packed texture must become its own grayscale texture.
kind=combined: Two same-size textures must be blended into a new texture with Multiply, Screen, Overlay or Add at a set opacity.
whenNotToUse: kind=gradient: A gradient is only needed inside one material and can come from its UVs and math nodes (use material.add_material_node).
kind=noise: The noise can be computed in the material graph instead of baked (use material.add_material_node with nodeKind=noise).
kind=pattern: A photo or authored image file must be brought into the project (use asset.import).
kind=text: The text belongs in the HUD or a menu (use manage_blueprint widget text), or must change at runtime (use a Text Render component).
kind=ao_from_mesh: Scene lighting must be built, not a per-mesh texture (use build_environment.build_lighting).
kind=normal_from_height: An existing normal map only needs a channel flipped (use texture.adjust_texture with adjust=invert).
kind=resized: Only runtime mip detail or memory must drop, not the source size (use texture.configure_texture).
kind=channel_pack: Separate textures can simply be sampled in a material (use material.add_material_node with nodeKind=texture_sample).
kind=channel_extract: A material only needs one channel of a texture (use material.add_material_node with a texture sample).
kind=combined: Two textures should blend per pixel at render time (use material.add_material_node).

name.description: Texture name.

path.description: Package path.

outputPath.description: Full output asset path, e.g. /Game/Textures/T_Noise; replaces name and path.

startColor.description: Start colour (default black) as {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1.

endColor.description: End colour (default white) as {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1.

noiseType.description: Perlin (default), FBM (same as Perlin), Ridged or Billow.

patternType.description: Checker (default), Grid, Brick, Stripes or Dots.

lineWidth.description: Grid line width as a fraction of a tile (default 0.02).

offset.description: Brick row offset, 0-1 (default 0.5).

primaryColor.description: Main colour (default white) as {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1.

secondaryColor.description: Second colour (default black) as {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1.

text.description: The words to draw; a newline starts a new line.

fontFamily.description: Font asset, e.g. /Engine/EngineFonts/Roboto (default) or a project font.

typeface.description: Face of the font: Regular, Bold, Italic, Light... (default Bold when the font has it). A face the font lacks is refused with the list it has.

letterSpacing.description: Extra space between letters, in thousandths of an em (0 normal, 100 airy, negative tighter).

justification.description: Line alignment of multi-line text: left, center (default) or right.

padding.description: Space kept clear around the text, in pixels (default 4% of the shorter side); the text is scaled to fill the rest.

color.description: Text colour (default white) as {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1.

backgroundColor.description: Background (default transparent, so the alpha channel is the text mask) as {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1.

samples.description: Occlusion rays per texel, 1-1024 (default 64); more is smoother and slower.

rayDistance.description: Farthest occluder counted, in cm; 0 (default) means unlimited, negative is refused.

uvChannel.description: UV channel to bake into (default 0, the one materials sample); a lightmap channel avoids overlapping UVs.

sourceTexture.description: Source heightmap texture path; its source must be an 8-bit BGRA8 or single-channel G8 texture, read as its luminance (a G8 source is its gray). Other source formats (G16, RGBA16, float, HDR) fail with an error naming the format found.

sourcePath.description: Source texture path; its source must be an 8-bit BGRA8 or single-channel G8 texture (a channel_extract result, read as gray in R, G and B with alpha 255). Other source formats (G16, RGBA16, float, HDR) fail with an error naming the format found.

redTexture.description: Red channel source: an 8-bit BGRA8 or G8 texture.

greenTexture.description: Green channel source: an 8-bit BGRA8 or G8 texture.

blueTexture.description: Blue channel source: an 8-bit BGRA8 or G8 texture.

alphaTexture.description: Alpha channel source: an 8-bit BGRA8 or G8 texture.

assetPath.description: Texture /Game path; its source must be an 8-bit BGRA8 or single-channel G8 texture (a channel_extract result, read as gray in R, G and B with alpha 255). Other source formats (G16, RGBA16, float, HDR) fail with an error naming the format found.

baseTexture.description: Base texture path; its source must be an 8-bit BGRA8 or single-channel G8 texture (a channel_extract result, read as gray in R, G and B with alpha 255). Other source formats (G16, RGBA16, float, HDR) fail with an error naming the format found.

blendTexture.description: Blend texture path; it must have the width and height of baseTexture. Its source can be BGRA8 or G8 whichever baseTexture is. Other source formats (G16, RGBA16, float, HDR) fail with an error naming the format found.

kind.description:
Which create texture variant to run.
gradient: Generate a gradient texture.
noise: Generate a procedural noise texture.
pattern: Generate a pattern texture (checker, grid, brick, stripes, dots).
text: Draw text into a texture with any Font asset and face, scaled to fit, for a print, sign, label or logo on a mesh.
ao_from_mesh: Bake a real ray-traced ambient occlusion texture of a static mesh in its own UV space (grayscale, linear): crevices come out dark, open surfaces white.
normal_from_height: Generate a normal map from a heightmap texture.
resized: Resize a texture to new dimensions.
channel_pack: Pack individual channels from multiple textures into one.
channel_extract: Extract a single channel from a texture.
combined: Blend two textures together.

details.description: Operation details.

inkBounds.description: Pixel box the drawn letters cover.

fontSize.description: Font size the text was fitted at, the largest whose lines (letter spacing included) fit inside the padding.

saved.description: Whether the texture was saved.

meanValue.description: Average texel over the whole texture, 0-1 (unused texels count as 1).

convexMesh.description: True when the bake is flat because the mesh is convex and cannot occlude itself.

examples.title: Create a texture: gradient, noise, pattern, text, normal from height, ambient occlusion baked from a mesh, resized copy, channel pack/extract, or a combination of two textures.

discovery.summary: Read a 2D texture asset: width and height, pixel format, mip count, sRGB, compression setting, LOD bias, and virtual texture and never-stream flags.
whenToUse: A texture's size, pixel format, mip count, sRGB flag and compression must be read before its pixels or settings are changed.
A texture setting must be verified after it was changed.
whenNotToUse: A texture setting must be changed, not read (use texture.configure_texture).
The texture group or another property not listed here must be read (use inspect.get_property).

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Read a texture's size and format
